It consists of seven complete tombs of respective Golconda Sultans, and an incomplete one for Abul Hasan Qutb Shah, who was buried in a modest grave at Khuldabad in present-day Maharashtra instead, as Mughal emperor Auragnzeb imprisoned him in Daulatabad till death. Other than the Golconda Sultans, there are tombs of Hayat Bakshi Begum, Fatima Sultana and Kulsum Begum. Hayat Bakshi was the sole daughter of Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, the fifth sultan, who married to Muhammed Qutb Shah, the sixth sultan. She gave birth to Abdullah Qutb Shah, the seventh sultan. Fatima Sultana was the sister of Muhammad Qutb Shah, while Kulsum Begum was his granddaughter. Outside the House of Golconda, there are tombs of two hakeems (unani practitioners) of Abdullah Qutb Shah, Nizamuddin Ahmed Gilani and Abdul Jabbar Gilani, both built in 1651.

attractions.name: Baobab Tree
attractions.description: This African Baobab (Adansonia digitata) tree is 400+ years old and happens to be the oldest tree in Hyderabad. The tree originates from Madagascar and was planted by wandering friars during their stay at Golconda. The circumference of the trunk measures 25 meters and is irregular in shape and roughly represents an elephant and hence the name Hatiyan Jhod (Elephant Tree). The huge trunk is hollow and covers a huge space. According to legend the space provided shelter for 40 thieves during the Qutab Shahi rule. They used it as a shelter during the day and committed the crime during the night.

attractions.name: Hyderabad Golf Club
attractions.description: The once-controversial golf course, now open to public.

attractions.name: Mulla Khayali Mosque
attractions.description: Built to honour the royal poet of the Qutb Shahi court.

attractions.name: Premamati Mosque
attractions.description: A 16th-century mosque built during the reign of Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah as a congregational mosque for a new city west of the Golconda Fort. However, the plan for the new city was abandoned due to the lack of a sustainable water source, leading his successor Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to establish the present-day Old City of Hyderabad further east in 1591, and thus Mecca Masjid as the architectural successor of the Premamati Mosque.

attractions.name: Deccan Park
attractions.description: A large green space opposite the Qutb Shahi Tombs.

attractions.name: Bansilalpet Stepwell
attractions.description: Nothing much is known about the stepwell and its builder. But architectural features state that it dates back over 300 years and was built during the Nizam rule. The Pharaoh & Co map mentions the well as Naganah Kunta in their 1954 map' Later a Britisher named T.H. Keyes developed the area and the project was funded by local businessman Seth Bansilal, after whom the stepwell is popularly known. In the 1980s two men died falling into the well. After this, the well was abandoned and turned into a garbage pit. In 2020 tonnes of garbage were removed and the stepwell was restored. The surrounding was landscaped and galleries were added. The galleries exhibit the transformation process along with the history of the stepwell.

attractions.name: The Hyderabad Public School
attractions.description: A former Nizam's palace and the Jagirdar's College. This Institution was founded in 1923 and is one of the oldest and largest public schools in the country. The campus is a recognised heritage site.

attractions.name: Osmania Arts College
attractions.description: Built during the period of the last Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan. The imposing façade of the building is a great sight.

attractions.name: Rashtrapati Nilayam
attractions.description: The official retreat of the President of India in Hyderabad, where the President stays for at least two weeks during winter and conducts official business. Like the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, the retreat's premises include a landscaped garden, seasonal flowering plants and display of potted plants around the main building, natural cascading water falls and seven different types of nutrition gardens.

attractions.name: Secunderabad Clock Tower
attractions.description: The landmark clock tower in Secunderabad.

attractions.name: Sir Ronald Ross Institute Of Parasitology
attractions.description: The medical laboratory where Ronald Ross discovered that malaria was transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes. It is a division of Osmania University, and has been transformed into a museum exhibiting old photos of Roland Ross along with his family members. Also, a set of diagrams and charts explains Ross' research. Outside the building is a bust of Ronald Ross and a marble plaque commemorates the event.

attractions.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Assumption
Musheerabad Mosque
attractions.description: A congregation mosque that was built in 1560 by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda. The mosque has five lofty arches and two minarets at the corners, similar to Hayat Bakshi Mosque. After the fall of Golconda, the mosque went into disuse till the area became a jagir of Nawab Arastu Jah, the Prime Minister during the reign of Nizam Ali Khan. Although the mosque was repaired in 1951, it is now dilapidated. A new four-storey mosque is later built to accommodate the namazis.

attractions.name: Spanish Mosque
attractions.description: A landmark mosque built in the Moorish Revival architectural style.

restaurants.name: Hyderabadi dum biryani
restaurants.description: Dum refers to the baking process and basmati rice and meat or vegetables are mixed in a pot and heated for a long time. During the Nizam's time, the biryani was made with goat carefully cooked with rice.

restaurants.name: Double Ka Meetha
restaurants.description: A dessert made from bread, milk and dry fruits.

restaurants.name: Falooda
restaurants.description: A favourite drink of Hyderabad.

restaurants.name: Gosht
restaurants.description: Made from a buck/billy/young goat, and is associated with the Hyderabadi cuisine. Hyderabadis prize the meat of a male goat.

restaurants.name: Hyderabadi Haleem
restaurants.description: A dish that is available only during the month of Ramadaan (Ramzan).

restaurants.name: Irani chai
restaurants.description: This is the tea of Hyderabad, available at any of the ubiquitous "Chai" shops. However, not all of them have the best hygiene and it is best to go with a local. The crowd at the stalls is composed mainly of blue-collar workers and college students so expect a noisy environment with conversational topics that range from movies to politics.

restaurants.name: Khubani ka meetha
restaurants.description: Hyderabad's preferred dessert sweet. It is made from apricots boiled in sugar syrup till they achieve a thick consistency. It looks similar to but tastes different from gajar ka halwa (carrot halwa). It is often topped with ice cream or cream.

restaurants.name: Mirchi ka salan
restaurants.description: Is another dish that serves as a tasty accompaniment to any rice dish, it is served with spicy chilli sauce.

restaurants.name: Osmania biscuits
restaurants.description: Drinking Irani chai is incomplete without Osmania biscuits. It is a traditional Hyderabadi treat made from Kesar strands, milk, flour, butter, sugar and salt.

restaurants.name: Bowl O'China
restaurants.description: This is a chain restaurant started by the same people who run Hyderabad House. Has multiple locations in the city. Average Indian Chinese food.

restaurants.name: Hyderabad House
restaurants.description: This is a chain of restaurants, serving Hyderabadi style food all over the city. There are also outlets that comprise just a takeaway counter. Try the Lukhmi. Vegetarians will have few choices.

restaurants.name: Minerva Coffee Shop
restaurants.description: Bit of a local institution, serving tasty vegetarian South and North Indian snacks and food. has 4 locations.

restaurants.name: Chutneys
restaurants.description: Vegetarian, and quite well-known in Hyderabad. South Indian dishes like dosas, idlis and uttappas. "North Indian" also available, but best avoided. Is extremely crowded on weekend nights, and there is a waiting time of up to 30 min. Does not serve alcohol.

restaurants.name: Cafe Bahaar
restaurants.description: Biryanis and meat curries, moderately priced.
restaurants.address: Opp. Commissioner Office, Old MLA Quarters, Basheerbagh

restaurants.name: Baawarchi
restaurants.description: Biryanis
restaurants.address: Plot no. 66, RTC Cross Rd's, Chikkadpally Musheerabad

restaurants.name: Kholani's Kitchen
restaurants.description: Try the excellent malai kebabs (chicken) and apollo fish
restaurants.address: 4-3-548/1, Shop No. 16 & 17, Needs Arcade, Tilak Rd, Abids

restaurants.name: Rayalseema Ruchulu
restaurants.description: Mildly spiced food from Rayalaseema, rustic decor. Not for vegetarians.
restaurants.address: 1st Main Rd, Shanti Nagar, in the lane behind JNTU, Masab Tank

restaurants.name: Taj Mahal Restaurant
restaurants.description: One of the original "Udupi" style restaurants, this is strictly vegetarian and does not serve alcohol. It is part of the Taj Mahal Hotel, not to be confused with the Taj chain of luxury hotels. The food in the restaurant is tasty and good, and like Udupi restaurants, serves South Indian, North Indian and "Chinese". You are advised to stick to South Indian. The ambiance in the air-con section is old-school.

restaurants.name: 4 Seasons
restaurants.description: Serves multiple cuisines, but raved about for its Arabic and Lebanese food. Lunch and dinner. Credit cards accepted.

restaurants.name: Ming's Court
restaurants.description: Mostly Indian Chinese.

attractions.name: Chintanamani Jain Temple
attractions.description: The Jain temple was constructed during the regime of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in 1699 AD. It is at Muglisara, near mausoleum of Mirjan Sami. It has not only religious importance but also establishes one of the best examples of wooden craftsmanship and drawing with vegetable dye of Gujarat. Though the temple is marked by its outward simplicity, the inner parts of temple is a treasury of art.

attractions.name: City Science Centre
attractions.description: at City Light Road near Parle Point. Has a planetarium, science models, art gallery & museum (shifted from Chowk Sardar Patel Museum.)

attractions.name: Diamond market
attractions.description: Surat is largely recognized for its textile and diamond businesses: 92% of the world's diamonds are cut and polished in Surat. Lots of diamond factory at Varachha road. Diamond trading and broker offices are situated at mini bazaar Varachha and Mahidharpura.

attractions.name: Dutch, English and Armenian Cemeteries
attractions.description: on Karatgam Road

attractions.name: Dutch Garden
attractions.description: The ancient Dutch gardens, the Dutch cemetery and Makaipul, the old original port from where the ships sailed to other parts of the world are other attractions.

attractions.name: Lake Garden
attractions.description: People can spend some private time there with their loved one. Lake View Restaurant is also good one

attractions.name: Mugal Sarai
attractions.description: The building which is used as an office complex by Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) is one of the ancient monuments of Surat city and was built as a 'Sarai' or Musafarkhana (travellers' inn). It was built during the period of Mugal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1644 AD. This building with its considerable architectural qualities as disposed by the skilful composition of its various parts combined with combination of arches, cornices, decorated parapets, sculptured patterns on the exterior facade etc. each being disposed in an artistic and effective manner upon a strong foundation with coherent strength is still intact and is in a very good state of preservation.

attractions.name: Nature Park
attractions.description: Nature Park Sarathana is at the north-east corner of Surat City, which is approachable by Surat Kamrej Road. The site is covered with an area of 81 acres with river Tapi on the north side and Surat Kamrej road is on its south side. Land is fully vegetated with trees of eucalyptus, casurina and mango. The site is an ideal place for the development of a zoo with the new concept of natural habitat design.

attractions.name: Rang-upavan
attractions.description: An open-air theatre with a capacity of around 4,000 spectators. This is one of the biggest theatres in the country

attractions.name: Sardar Patel Museum
attractions.description: This museum was established at the beginning of the 20th century and has a collection of over 10,000 specimens of arts and crafts.

attractions.name: Surat castle
attractions.description: This historical castle, which was planned and built between 1540 and 1546 by Khudawand Khan on the banks of the River Tapi, is one of the chief ancient monuments of Surat. The magnificent gateway is a massive structure with strong door shutters furnished with protruding spikes at the exterior facade, and there is a decorative architectural treatment at the interior facade.

attractions.name: Gopi Talav
attractions.description: Lake is renovated and now has very good garden, restaurant and boating facility available.

attractions.name: Science Centre Surat
attractions.description: Over and above Science Center (Fun science section), The complex has museum, art gallery, planetarium, auditorium, amphi theater, diamond gallery. It is host of many cultural events and art exhibitions.

attractions.name: Andrew Library
attractions.description: In 1850, a wealthy pearl merchant, Naginchand Jhaveri, donated funds for the construction of this library and named it after the British collector Andrews for his help. Its associated hall was used for stage shows and gatherings but later converted into part of the library. Inside are 18,000 books including a large number of Gujarati and Hindi novels as well as reference books on erstwhile princely states. It is associated with the Nanpura Parsi library too.

attractions.name: Marjan Sami Roza
attractions.description: The Roza is dedicated to governor of Surat, Khwaja Safar Suleimanim. It was built by his son in 1540. Example of an Indo-Persian architecture.

attractions.name: Causeway
attractions.description: Visit for water sports. Causeway is a low level check dam build on the River Tapi. Water sports facility is available in the upstream water. People flock to this place on weekend and winters. Visitors also include migratory birds such as gulls and terns. Usually closed for visitors during the monsoon (July to September).

restaurants.name: Saurashtra Bakery
restaurants.description: Nankhatai biscuits made by Nanubhai Saiyadwala's shop is worth trying.

restaurants.name: Sizzling Salsa
restaurants.description: Offers a wide range of cuisines including Italian and Mexican.
restaurants.address: # 1st Floor, Rajhans Cinema, Surat-Dumas Road, opposite Iscon Mall

restaurants.name: Crazy Bite
restaurants.description: Offers a wide range of cuisine including Italian and Mexican.

restaurants.name: Kandeel Revolving Restaurant
restaurants.description: In the centre of the Textile Market area, it gives a spectacular view of the city any part of the day. They have a fixed buffet system and have both vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes.

restaurants.name: Sugar n' Spice
restaurants.description: A restaurant chain.
restaurants.address: Ring road, Bhattar near Raj Empire and at Parle Point

restaurants.name: Golden Dragon
restaurants.description: Serves Indianised Chinese food.

restaurants.name: Budget Inn Bellevue
restaurants.description: A multi-cuisine vegetarian restaurant.

attractions.name: Amber Fort
attractions.description: This massive fort-palace complex built in hybrid Hindu-Muslim style dates back to Raja Man Singh and was the royal palace of the Kachwahas from c. 1600-1727. It's one of six UNESCO World Heritage forts in Rajasthan. The name has nothing to do with the rather pretty pastel yellow colour; instead, the fort is named after the area of Amber, in turn named after the goddess Amba.

attractions.name: Sheesh Mahal
attractions.description: A palace adorned with thousands on thousands of mirror tiles on the walls and ceiling.

attractions.name: Jaigarh Fort
attractions.description: Never conquered in battle, this was considered the strongest of the three forts in the area. It is best-known as the site of the world's largest cannon, the Jaivana, which was test-fired only once — according to legend, despite using only the half the design amount of gunpowder, the cannonball flew ! A better reason to visit the fort, though, are the scenic gardens at the other end and the spectacular views over the Amber Fort and the hills around. The remains of the foundry where the Jaivana (and many more) were cast are also in the fort grounds. There are multiple boards with "no tips allowed," in case someone is bothering you.

attractions.name: Nahargarh Fort
attractions.description: The smallest of the three forts, notable primarily for excellent views over Man Sagar lake and the vast sprawl of Jaipur. Built in 1734 by the Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in a mix of Indian and European styles, the fort also houses the (relatively) compact Madhavendra Bhawan palace, although its former splendour is fading under layers of graffiti and pigeon droppings. Some of the film Rang De Basanti were shot at this fort. To get to the area where the "Pathshala" song was shot, take a left turn as soon as you enter the fort. An autorickshaw can be taken from the stand in front of the Amber fort. The fort also houses the Jaipur's Wax Museum and Sheesh Mahal, although tickets for these have to be bought separately and are ridiculously expensive. Beware if buying the Wax Museum and Sheesh Mahal combo ticket, you'll be paraded through the largely unimpressive museum and then be told to queue for the Sheesh Mahal which can last from 30 minutes to 2 hours.

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.description: An imposing blend of traditional Rajput and Mughal architecture. It is a vast palace complex occupying nearly one-seventh of the Pink City. It was built by Maharaja Jai Singh II. The complex is divided into a series of courtyards, sprawling gardens and buildings. It is home to several palatial structures like the Chandra Mahal, (home to present Maharajah of Jaipur), Mubarak Mahal (housing a textile museum), Diwan-e-Khas (or Hall of Private audience housing the two largest silver vessels in the world, which are duly mentioned in the Guinness book), the Diwan-e-Aam ( or Hall of Public Audience) and the gateway Ridhi Sidhi Pol (with four small doorways decorated with motifs depicting the four seasons). Be warned that although they sell tickets for taking photos with a camera inside, most exhibits inside have a "no photography" sign.

attractions.name: Hawa Mahal
attractions.description: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Singh as part of City Palace, it was an extension of the Zenana (women's) chamber. Its purpose was to allow royal ladies to observe everyday life in the street below without being seen. It is a five storey high red sandstone structure complete with over 950 windows. The breeze (or hawa in Hindi) circulates through these windows, giving the palace its name. The iconic facade is best seen from the street, which is free.

attractions.name: Jal Mahal
attractions.description: This beautiful Jal Mahal or water palace was made by the King of Amber in the middle of the Man Sagar Lake. The Jal Mahal represents the use of Mughal and Rajput architecture style.

attractions.name: Mundota Fort and Palace
attractions.description: A 450-year-old palace, built around 1550 by Jaswant Singh.

attractions.name: Birla Mandir (aka The Marble Temple)
attractions.description: This is a relatively new temple made of white marble with beautiful carvings. It covers a vast area in Jaipur city and is built in a contemporary manner. Birla Temple is completely constructed with the finest high-quality white marbles. In addition to having statues and paintings of Hindu deities, the temple has pictures of famous philosophers from around the world including Socrates, Confucius and Zoroaster. No bags (besides purses), food, cameras. No photos allowed in the temple, but rules are not enforced outside.

attractions.name: Galtaji
attractions.description: An ancient Hindu pilgrimage site. The main temple, Galtaji, is constructed in pink stone. The temple has a number of pavilions with rounded roofs, exquisitely carved pillars and painted walls. The temple is surrounded by natural springs and reservoirs that are considered holy. There are also seven tanks or kunds here. There are two routes to reach the temple: if you arrive from west you will have to hike uphill and downhill for about 20 minutes; the eastern gate is easily accessible by car, though it is a longer journey to get there.
attractions.address: 10 km from Jaipur on Jaipur-Agra highway near Sisodia Rani Garden

attractions.name: Galwar Bagh
attractions.description: Locals and tourists come here to feed the surprisingly tame monkeys, use the temples, and enjoy the views. You can climb to the top of the hill and then down into the valley to see the Monkey Temple, while enjoying the company of countless monkeys, goats and other animals. At the top of the hill, you turn right to reach the Sun Temple for one of the best views of the city, especially at sunset. Monkey food is available for purchase at the bottom of the hill. Entrance to the temples are free, but local religious people may ask for donations and there is a ₹50 charge for using a camera.

attractions.name: Govind Devji Temple
attractions.description: For Vaishnavites, particularly followers of Lord Krishna, this is the most important temple in the world after Vrindavan. Lord Krishna presiding in the temple were brought to Jaipur from Vrindavan during Mughal rein. According to popular legend, Lord Krishna's idol in the temple looks exactly like Krishna's form while his incarnation of Earth. It is at Jainiwas Gardens, Jalebi Chowk, in the same campus as City Palace. The temple was constructed in 1590.

attractions.name: Jagat Shiromani Temple
attractions.description: A 17th-century Hindu temple, and one of the few in India where Meera Bai, the poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, is enshrined alongside Lord Krishna. It is also a site of cultural interest during festivals like Janmashtami, where devotees gather in large numbers for special darshan and bhajans dedicated to Krishna and Meera.

attractions.name: Jain Mandir
attractions.description: Jain temple in Shivdaspura, well known as “Bara Padampura”, famous in north India for its very beautiful statue of God Padamprabhu (The 6th Teerthankar for Jains). God is sitting in a crossed leg seating posture. The statue is 0.7 m high and made of pure white stone. It was found while digging for foundation of a house.

attractions.name: Moti Dungri Mandir
attractions.description: This temple, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, is the main centre of religion for Jaipur people. Moti Dungri, meaning Pearl Hill, is a small hill that hosts a temple and a palace. It is said that this temple was built before construction of the rest of the city was begun, so as to protect the city.

attractions.name: Shri Digamber Jain Atishya Kshetra Mandir, Sanghiji
attractions.description: A popular Jain temple.

attractions.name: Gaitore
attractions.description: A royal cremation site of the rulers of Jaipur.

attractions.name: Iswari Minar Swarga Sal
attractions.description: A minaret with great views of Jaipur. There is an alternative to the minaret that's open 24/7. Just across the other side of the road (Chandpol Bazaar) from the minaret is a shopping complex with stairs up to a rooftop area where you can get basically the same view as from the minaret. To get there, go through the arched gateway almost opposite the minaret, then as soon as you get to the courtyard, look to the left for a metal spiral staircase and keep climbing until you reach the roof, walk around the corridor to the next set of stair and go up another floor until you know you can't go any higher.

attractions.name: Jantar Mantar
attractions.description: This UNESCO world heritage site is the largest of five astronomical observatories build by Maharaja Jai Singh during the period 1727-1734 in Northern India. The observatory consists of fourteen major geometric devices (or yantra in Hindi) for measuring time, predicting eclipses, tracking stars in their orbits, ascertaining the declinations of planets and determining the celestial altitudes etc. There is signage providing elaborate explanations for the use of each device, and guides can be hired to provide much the same information in a more digestible format. Guides' charge is 200 rupees for 4 people. For a better explanation, you can take a guide. The audio guide at the observatory isn't great and doesn't tell you very much more information than the already existent signs. The observatory, the water and the wind palace are free on 18 May.

attractions.name: Panna Meena Ka Kund Stepwell
attractions.description: People come here to get water, swim or hang out with their loved ones.

attractions.name: Ram Niwas Garden
attractions.description: Built in 1868 by Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh of Jaipur, this garden contains a bird park, zoo, Ravindra Rang Manch Theatre, art gallery, exhibition ground, gymnasium and several cafes and picnic spots.

attractions.name: Sisodia Rani Palace and Garden
attractions.description: This palace was established by Sawai Jai Singh for his queen Sisodia, rulers of one of the oldest kingdoms of India. There are tiered multi-level gardens with fountains, watercourses and painted pavilions. A double-storeyed palace occupies the top terrace of the garden. The palace has many galleries, pavilions and beautiful murals depicting scenes from the life of lord Krishna.

attractions.name: Vidyadhar Garden
attractions.description: The garden is a real treat for those who want to see a fusion of Mughal and Hindu culture.

attractions.name: Zoological Garden
attractions.description: In the serene environment of Ram Niwas Bagh, this garden is prized for its rich flora and fauna.

attractions.name: Nahargarh Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: A wildlife sanctuary on the Aravalli Hills. It is home to species like leopards, sloth bears, wild boars, jackals, hyenas, peacocks, owls, eagles, and various species of snakes and frogs.

attractions.name: Jhalana–Amagarh Leopard Conservation Reserve
attractions.description: Another leopard sanctuary on the Jaipur Ridge.

attractions.name: Jawahar Circle
attractions.description: A large traffic circle with one of the biggest circular parks in India. Built by the Jaipur Development Authority (JDA), it is one of Jaipur's popular leisure destinations, close to the airport. There are multiple concentric tracks in the park, surrounded by rose gardens. The Patrika Gate may look like a Rajput-era structure, even though it was built in 2016.

attractions.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
attractions.description: A beautiful clean museum dedicated to the traditional art of hand block printing textiles, this museum is housed in a restored heritage haveli tucked into the back streets of old Amber. Small cafe (see "Eat"), clean toilets, small shop selling hand printed contemporary wearable clothes and textiles, friendly staff and a printer and block carver demonstrating their crafts every day.

attractions.name: Albert Hall Museum
attractions.description: A fine example of Indo-Saracenic architecture, this building was designed by Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob and was opened as public museum in 1887. Maharaja Ram Singh wanted this building to be a town hall, but his successor, Madho Singh II, decided it should be a museum for the art of Jaipur and included as part of the new Ram Nivas Garden. The museum has a rich collection of artefacts like paintings, carpets, ivory, stone, metal sculptures and colourful crystal works. It is named after King Edward VII (Albert Edward), during whose visit to the city as the Prince of Wales, its foundation stone was laid on 6 February 1876.

attractions.name: Amrapali Museum
attractions.description: A jewellery museum, with a collection of 4000 objects. Over 800 objects are displayed over two floors while the remaining objects are kept in visual storage. The museum has fine jewellery, hand-crafted antiques, and exquisite curios to showcase the craftsmanship and rich tradition of Indian jewellery. Several different types of Indian jewellery at the museum constitute a visual representation of history of art and process of jewellery making.[2] The collection ranges from tribal jewellery, in wood and metal, to silver and gold pieces. It is an extensive collection that shows how the traditional craftsmanship has impacted modern and contemporary design sensibilities.

attractions.name: Statue Circle
attractions.description: Statue Circle is exactly what it sounds like: a roundabout that contains a statue that is beautifully lit up at night. It is the life-size statue of the Great Ruler and Founder of Jaipur, Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II

attractions.name: Vidhan Bhavan
attractions.description: The seat of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha). The building was built in 1994-2001 to replace the Sawai Man Singh Town Hall as the seat of the legislature. The exterior features jharokhas, chhatris, Kamanis, baradaris, arches, todis, etc., all examples of traditional Rajasthani architecture.

attractions.name: Amber Fort Sound and Light Show
attractions.description: Experience the history, culture and life of Amber through this spectacular show. Amitabh Bachhan narrates the story of Rajasthani kings with a script written by Gulzar. Don't forget the mosquito repellent. The light show can be watched from outside the fort, but the sound won't be audible from there. There is also a sound and light show at Jantar Mantar for ₹100.

attractions.name: Sawai Mansingh Stadium
attractions.description: With a capacity of 30,000, this hosts the Rajasthan team and Rajathan Royals in IPL.

attractions.name: B.M. Birla Auditorium and Conference Hall
attractions.description: These are at the heart of Jaipur. This auditorium is spread over 9.8 acres and includes a computer centre, interactive science museum, an information processing centre, library, a processing planetarium, eight research divisions, a dissemination cell and an auditorium. The auditorium has a seating capacity of 1,350 and is among the largest in India. This auditorium is built up to international conference standards. However, people visiting Jaipur for leisure are likely to be most interested in the Planetarium (all shows in Hindi) or Science Museum (under renovation as of November 2015) that are part of the complex.
attractions.address: Birla Institute of Scientific Research, Statue Circle

attractions.name: Rajmandir Cinema
attractions.description: An experience in itself, and another "don't miss". Once known as the best cinema India, and still the best in Rajasthan, it offers an overwhelming experience. From the pushing, shoving, and general chaos in the ticket queue, to an audience that laughs, cries, cheers, claps, and consistently talks through the entire film, the Rajmandir provides an insight into Rajasthani culture. The films can be interesting; Masala movies are action, drama, mystery, suspense, and epics all wrapped into one single film, teeming with dances and obligatory wet sari scenes, and unabashedly lifting generous amounts of plot devices from Western films. The theatre-goers are very friendly and genuinely curious about overseas visitors who come to the Raj. Don't be put off by "House Full" notices at the entrance. The box office opens again a nominal 45 minutes before the next performance, and there are usually tickets available. Box seats at ₹120 go first, so it's worth going early to avoid disappointment. Shows
attractions.address: C-16, Panch Batti, Bhagwan Das Rd, C-Scheme

attractions.name: Heiwa Heaven The Resort
attractions.description: Heiwa Heaven is a Jaipur-based luxury resort that hosts parties and destination weddings.
attractions.address: Jaisinghpura Khor, Jamdoli Chauraha, Agra Rd

attractions.name: Central Park
attractions.description: The largest park in Jaipur, at the middle of the city. A big lush green beautiful garden and Rambagh Polo Ground and golf club nearby makes it an enjoyable place. The park also has a long jogging and walking track. A number of migratory and native birds visit the park during the year. Furthermore, there's a tall flag of India flying at the middle, one of the largest in India.

attractions.name: Nevta Dam
attractions.description: A popular destination among bird enthusiasts, with about 150 bird species flock around the eastern side of the dam every year, including the uncommon lesser whistling-duck and the widespread eastern cattle egret.

attractions.name: Chokhi Dhani
attractions.description: Around 18 km from Central Jaipur on the Jaipur-Tonk highway, Chokhi Dhani (Fine Hamlet in Rajasthani dialect) is a kind of virtual village and also a 5-star resort. There are lodging facilities available, but the real attraction is the evening fun-fairs. There are two excellent places to enjoy Rajasthani food served in the traditional mode at their resort. Chokhi Dhani a.k.a. Lalten Restaurant is a more popular place because it is on the main road near the airport and also has other attractions, such as horseback riding, camel riding, bullock cart rides, a maze, boating and kathputli (puppet) shows. You can also watch live folk dances and listen to live folk music for free. It gives the visitor a glimpse of culture from different parts of Rajasthan, and could be nice if you will not have time to see much of Rajasthan yourself. It opens at 5PM, and be sure to get there early as many of the sites are difficult to see when it gets dark. It's a 30-min rickshaw ride from Central Jaipur, or

restaurants.name: Gangaur Sweets
restaurants.description: Sweets for chamcham, also baked sweets and crispy samosas.

restaurants.name: Zolocrust
restaurants.description: The gourmet bakery and Italian restaurant is operated by chefs of Hotel Clarks Amer and serves exquisite bakery items, it also serves vegan and vegetarian food.
restaurants.address: Hotel Clarks Amer, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, Near Malviya Nagar

restaurants.name: Anokhi Cafe
restaurants.description: Mostly organic non-Indian-style ("international flavour") home-style cakes, freshly prepared sandwiches, pastries, savoury snacks plus organic coffee and a selection of good teas. Quiet, relaxing, good value for money, situated outside the Anokhi shop (see Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing listing in "See").
restaurants.address: 2nd Floor, KK Square, C-11 Prithviraj Road

restaurants.name: Ambrosia
restaurants.description: Serving vegetarian and vegan, Chinese food and barbecue atop a 100-foot-high building providing a breathtaking view of the city.
restaurants.address: In the Hotel Ramsingh Palace, B 2, Hathi Babau Ka Bagh, Kanti Nagar, Banipark

restaurants.name: Old Take Away
restaurants.description: Various chicken and mutton dishes for take-away.

restaurants.name: Peacock Rooftop Restaurant
restaurants.description: A rooftop restaurant serving Indian, Western and Chinese food. Fast service and good value.

restaurants.name: Shrinat Lassiwala
restaurants.description: Simple place for lassis, snacks and breakfast. Claiming to be the oldest lasso place in Jaipur.

restaurants.name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
restaurants.description: Do not miss the famous Pyaz ki Kachori, a spicy onion dish. Also, the ghewar and mawa kachori is famous.
restaurants.address: Opposite Polo Victory Cinema, Station Road, Sindhi Camp

restaurants.name: Apno Gaon
restaurants.description: Vegetarian food, including fresh vegetables and fruits. Slightly away from the main city: One has to go on a bumpy ride to reach there.
restaurants.address: 14, New Loha Mandi, Sikar Road, Vishwakarma Industrial Area

restaurants.name: Four Seasons Restaurant
restaurants.description: Indian and Chinese food, among the most popular vegetarian restaurants in Jaipur.

restaurants.name: Handi Restaurant
restaurants.description: Specialising in meat dishes; chicken, mutton, kebab, tandoori and the super spicy Rajasthani speciality lal maas.
restaurants.address: Maya Mansion, Opp GPO, MI Rd

restaurants.name: Little Italy
restaurants.description: Part of a chain with restaurants around India and some other Asian countries, as the name reveals, this is a place to go to for Italian food. Wide selection of pizza, pasta and other typical Italian food, also some Mexican dishes. Large range of wines.
restaurants.address: C/11, K.K. Square, Prithviraj Marg, C-Scheme

attractions.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
attractions.description: A massive church and school. Lot of celebrations take place around Christmas time and is packed.

attractions.name: Colvin Taluqdars' College
attractions.description: A must see place with great architecture. It was built in 1896 and named after British Indian colonial administrator Sir Auckland Colvin.

attractions.name: Firangi Mahal
attractions.description: The Oxford and Cambridge of India author/poet Shibli Naumani. For more details see the book Ul Farangi Mahal by Francis Robinson

attractions.name: Kukrail Reserve Forest
attractions.description: One of the three crocodilian breeding centres in India, including the freshwater gharials (Gavialis gangeticus), one of the 3 native species of crocodilians in India.

attractions.name: Marine Drive
attractions.description: Beautiful Gomti river-side and monumental structures view for fun with family and friends. Best time to visit is 4–6PM, during the sunset.

attractions.name: Dilkusha Kothi
attractions.description: The remains of an 18th-century house built in the English baroque style. The house was shelled during its involvement in the Siege of Lucknow in 1857, and only a few towers and external walls remain to this day, though the extensive garden is intact. The garden is packed by both local and foreign visitors during winter.

attractions.name: Bibiapur Kothi
attractions.description: A neoclassical building built by Nawab Asaf ud-Daula in the late 18th century. It was used as a country retreat, a place for the Nawab to escape the hustle of his royal court. After the dissolution of the Oudh State, the British used the building for military celebrations, and it became a part of the Lucknow Cantonment, although the building is open to the public.

attractions.name: Bara Imambara
attractions.description: A large and impressive tomb complex built in 1783. There is an interesting labyrinth inside, called Bhool Bhulaiya (भूल भुलैया Bhūl Bhulaiyā). You could easily spend half a day wandering around these beautiful but crumbling examples of Mughal architecture. If you hire a guide, do not expect him to know the way around; some are known to get lost in the labyrinth. The ticket also includes the Chhota Imambara, the Husainabad clock tower and picture gallery. Lone couples are not allowed to enter the labyrinth inside the complex without a guide. This prohibition is not brought to notice while buying the entry ticket. You will also have to pay a man ₹2 to mind your shoes while exploring the complex: shoes are not allowed inside.

attractions.name: Rumi Darwaza
attractions.description: An imposing gateway built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784, modelled after a historical gate in Constantinople (present-day Istanbul). It used to be a gateway to the Nawab's palace, but unfortunately the palace was destroyed by the British in 1857.

attractions.name: Teele Wali Masjid
attractions.description: A mosque with a tomb of Shah Peer Mohammad.

attractions.name: Chota Imambara
attractions.description: An imposing mausoleum built by the third Nawab of Awadh in 1837.

attractions.name: Husainabad Clock Tower
attractions.description: A British landmark, set in a park with a somewhat poorly-curated picture gallery, and a lake. A great place for sunset.

attractions.name: Chatar Manzil
attractions.description: The palace of the Nawabs of Awadh, built by Nawab Ghazi Uddin Haider.

attractions.name: General Wali Kothi
attractions.description: An observatory commissioned in 1832 by Nawab Nasir ud-Din Haidar Shah, and became functional in 1841 when Colonel Richard Wilcox, a Royal Astronomer, was appointed. The building was in derelict condition after the death of Wilcox in 1847, and the instruments disappeared during the 1857 rebellion. It was said that once a brass pillar stood in central chamber through the roof. It was later occupied by the Imperial Bank of India (now State Bank of India) in 1923, and the building is since an SBI branch head office.

attractions.name: The Residency
attractions.description: The bloody history of the demise of this Raj-era compound is immortalised in the museum in the basement. This was the scene of the 1857 First Battle for Independence, referred to by the British as `The Indian Mutiny.´ Although you can still clearly see numerous cannon ball marks in the ruined buildings, thankfully it is a peaceful place today. So much so in fact, that you are likely to stumble across couples taking a little private time in the leafy shady groves. The Residency is clearly recognised by the locals and tourists alike as a breezy haven to escape from the bustle and dust of a busy Indian city. The Residency will try to sell you a photo pass for an additional ₹25. The guard will also ask you if you have a camera. However once you are inside, no one will say anything if you take photos.

attractions.name: Safed Baradari
attractions.description: A white-marbled building built by Nawab Wajid Ali Shah as a "palace of mourning". After the annexation of Oudh in 1856, the Baradari was used by the British to hold court for petitions and claims by the officers and nobles of the deposed monarch's reign and his relatives. Later, around 1923, it was handed over to the Taluqdars of Awadh for the British India Association of Oudh. The Baradari is owned by the association since then.

attractions.name: Tomb of Nawab Saadat Ali Khan
Ambedkar Memorial
attractions.description: A large, 107-acre development to honour Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar who was the architect of the Indian constitution. Impressive stone work, statues and fountains intermix with carefully sculpted gardens.

attractions.name: Manyawar Shri Kanshiram Ji Green Eco Park
National Botanical Research Institute
attractions.description: A botanical garden, and a good place for nature lovers. It features peacocks, a cactus museum, and research labs.

attractions.name: Haathi Park
attractions.description: A popular hangout place among the locals, the public park has two rows of large elephant statues as its main attraction.

attractions.name: TORNOS
attractions.description: They offer some great heritage walks including a culinary walk.

attractions.name: Buddha Park
attractions.description: A small park on the side of a noisy congested road in Lucknow. A statue of the Buddha gives the park its name. The park features fun rides and boating facilities.

attractions.name: Nawab Wajid Ali Shah Prani Udyan
attractions.description: The central zoo of Lucknow, established in 1921, and popularly known as Banarasi Bagh (बनारसी बाग़ Banārasī Bāġ) or Chidiya Ghar (चिड़ियाघर Ciṛiyāghar). The zoo is home to 463 mammals, 298 birds, and 72 reptiles representing 97 species, including tiger, lion, wolf, gibbon, black bear, rhino, blackbuck, swamp deer, barking deer, hog deer, elephant, giraffe, zebra, European otters, hill mynah, giant squirrel, great pied hornbill, golden pheasant, silver pheasant etc. It's one of the only two zoos in India to exhibit an orangutan. It has toy trains for children and a large number of animals in here. Fish aquariums also available. Available here is tasty Western-style food.

attractions.name: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Park
attractions.description: A 76-acre park with courtyards, multiple jogging tracks, a fish pond and duck pond and a number of swings and benches for children.

attractions.name: Janeshwar Mishra Park
attractions.description: An urban park spread over 376 acres and partially modelled on London's Hyde Park. It has a human-made lake, cycling and jogging tracks, a sports centre and gymnasium and even gondolas.

attractions.name: Ekana Cricket Stadium
attractions.description: Powerplay overs have been bowled in less time than it takes to say. Completed in 2017 and with a capacity of 50,000, it's on the ring road southeast edge of the city, and hosts the Uttar Pradesh team plus Lucknow Super Giants in IPL.

restaurants.name: Alzaiqa
restaurants.description: You can find great non-vegetarian food here, specially chicken.

restaurants.name: Dainik Jagaran Chauk
restaurants.description: Cheap and delicious non-veg food

restaurants.name: Dastarkhwan Tulsi Theatre
restaurants.description: Famous for its Galawati Kababs.Mainly caters to meat eaters.
restaurants.address: VW2P+VCF, Wala Qadar Rd, DM Compound Colony, Kaiserbagh Officer's Colony, Qaisar Bagh

restaurants.name: Haji Sahib's Shop
restaurants.description: This is in the heart of Old Lucknow. Serves the juiciest Nihari (lamb shanks in gravy) and Kulchha (a traditional bread).

restaurants.name: Jai Durgmaa Hotel
restaurants.description: Very good vegetarian food etc.

restaurants.name: Prakash kie kulfi
restaurants.description: Try the faloodha kulfi.

restaurants.name: Ram Asrey Sweet Shop
restaurants.description: Very good sweets and snacks like Namkeen, Daalmonth etc.

restaurants.name: Tunday Kababi
restaurants.description: Has been serving authentic galawati kebabs for more than 100 years, established 1905. The place offers wonderful kebabs with paratha and also sells biryani and other Awadhi cuisine.

restaurants.name: Idrees Biryani
restaurants.description: Serves a good biryani.

restaurants.name: Cappuccino Blast
restaurants.description: Cafe, hookah lounge and restaurant serving continental, Indian and Chinese cuisine.

restaurants.name: Dastarkhwan
restaurants.description: Exotic non-vegetarian delicacies, specially the special chicken masala, shaami kebabs and rumali roti/mughlai parathas.

restaurants.name: DineOut Restaurant
restaurants.description: Pure vegetarian restaurant for family dining.

attractions.name: Bishop Cotton School
attractions.description: A heritage building from the British era. It is in the heart of city and pride of Nagpur.

attractions.name: Diamond Crossing
attractions.description: A unique marvel of engineering that exists in a very few places of the world. The double lines crossing from the north to the south and those from east to west form a square shape and is called the diamond crossing. It is crucial and is used widely.

attractions.name: Satpuda Botanical Garden
attractions.description: The botanical garden of Nagpur with several rare plant species. The garden is also popular among bird enthusiasts.

attractions.name: Lok Bhavan
attractions.description: The winter residence of the Governor of Maharashtra.

attractions.name: Vidhan Bhavan
attractions.description: The seat of the winter sessions of the Maharashtra Legislature. It was built in 1912 to house the government of the Central Provinces of Berar, as Nagpur was its capital. The province was later incorporated into Madhya Pradesh in 1952 after India's independence, and Nagpur remained the capital of the Indian state. However, the Vidarbha region of Madhya Pradesh was later incorporated into Maharashtra in 1960, and Nagpur became the winter capital of the then-new state under the Nagpur Pact to protect the interests and equal development of Vidarbha.

attractions.name: Zero Mile Stone
attractions.description: A monument marking the geographical centre of colonial India. It was built by British during the 1907 Great Trigonometrical Survey of India in Nagpur. The Zero Mile Stone consists of a pillar made up of sandstone and another small stone representing the GTS Standard Bench Mark, and four stucco horses that were added later. The height of the top of the pillar is above mean sea level.

attractions.name: Nagpur Central Museum
attractions.description: One of the oldest museums in India, founded in 1863. Its collection includes artefacts like dinosaurs' fossils, coins, ancient inscriptions, sculptures, arms and tribal artefacts. It has QR codes in display galleries, which provide information about artefacts in Marathi, Hindi and English, as well as 13 other languages.

attractions.name: Narrow Gauge Rail Museum
attractions.description: A railway museum with old & heritage articles from Indian Railways: old steam engines, coaches, saloons and many more things related to narrow gauge Indian Railway. A very good garden with a toy train.

attractions.name: Raman Science Centre
attractions.description: An interactive science centre, similar to Mumbai's Nehru Science Centre. Named after Nobel laureate C. V. Raman, the centre was developed to promote a scientific attitude, portray the growth of science and technology and their applications in industry and human welfare, and hold science exhibits.

attractions.name: Bohra Masjid
attractions.description: It is very big and beautiful mosque.

attractions.name: Deekshabhoomi
attractions.description: Buddhist temple.

attractions.name: Ramdham
attractions.description: Central India's largest spiritual - cultural tourism park which houses all Hindu deities under one roof. There are cultural shows like folk dances, magic and puppet shows every evening and tourists can look forward for a comfortable stay at the resort.

attractions.name: Gorewada Lake
attractions.description: A lake created by a dam.

attractions.name: Khindsi Lake
attractions.description: Khindsi is a picturesque lake 40 km from Nagpur city and is famous for the natural beauty and water-sports. The lake is in a valley covered by thick forest and is a very popular tourist destination of Central India. There are cottages for accommodation too.

attractions.name: Phutala Lake
attractions.description: Evening host for food in exotic lake view.

attractions.name: Sonegaon Lake
attractions.description: Migratory birds can be seen in winters.

attractions.name: Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium
attractions.description: One of India's largest cricket grounds by area, with a capacity of 45,000. It hosts Vidarbha in the Ranji Trophy.

attractions.name: Yashwant Stadium
attractions.description: A football stadium.

attractions.name: Gorewada Zoo
attractions.description: A zoological park named after Shiv Sena founder Bal Thackeray. Visitors can avail online booking through the official website.

attractions.name: Maharajbagh Zoo
attractions.description: Another zoo in Nagpur, in the city centre. It is home to leopards, lions, tigers, peacocks and other animals.

attractions.name: VOC park
attractions.description: The park includes a zoo and a children's park. Evening is the best time to visit the park. Nehru Stadium is nearby and also there are few small playgrounds for basketball, tennis, badminton, etc.

attractions.name: GD Museums
attractions.description: Interesting collection of inventions by G.D. Naidu, who is also referred to as the Edison of India. The complex houses three museums: Experimenta Science Centre, Gedee Car Museum and GD Science Museum. The museums are located in the same complex and has separate tickets. The museums also offer a ticket combo.

attractions.name: Gedee Car Museum
attractions.description: The museum was founded by GD Gopal in 2015 as a commemoration of his late father, Gopalswamy Doraiswamy Naidu.

attractions.name: GD Science Museum
attractions.description: Interesting science experiments. There are the History of Industrialisation in Coimbatore exhibition and an old motor bike which G.D.Naidu learned to assemble from a British officer after which he became interested in engineering. A gift shop is attached with the museum, where one can buy interesting toys from Germany. It is appropriate for children.

attractions.name: Experimenta Science Centre
attractions.description: The museum aims to stimulate curiosity, develop an inquiring mind and enable children & adults to learn science in an informal and fun-filled manner. There are a variety of interactive exhibits and exciting tasks to amaze and thrill the audience.

attractions.name: Gass Forest Museum
attractions.description: Natural history museum with exhibits and artifacts related to forests and their wildlife. It is housed in a heritage building, which is more than 100 years old. The museum was established in 1902 by H.A. Gass, the then Conservator of Forests of Coimbatore circle. His comprehensive collection was part of the display. The building dates back to 1915 and was built in Gothic style. There are about 10000 exhibits on display at the Gass Forest Museum. The exhibits on display at the museum cover various disciplines in science and geography like botany, zoology, geology etc. A stuffed full-grown Indian gaur is a prime exhibit. It has several stuffed animals, including a collection of over 1200 insects. The museum also exhibits non-forest items, which include a million-year-old meteorite.

attractions.name: Anjeneyar Kovil
attractions.description: This temple was constructed in one of the calmest localities. It is peaceful and is open in the morning till noon, and opens again from 5PM for public. Don't miss the various alangaarams done for the God.

attractions.name: Anubhavi Subramaniar Temple
attractions.description: This temple has a natural outflow, which spouts water all through the year. For this reason, the temple is quite popularly known and people never fail to make their visit. There are hundreds of steps to get to the temple, and no mechanical help available. This place is frequented by elephants and hence do not plan to visit the temple during evening hours. Don't forget to visit the Lalithambikai temple situated at its foothills.

attractions.name: Marudhamalai Murugan Temple
attractions.description: A huge temple complex, at least 1200 years old, on a picturesque hill.

attractions.name: Athar Jamad Masjid
attractions.description: A famous hundred-year-old mosque.

attractions.name: Infant Jesus Church
attractions.description: Here, devotees throng on Thursdays to attend the Novena.

attractions.name: Isha Yoga Center Coimbatore
attractions.description: This yoga centre is an ashram in the foothills of the Velliangiri Mountains beside the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Visitors can participate in yoga programmes and ceremonies in the temples. The centre is set in 150 acres of thick forest. Includes a Shiva temple and the Dhyanalinga Yogic Temple.

attractions.name: Race Course
attractions.description: A place for food and recreation. Ideal for morning and evening walk. There are various installations, which include the Eiffel Tower, Leaning Tower of Pisa, Red Fort and many more. A traffic island on the southern side houses a statue of a racing horse complete with a jockey.

restaurants.name: Ajmir
restaurants.description: Serves excellent mutton (beef) and chicken. Don't forget to taste their mutta poriyal and chicken fry that is great. It offers beef and chicken dishes.

restaurants.name: Brookfields Plaza
restaurants.description: Has everything from dresses to food like KFC, Rmkv, lifestyle, reliance trends.

restaurants.name: China town
restaurants.description: Serves excellent Chinese items like chili pork, dragon chicken, and their lumpfu soup
restaurants.address: Nehru stadium in the road between the park gate

restaurants.name: Dhabas
restaurants.description: Dhabas are famous in Coimbatore. They have a variety of foods and attached bars. There are many dhabas in Coimbatore. There was a dhaba near Maharaja World and one near Ramani's Mayuri, Chinnavedampatti. Most of the bars have individual huts accommodating about ten patrons apiece. They are evening hangouts.

restaurants.name: Four season
restaurants.description: Serves vegetarian and non-vegetarian food and beer; it is nice for parties. Try the Kerala chicken kudal.

restaurants.name: FUN Republic
restaurants.description: Has Coimbatore's first McDonald's restaurant.

restaurants.name: Hari Bavan
restaurants.description: Serves nonvegetarian food. At lunch there are four types of gravy (fish, mutton, chicken and Nattu Kolli). Try the karandi (omelette) and their side dish. Available only for lunch.
restaurants.address: RTO Road & Gandhipuram 4th Street & SO Bunk, Peelamedu

restaurants.name: Hotel Blue Berry
restaurants.description: Specialist in biriyani (mutton, chicken and fish). Serves a variety of nonvegetarian curries. Takes function orders and entertains home deliveries. Chettinad and Chengudu Chicken are standouts.

restaurants.name: Hotel Muthu Rowther
restaurants.description: Excellent place for non-vegetarians. The best dishes are Beef Biryani and Beef Chukka.

restaurants.name: Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC)
restaurants.description: This is crowded. There is a branch in Brooke Fields Mall, also.

restaurants.name: Paati Amma Dosai Kadai
restaurants.description: Serves a wide variety of dosas and sevai like chola,kambu, tomato, ragi, cauliflower, mushroom, babycorn, panner dosai and seva. Don't forget to order butter appam yummy.
restaurants.address: Near Gem Hospital or Archana Darchana Theater Gandhi Park

restaurants.name: Seasons
restaurants.description: Offers cheap, healthy vegetarian food. The corn and spinach sandwich and all fruit juices are good. It's usually crowded. The ice cream is so nice.

attractions.name: Annapurna Temple
attractions.description: It is a famous temple of the goddess of food. The name of the temple Annapurna means "anna" which literally means food. The people in town have great faith in the temple. The temple is made with beautiful colourful work done at the entrance gate.

attractions.name: Bada Ganpati
attractions.description: Better known for its size than antiquity, this temple houses perhaps the largest Ganesh idol in the world measuring 25 feet from crown to foot. Created as a result of the dream of an Avantika (Ujjain) resident, Shri Dadhich, it was built in 1875.

attractions.name: Bapna Statue
attractions.description: Right across from the famous MY Hospital in Indore, in the Jaora Compound Area, is the statue of Rai Bahadur Sir Siremal Bapna, the legendary Prime Minister of Holkar State during the reign of HH Maharaja Yeshwant Rao Holkar. He is credited with bringing Indore into the modern age and he was an able and honest administrator, a great social reformer, a great philanthropist and a modern day saint.

attractions.name: Central Museum
attractions.description: The Indore Museum houses the finest collection of Parmar sculptures from Hinglajgarh. The Parmar style originated here, and is characterized by proportioned figures, carefully and ornately depicted in stone. The museum is also known for its collection of coins, arms and armor.

attractions.name: Chhatris
attractions.description: Chhatris are the tombs or cenotaphs erected in memory of dead Holkar rulers and their family members. The Chhatris picturesquely poised on the Khan river banks near Rajawada are incomparable in terms of Maratha architecture and sculpture of their period. At Chhatri Baag is the main collection of tombs housed in two compounds. Close by is the beautiful Bolia Sarkar's Chhatri constructed in 1858 AD in memory of Sardar Chimnaji Appa Sahib Bolia.

attractions.name: Geeta Bhawan
attractions.description: One of the most famous temples in the city. Located near the heart of town (Palasia). You can find idols of almost all gods and goddesses and the peace found here is unique.

attractions.name: Gomatgiri
attractions.description: On the hill 10-12 km away from the heart of the city, the Jain Samaj has constructed a 21-foot statue of Lord Gomateshwar, a replica of the Bahubali statue of Shravanbelagola. Also built here are 24 marble temples with shilars for each tirthankar. This place offers a breathtaking view of Indore city by night.

attractions.name: Kanch Mandir
attractions.description: This Jain temple is an architectural marvel in glass. The walls, ceilings, floors, pillars and door knobs are entirely inlaid with glass. Even paintings are done in glass. Atop is a special glass chamber which multiplies the three statues of Lord Shantinath,Aadinath & Mahavira installed there into an indefinite number (said to be visible up to 24 times, corresponding to the 24 tirthankaras).

attractions.name: Khajrana Ganesh Temple
attractions.description: The citizens of Indore have great faith in this Ganesh temple, built during the reign of Ahilyabai Holkar. It is believed that all wishes are fulfilled by praying here. Nearby is the dargah of Nahar Sayed. This is an important pilgrimage place for Maita Muslims.

attractions.name: Lal Baag Palace
attractions.description: One of the grandest monuments the Holkar dynasty left Indore. A reflection of their taste, grandeur and lifestyle, its construction began in 1886 under Tukoji Rao Holkar II, and was carried out in three phases. The final phase was completed in 1921 under Tukoji Rao Holkar III. Many royal receptions were held here. It has a total area of 28 hectares, and at one time it had the reputation of having one of the best rose gardens in the country.

attractions.name: Rajawada
attractions.description: Synonymous with the heart of Indore city, it stands today as a mute witness to the bygone splendor of the Holkar rulers. This 200-year-old, seven-storey historic palace of the Holkars is built in a mixture of Muslim, Maratha and French styles. The lower three floors are made of stone and the upper floors are made of wood, which made it very vulnerable to destruction by fire. Rajwada was burnt three times in its history; the last fire in 1984 took the greatest toll. Today only the front facade remains. Renovations have recreated some of the old glory of this beautiful palace.

attractions.name: Ravindra Natay Grah
attractions.description: This is one of the examples of a complete makeover. Few years back it was an old and not so good auditorium. After some years it was decide to renovate it with public private partnership. it was then done complete makeover and now it is one of the best auditorium in town with many modern facilities.

attractions.name: Sapna- Sangeeta Road
attractions.description: It is another very famous and one of the busiest road in the town. Many national and international brand stores are present here. the road which is officially named after great Shri Agrasen Maharaj is popularly known after one of the best multiplex sanpna sangeeta which in earlier days was a single screen theatre having two theatres, is now a multiplex with three screens of inox. The road is the busiest one and addresses many local national and international brands.

attractions.name: Sirpur Lake
attractions.description: The lake hosts the habitats for major migratory bird species. The natural beauty of the lake and scenic view is hard to forget. the government has decided to develop a garden near the lake.

attractions.name: Town Hall
attractions.description: Built in 1904 as the King Edwards Hall, it was renamed Mahatma Gandhi Hall in 1948. Its architectural style is Indo-Gothic. Made in Seoni stone, its domes and staples are a landmark of Indore today. It has a four-faced clock tower in front, because of which it is locally known as Ghanta Ghar. It is frequently the venue for the various book and painting exhibitions, fairs and festivals held throughout the year. The building also has a library, a children's park and a temple.

attractions.name: Vaishnav Dhaam
attractions.description: It is a famous temple of the goddess. It is beautifully constructed in white and is located away from the city traffic. The idols here are very beautiful to see.

attractions.name: Venkatesh Temple
attractions.description: Where India's third largest and largest Rath-yatra procession is carried and thousands of people participate in that and temple was built 50 years before in mid of Indore city by Nagoriya Pithdishwar

attractions.name: Meghdoot Uapvan
attractions.description: It is a huge garden with a fountain show and many kinds of plants and flowers are planted here. It brings you close to nature within the city itself and lovely point for couples.

attractions.name: Nakhrali Dhani Water Park
attractions.description: A one of its kind Rajasthani Village-themed park become amusement park and restaurant. This is an exclusive park in Indore which lets you enter into the world of a Rajathani village.

attractions.name: Regional Park
attractions.description: The most beautiful park in town. It was developed by Indore Development Authority on the banks of ancient pipliyapala lake. The park has been developed beautifully with estimated cost of ₹70 crores. The amazing light work in night and various new species of plants make it most attractive. The park is divided in four parts, the lake having been renewed and fitted with five jet-fountains which in night create a beautiful atmosphere with there light-effects. Plans are in pipeline to start boating in the pond, a food court and children play zone. Water sports are practised in the lake. It's a must-visit spot when you are in Indore.

attractions.name: Shell City Water Park
attractions.description: Another famous water cum amusement park in the outskirts of the busy town. A park that offers wide range of entertainment.

restaurants.name: Celebration
restaurants.description: A self-service food joint offering fusion Chinese food, bakery items, chaats, chole kulche, etc., favoured by young single people and families.

restaurants.name: Celeberity
restaurants.description: Has the best North Indian food tasty buffet in town, good entrées and a great coffee shop.

restaurants.name: Chappan Dukaan
restaurants.description: It has 56 shops, where you can get different types of food. Must tries include; Madhuram Sweets- Shikanji, Dry fruit Paan, Jain Sweets-Jalebi, Jhonnys-Hot Dog, Young Tarang-Poha morning hours and many chat and delicacies.

restaurants.name: Chokhi Dhani
restaurants.description: Good Rajasthani food and entertainment, but smaller than Nakhrali Dhani.

restaurants.name: City Centre
restaurants.description: Great South Indian food.

restaurants.name: Crown Palace
restaurants.description: Has great buffet, good coffee shop and good rooftop restaurant.

restaurants.name: Guru Kripa
restaurants.description: Famous restaurant in the city.

restaurants.name: Hakeem
restaurants.description: It's a great non-veg family restaurant. Speciality is Tawa Gosht and Mughlai Biryaani.

restaurants.name: Little Italy
restaurants.description: Authentic vegetarian Italian cuisine offers delectable Italian and Mexican food.

restaurants.name: Nafees Cakes
restaurants.description: Bakery and non-veg restaurant.
restaurants.address: 30-B Apollo Ave, Greater Kailash Rd, New Palasia

restaurants.name: Nakhrali Dhani
restaurants.description: Rajasthani food and entertainment.

restaurants.name: Pishori Dhaba
restaurants.description: Punjabi/North Indian

attractions.name: Baroda Museum & Picture Gallery
attractions.description: The museum displays Indian musical instruments, Mughal miniatures, sculptures, textiles and objects from Japan, Tibet, Nepal, Egypt. The museum's artifacts were collected by Maharaja Sayajirao, devoted to travel. The Picture Gallery displays paintings by British artists, also from Sayajirao's private collection.

attractions.name: The EME temple
attractions.description: Vadodara is quite serene. It was built by the Military and one can enjoy a pleasant hour in its premises.

attractions.name: Fateh Singh Museum
attractions.description: The royal family of Baroda has a notable collection of his works. Apart from these, there are many art works of masters collected and commissioned by Maharaja Sayajirao. If you are art lover, keep aside a day for the palace and museum. The museum itself is in the palace premises. to view several Raja Ravi Verma originals.

attractions.name: Hazira Maqbara
attractions.description: The mausoleum contains the graves of Qutb-ud-din Muhammad Khan and his son Naurang Khan. It is an octagonal structure in the style of Mughal tombs.

attractions.name: Khanderao Market
attractions.description: Another palatial building created by Sayajirao III in 1906 at a cost of 3 lakhs. It was a present by him to the Municipality to mark the Silver Jubilee as his administration. The offices of Vadodara Municipal Corporation are located in this building.

attractions.name: Kirti Mandir
attractions.description: The cenotaph of the Maharajas of Baroda.

attractions.name: Laxmi Vilas Palace
attractions.description: The imposing palace was built in the Indo-Saracenic tradition, with an eclectic mix of Indian, Islamic, and European elements by Maharaja Sayajirao III in 1890. Major Charles Mant was the architect. The interior, full of multi-coloured marble and mosaic tile, include a museum, containing portraits of the Royal family and original paintings by Raja Ravi Varma.

attractions.name: Maharaja Sayajirao University
attractions.description: The world-famous Maharaja Sayajirao University has one of the largest campuses in Gujarat, full of beautiful historical buildings including Kala Bhavan, a former palace which is pictured in this article.

attractions.name: Makarpura Palace
attractions.description: The former royal summer palace now houses a training school by the Indian Air Force. It's a magnificent building modeled after Italian Renaissance prototypes, well worth a sight from outside.

attractions.name: Sevasi Vaav
attractions.description: Stepped well with some beautiful carvings on its pillars

attractions.name: Surya Narayan Temple
attractions.description: The oldest temple of the city.

attractions.name: Tambekar Wada
attractions.description: The private mansion (Haveli) of a chief minister (diwan) of Baroda who lived during the last Mughal Empire. It's a wooden four-storey building notable for its miniature-style painted murals, depicting scenes from Lord Krishna’s life, from the Mahabharata, and from the Anglo-Maratha war. Tambekarwada is a heritage monument under the protection of the Archaeological Survey of India. Only a small part of the historical mansion is open to the public.

attractions.name: Sardar Patel Planetarium
attractions.description: The pyramid-like building has four floors housing an amphitheatre, a planetarium chamber, an exhibition space and an observatory. Daily shows.

attractions.name: Central Library Baroda
attractions.description: One of the oldest public libraries in India.

attractions.name: Gendi Gate
attractions.description: One of the few survived gateways to the old city.

attractions.name: Nazar Baug Palace
attractions.description: a former royal guesthouse now converted into the Railway Staff college. The palace is scheduled to be demolished in early 2015.

attractions.name: Nyaya Mandir
attractions.description: A building designed in a grand Byzantine architectural style. It now serves as the District Court of Vadodara.
attractions.address: National Highway No. 8 G.N.F.C Corner, Zadeshwar

attractions.name: Sursagar Lake
attractions.description: Built in the 18th century, the Sursagar is also known as Chand Talao. It marks the center of the city of Vadodara, surrounded by the thrum of commerce in the Old City. A tall statue of Lord Shiva, which is lit up on Maha Shivratri, works as a veritable beacon over the lake. The perennial lake has several gates at the bottom that are opened in case of overflooding. The water then pours into the Vishvamitra River. In 2023, the statue was covered in gold weighing 17.5 kg worth approximately ₹12 crores.

attractions.name: Cinepolis
attractions.description: Good 3D effect.

attractions.name: The Gaekwad Baroda Golf Club
attractions.description: Baroda’s premier club and Gujarat’s oldest private golf club

attractions.name: Inox Multiplex
attractions.description: By far the best movie theater in town. Also at Seven Seas Mall 4th Floor
attractions.address: Race Course Road, Gopal Baug, Ellora Park

attractions.name: Mahatma Gandhi Nagar Gruh
attractions.description: Dance shows, and musical events

attractions.name: S-Cube Water Park
attractions.description: Water park with many slides, family pool, wave pool and six cuisine restaurant.
attractions.address: Opp. Ajwa Lake, Near Vrundavan Garden

attractions.name: Sayaji Baug Garden
attractions.description: Set on the banks of the Vishwamitri river, the garden is home to the Baroda Museum, the Sardar Patel Planetarium, and the Sayaji Baug Zoo. A toy train runs around the garden covering a distance of 3.5 km.

attractions.name: Sir Sayajirao Nagargruh
attractions.description: The 1000-seat auditorium is Baroda music and dance main venue.

restaurants.name: Dairy Den
restaurants.description: This is Baroda's first ice cream parlor that serves soft cones. You can enjoy a variety of flavors over here.
restaurants.address: Dairy Den Circle, opposite SBI Bank,

restaurants.name: Frigtemp
restaurants.description: Recommended for Frankies, at (Fatheganj, Karelibaug & Old Padra Road).

restaurants.name: The Goodies Cafeteria
restaurants.description: Goodies, also in Sayajiganj, Makarpura, Fatehganj and Natubhai Circle, are favorite hangouts for youngsters apart for their bakery delights & junk food!

restaurants.name: Govinda's Restaurant
restaurants.description: Veg Restaurant. Samosas, alu (bataka) wadas, dahi wadas and gulab jamuns. The "prasad snack bar", where many items are available daily from 5PM until 9PM (9:30-10PM on Sundays and holidays) is located in the northeast corner of ISKCON Temple.

restaurants.name: Kalyan Restaurant
restaurants.description: Here you can get a variety of food choices from Chinese to continental along with Chaats, South Indian foods, etc. It is a self-service restaurant with good quality food. The best thing is the sizzler at the very low price of ₹130 and good in taste.

restaurants.name: Mahakali Sev Usal
restaurants.description: Food stand, delicious Sev Usal

restaurants.name: Millenium Restaurant
restaurants.description: Most popular for Biryani. Also in Alkapuri
restaurants.address: 1st Floor Fatehgunj Main Rd, Jayesh Colony

restaurants.name: Mirch Masala
restaurants.description: Veg and Nonveg Punjabi food. Try out the dilli chaat. Also inside Inorbit Mall.

restaurants.name: Nayab Restaurant
restaurants.description: Although menu is extensive at Nayab Restaurant, their delicious tandoori items are highly recommended and make for an excellent dining at very low prices. Takeaways are available

restaurants.name: Pooran Singh's kababs and parathas
restaurants.description: He's an ex-Welcomgroup chef who runs his own place now.

restaurants.name: Raju Omlet
restaurants.description: Eggetarian delights in Karelibaug in VIP Rd.

restaurants.name: Vanity
restaurants.description: Tasty non-vegetarian food.

attractions.name: Taj-ul-Masajid
attractions.description: One of the largest mosques in the country.

attractions.name: Manua Bhan Tekari
attractions.description: A very beautiful place with an ancient Shwetambar Jain temple on the hill. You can see a beautiful view of Bhopal from this Takeri. You can drive up to the temple, but there is limited parking. There is parking available at the base of the hill. A ropeway cable car is available to go up. Tickets are ₹90 for a way ride and ₹60 for a way ride. Cash and UPI payments are accepted.

attractions.name: Bharat Bhavan
attractions.description: Bharat Bhavan is a world-famous art complex and museum.
attractions.address: J. Swaminathan Marg, Shamla Hills, Near Upper Lake

attractions.name: Regional Museum of Natural History
attractions.description: Regional Museum of Natural History, Bhopal is a branch of the National Museum of Natural History, New Delhi, it is the center of an informal environment education, whose main purpose is to make people aware of environmental protection through various internal and external activities.
attractions.address: Shahpura Rd, near State Bank, E-5, Arera Colony

attractions.name: Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Manav Sangrahalaya
attractions.description: Another impressive museum, the Museum of Man created by the government of Madhya Pradesh, showcases how the people of the state live in their natural form, what they cultivate, the kind of tools they make and utilise in their daily lives, etc. It has been created sprawled on a small hill and gives breathtaking views of the city.

attractions.name: MP Tribal Museum
attractions.description: A museum of tribal culture. The exhibits depict the ways of living of various tribes across India. There are model houses, courtyards, artefacts of worshipping rituals, marriage rituals and everyday life. The museum is well-maintained. There is a restaurant for tea and snacks.

attractions.name: Science Centre
attractions.description: A science museum at Shyamla Hills.

attractions.name: Shaurya Smarak
attractions.description: A war memorial, museum and public park honouring Indian soldiers, in particular those from the state of Madhya Pradesh, who have fought in recent wars. There is ample parking space, and audio tours are available.

attractions.name: Upper Lake
attractions.description: A beautiful water body created during the time of King Bhoj. The water of Upper Lake was reputed to have cured Raja Bhoj of a skin disease which otherwise remained untreated. Today, you can rent boats, indulge in other water sports-related activities and enjoy the splendour of the lake.

attractions.name: Lower Lake
attractions.description: This lake is separated from the Upper Lake by an over-bridge. It was created during the Mughal Empire.

attractions.name: Van Vihar National Park
attractions.description: Van Vihar is a wildlife sanctuary. It has a diverse range of fauna, including several species of deer, big cats, snakes, birds and gharials which can be seen basking in the ponds.
attractions.address: Lake View Walk Path, Krishna Nagar, Shymala Hills

restaurants.name: Chhapan Bhog
restaurants.description: Basically a restaurant-cum-sweets shop.

restaurants.name: Hotel Rajhans
restaurants.description: Tasty and unlimited thalis at a very reasonable price.

restaurants.name: Manohar Dairy and Restaurant
restaurants.description: Clean restaurant with a very wide selection of food and sweets. Tasty but portions are small. They seem to have a few branches in the city.

restaurants.name: Pin & Pan Cafe
restaurants.description: Pin & Pan Cafe - A Global Cuisine Restaurant.
restaurants.address: Fortune Business Arcade, near Aakriti Ecocity, Bawadiya Kalan, Salaiya, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh 462026

attractions.name: Golghar
attractions.description: Captain John Garstin built a Golghar for the storage of food for the British army with storing capacity of 140,000 tons in 1786.

attractions.name: Mahatma Gandhi Setu
attractions.description: The bridge over the river Ganges connecting Patna and Hajipur.

attractions.name: Kumhrar
attractions.description: Explore the ancient ruins of Pataliputra. Of the 80 pillars (Fa Hien, in 5th century CE, found the pillars shining as bright as glass) excavated at the site; only one remains.

attractions.name: Bihar Museum
attractions.description: Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar. It has several galleries, including the regional gallery, the contemporary gallery, the historical art galleries and the gallery on Bihari diaspora.
