The museum is open from 10:00 to 19:00 except Monday. However, the history part is closed after 17:00 hours and only the Children's Gallery is open from 17:00 to 19:00. Ticket costs for Indians are as follows: Adults - ₹100, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹50, Students - ₹50, while for foreigners is: Adults - ₹500, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹250, Camera - ₹100

attractions.name: Deep Narayan Singh Museum
attractions.description: Small local history museum, named after independence hero and first minister of Bihar, Deep Narayan Singh, who was born in Hajipur.

attractions.name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya
attractions.description: A public museum showcasing the life and principles of Mahatma Gandhi. It contains an exhibition containing photos, paintings, sculptures, manuscripts and quotations; all the major events in his life are told here. There is also a section containing photographs of his childhood through the various phases of Gandhi's life, including being taken to the crematorium. The building also houses a library which has a rich collection of books, magazine, literature and audio-video material related to Gandhi's life.

attractions.name: Indira Gandhi Planetarium
attractions.description: Among the largest and best planetariums in Asia, it attracts a large number of both domestic and foreign tourists. The planetarium has regular film shows on subjects related to astronomy and also holds exhibitions.

attractions.name: Patna Museum
attractions.description: It has more than 50,000 rare art objects, with many related to India in the ancient, middle ages and the British colonial era. Don't forget to see the Holy Relic Casket with the sacred ashes of Lord Buddha, and the beautiful statue Yakshani.

attractions.name: Shrikrishna Science Centre
attractions.description: The main science museum in the city with over 50 exhibits on physics and mathematics, with an emphasis towards optical illusions. Targeted towards kid aged 10 and over but adults will also have an enjoyable time the first time around.
attractions.address: West Gandhi Maidan, Raja Ji Salai, Dujra Diara

attractions.name: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Science City
Rajendra Smriti Sangrahalaya
attractions.description: A museum dedicated to Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India.

attractions.name: Bharatiya Nritya Kala Mandir
attractions.description: A crafts museum and a multi-purpose cultural centre. The building contains dance and drama studios, a gallery space, and an art museum.

attractions.name: Kali Temple-Darbhanga House
attractions.description: One of the oldest temple of Goddess Kali.

attractions.name: Pathar ki Masjid
attractions.description: Built by Pervez, the elder brother of Shah Jahan and the first Mughal prince who made Bihar his residence.

attractions.name: Padri Ki Haveli
attractions.description: Oldest church in Bihar. When Roman Catholics first arrived in Bihar, they built a small church in 1713.

attractions.name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
attractions.description: The birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

attractions.name: Maner-Sufi Saint Shrine
attractions.description: You can buy famous Maner Ka Ladoo(Sweets). Maner Sweets is one of the popular shops that specializes in these. However, avoid going there in the late evening or night.

attractions.name: Sonepur Cattle Fair
attractions.description: Largest cattle and animal fair in Asia. It is held in November in Sonepur which across the Ganges from Patna.

attractions.name: Buddha Smriti Park
attractions.description: A large park constructed in former jail ground is an oasis from noise and bustle of the city. Quiet meditative place and air conditioned libraries are the real relief even for a waiting time for the train. The large stupa is where ashes of Buddha originally from Vaishali are kept. There is a laser show in the evenings, which is related to the history of Bihar from the Ramayana to present.

attractions.name: Funtasia Water Park
attractions.description: Contains attractions like waterslides, wave pool, swimming pools, multi-cuisine restaurant, coffee shops, souvenir shops and a banquet hall.

attractions.name: Gandhi Maidan
attractions.description: Gandhi Maidan is the heart of this city today.

attractions.name: Sanjay Gandhi Jaivik Udyan
attractions.description: One of the most popular picnic spots in Patna. It consists of a zoo and a botanical garden.

attractions.name: Shaheed Veer Kunwar Singh Azadi Park
Patna Golf Club
attractions.description: With some very tough holes, this well-maintained course situated downtown will prove interesting to amateur and pros alike. The Patna Golf Club is set in beautiful surroundings.

attractions.name: Anjaneri Parvat
attractions.description: Located near Trambakeshwar, it is well known for waterfalls during monsoon season.

attractions.name: Deolali Camp Cantonment Board
attractions.description: Artillery centre - Deolali camp's, Lahawit market is for shopping, Deolali South has Khandoba temple hill, golf course, sun rise & set point as well.

attractions.name: WeGo Art Gallery & Art Exhibition
attractions.description: Texture painting by needle on canvas.

attractions.name: Nandur Madhmeshwar Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: A bird sanctuary near Niphad. It is a mesmerizing place for nature and bird lovers alike.

attractions.name: Panchavati
attractions.description: A sacred place where five sacred Banyan trees are still present. All important temples are in this area.

attractions.name: Phalke Smaarak
attractions.description: Excellent views, landscape, musical fountain, video songs, Buddha smaarak, water park. located on foot of Pandav Caves hill. A reliable place where most of the people in Nasik spend their weekend evenings.

attractions.name: Ramshej Fort
attractions.description: Located near Ashewadi village on Peath Road. from Nashik. Good for a small trekking experience. The fort provides a good view of the whole city from the mountaintop.

attractions.name: Bhaktidham
attractions.description: A temple on Peth Naka.

attractions.name: Chambhar Leni
attractions.description: Temple of Bhagwan Mahavir on a hillock inside a cave.

attractions.name: Dharmachakra Jain Mandir
attractions.description: It has a 12 ton Panchdhatu idol of Bhagwan Mahavir. It's at Vilholi on Nashik- Mumbai highway.

attractions.name: Ganga Ghat
attractions.description: Ramkunda, Panchavati

attractions.name: Goda Ghat
attractions.description: A popular place to visit.

attractions.name: Kalaram Temple
attractions.description: An important temple and landmark in Panchavati area.

attractions.name: Muktidham
attractions.description: A big marble temple and picnic spot at Nashik Road.
attractions.address: Mahatma Gandhi Rd, Gayakhe Colony, Nashik Road

attractions.name: Nashik Caves
attractions.description: Buddhist and Jain Caves dating back to 2nd century BCE on Nashik- Mumbai highway near Pathardi phata. They are on top of a hill. The view of the surrounding countryside including the city of Nashik is worth climbing up for.

attractions.name: Shree Navashya Ganpati Mandir
attractions.description: A temple on banks of Godavari River, very scenic views.

attractions.name: Sita Gufaa
attractions.description: Caves where Lord Ram and Sita worshipped Lord Shiva during their exile. The shivlinga is still present at that same spot. It is believed that Ravana kidnapped Sita from this place. It is always visited by devotees and tourists.

attractions.name: Someshwar
attractions.description: Temples, picnic spot, boating, and waterfall on Gangapur road.

attractions.name: Tapovan
attractions.description: Tapobhumi, Shurpanakha's nose fell here, Tasty Guavas, try them out. Once upon a time, it was a part of the sacred Dandakaranya forest. Tapovan is a picturesque place, also contains a close connection with the epic Ramayana.

attractions.name: Shri Tryambakeshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
attractions.description: One of the 12 Jyotirlingas in India, and is the most sacred place in Nashik. Nearby is also the Brahma giri, where lord Shiva performed the tandava dance.

attractions.name: Mineral Museum
attractions.description: It displays very precious stones.

attractions.name: Tarangan
attractions.description: This planetarium is named after the late Shri Yashwantrao Chavan and was inaugurated by President Pratibha Patil. Daily 3 shows are conducted at 1:30PM in English, 3:30PM in Hindi and 5:30PM in Marathi.

attractions.name: MFL's Zonkers Adventure Park
attractions.description: Features go karting, artificial rock climbing, rope activities, archery and various other activities.
attractions.address: Opposite Beyond Resort by Sula, Gangapur-Savargaon Rd

restaurants.name: Agrawal Bros K Mithaiwala
restaurants.description: Hot snacks, sweets, cold drinks, ice-cream, samosas.

restaurants.name: Budha Halwai
restaurants.description: "Keep Calm and eat Jelebi!" is their motto.

restaurants.name: Cafe Bliss
restaurants.description: Serves 80 types of coffee and tea, and sandwiches, wraps, pizzas, burgers and desserts.

restaurants.name: Cafe xpress
restaurants.description: There is another branch on Nashik Road.

restaurants.name: Carnival
restaurants.description: at College Road serves very good quality Chinese & Indian food.

restaurants.name: Chai Tapri
restaurants.description: Loosely translated as "tea shack", Chai Tapri is one of the typical establishments in the area where you can sip tapri tea with locals.
restaurants.address: 2, Thatte Wadi Rd, Thatte Nagar, Karvan Society

restaurants.name: Chetana dining hall
restaurants.description: Vega restaurant, traditional Thali meals.

restaurants.name: Domino's
restaurants.description: Tasty pizza.

restaurants.name: Goli Vada Pav
restaurants.description: Indian-style burgers. Other outlets at Sharanpur Road and Indira Nagar (opposite Raj Sarthi Society.)

restaurants.name: Hotel Samrat
restaurants.description: 24-hour restaurant serving Gujrathi Thali and pure veg Indian dishes

restaurants.name: Jalaram Sweets
restaurants.description: Serves amazing chaats along with a range of sweets. One should not miss their Kachori, Samosa and Khajur/Imli Chutney.

attractions.name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
attractions.description: This museum houses Gandhi's bloodstained dhoti and little else by way of artifacts. Those interested in the freedom struggle, though, will be interested in the extensive library housed here. The portrayal of freedom struggle is very inspiring and Indian tourists particularly students should consider visiting this place. Tamil speakers and long-term visitors may be interested in the classes and workshops offered in subjects as diverse as t'ai chi and local herbs. There is also a khadi bhavan (store selling village and handloom products) and bookstore, with (mostly Tamil) books on spiritual and natural health topics. Also located on the campus of the museum is a government museum (across from the library).

attractions.name: Melamadai Vandiyur Lake
attractions.description: Boating, swimming, and Fishing in Melamadai Vandiyur Lake provides some more ever green memories. These are only allowed if the Madurai Corporation authority provides permission. Migratory Birds are observed at the Melamadai Vandiyur Lake.

attractions.name: Samanar Hills
attractions.description: These rocky hills are home to various Jain and Hindu monuments dating between the 2nd-century BCE and the 12th-century CE. Situated 10 kms west of the Madurai city proper, it is declared as a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India. Rock-cut stairs lead to the monuments from the base of the hills, with a maximum elevation of around 150 metres. Jain reliefs of Mahavira, and the Tirthankaras are found, along with several inscriptions.

attractions.name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Mahal
attractions.description: The remains of the palace of the 17th-century ruler Thirumalai Nayak who contributed extensively to the Meenakshi Temple. Only a small portion of the original structure which was four times as larger remains. There were originally two parts – Swargavilasa heavenly pavilion, meant for the King's harem and housing the darbar court, and the ranka vilasa, which was for the servants. Entrance to the roof is prohibited until the renovation work being carried out by the Archaeological Department is conpleted. There is a sound and light show in the evening (both English & Tamil version of the show). There is also a museum, which houses not only the original portraits of Thirumalai naicker, but also unearthed stine carvings of the 17th century, along with many sculptures of Hindu gods like Brahma, Nataraja, Saraswati of the period. There is one rare painting on one of the pillars, which the Archaeological Department claim to have unearthed from one of the pillars. There is a painting hidden in

attractions.name: Goripalayam Dargah
attractions.description: The name Goripalayam comes from the Persian word Gor which means Grave. This area is called as Goripalayam because the Graves of the two famous saints of Islam and rulers of Madurai Hazrat Sulthan Alauddin Badusha (Radiyallah) and Hazrat Sulthan Shamsuddin Badhusha (Radiyallah) are located here. A beautiful green coloured tomb can be seen from the A.V. Bridge Madurai, which is the Goripalayam Dargah in the northern banks of Vaigai River. It is amazing to see that the dome, which is 70 feet in diameter and 20 feet in height, is made of a single block of stone which was brought from the Azhaga Hills. People from all over Tamil Nadu come here to seek blessings and go back fruitfully. The two rulers were brothers who ruled the northern part of madurai after coming from Oman during 13th century to spread Islam. Hazrat Kazi Syed Tajuddin Radiyallah of Kazimar street was Govt. Kazi (Islamic Legal advisor and jury) to them. An ancient Tamil inscription, can be found planted on the outer campus

attractions.name: Kazimar Big Mosque and Maqbara
attractions.description: This traditional mosque (masjid) is at the heart of Madurai city, within 500 m of the Periyar (Central) bus stand and within 1 km south east of the Madurai Railway Junction. Hazrat Kazi Syed Tajuddin, who came from Oman during 13th century, received this land from the then Pandyan king, Koo(n) Pandiyan, and constructed the mosque which is the first Muslims' place of worship in Madurai. Maqbara the dargah of the Madurai Hazrats (Hazrat Meer Ahamad Ibrahim, Hazrat Meer Amjad Ibrahim and Hazrat Syed Abdus Salaam Ibrahim Rahmatullahi Alaihim) is also located inside the mosque premises. All of Kazi Syed Thajuddheen's descendants (Huqdars - shareholders of this mosque called as Syeds) have lived in the same locality (Kazimar street) for more than 700 years, and have managed the mosque since then. Syed Tajuddin was appointed as Kazi of the sultans, and still his descendants who live at Kazimar street, Madurai, are appointed as Kazis to the Government of Tamil Nadu. All Syeds belong to the Sun

attractions.name: Thiruparankundram Dargah
attractions.description: An Islamic dargah is at the top of the Thiruparankundram Hill, where the grave of an Islamic saint Hazrat Sultan Sikandhar Badushah shaheed Radiyallah Ta'al anhu, who came from Jeddah along with Hazrat Sulthan Syed Ibrahim Shaheed Badushah of Madinah (now in Erwadi) during the early 13th century, is found. Irrespective of religion, people from all parts of Tamil Nadu and from Kerala visit this durgah. People who visit the Ervadi Durgah are supposed to visit this durgah. Many poems were written in praise of Hazrat Sultan Sikandhar Badhusha, by Syed Abdussalam Ibrahim Saalim Hazrat, the third in the list of Madurai Hazrats and his Maternal grandson Syed Abdus Salaam Ibrahim Saahib Hazrat. It is seen that people who come here with a wish see it answered in a very short time, and so He is also called Mustajab ad Du'aa Sikandhar Badhushah. Mustajab Ad Du'aa in Arabic means A saint whose Supplications are immediately answered by Allah. The Anniversary urus festival of Hazrat Sulthan Sikandar

attractions.name: Alagar Koyil
attractions.description: Another Vaishnava temple Alagar Koil, 20 km away from the city located in the nearby hills. At the top of the hill is a natural stream from where the water is carried fresh daily by the temple priest for the Lord. Famous for Chittrai Festival (First Tamil month, 9 April–May) - Summer Festival. The Lord is considered the brother of Meenakshi (Goddess Paravati) given in wedding with Sundareshwar (Lord Shiva).

attractions.name: Koodal Azhagar Temple
attractions.description: Important Vaishnava Temple magnificent, has three stairs of the lord posture. Sitting posture of the lord (Main moola deity), one level up is a standing posture of the lord, and the 3rd level up is the lying down posture of the lord. The temple is a spectacular one. It is in the heart of the city, one of the Divya Desams (108). Worshipped by "Alwars - Vasihnav Saints". Worth to see and worship.

attractions.name: Mandi Kovil
attractions.description: A very old temple which said to be around more than 600 years old. Preferable days to visit Pandi Kovil are Tuesdays and Fridays.

attractions.name: Murugan Temple
attractions.description: Near to Alagar Koil, important temple for Lord Karthikeya on the hills, of course inside of Solai - jungle. One of the six important temple for Lord Muruga - Karthikeya. This is a very large and beautiful temple. You can take an auto rickshaw from the Meenakshi temple to visit this temple for a charge of around ₹100 (2007). Regular bus service is offered by the Transport Corporation. There is an utsavam of the deity on a golden chariot at 7PM.

attractions.name: Subramaniya Swamy Temple
attractions.description: One of the important old Temple dedicated to Lord Muruga - Karthikeya on a hillock approximately 8 km from the city. First Arupadai Veedu. References to this ancient temple are available in scriptures from 6th century AD (Paripadal). The temple interior is a huge rectangular chamber carved out of the hill, with side chambers housing various deities of Hindu religion approached via narrow passages. The Thiruparankundram temple is accessible via road from Madurai and has a railway station 1 km away. Most express trains do not stop there though.

attractions.name: Vandiyur Mariamman Teppakulam
attractions.description: A temple built in the middle of a man-made pond. Mariamman Teppakulam Famous for its float festival (teppa tiruvila) conducted during the Thai Poosam (falls in the second half of January). Popular story is that the spot was excavated for its soil to be used for building Tirumala Nayakkar Mahal. The king had ordered excavated spot to be converted into a 16-acre lake fed from Vaigai river through under ground channels. The river has water only during North-East Monsoon season (Oct-Nov) and hence the lake has water from Nov to Feb.

attractions.name: Pazhamudircholai Murugan Temple
attractions.description: This is one of the six of the holiest of Murugan shrines referred to as the Aarupadai Veedugal. Unlike the other five temples, there is no grand edifice surrounding the central shrine of worship. However, this is a holy shrine venerated by the Skanda Puranam and by Nakkeerar's Thirumurugatrupadai of the Sangam period. Arunagirinathar's Thirupugazh also reveres this shrine.

restaurants.name: Amma Mess
restaurants.description: Amma (Tamil for mother). This mess (restaurant) is a popular among the locals residents and those travelling from neighboring cities. Their lunch is very popular. Don't miss their speciality dishes like rabbit biriyani, dove biriyani, crab omelette and bone marrow omelette.

restaurants.name: Hotel Kanna
restaurants.description: Tasty biryani, parota, non-vegetarian dishes. Close to shopping. This hotel is famous for its mutton fry and fish.

restaurants.name: Hotel Janakiram 1
restaurants.description: Great non-vegetarian restaurant. Amazing service.

restaurants.name: Modern Restaurant
restaurants.description: $/NN/[S]/[T]/[V] Great place to savour a traditional south Indian meal. They serve authentic idly, dosa, pongal and kesari (as you would find in a traditional Iyengar household). Their clientele has boasted of Jawaharlal Nehru and Mahatma Gandhi. Even till a few years ago, their walls were covered with photographs of who's who of India.

restaurants.name: Vaigai mess
restaurants.description: A first class non-veg hotel. It is popular in the noon. you can have your lunch there. Chicken biriyani, mutton biriyani are famous there. Fish fry, mutton fry, chicken fry and a lot of spicy dishes to taste.

restaurants.name: Konar Kadai
restaurants.description: Non-vegetarian. taste is very good
restaurants.address: Near Railway Station & Tamil Changam Rd

restaurants.name: The banyan
restaurants.description: Geoffery Bawa designed this hotel so the restaurant faces the old banyan tree and has a lot of daylight. The food is delightfully moderate on both price and spices! They offer Indian and continental menus. The staff speak English, so it's probably the best place to eat quality food in Madurai.

restaurants.name: Arul Anandam Mess
restaurants.description: Non-vegetarian dishes

restaurants.name: Taj Restaurant
restaurants.description: Quality non-vegetarian restaurant catering to foreign tourists.

attractions.name: Watson Museum
attractions.description: The Watson Museum was established in 1888 and was named after the British Political Agent of Kathiwad, Colonel John Watson. The Museum exhibits copies of artifacts from Mohenjodaro, sculptures, costumes of the local tribal people.

attractions.name: The Lang Library
attractions.description: The library has an extensive collection of old books and a repository of reference material linked to the colonial era.

attractions.name: Mohandas Gandhi High School
attractions.description: Where Mahatma Gandhi got his primary education. The buildings were built by the Nawab of Junagadh and took the name of the Duke Alfred of Saxe-Coburg and Gotha

attractions.name: Kaba Gandhi No Delo
attractions.description: Mahatma Gandhi's childhood residence. It has now been converted in to a memorial called "Gandhi Smriti". The museum displays and consists of photographs, objects and the belongings of Mahatma Gandhi.

attractions.name: Rotary Dolls Museum
attractions.description: This unique museum gives an overview to the culture and traditions of the world at large through a medium of various dolls

attractions.name: Rashtriya Shala
attractions.description: Founded in 1921 by Mahatma Gandhi, the centre supports small industries such as Khadi spinning. A centre for patola sari weaving is also located here. There is a memorial room where Gandhi fasted during the Indian civil disobedience movement.

attractions.name: Race course
attractions.description: Where people head for a stroll in the mornings and at nights. The site of major events in the city. Also, Madhavrao Schindia Cricket Stadium is located in the area

attractions.name: Swaminarayan Temple
attractions.description: A temple of BAPS, a socio-spiritual Hindu organization with its roots in the Vedas. It was revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan (1781-1830) in the late 18th century and established in 1907 by Shastriji Maharaj (1865-1951).

attractions.name: Shri Ramkrishna Ashram
attractions.description: Has a permanent exhibition showcasing the life of Shri Ramkrishna plus a public library and an Ayurvedic centre.

attractions.name: Ishwariya Mahadev
attractions.description: Located on a hilltop in the outskirts of the city. The surrounding area is a traditional picnic spot.

attractions.name: Panchmukhi Hanuman
attractions.description: The Temple of Lord Hanuman that is believed to keep the area free of rakshasas (demons). A large number of devotees visit the temple every day to get rid of evil spirits.

attractions.name: Aji Dam
attractions.description: A beautiful dam site constructed during British Raj.

attractions.name: Nyari Dam
attractions.description: A beautiful dam site. Very good for weekend stay and bird watching

attractions.name: Rajkumar College
attractions.description: Founded in 1868 for educating royal princes and elites of Kathiawar states, it is now public school. The 11-hectre campus in centre of the city houses buildings with Gothic architecture.

attractions.name: Krishna Water Park
attractions.description: This small amusement park includes a wave pool, a high pendulum slide and a rain discotheque for kids only.

restaurants.name: Temptations
restaurants.description: Family restaurant with mixed cuisine including Italian (lasagne), Chinese and Mexican — all vegetarian and crowded.

restaurants.name: Flavours
restaurants.description: Multi-cuisine restaurant (Punjabi/North Indian, Mexican, etc.). Immaculately clean and impeccable service. Busy on weekends

restaurants.name: Raju Pavbhaji
restaurants.description: Vegetarian restaurant.

restaurants.name: Apple Bite
restaurants.description: Very popular multicuisine restaurant. (Punjabj, Italian, Mexican, Continental, Chinese). Good ambiance, courteous staff

restaurants.name: Sankalp
restaurants.description: South Indian food
restaurants.address: Race Course Ring Road, Nr. Zilla Panchayat Chowk

restaurants.name: Big Bite the Food Court
restaurants.description: Popular Fast Food - Chinese, Continental. Indian dishes include chhole puri, garlic bread, rice pulao

restaurants.name: Subway
restaurants.description: Fast food, veg & non-veg sandwiches
restaurants.address: Shop No. 8 & 9, Race Course Ring Road

restaurants.name: Green Fuel
restaurants.description: Veg Rest.
restaurants.address: 150 Feet Ring Road, Near Madhapur Chokdi, Krishna Society, Madhapar

attractions.name: Bhatia Park
attractions.description: This park is at Shastri Nagar along the banks of the Kharkhai river.

attractions.name: Bhubaneshwari Temple
attractions.description: Located in Telco, atop a small hill. Offers a panoramic view of the city, and the scenic surroundings (breathtaking view of a meandering river.) The temple premises add a serene and spiritual touch to the surroundings.

attractions.name: Dimna Lake
attractions.description: Located approximately 13 km from the centre of the township. It is a manmade lake built by Tata Steel for water supply to the town. It has wonderful scenario near the Dalma hills. This lake is surrounded by mountains in all four directions, and has a guest house of Tata Steel.

attractions.name: Hudco Lake
attractions.description: Located in Telco Colony, is a beautiful park and picnic spot with an artificial waterfall and lake.

attractions.name: Jubilee Park
attractions.description: This park was a gift by Tata Steel to the citizens of Jamshedpur on its 50th anniversary. This 200-acre park, with a rose garden and a lake, now has a zoo and an amusement park. A favourite with joggers, cyclists and anglers. The Laser show and the musical fountains (introduced in 2000) is an excellent centre of attraction for the visitors.

attractions.name: Kali Temple
attractions.description: Very famous temple of Goddess Kali, made on a raised cut mountain.

attractions.name: Keenan Stadium
attractions.description: This well known stadium has hosted several One Day International cricket matches, but is no longer in use.

attractions.name: Rivers Meet
attractions.description: The confluence of rivers Kharkai and Subarnarekha. A popular picnic spot.

attractions.name: Russi Mody Centre of Excellence
attractions.description: A unique structure, just outside the Jubilee Park, designed by the famous architect, Hafeez Contractor, is home to the many professional associations of Jamshedpur. It also houses the Tata Steel Archives, where one can see documents relating to the history of the Steel Company and the city.

attractions.name: Sir Dorabji Tata Park
attractions.description: This park is near Keenan Stadium, and hosts Jamshedpur's annual flower show in December.

attractions.name: Tata Zoological Park
attractions.description: Located in Sakchi, one of the favourite tourism place in Jamshedpur.

attractions.name: Dhatkidih Masjid
attractions.description: A famous mosque in Dhatkidih, fully in white colour like Taj Mahal.

attractions.name: Regal Building
attractions.description: It was built in 1936. Nowadays it is a shopping mall.

attractions.name: Dalma Hill
attractions.description: Drive 20 min through Tata-Purulia Highway towards Purulia. There is a driveway from the base to the top of the hill, where you can stay. There are two facilities, one provided by JUSCO and the other by the Forest Dept.

attractions.name: Gol Pahari
attractions.description: This temple is atop a small hill and offers a panoramic view of the city.

restaurants.name: Appetite
restaurants.description: A great multicuisine restaurant with a great view of the Tata Steel factory (best viewed at night). Located next to the Gurudwara in Sakchi.

restaurants.name: Blooms
restaurants.description: A suburban bar and restaurant in Bistupur.

restaurants.name: Cinnamon
restaurants.description: Good value for moeny. At the Sonnet Hotel, South Park Bistupur. It's a 24/7 facility. Breakfast here starts at 6AM.

restaurants.name: Country Club
restaurants.description: It is a beautiful Bar with Egyptian background on the walls, a swimming pool, and an ice cream parlour.

restaurants.name: Daavat
restaurants.description: Is a part of Hotel Asian Inn at Dhatkidih. Best Mughlai food you can ever have and don't miss the sizzlers if you happen to be there.

restaurants.name: Deep Purple
restaurants.description: A new restaurant on a slightly expensive side in Sakchi Area in the Hotel Smita International. Has a big screen to entertain you with music videos or any important sports event that are on.

restaurants.name: Delhi Darbar
restaurants.description: Quite cheap place for non-vegetarians, situated at Sakchi next to Shopper's Square mall.

restaurants.name: Equinox
restaurants.description: The most expensive restaurant of Jamshedpur, part of the Sonnet Hotel.

restaurants.name: Ganga Regency
restaurants.description: A luxurious hotel with spacious parking lots and excellent quality food and service available.

restaurants.name: The Host
restaurants.description: This is not a part of a hotel. Very good food and not very expensive. Located Near Hyundai Showroom, Bistupur.

restaurants.name: Hotel Smita
restaurants.description: The best hotel for authentic Bengali cuisine. The Taj festival is also famous .

restaurants.name: Little Italy
restaurants.description: The Fortune Hotel Centre Point in Bistupur has this great vegetarian Italian Restaurant.

attractions.name: Dal Lake
attractions.description: Dal Lake is one of the prime attractions of Srinagar. At the very centre of the city, the lake covers an area of 21 km², which includes 3 km² of wetland. The lake has a circumference of 15.5 km. The lake is best explored on a shikara, a beautifully decorated boat that features in the logo of Jammu & Kashmir Tourism. Apart from open waters the lake also consists of floating markets, locally called rad. They basically constitute of matted vegetation and earth, but are floating. These are detached from the bottom of the lake and drawn to a suitable place and anchored. With nutrients from both land and water, these floating islands are used for cultivating tomatoes, cucumbers and melons. The area is a complex maze of floating cultivation patches separated by narrow water channels. The shikara negotiates through this complex maze with the skipper making his way through the complex maze of land and water. Floating market is another interesting area of the market. The market operates on float

attractions.name: Nagin Lake
attractions.description: Unlike the other three parts of Dal Lake the Nagin Lake is a separate lake connected to the Dal Lake by a narrow water channel. It is located on the western side of the Dal Lake and at the foot of Hari Parbat. It also has its share of floating vegetable gardens and house boats.

attractions.name: Mughal Gardens
attractions.description: These beautiful gardens line the periphery of the famous Dal Lake in Srinagar. Decorated with colourful flowers, fountains and mighty Chinars, strolling in these gardens gives one a royal feeling.

attractions.name: Rupa Lank
attractions.description: Rupa Lank, literally meaning silver island, is in the Dod Dal (central area of Dal Lake). The man-made island was constructed by Murad Baksh, brother of the last Mughal emperor, Aurangzeb. The island consists of four giant chinar trees in the four corners and the entire island consists of manicured lawns and paved pathways. There is a small house boat restaurant next to the island.

attractions.name: Sona Lank
attractions.description: Sona Lank, literally meaning gold island, is located in Lokut Dal, in the northern part of Dal Lake. It is next to the shrine of Hazarat Bal. This too follows a similar plan with four chinar trees at the four corners and is also made by Murad Baksh.

attractions.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Botanical Garden
attractions.description: A well-maintained park with lake by Dept of Floriculture with organised parking lot next to the park. The park occupies a large area and has a beverage shop run by the J&K Tourism department. They serve hot and flavoured "Kahva", a traditional drink of Kashmir. A cup costs ₹25. The nearby Tulip Park only has seasonal access. There is adequate parking adjacent to the park.

attractions.name: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden
attractions.description: Located on the eastern side of the Dal Lake, the Tulip Garden covers an area of 30 ha (74 acres) and is the largest tulip garden of Asia. It is located at the foothill of Zabarwan Range and overlooks the Dal lake. The garden was opened in 2007 with the aim of promoting floriculture tourism. It used to be known as Siraj Bagh. The garden is home to 65 varieties of tulip along with several other plants including daffodils, hyacinth and ranunculus. During its opening about 1.5 million bulbs of Tulip were flown in from Amsterdam. The Tulip Garden is also the venue for the Tulip Festival which happens every year in the month of April.

attractions.name: Chashme Shahi Garden
attractions.description: Chashme Shahi is the smallest of the three Mughal gardens of Srinagar, but in spite of its small size, the garden has its share of elegance. Cheshma Shahi (or Royal Spring) derives its name from a water source, a spring located at the uppermost terrace of the Garden. The water of the spring is said to possess some curative properties, especially for stomach ailments. The triple terrace garden is located on the southeastern edge of Dal Lake and offers a great view of the lake area and the Jhelum River valley. The garden was constructed by Ali Mardan Khan, governor of Emperor Shah Jahan in 1632 – 33.

attractions.name: Nishat Bagh
attractions.description: Located on the eastern banks of Dal Lake, with the Zabarwan Mountains as its backdrop, the garden was designed in 1633 by Asaf Khan, brother of Nur Jehan. Literally meaning the 'garden of bliss' it commands a magnificent view of the lake and the snow-capped Pir Panjal mountain range which stands far away to the west of the valley. Although a Mughal garden, it plans were altered because of the hilly terrain. It has an elongated plan (instead of a square plan of Mughal garden) of 548 m X 338 m and is centred around a water channel, measuring 4 m wide and 20 cm deep. The channel flows in the east to west direction and is decorated with fountains and occasionally fountain pools. The garden consists of 12 terraces, representing the 12 signs of the zodiac. However, it has only two sections, namely the public garden and the private garden for the Zanana or harem. The terraces are lined along the central channel and consist of stoned paved pathways and short flights of stairs. The pathways are

attractions.name: Shalimar Bagh
attractions.description: Shalimar, literally means abode of love, is a Mughal garden located on the northeast corner of Dal lake. It was built by Mughal Emperor Jahangir, for his wife Nur Jahan, in 1619. During Jahangir's reign, Srinagar served as the summer capital of the Mughal empire and Shilimar Bagh served as the Mughal court. Like Nishat Bagh, Shalimar Bagh follows the elongated plan with a dimension of 587 m by 251 m. The three-stage garden covers an area of 12.4 hectares (31 acres) and is centred around a central water channel. The lowest terrace contains the Diwan-e-Aam (public audience hall). The Diwan-e-Khas (the Hall of Private Audience) is located in the second terrace. The third and the uppermost terrace is topped with a central Zenna (Harem) pavilion, whose entrance is flanked with two smaller pavilion. The garden has paved pathways lined with chinar trees. The water channels consist of fountains and pools. The garden provides a grand bird eye view of the Dal Lake and the surroundings.

attractions.name: Hazratbal Mosque
attractions.description: The mosque houses a strand from the Prophet’s beard and hence the name Hazrat Bal. The strand of the beard is displayed on special days. The mosque is located on the western bank of Lokut Dal, the northern portion of the Dal Lake. Visible from the mosque compound is the island of Sona Lank, with four chinar trees in the four corners. The white mosque is breathtakingly beautiful. Women may enter only the first part of the mosque. The adjoining area is a foodie's delight with several makeshift food shop selling deep-fried snacks.

attractions.name: Jamia Masjid
attractions.description: One of the most important mosques in Kashmir, at the centre of Srinagar's religio-political life. Built between 1394–1402, the mosque has been a platform to debate and discuss the complex politics of Kashmir.

attractions.name: Dastgeer Sahib
attractions.description: A Sufi shrine housing the relics of saint Abdul Qadir Jeelani (1077–1166) who earned deep reverence across the subcontinent, despite never having set foot in the region.

attractions.name: Khanqah-e-Moula
attractions.description: A Sunni mosque built in 1539, and is held to be the first khanqah (mosques associated with specific saints) in the Kashmir Valley. It is one of the best examples of Kashmiri wooden architecture, and is decorated with papier-mâché.

attractions.name: Pathar Masjid
attractions.description: A Mughal-era stone mosque, built by empress Noor Jehan, the consort of Jahangir, in 1623.

attractions.name: Shankaracharya Mandir
attractions.description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva on a hilltop. It can be reached by car or taxi or auto rickshaw. You can walk too. It is a 5 km walk from the entrance of the hill. No cameras or mobiles phones are allowed within the temple, and you are supposed to leave them in the vehicle before entering the temple premises. The army checkpoint can also keep your camera and mobile phones. Cigarettes and alcoholic drinks should also be deposited with the police before the ascent of the hill, as these items are against Hinduism. Locals from Dal Gate say there are 250 steps to reach the temple. The temple is visible from Dal Lake Area. The temple complex offers a great bird eye view of the Dal Lake area and beyond.

attractions.name: Tomb of the Mother of Zain-ul-Abidin
attractions.description: Hidden in the streets between river and Zainda Kadal, this extraordinary brick mausoleum marks the final resting place of Sultan Sikande’s wife.

attractions.name: Ziarati Hazrati Youza Asouph
attractions.description: This tomb, also known as Roza Bal, is believed by some to be the tomb of Jesus (part of the larger theory that he survived the crucifixion and made his way to Kashmir where he lived until at least the age of 100). It has been made popular by books such as Jesus Lived in India by Holger Kersten (1983) among others. It's down a little side road - ask around, pretty much anyone in the area can point you in the right direction. It was closed in 2011 and sealed, photography and videography are not permitted.

attractions.name: Burzahom
attractions.description: A pre-Indus archaeological site.

attractions.name: Pari Mahal
attractions.description: Pari Mahal, literally meaning the palace of the fairies, is a seven terraced garden located at the southeast corner of Dal Lake. The garden was constructed by Dara Sukho, elder brother of Aurangzeb, the last of the great Mughals. It was constructed in the mid 17th century. The uppermost terrace contains two baradari-styled structures and a reservoir. The walls consists of arched gateways and there are several other structures in the compound.

attractions.name: Parihaspora
attractions.description: Visit the ruins located on the outskirts of Srinagar on way to Gulmarg. See the palaces of Kashmir's Buddhist and Hindu rulers and Buddhist places of worship.

attractions.name: SPS Museum
attractions.description: This museum established in the late 19th century houses around 80,000 artefacts mainly from the broader Jammu and Kashmir region.In 2017, a second building which is more resistant to earthquakes and other natural disasters was constructed, and many of the more valuable and vulnerable artefacts were moved there. The original building is still in use.

attractions.name: Musical Fountain
attractions.description: The musical fountain along with laser show was inaugurated in April 2019. It runs three times a day after 7 pm and consists of a 15-minute show. Apart from the musical fountain the show also depicts the history of Kashmir through a laser show.

attractions.name: Dachigam National Park
attractions.description: Home to the critically endangered Kashmir stag (hangul). Grasslands, alpine meadows, waterfalls and craggy cliffs provide a home for various species of mammals such as the Himalayan black and brown bears, jackal and leopard and birds such as the woodpecker, pygmy owl and cinnamon sparrow.

attractions.name: Hokersar
attractions.description: A Ramsar site and a bird sanctuary.

attractions.name: Aurangabad Caves
attractions.description: This is a fine piece of architecture, is presented in the most unembellished manner. The caves lie just outside the city and are believed to have been excavated between the 2nd and the 6th century. They house the most stunningly intricate carvings. There are nine caves in all, most of them being the viharas. The 4th and the 7th cave are worth a dekko. The 4th cave stands well supported on 12 columns carved with scenes depicting the stories from the Jataka tales, whereas the 7th cave is embedded with carvings of women, adorned with jewels. The main attraction is the sculpture of a 'Bodhisatva' praying for deliverance.

attractions.name: Bibi ka Maqbara
attractions.description: A replica of the Taj Mahal, the Bibi-ka-Maqbara is the only example of the Mughal architecture of its kind in the Deccan plateau. It was built in 1679 by Aurangzeb’s son, in tribute to his mother, Begum Rabia Durani.

attractions.name: History Museum - Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University
attractions.description: It has on display a good number of ancient Indian paintings, coins, fabrics, arms, artifacts, etc. The museum collection is huge and has some fine sculptures from the excavation at Bhokardan, a nearby historic site.

attractions.name: Pan Chakki
attractions.description: This is a 17th-century water mill. The name has been derived from the mill that crushed grain for the pilgrims. There is a picturesque garden here that houses several beautiful fish tanks and it plays abode to the memorial of a Sufi Saint.

attractions.name: Shrimant Chatrapati Shivaji Raje Museum
attractions.description: As the name suggests, this museum is dedicated to the great warrior of Maharashtra - Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. A number of exhibits associated with Lord Shivaji are on display.

attractions.name: Soneri Mahal
attractions.description: an old historic monument now converted into museum houses a variety of ancient Indian pottery, dresses, remains of local palaces and antiques of daily use. A number of sculptures and reliefs from the local excavations are also on display.

attractions.name: Siddharth Garden
attractions.description: This is a beautiful landscaped garden, with good variety of trees and shrubs. There is a small aquarium inside the garden, however the biggest attraction is the Siddharth Garden Zoo, with a large variety of animals, viz. lions, tigers (white & Bengal), leopards, crocodiles, snakes (snake-house), civet cats, hyena, fox, porcupine, emu, deer and sprawling lawns to sit and have a great picnic.

restaurants.name: Gayatri Chaat Bhandaar Road Side Eatery
restaurants.description: Other unit at Kranti Chowk and are the oldest road side eateries in town. They serve excellent deep fried snacks like Kachoris, Samosas and Bhajjiyas hot and fresh prepared in front of you on a 'Chulha' (clay oven). However, it is not very hygienic.

attractions.name: Jantar Mantar
attractions.description: Jantar Mantar literally means a combination of instruments and formulas (jantar = instrument and mantar = formula). It is an observatory consisting of a series of masonry architecture of unique form, each with a specialized function for astronomical measurement. Jai Singh, king of Amber, built 5 such observatories across northern and western India. Apart from Varanasi the other 4 places are Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain and Mathura (one in Mathura no longer exist). The Varanasi Jantar Mantar is much smaller compared to the ones in Delhi and Jaipur. The observatory houses 6 instruments of 5 types (it has 2 Samrat Yantra or sun dial). Apart from the observatory, the Man Mahal houses a Virtual Experiential Museum showing a series of light and sound shows. The shows include one on the mythology of the Ganges and its course. There are models depicting life in Varanasi and including a model of a pan shop. There is an interactive musical gallery.

attractions.name: Rajghat
attractions.description: This archaeological site was the result of a chance discovery in the 1940s when the Kashi Railway Station was extended. After a couple of excavations, a structure was unearthed dating back to the 2nd century BCE. The archaeological evidence suggested that the place was continuously inhabited since the 8th century BCE. Today it consists of several scattered brick structures rising only to a height of {{ft|3|to|4

attractions.name: Rani Laxmibai Janmasthali
attractions.description: Birthplace of Rani Laxmibai. It has been converted into a small gallery. A statue of Laxmibai riding a galloping horse welcomes visitors to the gallery. The walls behind and on the two sides of the statue are converted into a gallery complete with images and writeups. They depicts the life of Rani Laxmibai. Most of the writings are in Hindi.

attractions.name: Panchganga Ghat
attractions.description: the meeting of the five rivers.

attractions.name: Manikarnika Ghat
attractions.description: The main cremation ghat; a must-see, but remain quiet and avoid taking photographs (scams are plentiful here; see the "Stay Safe" section). There's a temple on the ghat called Ratneshwar Temple, which is leaning by 9°, more than the Leaning Tower of Pisa. Its sanctum is generally underwater most of the year, except during the summer.

attractions.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
attractions.description: Known as the 'main' ghat, this is the site of the large evening aarti ceremony. The ceremony starts right after the sunset and lasts for around 45 minutes.

attractions.name: Rana Ghat
attractions.description: The ghat is on the banks of the Ganges which helps people to do religious ceremonies without any difficulty.

attractions.name: Kedar Ghat
attractions.description: Brightly painted in stripes and busy with bathers, very photogenic.

attractions.name: Narad Ghat
attractions.description: The ghat on which bathing with spouse is not advised because of the myth of contention.

attractions.name: Harishchandra Ghat
attractions.description: The cremation place where Raja Harishchandra did the last rituals of his son.

attractions.name: Hanuman Ghat
attractions.description: It used to be known as Ramesvaram Ghat and is at a holy spot known as Juna Akhara in Varanasi. People believe that the Ghat was constructed by Lord Rama and hence it is dedicated to his favourite disciple, Lord Hanuman.

attractions.name: Shivala Ghat
attractions.description: The ghat was constructed by King Balwant Singh and played an important role during the Middle Ages. It comes under the western part of Varanasi and as the name suggests disciples connected the ghat with Lord Shiva.

attractions.name: Tulsi Ghat
attractions.description: Site of the large water purification plant.

attractions.name: Assi Ghat
attractions.description: A popular place for tourists, long-term students and researchers to stay, with many hotels, restaurants, and internet cafes nearby. The morning aarti, known as Subah e Banars, is held at the Assi Ghat.

attractions.name: Lal Khan Tomb
attractions.description: Lal Khan was the minister and commander of Balwant Singh (reign: 1740 – 70) the King of Varanasi (then Banaras). His last wish was to be buried in such a place so that he could keep an eye on the gateway of the royal palace. The king kept his last wish by building him a magnificent tomb on the northern edge of Varanasi. The tomb stands at the centre of a Mughal garden, marked with four chhatris on four corners out of which three stand to this day. The tomb stands on an elevated square plinth, which also houses several graves. so that he could keep an eye on the gateway of the royal palace. The tomb is crowned with a single dome flanked with chhatris on four corners. Each side has three arches with the central arches slightly higher than the side ones. The highlight of the tomb is the decorative multi-coloured tile work. Sadly, the colours have faded, robbing the tomb of its elegant look.

attractions.name: Alamagir Mosque
attractions.description: Overlooking Panchganga Ghat, it's a great place for a bird's eye view of the area.

attractions.name: Gyanvapi Mosque
attractions.description: A rather controversial mosque built during the rule of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. It is believed among the Hindus that the Gyanvapi Mosque is the original site of Kashi Vishwanath Temple. Photography is prohibited.

attractions.name: Bharat Mata Temple
attractions.description: The Bharat Mata temple at Varanasi is the only temple dedicated to Mother India. It is located in the Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth campus. The Bharat Mata temple was built by Babu Shiv Prasad Gupt and inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1936. The statute of Bharat Mata is built in marble and is a model of undivided India, depicting the mountains, plains and oceans. The most peculiar thing about the Bharat Mata Temple is that instead of the customary gods and goddesses, it houses a relief map of India, carved out of marble.

attractions.name: Durga Mandir
attractions.description: Built in the 18th century, the Durga temple was made as a tribute to Goddess Durga. It is also one of the well-known temples in Varanasi.

attractions.name: Gauri Matha Temple
attractions.description: The devi at this temple is supposed to be the sister of the lord Kashi Vishwanath. It is a tradition to visit her just before you leave Kashi. You buy sea shells at this place and offer them to God saying that the virtues of donating the shells go to her while you keep the virtues of having visited the holy shrines in Kashi and bathing in the Ganges. The trip to Kashi is expected to yield results only after completing this custom.

attractions.name: Kaal Bhairav Temple
attractions.description: It is the temple for Kaal Bhairav - a dreadful form of Lord Shiva symbolising death. It is a tradition to buy black threads (costs about ₹15 per 50 threads as of Sep 2009), keep it in the shrine and then wear it on the arm, wrist or around the neck as a protection against evil forces.

attractions.name: Nepali Hindu Temple
attractions.description: This small, golden temple was built by the 19th-century exiled king of Nepal, Rana Bahadur Shah. It is shaped in the typical Nepali pagoda architectural style.

attractions.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
attractions.description: The most famous temple in the city, dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas of Shaivism. The temple was destroyed multiple times by Mughal invaders and was reconstructed by Hindu kings who followed them. There are four gates to enter the temple. The main gate, called "Ganga Dwar", is accessible from the Manikarnika Ghat. There is a wide corridor leading to the main temple. Security is tight making entrance to the main temple difficult and sometimes completely off-limits to foreigners. Bags, mobile phones or pens are not allowed inside the main temple, although they are allowed within the corridor. You have to deposit them at the "mobile lockers" within the corridor area. If you enter the temple from other three gates, you have to deposit the prohibited items at the nearby shops.

attractions.name: Tulsi Manas Temple
attractions.description: Located near the very popular Durga temple, this marvellous temple is dedicated to lord Rama. Tulsi Manas temple was established during 1964 in the form of white marble structure.

attractions.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
attractions.description: Sankat Mochan Temple is dedicated to the Lord Hanuman. This temple is also called as the Monkey temple because of the presence of lot of monkeys inside the premises. It is one of the holy temples of the Lord Hanuman and the main location for Hindus for their many religious as well as cultural festivals. It is located in the southern part of Varanasi, on the way to the Durga Mandir and New Vishwanath temple BHU. The meaning of the Sankat Mochan is relief from all the problems (Sankat means problem and Mochan means relief giver). Sankat Mochan Temple was constructed by the educationist and freedom fighter Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya (the founder of the BHU) in the early 1900s. The Hanuman Jayanti (birthday of the Lord Hanuman) is celebrated every year by organising a special Shobha Yatra (a parade) from Durga temple (Durga Kund) to the Sankat Mochan Temple.
attractions.address: 27, Durgakund Rd, Jawahar Nagar Colony, Bhelupur

attractions.name: Siddharth Yoga Centre
attractions.description: Small-group yoga classes with a view of the Ganges. Taught by Siddharth.

attractions.name: Yoga Training Centre
attractions.description: Run by Sunil Jhingan Kumar. Highly recommended.

attractions.name: Punarnava Health
attractions.description: Classes and treatments in Ayurvedic food habits, daily routine, massage, Shirodhara, steam bath, leech therapy, and Panchkarma.

restaurants.name: Ganga View
restaurants.description: One of the myriad guest house rooftop restaurants in Varanasi and not a particularly memorable one at that. Serves Indian continental and western food (non-veg not available). Like most places in the area the rooftop is enclosed in a cage to keep the monkeys out (or is that humans in?) which detracts from the view.

restaurants.name: Nice cafe
restaurants.description: Great food cooked only by mum and family. Home kitchen. Clean. Friendly and helpful owner. Very reasonable prices, except on festival days when hot chocolate is poured over everyone for a fixed price of ₹1000 per person. Check out the garlic / cheese nan and the pancakes!

restaurants.name: Spicy Bites
restaurants.description: One of a number of restaurants along Bangali Tola, this place is great for breakfast as they have a full on espresso machine and serve good food. Free WiFi.

restaurants.name: Brown Bread Bakery
restaurants.description: A good bakery run by a German baker in Varanasi. Be wary of the Indian run bakery on the opposite side of the road who claims to be charitable but is just fake. Breads and pastries made from organically grown ingredients. Also a nice range of cheeses. The restaurant has a large menu including Continental, Italian, German and Indian classics, has a great rooftop and offers a breakfast buffet from 7AM to noon. Quality is pretty good and a part of the proceeds supports the Learn For Life society which operates a free school for disadvantaged children in Aurangabad, Varanasi.

restaurants.name: Dolphin Restaurant
restaurants.description: The food and service are good, not great, but the real reason to come here is for the rooftop overlooking the Ghats and the river. Also has free and fast WiFi.

restaurants.name: Filocafe
restaurants.description: A space to study, read, network, converse, experiment, think. Equipped with free Wi-Fi and electric outlets available to all, Filocafé offers a variety of over 45 types of teas, Italian espresso coffee (yes, coming out from those Italian machines) and its creative varieties, fresh juices and a few munchies.

restaurants.name: Madhur Milan Cafe
restaurants.description: A nice place for Indian snacks and meals at cheap prices. Cafe is primarily famous for its fried hot samosas, dosa and kachori sabji.

restaurants.name: Varuna
restaurants.description: And Chowk, Taj Ganges Hotel, Nadesar Palace Grounds. - Two restaurants respectively offering Indian and Western cuisine. The Taj is excellent as usual.

attractions.name: Jallianwala Bagh
attractions.description: The site of the 1919 Amritsar massacre, turned into a park memorial. On April 13 of that year, British Indian Army soldiers opened fire on an unarmed gathering of men, women and children. The firing lasted about 10 minutes and 1650 rounds were fired, killing 1579 people. A memorial was built on the site and inaugurated by the then-President of India, Rajendra Prasad, on 13 April 1961. The bullet holes can be seen on the walls and adjoining buildings. The well into which many people jumped and drowned attempting to save themselves from the hail of bullets is also a protected monument inside the park. The area near the entrance is only for pedestrians with shops and restaurants.

attractions.name: Gobindgarh Fort
attractions.description: A large 1760 fort that is being turned into a tourist spot with several museums and performances. The fort was built of bricks and lime by Gujjar Singh Bhangi and armed with 25 cannons. In the 19th century it was conquered and enhanced by Maharaja Ranjit Singh, then captured by the British and also used by the Indian army. After restoration it was opened in 2017 to the wide public in a form of something between a museum and amusement park. Among the attractions there is a central stage with live performances; several rooms showing Punjabi clothing, coins and warfare; multimedia shows such as Sher-e-Punjab, a camel ride and a few restaurants and shops.

attractions.name: Ram Bagh
attractions.description: This is a beautiful garden. A tribute to Guru Ram Das, the founder of the city. Famed as the summer palace of the Maharaja Ranjit Singh (Ranjit Singh Panorama?), it has now been converted into a museum which exhibits weapons from Mughal times to portraits of ruling houses of Punjab and the replica of "Kohinoor" diamond.

attractions.name: Maharaja Ranjith Singh Museum
attractions.address: Maharaja Ranjit Singh Bagh (Ram Bagh), Lawrence road

attractions.name: Statue of Netaji
attractions.description: Subhas Chandra Bose (Netaji) was an important leader in the Indian struggle for independence. He led the Indian National Army and formed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind in exile.

attractions.name: Summer Palace of Maharaja Ranjit Singh'
attractions.description: The palace houses a museum, exhibiting oil paintings, miniatures, coins and weapons from the Sikh period. In this park is the Maharaja Ranjit Singh Panorama, so ask, if you are at the right museum.
attractions.address: Maharaja Ranjit Singh Nagar, Hasanpura Chowk

attractions.name: Baba Atal Rai Tower
attractions.description: This is a great viewpoint over the city and the nearby Golden Temple. It is standing in another Gurdwara, namely the one of Baba Atal Rai Sahib Ji. Try the cimmunity kitchen of this Gurdwara if you are keen.
attractions.address: Bazar Chure Wala, Papraha Wala Bazar, Katra Ahluwalia

attractions.name: Tarn Taran Sahib
attractions.description: Mughal architectural style. There is a big holy tank and believed that its water has magical healing power. Amavas, or no moon day, is the most popular Feast, also Diwali, Baishakhi and the various Guru Parabs festivals held here.

attractions.name: Sarovar Ramsar Sahib
attractions.description: Gurudwara and pool.

attractions.name: Statue of General Sham Singh Attariwala and India Gate
Mata Temple
attractions.description: Highly recommended! This is a cave labyrinth Hindu temple devoted to the female saint Lal Devi. Traditionally, women wishing to become pregnant come here to pray. The roundabout path to the main temple passes through low tunnels, caves full of ankle-deep water, inclined walkways, and mirrored hallways that make the experience seem more like a fun house than a place of worship. The colours, wide variety of deities and elaborate mirrored image make this a psychedelically unique temple. This is called Sheesh Mahal, and some people also seem to call it "Lal Dev."

attractions.name: Durgiana Temple
attractions.description: The temple is enshrined with Goddess Durga. Daily rituals devoted to Durga Ma is performed in here. A dome and a tank are the prime possession of Durgiana Temple. Apart from Durga Devi, Durgiana Temple is also famous for Lord Krishna and Lord Vishnu. Believers whom devotees of these Goddess Lakshmi and Narayan also visit the shrine to gather the blessings.

attractions.name: Gurdwara Toot Sahib
attractions.description: Gurdwara Shib of Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.

attractions.name: Gurudwara Pipli Sahib
attractions.address: Guru Arjun Dev Nagar quarter, Merchant Rd.

attractions.name: Gurudwara Baba Budha Sahib
attractions.address: one block north from Sultanwind Rd.

attractions.name: Jama Masjid Khairuddin
attractions.description: It was built in 1976 by freedom fighter Mohammed Khairuddin. This is a mosque where Tootie-e-Hind, Shah Attaullah Bukhari protested against the British Rule.

attractions.name: Golden Temple Complex
attractions.description: This is the main attraction in the city, and the most important religious place to the Sikhs. It's a stunning complex, and always full of thousands of pilgrims from all over India, excited to be at a place that they usually only see on television. The excitement to be here is infectious, and many people will be more than happy to tell you all about their religion and customs, and show you around the temple. As you arrive near the complex, you will more likely than not be accosted by hawkers trying to sell you bandannas to cover your head, but there's also a big barrel of free ones to choose from at the every entrance. Head covering and removal of shoes is mandatory for everyone—free cloakrooms are available at all entrances.Besides walking around and enjoying the sight, have a meal and a chai at the free community kitchen southeast of the pool. It is also highly recommended to stay one or two nights in the temple itself—if you do not want to sleep next to the pool, there is a tourist d

attractions.name: Akal Takht
attractions.description: This is where the highest council of Sikhs sits and deliberates. At night, the Guru Granth Sahib is taken to the Akal Takht.

attractions.name: Amrit Sarovar
attractions.description: The giant pool of water that surrounds and reflects the Golden Temple. Sections (marked off by ropes) are set aside for (male) pilgrims wishing to bathe.

attractions.name: Central Sikh Museum
attractions.description: Devoted to large gallery of paintings, mostly showing the gruesome ways countless Sikhs have been martyred, and various items from the gurus.

attractions.name: Ghanta Ghar
attractions.description: This is the main entrance, sporting a distinctly Victorian clock-tower. Wash your feet in the water at the entrance in order to keep the temple clean.

attractions.name: Harmandir Sahib
attractions.description: This is the Golden Temple itself, floating above the Amrit Sarovar, housing the sacred Adi Granth scripture which is recited out loud during the day. This is the most crowded point, accessible by a bridge from the edge of the pool, and entry here is regulated by traditionally dressed Sikh guards. It's a 2-storey structure where Sikh saints are seated on each floor.

attractions.name: Kaulsar Sarovar
attractions.description: This is one of five sarovars in the city. This sarovar is in honor of Mata Kaulan, a Muslim woman, who was taken into care by the sixth Sikh Guru, Guru Hargobind on instructions of Mian Mir, a close friend of the Sikh Gurus and a pious and wise Muslim pir. All Sikhs are encouraged in their lives to do volunteer services at any gurdwara or in the greater society, and everyone you see working here is fulfilling that duty. It's likely possible that you can join in if you feel so inclined: you could enquire by asking the people outside peeling vegetables, or those washing dishes.

attractions.name: Langar Ghar
attractions.description: Free communal kitchen, where people of any colour, caste, creed or religion, can eat food (langar) sitting together. Also enjoy a free chai at the bottom level. In case you are keen for a picture of the Golden Temple from above (especially during sunset), follow the left staircase up further onto the roof and roam around a little. Also, people won't mind if you walk around in the place where the prepare the bread or wash the dishes.

attractions.name: Sarai Shri Guru Ramdass Ji
attractions.description: Built in 1931. Lodging place for pilgrims in 228 rooms, including 1 dorm with AC and fans for foreigners.

attractions.name: Guru Arjun Dev Niwas
attractions.description: Another lodging place for pilgrims.

attractions.name: Sri Guru Nanak Dev Niwas
attractions.description: This building houses sectarian offices of the different departments of SGPC and provide lodging facilities for pilgrims. Twenty rooms for pilgrims.

attractions.name: Guru Hargobind Niwas and Sri Guru Ramdas Library
attractions.description: Rooms for pilgrims.

attractions.name: Gurudwara Goindwal & Baoli Sahib
attractions.description: Located on western shore of Beas River, Northeast 30 km. It was the first centre of Sikhism, holds immense significance in reference to the Sikh pilgrimage sites. A popular pilgrimage destination for both Sikhs and Hindus. The entrance of place is well decorated with murals describing significant scenes of the Sikh history. The massive langar of the community kitchen provides food to a large number of visitors every day. Guru Amar Das Ji (the third Guru) established this place. There is a Baoli (well) with 84 steps leading down to it. The devout believe that by reciting Japji Sahib, the divine Word revealed to Guru Nanak Dev at each step after taking a bath in the Baoli.

attractions.name: Harike Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: The second largest bird sanctuary in India. Also a National Wetland & Wildlife Sanctuary. Hari-ke-Pattan is one of India's leading in-land sweet water fish market and home of varied wild life.

attractions.name: Pul Kanjari village
attractions.description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh had been staying here in a Baradari as and when he passed by with his troops. It has been declared as a World Heritage Site by the UNESCO. It is said that once when a young dancer was going to Maharaja's Baradari for a dance performance, her shoe slipped into the water channel. A bridge (pul) was especially constructed to take her shoe out and hence this place got its name. Here is also a temple, a mosque and a Gurudwara. Popular shopping place for locals.

attractions.name: Ram Tirth
attractions.description: Consecrated by the appearance of Devi Sita, Ram Tirth was the birth place of the sons of King Rama. Making a special place in the holy scripts of ancient religions, the place was once the ashrama of saint Balmiki. The saint is believed to have scripted many of his sacred manuscripts at this place. A hut of Rishi Balmiki is still found at Ram Tirth where he once lived. After giving birth to Luv and Kush, Devi Sita used to stay at this place for a considerable period of time. The evidence of her stay still exists in the form a well which, it is believed, was dug by Hanuman. Devotees of King Rama and Devi Sita flock to this place every year to offer their prayers to the respected deities. As the locational position of the Ram Tirth is facilitated by easy accessibility, hence, the visitors conveniently reach this place of worship without any extra hassles.

attractions.name: Amritsar Heritage Walk
attractions.description: Despite visiting Amritsar and Golden temple several times, visitors find Heritage Walk experience extremely enjoyable and informative.

attractions.name: Old City Shopping
attractions.description: As you move through narrow path of old city and some other heritage buildings, you can see stalls selling everything from jootis to roasted sweet potatoes.

restaurants.name: Golden Temple Community Kitchen
restaurants.description: A dining hall (langar) serving free basic meals to all. Plates and spoons are handed out near the entrance, then follow the crowds inside and take the next vacant spot in one of the rows on the floor. Servers come by with large buckets of dal, chapatis and rice. Make sure to finish everything on your plate (wasting food isn't an option here) then take it outside to volunteers at the washing area. It's inside the complex which means no shoes and cover your head. At the ground floor of the building, they are serving chai. At the exit, there is a donation box for the free meals.

restaurants.name: The Brothers or Bharavan the Dhaba
restaurants.description: Serves traditional food or Chinese, continental at affordable prices. However, the food and service drops during peak times like weekends.

restaurants.name: Bubby Dhaba
restaurants.description: serves authentic Punjabi food at a very reasonable cost. Just metres from the main entrance of the Holy Golden Temple

restaurants.name: Charming Chicken
restaurants.description: Established in 1958. Very popular family restaurant, particularly for butter chicken with naan. No alcohol is permitted.

restaurants.name: Kesar da Dhaba
restaurants.description: It offers good Punjabi food made in pure ghee. Daal Makhni is worth trying. Don't forget to try a glass of Lassi after a heavy meal.

restaurants.name: Moolchand Fish Shop
restaurants.description: This tiny place is the definition of hole-in-the wall. If it looks like it has been there for 50 years, it's because it has! They'll weigh out your fish based on how much you want to pay, fry it, put some delicious spices on it, and serve it with spicy green chutney and raw onions. A little hard to find, but worth it.
restaurants.address: Off of GT Road near Tourist Guesthouse.

restaurants.name: My Kind of Place
restaurants.description: Offers fast food such as pizza, burgers, and chips. It offers Chinese & Continental food also.

restaurants.name: Neelam's
restaurants.description: Offers pizza and other basics.

restaurants.name: New Punjabi Rasoi
restaurants.description: It's one of the most popular restaurants in town and serves up great Indian food including tasty masala dosas.

attractions.name: Kanaka Durga Temple
attractions.description: This temple is on a hill (Indrakeeladri) overlooking the city and the River Krishna. One can either motor up the ghat road or take the steps on foot. Inscriptions of different dynasties are found in the temple. During the Dasara Festival, thousands of devotees come from the city and its environs throng to the temple after a holy dip in the River Krishna.

attractions.name: Gandhi Hill
attractions.description: The first Gandhi Memorial with seven stupas in the country was constructed on this hill at a height of 500 ft (150 m). The 52 ft (16 m) stupa was unveiled on 6 October 1968 by Dr. Zakir Hussain, the President of India. Gandhi Memorial Library, a Sound and Light Show on Mahatma Gandhi's life and a planetarium are the other attractions. A toy train journey will be a memorable experience at that height on the hill.

attractions.name: Bhavani Island
attractions.description: Bhavani Island is on Krishna River close to the city. AP Tourism is converting this 133-acre (54-hectare) island into a tourist spot and a river-front resort. The island offers some cottages to stay in and some adventure and fun sports. The journey to the island by boat is very pleasant.

attractions.name: Prakasam Barrage
attractions.description: Built across the river Krishna connecting this city with Amaravati, Prakasam Barrage has created a panoramic lake. Its three canals that run through the city give Vijayawada a Venetian look.

attractions.name: Rajiv Gandhi Park
attractions.description: Created by the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation with great care, this park is at the entrance of the city and features an impressive horticultural network. It also has a mini zoo and a musical water fountain.

attractions.name: Akkanna Madanna Caves
attractions.description: A group of 7th-century rock-cut caves dedicated to Shiva.

attractions.name: Mogalrajapuram Caves
attractions.description: Said to have been excavated in the 5th century, these caves are reputed to be the first of their kind in South India. The idols of Lord Nataraja, Vinayaka and Ardhanareeswara are carved here.

attractions.name: Bapu Museum
attractions.description: A place for archaeology lovers, Victoria Museum has a carefully preserved collection of ancient sculptures, paintings, idols, weapons, cutlery, and inscriptions.

attractions.name: Krishnaveni Mandapam
attractions.description: This is in front of Prakasam Barrage. It was constructed by Vijayawada Industrialists & Fertilizers Association. It consists of 4 rooms depicting the story of Krishna River and also statue of Krishnaveni. Krishna River on the bank consists of Bridge Museum, just beside the bus stand. Some more places to visit nearby are Swathantra Samarayodhula Samsthanam which too is beside Pushkar Ghat.

attractions.name: Gunadala Matha Shrine
attractions.description: In 1925, Rf. Arlati, the Rector of St. Joseph's Orphanage at Gunadala, installed a statue of Our Lady. Later, a church was built and consecrated in 1971 and is known as St. Mary's church. Since then, the Feast of Our Lady of Lourdes has become an annual event, attended by hundreds of people. The church is situated on a hillock on the eastern side of the city.

attractions.name: Hazarat Bal Mosque
attractions.description: A holy relic of the Prophet Mohammed is kept here and displayed once a year. A large number of non-Muslims join the celebrations, too.

attractions.name: Hinkar Thirtha
attractions.description: Hinkar Thirtha is a Jain temple. It is stated to be the biggest Jain temple in the region.

attractions.name: Sri Nagarala Sri Maha Lakshmi Ammavaru Temple
attractions.description: This temple is in the area of Chiitinagar. During the Dasara Festival, thousands of devotees arrive from the city. It is maintained by the Nagaralu Community.

attractions.name: Subramanya Swamy Temple
attractions.description: This temple is on a hill (Indrakeeladri) overlooking the city as well as the River Krishna. One can take to the steps on foot. During Skanda Shashti Festival, thousands of devotees come from the city. Some even come from as far away as Tamil Nadu. This Temple is maintained by the Iddipilli Family.

restaurants.name: The Chocolate Room
restaurants.description: The Chocolate Room places an emphasis on a hip, modern atmosphere. Service can be slow, but this place is geared more towards those who are seeking a place to "chill" and be seen, not those who are on a lunch business meeting.

restaurants.name: Hotel Anjaneya Vilas
restaurants.description: This location serves authentic Andhra food in the Kaleswara Rao Market. There can be long lines but the food is often worth it. The thalis are priced around ₹30. Only vegetarian food is served.

restaurants.name: Minerva Coffee Shop
restaurants.description: The Minerva Coffee Shop offers purely vegetarian food.

restaurants.name: Seven Days Café
restaurants.description: There are three locations in Vijayawada: one on Prakasam Road (this one also goes by Sarada foods), not far from Karl Marx Road; one on Museum Road; and the other on Pinnamaneni Polyclinic Road, close to 6th Lane. Serves coffee, cake, and pizza.
restaurants.address: #60-9-1/a Pinnamaneni Poly Clinic Road Siddhartha Nagar, 6th Lane

restaurants.name: Silver Spoon Restaurant
restaurants.description: A multi-cuisine restaurant both affordable and very hygienic. A 4-course meal for 2 cost less than $10 or ₹400.

restaurants.name: Sweet Magic
restaurants.description: A candy and cake maker with attached restaurant. This is a decent place to purchase traditional Indian sweets. The staff can sometimes be a bit dismissive. The restaurant part is well decorated and clean. The food is nothing special but the quality is consistent.

restaurants.name: Tycoons Bar and Restaurant
restaurants.address: No. 40-8-19A, Near Dr. Ravi Hospital, Mogalarajpuram, Shanti Nagar, Labbipet

restaurants.name: Rusted Spoon
restaurants.description: This is more like a fine-dining restaurant. It is a multi-cuisine restaurant that specializes in fusion cuisines. The ambience is upscale and clean. Try their makhani pizza, bhatti ka murgh and nalli biryani.
restaurants.address: Jasti Venkata Ratnam St, Opposite Manor Food Plaza, Moghalrajpuram, Sidhartha Nagar, Labbipet

attractions.name: Aqua World
attractions.description: An aquarium, game parlour and food court are worth seeing and good values.

attractions.name: Pahari Mandir
attractions.description: It gives an excellent 360-degree view of the city. A must visit.

attractions.name: Tagore Hill
attractions.description: Tagore Hill is about 90 m (300 ft) above its base. The elder brother of Rabindranath Tagore, Jyotirindranath Tagore purchased the hillok Morabadi and built up an ashram after the suicide of his wife Kadambari Devi. You can get a panoramic view from the top of the hill, and a great part of Ranchi can be seen from this place.

attractions.name: Yogoda Satsanga Society of India- Ashram
attractions.description: Paramahansa Yogananda, the author of Autobiography of a Yogi, began his life's work here. The natural beauty and peaceful atmosphere offer refreshment to mind and spirit.

attractions.name: Ranchi Science Centre
attractions.description: The first science museum established in the state of Jharkhand. It houses several exhibits on astronomy, evolution and topics connected to the area such as coal mining.
attractions.address: Tagore Hill Road, Near, Temple Rd, Chiraundi, Morabadi

attractions.name: State Museum Hotwar
attractions.description: An arts and cultural heritage museum showcasing Jharkhand's rich history.

attractions.name: Tribal Research Institute and Museum
attractions.description: The museum is dedicated to the 32 tribal groups of Jharkhand and providing a platform to learn about many of the lesser known tribal cultures in the state.

attractions.name: Ranchi Lake
attractions.description: Excavated in 1842, it is centrally situated. The lake has boating facilities.

attractions.name: Rukka Dam
attractions.description: A big dam on the outskirts of the city. It offers an excellent ambiance for picnic and recreation.

attractions.name: Dhurva Dam
attractions.description: A reservoir on the outskirts of the city. An excellent place to enjoy a scenic sunset view.

attractions.name: Rock Garden
