restaurants.name: Shree Bikaner, Pure Veg Restaurant
restaurants.address: near Andaman Book centre, Goal Ghar, Junglighat

restaurants.name: Sea Food Delights
restaurants.description: At Seafood Delights we serve Indian - Continental - Tandoori - Chinese. Both Vegetarian and Non Vegetarian options are available.
restaurants.address: MA Rd, Phoenix Bay, Sri Vijaya Puram, Andaman and Nicobar Islands 744101

attractions.name: Naval Aviation Museum
attractions.description: This is a great place to see vintage aircraft like the Sealands, Doves, Alizes, Seahawks, Vampires and Hughes Helicopters, along with the relatively newer Sea Harriers and a Super Constellation.

attractions.name: Dodrupchen Monastery
attractions.description: A monastery in the Nyingma tradition, famous for its large chorten. When in residence, Dodrupchen Rinpoche receives devotees to offer blessings from around 20:00 to 21:30.

attractions.name: Do-drul Chorten
attractions.description: a Buddhist stupa complex constructed in 1945.

attractions.name: Enchey Monastery
attractions.description: A 200-year-old monastery in the Nyingma tradition of Tibetan Buddhism, located above Gangtok, just off the road to Lake Tsomgo.

attractions.name: Flower show
attractions.description: Near the White-Hall, flower show is at its best during the flowering season which is mid March to end of May in spring and October to mid December in autumn. The annual Cymbidium Orchid Show is from mid-March to mid-April.

attractions.name: Guru Lhakhang
attractions.description: A Nyingma monastery famous for its large Guru Rinpoche statue and 100,000 smaller statues. A larger version of the Guru Rinpoche statue was supposed to have been constructed in Tibet to protect it from invasion, but the authorities neglected to follow the advise of a high lama, and a smaller statue was built. HH Dalai Lama regretted this oversight, and to compensate had a number of statues built throughout the Himalayas. Those at Guru Lhakhang were created as a result of this command.

attractions.name: Kanchenjunga Tourist Complex
attractions.description: A combination hotel and family amusement park.

attractions.name: Lake Tsomgo
attractions.description: A popular and scenic lake around 40 km from Gangtok at an elevation of 3,780 m. Make sure to see Hanuman Tok and Ganesh Tok along the way, monasteries with views of Kangchenjunga.

attractions.name: Namgyal Institute of Tibetology
attractions.description: A museum and library dedicated to Tibetan culture, language and history. The foundation stone was laid by the 14th Dalai Lama in 1957 and the institute was inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1958. Photography is not permitted inside the museum.

attractions.name: Ranka Monastery
attractions.description: Ranka Monastery is newer and quieter but also very beautiful.

attractions.name: Mahatma Gandhi Marg
attractions.description: A pedestrian only avenue which forms the main shopping district. Near the main entrance of MG Marg is the tourist information office and a taxi stand, the final destination of many taxis from other parts of the city.

attractions.name: Rumtek Monastery
attractions.description: One of the most famous things to see near Gangtok.

attractions.name: Tsuklakhang Palace
attractions.description: The palatial monastery of Sikkim's former royal family.

attractions.name: Banjhakri Falls
attractions.description: This waterfall has an entrance fee of ₹30 for two people and parking fee of ₹20. The site is developed with pathways and bridges around streams leading up the waterfall, decorated with sculptures. The waterfalls are accessible and soft enough to swim in. There is also a restaurant and gift shop.

restaurants.name: Agarwal's
restaurants.description: Serves South Indian and North Indian snacks and sweets. Good place to have breakfast. There are two outlets, one on MG Marg and other on the way near the taxi stand. Dosas are not so good.

restaurants.name: House of Bamboo
restaurants.description: Tibetan and Indo-Chinese cuisine. The pork chilli, the momos and the tea momos are recommended.

restaurants.name: Potala
restaurants.description: This place has excellent Sikkimese and Tibetan food. You might find yourself to be the only tourist/ non-local at any time of the day. Good selection of thenthuk, thukpa, faley, momos, chowmein, meat dry fry, rice plates, etc offered with beef, pork or chicken. Vegetarians may have some difficulties. A big bottle of beer starts from ₹90. Definitely try their pork thenthuk and pork momos.
restaurants.address: 1st Floor, Sypraj Plaza, Opposite Denzong Cinema Hall, Lal Bazaar

restaurants.name: Porky's
restaurants.description: Amazing sizzlers and momos.

attractions.name: Bara Basti
attractions.description: Supposedly the second largest village in Asia. See the traditional Angami way of life.

attractions.name: Catholic Church on Aradhurah Hill
attractions.description: Located near the Little Flower School. This is the biggest church of its kind in the predominantly Christian north-eastern region of India. The view of the town from this church is outstanding.

attractions.name: The Deputy Commissioner's Bungalow
attractions.description: For over a month, Japanese troops battled British and Indian troops at this small bungalow in Kohima. The battle, known as the Battle of the Tennis Court, was the turning point in the fight against Japan and the bungalow still stands in this state capital. The Tennis Courts are now a part of the Kohima War Cemetery.

attractions.name: Nagaland State Museum
attractions.description: Though information is somewhat limited, the museum has nice displays and some rare Naga artifacts and archaeological finds; as of April 2019, there is a very interesting photo exhibition and models of traditional sports equipment. There are also a few statues and a tank turret outside.

attractions.name: Kohima War Cemetery
attractions.description: The cemetery is maintained by the Commonwealth Graves Commission for the Allied war dead. The cemetery lies on the slopes of Garrison Hill, in what was once the Deputy Commissioner's tennis court, which was the scene of intense fighting known as the "Battle of the Tennis Court".

attractions.name: Kohima Zoo
attractions.description: You can see the rare Tragopan bird, the state bird of Nagaland and the Mithun, the state animal.

attractions.name: Naga Bazaar
attractions.description: You can find nearly anything that is living and moving here on sale. Nagas have a wide-ranging cuisine encompassing the entire spectrum of living things.

attractions.name: Bhagvati Bundar
attractions.description: An old harbour, no longer in use as such but, instead, as a good white sand beach. A good beach with black sand is Mandvi Bundar.

attractions.name: Bhatyachi Khadi- Khadi
attractions.description: An area where river meets to sea. The village near this place is Bhatye, so known as Bhatyachi Khadi. The place is beautiful with a view of river & sea both. There is good casuarina cultivation on the sea shore. Also there is regional research centre for coconut & spices just near the casuarina plantation.

attractions.name: Ganapatipule
attractions.description: A clean seashore and Ganpati temple, about 30 km North from Ratnagiri. This temple is reconstructed in Rajasthani stones and look.

attractions.name: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak Smarak
attractions.description: The monument and the home of a man who set off the 'Swadeshi Movement' and spearheaded the fight against the British Raj

attractions.name: Patit Pawan Mandir
attractions.description: The temple built by Swatantryaveer Savarkar for patit class of people.

attractions.name: Ratnadurga Fort
attractions.description: A fort covered by sea on 3 sides, with a temple of Goddess Bhagwati inside.

attractions.name: Thibaw Palace
attractions.description: The last Burmese king Thibaw was imprisoned in this palace by the British, built in Pagoda style. The Government has given up part of this palace for a Polytechnic.

attractions.name: Agnigarh
attractions.description: This is the legendary hill where Banasura locked his daughter. The access to this place is quite interesting to reach the top of the hill one should take a circular staircase and is a good option for trekking. On your way to the top of the hillock, you will see lot of images relating to the legend behind the construction of the fort.

attractions.name: Bamuni Hills
attractions.description: The ruins of Bamuni hill is famous for its artistic beauty. The structural remains present here date back to the 9th and 10th century and attract historians and art lovers from all over the world.

attractions.name: Bhairabi Temple
attractions.description: The Goddess Bhairavi is worshipped here. The stones of the temple is adorned by intricate carvings and images that date back to 9th century. The backdrop of the temple is a view looking towards the Kolia Bhomora Setu (bridge) across the Brahmaputra River.

attractions.name: Mahabhairab Temple
attractions.description: This temple is believed to have been established by king Banasura with a Shiva lingam. It is thought to be from the 8th century. It was rebuilt with concrete and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is one of the most popular sites to visit in the city

attractions.name: Ketakeshwar Dewalay
attractions.description: It is reputed to have one of the largest Shivalingas in the world. This shrine is open to all visitors and there is a local committee which oversees the development of the area around the site. Legend has it that during a severe earthquake, in the past the lingam was uprooted from its base and deposited where it now stands.

attractions.name: Kolia Bhomora Setu
attractions.description: Kolia Bhomora Setu is a bridge connecting Nagaon with Tezpur. About two centuries ago, a massive stone inscription was made by the Ahom General Kalia Bhomora Phukan, who had initially planned to construct the bridge. In 1987, the bridge was constructed, 3.05 km long and dedicated to this great Ahom general.

attractions.name: Da Parbatia Gate
attractions.description: This is the ruins of a door frame from the Gupta-era which shows an exquisitely carved door. On either side of the door are carvings of the Goddesses Ganga and Yamuna, with garlands in their hands. The entire door frame is covered with elaborate carvings of flowers and foliage.

attractions.name: Padum Pukhuri
attractions.description: This park is the perfect place for the peace lovers. It has two bridges over its lakes taking you to the island between the lake. It also offers boating services. You can take some stunning photographs in here.

attractions.name: Chitralekha Udyan
attractions.description: It is a very picturesque park. It is named after Chitralekha, the artist in the Aniruddha-Usha love story. A replica of the famous Bhomoraguri inscription which recorded the ancient plans to build a bridge exists here. It is the largest park in the city. Many activities like bumper cars, paddle boating are available here. Other elements of attraction are a concrete map of India and a model of the jet-fighter MiG-21 of the Indian Air Force.

attractions.name: River rafting at Eco Camp
attractions.description: Angling and water rafting on the Kameng River is popular among tourists.

attractions.name: Koliabhomora Water and Recreation Park
attractions.description: A basic water park with other recreational activities.

attractions.name: Trip to Tawang
attractions.description: Hire a jeep at the bus terminal and take a trip to Northern Arunachal Pradesh. Tawang, Dirang and Sela Pass are the most popular destinations. A full tour takes about 3-4 days. Tourists with altitude sickness must consult with their doctors or reconsider their travel as these places are located at an altitude of 5,000-13,000 ft

attractions.name: Anwar Cinema Hall
attractions.description: A popular movie theatre with a cafeteria. All popular movies, mostly Hindi are screened here.

attractions.name: SVF Cinemas
attractions.description: One of the popular theatres. There are 2 screens and offers movies in 3D. Screens Hindi, Assamese and English movies.
attractions.address: G Square Mall, 5th Floor, Mahatma Gandhi Rd

attractions.name: Gold Digital Cinema
attractions.description: A reasonably priced movie theatre.

restaurants.name: Pizza Hut
restaurants.description: A quick stop for a Pizza bite.

restaurants.name: Spring Valley
restaurants.description: A chain of specialty restaurants in the city offering snacks and meals at an affordable price. It is the go to place for good quality snacks.

restaurants.name: Salt & Pepper
restaurants.description: A vegetarian restaurant serving full meals and snacks. Known for its availability of wide variety of Indian cuisine.

restaurants.name: Singpho Shat Gawk
restaurants.description: Serves authentic Singpho cuisine.

restaurants.name: Laziz Pizza
restaurants.description: A pizzeria with exotic combinations.

restaurants.name: Madhuban Sweets & Bakery
restaurants.description: A popular bakery store proving sweets and often snacks. Part of a chain of sweet stores around the city.

restaurants.name: Jyothi's Kitchen
restaurants.description: A 24X7 pure vegetarian restaurant offering Oriental, Continental and Indian delicacy for vegans.

restaurants.name: Heritage Tezpur
restaurants.description: A restaurant cum hotel offering Assamese and Indian cuisine. Tall visitors beware, the ceiling of this restaurant is a bit low.

restaurants.name: Hotel Susuma
restaurants.description: A popular meal serving restaurant at the Mission Chariali Highway Intersection

restaurants.name: Red Chilli Restaurant
restaurants.description: A decorated restaurant with good service.

restaurants.name: KFC
restaurants.description: Restaurant chain known for its buckets of fried chicken, plus wings & sides.

restaurants.name: Domino's Pizza
restaurants.description: A restaurant chain offering a wide range of pizzas & a variety of other dishes & sides.

attractions.name: Goa State Museum
attractions.description: Hindu and Jain sculptures, including bronzes, from the 4th to the 8th centuries. The Christian Art Gallery shows different sculptures from the Portuguese period. Also on display a printing press that was brought to Goa by the Portuguese in 1556 AD.

attractions.name: Goa Science Centre and Planetarium
attractions.description: At a scenic location along Miramar Beach, this is a great place for kids. There's also a movie theatre showing 3D science-related films..

attractions.name: Gallery Gitanjali
attractions.description: Run by Ajit Sukhija in a building that once was the People's High School at Panjim's Latin quarter of Fontainhas.

attractions.name: Casino Caravela
attractions.description: Casino Caravela, on board a yacht, offers a combination of sightseeing and gaming - American Roulette, Black Jack, Rummy, Stud Poker, Baccarat, Pontoon and Flash. ₹2000 (For entry and buffet.) Includes ₹1000 casino chips that cannot be cashed in.
attractions.address: Caravela Jetty, Opposite Mandovi Hotel, Fisheries Building, D B Mart, In the starting point for the cruise

attractions.name: INOX - Old GMC
attractions.description: Watch the latest Bollywood flicks at the INOX theatre at Panaji.
attractions.address: Old GMC Heritage Precinct, D.B. Road, Campal

attractions.name: Mandovi River Sunset cruise
attractions.description: Go for a short boat ride on one of the many "Cruise" boats, that sail up and down the river, with loud music, and frantically dancing revellers. Beside the Captain of Ports jetty on the Mandovi river at Panaji. The Santa Monica and Goa Boat Cruise is the oldest and best known of the lot, though the others are as good. Cruises start from around Sunset. There is also a floating restaurant, on the same pier.

attractions.name: Miramar Beach
attractions.description: Relax under a palm tree on Miramar beach, feel the sea breeze in your hair and watch the surf on the waves. Watch the many iron ore barges cruise lazily down the river towards the Arabian sea, in a typical "Socegad" Goan manner.

attractions.name: Dr. Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: On the western tip of the island of Chorao, along River Mandovi and can be easily accessed from Panaji. Take a bus, or drive down the causeway along the river Mandovi towards Old Goa. A little after the turn at Ribandar, take a ferry across the river to reach the Bird Sanctuary. The best time to spot birds is between October and March, when many species of migratory birds visit the sanctuary from as far as Siberia. Don't forget to bring along some mosquito repellent, as the marshy land and mangrove forests have a lot of mosquitoes

restaurants.name: Avanti Bar & Restaurant
restaurants.description: Serves excellent vindaloo, sausages and Goan fish curry and rice.

restaurants.name: Cafe Real Tea Room
restaurants.description: Serves excellent vegetarian snacks. Piping hot, Bhaaji pao (Curried vegetables with local Goan Bread), Crisp Hot Kandea Bojjea (batter fried Onions), Mirchi Bojjea (Batter fried Green Peppers that are not half as hot as you would have imagined) over a hot cup of tea shouldn't be missed.

restaurants.name: Fidalgo Hotel
restaurants.description: 6 restaurants serving different types of food (veg, non-veg, Goan, etc.) Prices are high by local standards, but inexpensive for foreigners. Food is of excellent quality and there is something to be found for everyone! Aloo-stuffed paratha recommended at the Legacy of Bombay restaurant.

restaurants.name: George
restaurants.description: Recommended for the Goan specialty of tongue roast.

restaurants.name: Godinho's and George Bar and Restaurant
restaurants.description: Serve authentic Vindaloo, Sorpatel, Cafreal and Goan Sea food dishes.

restaurants.name: Gujarat Lodge
restaurants.description: Excellent snacks and sweets. Busy in the evening when they have hot samosas (₹5/- each!) and other snacks. Also have great packaged snacks like chevda and banana chips to take home.

restaurants.name: Horse Shoe
restaurants.description: Portuguese Goan cuisine. If you are in need of some good western food, this is an excellent choice. Recommended!

restaurants.name: Kamats
restaurants.description: Serves good Goan vegetarian dishes. Famous for their vegetarian Thaali (a stainless steel tray with rice, puris, various types of daals and vegetables served in small steel bowls)

restaurants.name: Shanbag Cafe
restaurants.description: A clean, simple cafe serving South Indian food, Indian snacks and thalis. Prices are excellent and the food is very tasty. Veg thali highly recommended (₹25/-).

restaurants.name: Viva Panaji
restaurants.description: Tucked away in a small side street, Viva Panjim offers a variety of traditional Goan dishes at astonishingly good prices. The proprietor, Linda, makes the rounds to chat and make sure people are happy. The food is delicious, and authentic (read spicy).

attractions.name: Kathakali and Kalarippayattu performances
attractions.description: In this cultural centre you can see the local art of Kathakali, which is a drama showcasing thick face make up and face gestures. Also, there are Kalarippayattu performances, which is an ancient Martial Art that was used to train soldiers already before the Common Era started.
attractions.address: Thirumeni Cultural Centre in Temple Road

attractions.name: Atukkad Waterfalls
attractions.description: A scenic waterfall amidst hills and jungles.

attractions.name: Chithirapuram
attractions.description: Chithirapuram has old playgrounds and courts, bungalows and sleepy little cottages which all give this place an old world charm. This town is also famous for its tea plantations.

attractions.name: Pothamedu View Point
attractions.description: A small village 1 km away from headworks dam. Coffee and Cardamom plantation are sights to behold.

attractions.name: Floriculture Centre
attractions.description: Run by the Kerala Forest Development Corporation. A well-kept garden with a large variety of flowers and some herbal/ foliage plants, all against the backdrop of the tea plantations. Nice for taking pictures with pretty flowers.

attractions.name: Kundala Lake
attractions.description: This lake is very beautiful amidst lush jungles. Hiring a pedal boat and exploring the lake and its surroundings is an awesome experience. Except at the place you hired the boat, don't expect to find humans around the lake as it is surrounded by scenic jungles and hills. Unless you know how to row a boat, prefer a pedal boat, each trip lasts around 30 min and will be closed at 4:30PM

attractions.name: Mattupetty Dam
attractions.description: This popular picnic spot offers activities like boating and horse riding and is a great place to spend the day, especially if visiting with children. You could take the speed boat ride which is fantastic. It costs ₹300 if you have to hire a boat for you alone. The ride is for 15 min. The maximum capacity is 5 persons and you could save some money if you are a group of 4-5.

attractions.name: Mattupetty Indo-Swiss Farm
attractions.description: Once upon a time, Tamil migrant labourers reared cattle here. The cool climate and abundance of fodder made it the ideal location for the Indo-Swiss dairy farm. Established in 1961, the Kerala Livestock Development Board (KLDB) manages this highly specialised dairy farm. The dairy farm is a unique one of its kind with more than 100 varieties of high-yielding cattle being reared. Tourists are not allowed to enter the farm.

attractions.name: Munnar Echo Point
attractions.description: A small lake set amidst rolling hills. Every loud call made from a spot on the lake embankment is returned manifold by the echo from the surrounding hills. Young tourists throng to this place to listen to the echoes of their friendship calls.

attractions.name: Photo Point
attractions.description: It is a small place filled with woods and a small stream. Good location to take photos.

attractions.name: Top Station
attractions.description: Great views of the Western Ghats. Top station is the "top"-tourist attraction. This place gives a real 'above the clouds' experience. Regular buses go from Munnar (1h). A jeep costs ₹400. The area is known for the Neelakurunji plant, which flowers only once every 12 years. The flower is violet.

attractions.name: Anamudi Peak
attractions.description: The highest peak (2,695 m) south of the Himalayas, towers over the sanctuary in majestic pride. The slopes of the hills abound in all kinds of rare flora and fauna. The Atlas moth, the largest of its kind in the world, is a unique inhabitant of the park. Other rare species of fauna found here are the Nilgiri Langur, the lion-tailed macaque, leopards, tigers. An ideal place for trekking, facilities are provided here and tourists are allowed to go on foot up to 2 km from Anamudi. Going up to the peak is no longer permissible unless you have special permissions from forest department.

attractions.name: Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: Chinnar wildlife sanctuary is in the Western Ghats of Kerala. This wildlife sanctuary has a large number of plants and animals. This wildlife sanctuary is spread in around 90² km of area. This sanctuary is one of the protected areas in the western ghats because of the significance of its flora, geomorphologic features, ecology and local cultural.

attractions.name: Eravikulam (Rajamalai) National Park
attractions.description: See Nilgiri Thar (Hemitragas hylocres) - an endangered species of mountain goats, rolling grasslands and sholas, spread over 97² km in the Rajamalai hills, rare flora and fauna, Atlas moth (largest in the world), lion-tailed macaque, leopards, tigers, The Kurichi or Neelakurinji Flowers turn the hills of Rajamalai blue every 12 years. The next bloom will be in 2018. One can actually debate if going to the high peak just to see some goats is worth all the effort or not. However, the walk along the park is very romantic and has some breath taking view. Please be aware that this park remains closed every year around February–March due to the breeding program of the Nilgiri Thar. Before visiting Munnar please check if the park is open or not. Tickets can be bought from the counter or online. Please be warned that if you do not reach the counter before 8:30AM, the queue can get so long that it may take a couple of hours to get the tickets. The visit to the park is arranged by buses. While c

attractions.name: Lakkam Water Falls
attractions.description: (24 km from Munnar). A small waterfall.

attractions.name: KDHP Tea Museum
attractions.description: Tourists can see a collection of odd bits from the colonial era. A very enthusiastic 30-minute film is screened, and visitors are then taken around the factory to understand how tea is processed. If you are not a tea connoisseur you can skip visiting this museum.

attractions.name: Thattekkad Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: There are woodpeckers, Malabar gray hornbills, Ceylon frogmouths, parakeets, and rose-billed rollers. This sanctuary is located 20 km from Kothamangalam on the road between Ernakulam and Munnar. There are basic and mid-range hotels in Kothamangalam and an Inspection Bungalow in Boothathankettu. You can take a boat cruise from Boothathankettu to Thattekkad. Admission foreigners: ₹40, Indian ₹10.

attractions.name: Wild elephant spotting
attractions.description: Take one of the many tour operators (such as Great Think Adventures) in Munnar and share a jeep with 4-6 other people to go to the Elephant Salt Ponds in Anakkulam. The drive is 1,5 hours, and your waiting time is only limited by your patience. Usually, one or more elephants come to the pool in the stream to drink - because they like the salty flavour of the minerals in the ground. But there's no guarantee you will actually see an elephant. Tourists and elephants are separated by a big meadow and some concrete steps or steel cables, so that the animals can go about their business undisturbed. Little stalls serve chai, snacks and even food.

attractions.name: Bicycle
attractions.description: Experience the natural beauty of Munnar by riding a bicycle through beautiful paths of Munnar and pass through a tea state called Madupatty, around 14 km from Munnar.

attractions.name: Yoga @Kaivalyam Retreat
attractions.description: Holistic health retreat in midst of the tea valleys of Munnar. Open year round, they teach a holistic lifestyle with traditional form of yoga and organic dining.

attractions.name: Trekking in Mannavanchola Forest
attractions.description: Organized by Forest Checkpost at Perumala, two kilometers from Kanthalloor town (56 km from Munnar via Marayur). This forest is 7.5 km² in area and protects many tigers, leopards, elephants and bison.

restaurants.name: Silverspoon Restaurant
restaurants.description: This place does a great value buffet breakfast of cornflakes, toast, omelet plus Indian breakfast food for ₹95.

restaurants.name: CampNoel
restaurants.description: Multi cuisine restaurant at 2075 m (6,800 ft) above sea level and possibly the highest altitude restaurant in Kerala. If coming from Top station, turn right at 19 mile. Road is bad so make sure you have a suitably robust vehicle or inform them and they will pick you up. The journey is worth it. Please inform them early if you are going there for only for food.

restaurants.name: Sri velavan stores
restaurants.description: All provisions available at reasonable prices.

restaurants.name: Patel Gujarati Restaurant
restaurants.description: Gujarati and Marwari meals.

restaurants.name: Purohit Restaurant
restaurants.description: Bombay, Jain, Gujarati, Rajasthani, Punjabi and South Indian food. Good Gujarati, unlimited Thali at ₹85.
restaurants.address: Inside Hotel Dhanyasree, Dhanyasree Jn. Chilling Plant Rd

restaurants.name: Mahaveer Veg Restaurant
restaurants.description: Provides authentic North-Indian food with style ranging from Gujarati to Punjabi and delicious rotis. Meals start from ₹105/-. Only vegetarian food served. The downside to the place is cleanliness at the tables. Mahaveer has a branch near Purohit restaurant; this one is larger and cleaner.

restaurants.name: Kaivalyam Retreat
restaurants.description: Kaivalyam retreat has a 100% pure vegetarian restaurant which serves organic and healthy yogic food. As it is a yoga retreat more emphasis is given to food quality and hygiene. Serves North Indian, South Indian and a few continental dishes. Their desserts are good. Set in the midst of cardamom and pepper plantation.

restaurants.name: Tall Trees Restaurant
restaurants.description: It is famous for their fish fry.

attractions.name: Jaisalmer Fort
attractions.description: Also known as the “Sonar Quila” or "Sonal Kella" or "Sonar Kila" as pronounced differently in parts of India. Colourful shades of the setting sun and golden hues of the desert ambience give a fairy tale look to this mega structured fort. The interior of this fort is amazing. It is a 'working fort' meaning that unlike every other fort in India, there are people living and working within its walls. Tourists can also visit many 'havelis' or Grand Houses of rich merchants, which are also having a touch of great classical interior and design.

attractions.name: Gadisar Lake
attractions.description: This is a rainwater lake which supplies water to the city. It is surrounded by temples and tombs of saints. Boat rides are offered. Nearby is the desert cultural centre and a local museum built out of the collections of a local schoolteacher Mr N.K. Sharma. This centre conducts puppet show in the morning and evening. There are people who will try to sell you bread to feed the huge number of catfish in the lake.

attractions.name: Jaisalmer War Museum
attractions.description: A museum displaying India's modern military history. There is a hall dedicated to the noted Battle of Longewala fought near Jaisalmer during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.

attractions.name: Jaisalmer Folklore Museum
attractions.description: A museum showcasing Rajasthan's folk heritage, arts and customs. There are two nightly half-hour long traditional puppet shows, starting at 6:30PM and 7:30 respectively, which is the highlight in the museum.

attractions.name: Sam Sand Dunes
attractions.description: These sand dunes are around 50 km from Jaisalmer city but one has to go there to have this altogether different experience. This is an amazing sight and the sunset view from there is stunning. Also don't miss the camel ride or a camel cart ride over the semi desert. You can stay overnight in one of the tented lodges along the road. There are many to choose from - the lodges stretch for about 10 km.

attractions.name: Suryagarh
attractions.description: It's "only" a hotel, but you still wonder how they built it in the middle of the desert. Lush gardens, lovely pools and fountains, impressive stone carving techniques. While most cannot afford to stay there, stopping to have tea is an option that allows you to have a look at lesser cost.

attractions.name: Sunset point
attractions.description: Lovely cenotaphs. Fantastic pictures.

restaurants.name: Anchal Sweets
restaurants.description: Fresh kachori and samosa.

restaurants.name: Free Tibet Restaurant
restaurants.description: The restaurant has one of the highest rooftops in Jaisalmer. They serve a combination of Tibetan, Chinese, Indian and European cuisine. The thukpa is highly popular. It is more affordable than the other restaurants with good views of the fort.
restaurants.address: Fort Rd, Khejer Para, Manak Chowk, Amar Sagar Pol

restaurants.name: German Bakery
restaurants.description: Good lemon cake. Decent croissants. Almond cookies. Delicious tea. Great place to have a "western-style" breakfast.

restaurants.name: Lakeview Lounge Restaurant
restaurants.description: This restaurant serves excellent food. The Porridge w/ Banana Honey (₹40), Mushroom Cheese Tomato Burger (₹65) and the 'Speghatti Spinesh Tomato Cheese' (₹70) are highly recommended. The service is excellent as well because of the speed and courtesy of their staff. The restaurant has some of the best views in all of Jaisalmer, at the second level of the restaurant. They also have free WiFi at the restaurant and the attached Hotel Surja.

restaurants.name: Little Italy
restaurants.description: Real pizza, with actually good mozzarella cheese. Very decent pasta as well. Amazing view on the Fort from the terrace, fun low tables-and-cushions concept inside.

restaurants.name: Midtown restaurant
restaurants.description: This restaurant is in front of the Golden fort. The view is amazing and the food is fine with friendly service. The homemade Dutch apple pie is delicious. Pullavs are great.

restaurants.name: Seema Restaurant
restaurants.description: The unique thing about this restaurant is that everything is made fresh; however, it is a bit dingy.

restaurants.name: The Seven Spice Restaurant
restaurants.description: The seven spice restaurant give you a real taste of Indian spice with Indian cuisine or Tibetan food. located at heart of the city with nice market view. Best sunset location.

restaurants.name: Trio
restaurants.description: Nice food. Reasonable prices.

attractions.name: Bharat Mandir
attractions.description: One of the temples set up by 'Adiguru Shankaracharya' during the 12th century. This temple is a real tribute to Vishnu, the idol of which is carved from a sole piece of Saligram.

attractions.name: Chaurasi Kutia
attractions.description: Historic ashram where The Beatles stayed and composed music in 1968. Now maintained by the Forest Department, featuring graffiti art in the former meditation caves and cathedral-like lecture hall.
attractions.address: Swargashram area, within Rajaji Tiger Reserve

attractions.name: Gita Bhavan
attractions.description: Place of Guru Shri Ram Sukh Daasji (the great thinker of his time) and popular among the Hindu Brahmin community. Twice a year people gather at this ashram to read the Ramayana together.

attractions.name: Janki Setu
attractions.description: Modern 346-meter suspension bridge opened in late 2020 featuring dedicated two-wheeler and pedestrian lanes, easing congestion between Muni Ki Reti and Swargashram.
attractions.address: Between Muni Ki Reti and Swargashram

attractions.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Mela
attractions.description: One of the most sacred temples in Rishikesh. Located on hill over Swarg Ashram at a height of 1,675 m. A religious fair is held during July–August when many disciples from different corners of India visit.

attractions.name: Parmarth Niketan Ashram
attractions.description: One of the few ashrams left in India where children get the Vedas education. A must-visit in the evening for the Pooja/Aarti, at 5PM in winter and 6PM in summer.

attractions.name: Patna Waterfalls
attractions.description: Reaching Patna Waterfalls requires a little bit of trekking (600 metres), but you will find scenic spots at the top. There are a few tea stalls along the way.

attractions.name: Swarg Ashram
attractions.description: Swargashram (Heavenly Abode), as the name connotes, is a beautiful place situated in picturesque surroundings at the foot of Himalayas on the left bank of the Ganges between Rishikesh and Laxman Jhula. It is the spiritual “ground zero” of Rishikesh, filled with a concentration of ashrams and temples. The areas is known for its healthy and satwik living environment. It is this spot where from ages of yore the famous yogis and rishis have been doing the Tapasya. Numerous mentions of this spot occur in the holy scripture Puranas.
attractions.address: Shri 108 Baba kali Kamli Wale Swami Atam Prakash Ji

attractions.name: Trayambakeshwar Temple
attractions.description: It is 13 stories high, with different deities throughout.

attractions.name: Triveni Ghat
attractions.description: This is a bathing ghat. Every morning and evening, thousands of visitors bathe here and enjoy the Maha Aarti being performed. It is very soothing to sit on the banks of the river and enjoy the cool breeze from the river. Here the water is much cleaner than downstream.

attractions.name: Indian Palmistry Institute
attractions.description: Centre for learning palmistry and astrology.

attractions.name: Ganga Astrology Centre
attractions.description: Personal horoscopes and palm reading from Dr. Gaurav Agrawal and the astrologer B.P. Uniyal. The horoscopes can be made on a distance, using your place and date of birth.

attractions.name: Soma Reiki centre
attractions.description: Run by soma a local reiki master which is in Gita Ashram.

attractions.name: Maayaa International Healing School
attractions.description: Maayaa offers sound healing, reiki, chakra healing, numerology, Tarot reading, physic counselling, aromatherapy, Kundalini meditation, dowsing, chakra balancing. Also these residential courses: sound healing teacher training course, meditation teacher training course, aromatherapy course, chakra plus crystal intensive program and yoga & meditation retreats.
attractions.address: Near Dharam Raj Temple, Laxman Jhulla Road, Paurhi

attractions.name: Chakra Ayurvedic Wellness
attractions.description: Panchakarma, Ayurveda, Physiotherapy, Yoga & Ayurveda retreat.

attractions.name: Divine School of Ayurveda
attractions.description: Panchakarma, sound healing, astrology or Jyotishshastra, Ayurveda nutrition, yoga & Ayurveda retreat.
attractions.address: Laxman Jhula Road, Near Dharamraj Temple below Maestro Galleria, Pauri Garhwal

attractions.name: Bhuwan Chandra Music School & Store
attractions.description: Run by a sitar player Bhuwan Chandra. Travelers can learn and buy sitar, tabla, harmonium, mantra chanting, and improve vocal skills.
attractions.address: Ram Jhula, Swaargashram, near Ram Jhula Bridge

attractions.name: Mukeshji's Jungle Vibes
attractions.description: Make Australian didgeridoos, African djmbes and other musical instruments under the guidance of Mukeshji, while he regales you with his hilarious stories and takes you along with him in his Himalayan journeys.

attractions.name: Pankaj Music School
attractions.description: Extremely professional artist Pankaj teaches sitar, harmonium, tabla and bansuri in different styles in a slow-paced, yet intensive way.

attractions.name: Yoga and Music Festival
attractions.description: Free concerts of live classical Indian music and free yoga classes with local top yoga teachers.

restaurants.name: Ganga View Restaurant
restaurants.description: Probably the best cooks in town, these guys will serve you any food you like. Be prepared to wait 40-90 minutes as the place is extremely popular.

restaurants.name: German Bakery in Tapovan
restaurants.description: Don't miss their super-popular spinach pie. Come at 10AM to get a piece.

restaurants.name: Little Buddha
restaurants.description: One of the best known cafes in town. Here you can get delicious Nepali, Indian, European, and Thai food for under ₹100 per dish. Three storeys, nice Ganga view.

restaurants.name: Moon Dance Cafe
restaurants.description: Italian, Mexican American, Indian, Tibetan, Nepali, Israeli cuisine with all food prepared with fresh water. Great choice of delicious meals. Be prepared to wait for at least 40 minutes.

restaurants.name: Pundit G Ka Rajasthani Restaurant
restaurants.description: Has a very good variety of North Indian food.

restaurants.name: Red Night Restaurant
restaurants.description: Open air, river-facing restaurant and terrace

restaurants.name: Zorba Organic Restaurant & Cafe
restaurants.description: Serves Indian, Italian, Chinese, cafe-style, Tibetan and Israeli food. Vegetarian-friendly with vegan options, to eat in or take out. Outdoor seating with view of the Ganges. No smoking, child-friendly.

attractions.name: Arakkal Palace & Museum
attractions.description: Samples of pre-colonial art and architecture, Moplah Bay is nearby.

attractions.name: St. Angelo's Fort
attractions.description: Built in 1505 by the Portuguese. Very good garden and view to the sea. Short footpath into the sea near Malsyafed office.

attractions.name: Valapattanam
attractions.description: Riverside village.

attractions.name: Science Park
attractions.description: The science park is a small facility containing displays of scientific and technological topics meant for school students.

attractions.name: Azhikkal beach
attractions.description: 2-km long footpath into the sea, fishing village. Beautiful garden and beach at Chalil village. Spectacular beach at Meenkunnu.

attractions.name: Drive in Beach, Muzhappilangad
attractions.description: 4-km-long beach with strong sand, the longest drive-in-beach in India. The village has about 24,000 people (2011). Another beach is available at Edakkad.

attractions.name: Southern Beaches
attractions.description: Spectacular and private beaches are available at Thayyil, Kizhunna and Thottada. Adi-Kadalayi beach is a very peaceful place. Popular with European visitors. Locals are absent. Direct buses are available from State Bank area.

attractions.name: Payyambalam Beach
attractions.description: Very crowded place and popular with the locals. There is no esplanade, but there is a pretty little park. You can sit inside the park and watch the sunset. The park is less crowded because there is an entrance ticket. There is a very big statue of a sleeping woman made of grass inside the park. There is a perfectly formed cliff near the beach where you can walk and take photographs and this area is less crowded in spite of being more beautiful than the actual beach. The lighthouse museum has old types of lamps used by lighthouses around the world on display.

attractions.name: Muthappan Temple
attractions.description: A temple which is unique in the whole of India, where there is no idol to worship, rather a ritualistic art-form (Muttappan Theyam) to worship. The temple is built in concept of Eternal Unity and Universal worship, and does have many legends. The Muttappan is believed to be a form of Lord Shiva, in a non-Brahmincal form, thus making it a general mass figure. Here regular performances of Theyyam are considered sacred and many unique customs are followed. Free food for visitors.

attractions.name: Mohyidheen Juma Masjid, Ayikara
attractions.description: A 300 year old mosque built under the patronage of Arakkal Royal Dynasty

attractions.name: Birdwatching
attractions.description: At Munderi Bird Sanctuary, near Varam. Many exotic birds can be spotted at Madayippara near Pashayangadi, 24 km.

attractions.name: City Esplanade @ Caltex
attractions.description: Start walking from Caltex junction. Proceed to the collectorate and turn right to old bus stand. You will pass the police parade ground, exhibition ground and the oval stadium complex building. After the Stadium complex, you can turn left twice and walk in front of the policemen's houses and again turn left to reach Caltex junction. The total distance to walk is 5 km.

attractions.name: Climbing a Hill
attractions.description: You can start from Thazhe Chovva bus stop and go beyond Chovva Railway Station up the hill. There are paved roads all around the hill, up the hill and down the hill. If you don't like such a steep climb, you can also access the hill from Marakkar Kandy village on the beach side. Please note that the locals here do not know that trekking is a hobby. They might stare at strangers but never attempts to interfere. But they are very helpful if you approach them speaking English.

attractions.name: Hill Walk
attractions.description: The hills and grounds around Sri Narayana College, Thottada are an ideal place for peaceful walking because there is very little traffic and open spaces are more in this region. You can access Kizhunna beach and Ezhara beach from here. The famous Muzhappilangad drive-in beach is another 3 km from here.

attractions.name: Island Walk
attractions.description: All coconut and areca nut. Beautiful bridge wide enough for a small car. Two more islands called AKG Island and Polthuruthy are nearby.

attractions.name: Rajayoga Meditation @ Brahmakumaris
attractions.description: Meditation centre. Free Sattvic food, meditation practice and lecture sessions. Beautifully furnished meditation hall upstairs.

attractions.name: Ride in the local ferry
attractions.description: Frequent passenger ferries are available from Azhikkode to Parassinikkadavu, Mattool and Valapattanam.

attractions.name: Trekking @ Pythalmala
attractions.description: Naduvil village. 1,450 m above sea level. Limited facilities are available on the mountain track. Look for leeches and wild elephants.

attractions.name: Water Theme Park
attractions.description: Vismaya at Parassinikkadavu

attractions.name: Tejaswini River
attractions.description: White water rafting.

restaurants.name: Acquaris Vegetarian
restaurants.description: No parking facility.

restaurants.name: Bharath Vegetarian
restaurants.description: The best place for Masala Dosai, a fermented crepe made from rice batter, black lentils, potato and onions. ₹35

restaurants.name: Grass Hopper Vegetarian
restaurants.description: Paid parking facility.

restaurants.name: Golden Dish Restaurant
restaurants.description: With a peaceful attic section. No parking facility.

restaurants.name: India House Vegetarian
restaurants.description: No parking facility.

restaurants.name: Indian Coffee House
restaurants.description: No parking facility.

restaurants.name: Komalavilasam Vegetarian
restaurants.description: No parking facility.

restaurants.name: Omar's Inn
restaurants.description: Little cosy restaurant. No parking facility.
restaurants.address: North side of the Railway Station

restaurants.name: Thiruvathira Vegetarian
restaurants.description: Crowded eatery. No parking facility.

restaurants.name: Brownies Coffee shop
restaurants.description: Favourite hangout of couples.

restaurants.name: Dakshin Vegetarian
restaurants.description: Good dosai and idlis.

restaurants.name: Ranjith Restaurant
restaurants.description: Lunch ₹50, fish fry ₹60, Kada eggs ₹60.

attractions.name: Bihariji
attractions.description: The best-known temple in Vrindavan, home to a Krishna idol known as Thakur-ji. The idol's eyes are said to be so powerful that it is kept hidden from view behind a curtain, which is opened and closed every few minutes.

attractions.name: Jaigurudeo Temple
attractions.description: It resembles the Tajmahal, built with white marble. It is a unique temple in that you are prohibited from donating if you are a non-vegetarian.

attractions.name: Krishna Balaram Mandir
attractions.description: Better known as the ISKCON Temple. A major draw for Hare Krishna (ISKCON) pilgrims to India, and uniquely among Vrindavan's temples well equipped to deal with foreign visitors. Free breakfast and lunch are available. Great restaurant. Comfortable guesthouse on the Temple grounds.

attractions.name: Prem Mandir
attractions.description: The temple was constructed in 2012. There are fantastic light shows and designs. The light show closes at 7:30PM in the winter days, and at 8PM in the summer.

attractions.name: Radhavallabh Mandir
attractions.description: A very well-known ancient temple of Vrindavan, founded by Shri Hith Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Sri Radhavallabh Lal's idol resemble Sri Radha and Sri Krishna to be embodied in it together: "One soul and two bodies".

attractions.name: Rangji Mandir
attractions.description: The single largest temple in Vrindavan, built in 1851 in a South Indian style, complete with intricate seven-story gopuram (gateway) at the entrance. Inside is a 50-ft high wooden chariot, taken out yearly for festivals, and in the inner courtyard is the 50-ft high gold-plated pillar known as Dhwaja Stambha.

attractions.name: Nidhi Van
attractions.description: Krishna rested with His beloved Sri Radha. The shrine inside has a bed, which is decorated with flowers by the priest every evening. No one is allowed to stay inside after dusk because according to popular belief the Lord visits the spot with Sri Radha. The samadhi (memorial) of Svami Hari Das is also within this complex. All the groves of Vrindavan are notorious for monkeys that have a special fascination for cameras and spectacles. The Yamuna river flows through Vrindavan and Mathura. It is one of the most sacred rivers in India as it is so intimately connected with Krishna's pastimes.

restaurants.name: Bharati Foods
restaurants.description: This is the Most Genuine restaurant in Vrindavan, they serve North Indian, South Indian, Chinese foods and also Indian Sweet Dishes at reasonable prices. Seating facilities are good.
restaurants.address: Near Ramjibai Satsang Bhavan, Vidhyapeeth Chauraha

restaurants.name: Govindas Restaurant
restaurants.description: Excellent vegetarian food. Air conditioned. Serves Indian, Italian, Chinese, South Indian cuisines.
restaurants.address: On the backside of Krishna-Balaram Mandir

restaurants.name: MVT Restaurant
restaurants.description: Best place to get Western food that is cooked by Westerners. A lot of fresh organic salads, pasta, great pizza, lasagna and Baskin Robins ice cream.

restaurants.name: 56 Delight's Restaurant
restaurants.description: all-day dining: buffet, à la carte meals and regional specialties.

attractions.name: Ganga Lake
attractions.description: A green lake popular for its scenic beauty and a place for recreation and picknicking

attractions.name: Bhushi Dam
attractions.description: A waterfall near the dam is a popular spot between Lonavla and I.N.S. Shivaji. Buses running on the I.N.S. Shivaji Road stop here.

attractions.name: Celebrity Wax Museum
attractions.description: Another point in the town of Lonavla is the wax museum founded by Sunil Kandaloor, a 37-year-old wax artist from Kerala. Amitabh Bachchan, Shah Rukh Khan, Hariharan, Baba Saheb Ambedkar, Mother Teresa, Sai Baba, AR Rahman, Chhatrapati Shivaji, Charlie Chaplin, Kapil Dev, Mahatma Gandhi, Balaji Tambe and Yesudas are among some of the famous personalities in the wax museum in Lonavla.

attractions.name: Duke's Nose
attractions.description: Duke's Nose stands 12 km from Lonavla, clearly visible from the highway while driving towards Mumbai. This landmark in Khandala is popular with hikers. The cliff owes its name to the Duke of Wellington, whose ample nose it resembles.

attractions.name: I.N.S. Shivaji
attractions.description: A naval engineer training base.

attractions.name: Karla Caves
attractions.description: Karla, near Lonavla, is a complex of cave shrines built by Buddhist monks around 3rd to 2nd century BC.

attractions.name: Lonavla Lake
attractions.description: Lonavla Lake is surrounded by natural scenery, about 1.6 km from the town. The lake dries up during the winter months.

attractions.name: Rajmachi Point
attractions.description: Rajmachi Point is about 6½ km from Lonavla. It falls on the way from Mumbai to Lonavla, just before the starting point of the Ghat. This point commands a view of Shivaji's famous fort, Rajmachi (Royal terrakouioce) and the surrounding valley. Regular State Transport buses ply between Rajmachi Point and Lonavla from the State Transport Bus Stand. Further adding to the attraction of Rajmachi Point is Vaghjai Dari, located nearby.

attractions.name: Ryewood Park & Shivaji Udyan
attractions.description: Adding to the lush green surroundings of Lonavala are Ryewood Park and Shivaji Udyan. The stunning gardens are amongst the favourite picnic spots of the children, owing to the soaring trees and spacious open spaces provided by them. The swings set up at the parks further add to their appeal. An ancient Shiva Temple, situated inside one of the parks, is visited by a large number of people every day.

attractions.name: Shivlinga
attractions.description: On the way to Tiger's Leap, you would see a small board on the right: Shivlinga (swayambhu). From the road, it looks like just another place to view the deep valleys around Tiger's Leap, but it has some real breathtaking views including the mountain housing the "Shivlinga". Besides, due to the lack of popularity vis-à-vis Tiger's Leap and Bushy Dam, the place offers a quiet and serene view of the Sahyadris. Like most places, there is a small shop to relish hot bhajiyas (an Indian Fried snack) and Cutting Chai. Tea costs about ₹10 per cup while the snacks would cost ₹30-40 per plate. There is a tendency, however, to extract more money from unaware foreign tourists.

attractions.name: Shooting Point
attractions.description: Another scenic point in the town of Khandala (Bazaar peth), which provides magnificent view of the Rajmachi Fort and the valley. Also the home for the St. Mary's villa.

attractions.name: Lion's Point
attractions.description: Scenic point midway between Bhushi Dam and Amby Valley.

attractions.name: Tiger's Leap
attractions.description: Tiger's Leap is a cliff-top with a sheer drop of over 650 m, giving an extensive view. Just around tiger's leap, there is a small waterfall active only during the monsoon. It serves the purpose of relaxing in the water better than Bushy dam, as the force of the fall is higher. Also, after the brief steep descent, the fall becomes a stream with a fair amount of force to go all the way down to the base of the Tiger's Leap. Adventurers can trek down the stream whilst intermittently stepping back on land where the water current is too strong and the fall is steep.

attractions.name: Tungarli Lake and Dam
attractions.description: Tungarli Lake makes a very popular picnic spot for the residents of Lonavla, Khandala and the neighbouring cities. Apart from being a splendid creation of nature, this lake is also a very important source of water for the people of the hill station. This lake and dam come to life during the Monsoon season, where youth climb the mountain top to the dam. This dam was built during the British era and features a serene surrounding.

attractions.name: Valvan Dam
attractions.description: Valvan Dam has a garden at its foot, and is a popular evening spot 2 km from the town. The dam supplies water to the Khopoli power station at the foothills of the Sahyadris for generating electricity. The Kundali River feeds into the dam's reservoir.

attractions.name: Kune Falls
attractions.description: A three-tiered waterfall with a total height of .

restaurants.name: Buvachi Misal
restaurants.description: Serves a wide variety of authentic Mumbai street food. Many kinds of misal pav (moth bean curry with Indian bread rolls) and bhajjis.

attractions.name: Elaveezha Poonchira
attractions.description: A hill station with large hills around high. Beautiful hillocks named Mankunnu, Kudayathoormala, Thonippara and Poonchira are here. A pool here is remembered in local folklore as a bathing place used by Panchali, the legendary heroine of the Mahabharata.

attractions.name: Erumely
attractions.description: Important pilgrimage centre for Hindus and Muslims.

attractions.name: Ettumanoor
attractions.description: Famous for having an ancient Shiva temple. Wall paintings in the temple are thousands of years old. The temple is also famous for its seven and a half golden elephants, a sequence of seven large and one small statues of elephants.

attractions.name: Kumarakom
attractions.description: The place is famous for its bird sanctuary, house boats, backwaters, canals and the bungalow of Henry Baker (now run as part of a resort managed by the Taj group of hotels).

attractions.name: Manarcaud
attractions.description: St. Mary's Shrine here attracts people of all faiths. Various kinds of offerings are made here devotees.

attractions.name: Pathiramanal Island
attractions.description: This is a small white sand island. It gets its name from the brilliant reflection of moonlight from the sand.

attractions.name: Poonjar Palace
attractions.description: The Palace of Poonjar Royal family, one of major principalities of Travancore Kingdom, was home of one of Kerala's famous prince, Prince G.V. Raja. This building is famous for its collection of antiques, exquisite furniture, chandeliers, palm leaf engravings, jewel boxes, a variety of lamps, sculptures of Nataraja (Shiva as Lord of the Dance), grain measures, statues and weapons.

attractions.name: St. Mary's Church
attractions.description: Belonging to the Malankara Orthodox Church was built in 1579 by the Raja of Thekkumkur for his Christian subjects. The interior murals, painted using vegetable dyes, depict Biblical themes.

attractions.name: St.Mary's Forane Church
attractions.description: One of the oldest churches of Kerala is the St Mary’s Church Kuravilingadu, which was supposed to have been established in 105 AD. It is believed that Mother Mary's first appearance in the world, was in Kuravilingadu. Our Lady appeared to a few children at Kuravilingadu, who were tending their flock in the bushes. Mary asked them to build a church at the place from where a miraculous perpetual spring sprouted, a spring which exists even today. The children reported this matter to the elders and a church was built there. The statue of the Blessed Virgin Mary kept at the side altar is unique. It is carved from granite and it is believed that it was brought from North India. This is a miraculous statue and the devotees call this statue "Kuravilingadu Muthiyamma". The granite cross in a single block of 48 feet in front of the church was erected around 1597. The devotees offer coconut oil in the lamps at the foot of the cross. On first Fridays devotees stand in a queue from early morning to

attractions.name: Thazhathangady Juma Masjid
attractions.description: One of the oldest mosques in India and is more than 1000 years old. The mosque is famous for its richness of architecture, wood carvings and the beauty. This mosque is situated on the banks of the Meenachil river. Thazhathangady Juma Masjid is also called as the “Taj Juma Masjid”. The ancestors of this Masjid came and settled in Kottayam, from different parts of Kerala. The Muslims who lived here played an active role in Freedom Struggle and other National Movements.

attractions.name: Thirunakkara Mahadeva Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple built in the Kerala style of temple architecture, and with interior murals depicting themes from the Hindu epics. It was built at the beginning of 16th century by the then Raja of Thekkumkur. The annual temple festival that culminates in a ceremony called the Aaraattu, attracts large number of devotees.

attractions.name: Vaikom Temple
attractions.description: Famous for its Shiva Temple.

attractions.name: Vembanad Lake
attractions.description: 83.72 km length and 14.48 km width. Cruise boats, house boats and traditional cargo boats.

attractions.name: Wagamon
attractions.description: Enchanting hill station at an elevation of 1100 m, with tea gardens and meadows.

attractions.name: Puthupally
attractions.description: Puthuppally St. George Church is one of the oldest and renowned churches of Malankara Orthodox Church. The patron saint of this parish is St. George. It's by the side of coconut palms and a wide stretch of paddy fields, at a beautiful and serene village called Puthuppally which is about 8 km from Kottayam Town. This church is the refuge of thousands of people all over the world who seek the intercession of St.George. It is believed that this church was established as a shrine of Changanacherry Pally which in turn was a shrine of Niranam pally, one of the "Ezhara Pallis" consecrated by St.Thomas Theapostle of India.

attractions.name: Public Water Transport Kottayam to Alappuzha
attractions.description: Kottayam to Alappuzha. 6.35 am , 11.30 am, 1.00 pm and 3.30 and 5.15 pm.

attractions.name: Annual Food Festival
attractions.description: Kottayam also has an annual food and flower show. These events are quite popular and are worth a visit, if you are in town when it happens.

attractions.name: Boat Races
attractions.description: Lots of boat races with traditional boats of different sizes - around 50 types - in the months of July, August and September during Onam.

attractions.name: Nalumanikkattu Paddy Fields
attractions.description: Local food, children's park and hiking options, very green surroundings.
attractions.address: 10 km on Manarcaud to Ettumanoor Road

attractions.name: Panchalimedu Hills
attractions.description: Trekking facility in snowy mountains above sea level, organized by Peruvanthanam village council. You can see the Alappuzha sea on clear days. Famous Panchaly Pond with legendary associations with the Indian epic Mahabharatha. According to the myths, Pandavas along with their spouse Panchali had a sojourn there at time of one-year exile. The place can be also accessed from Murinjapuzha (5 km) and Amalagiri (6 km) on the Kottayam - Kumily state highway (K.K road).

attractions.name: Ram Mandir
attractions.description: The colossal temple in Ayodhya, built on the supposed birthplace of Rama. Although visited by pilgrims throughout the year, this sacred place attracts devotees from all over India and abroad on Ram Navami, the day of Lord's birth, which is celebrated with great pomp and show, in the Hindu month of Chaitra (March-April).

attractions.name: Bahu Begum ka Maqbara
attractions.description: Tomb and still one of the highest buildings in Faizabad.

attractions.name: Gulab Bari
attractions.description: Gulab Bari translates to "garden of roses" and this tomb of the 16th century ruler of the Kingdom of Oudh, Shuja-ud-Daula, has both a magnificent mausoleum and a rose garden.

attractions.name: Lakshman Ghat
attractions.description: This is where Rama's brother Lakshmana is said to have voluntarily given up his life-an act called samadhi. Another version says that he gave up living after he broke a vow.

attractions.name: Mani Parbat
attractions.description: A former Buddhist vihara (cave with cells) that became a Hindu temple. It is dotted with little shrines and if you stand on the topmost terrace you get a splendid view of Ayodhya, one that includes a cluster of small white buildings at the base of the hill that turns out to be a Muslim graveyard.

attractions.name: Memorial of Heo Hwang-ok
attractions.description: The legendary Korean queen Heo Hwang-ok, also known as Suriratna, is believed according to the Samguk yusa to have been an Indian princess from Ayuta, nowadays identified with Ayodhya. A memorial to honour was set up in 2001 which was expanded and beautified in 2018.

attractions.name: Ram ki Paidi
attractions.description: A series of ghats on the bank of the Sarayu River. It is known for the Ayodhya Deepotsav during Diwali.

attractions.name: Swarg Dwar
attractions.description: According to mythology, Lord Rama is said to have transformed himself into Lord Mahavishnu and left for Vaikunth.

attractions.name: Choti Chawni
attractions.description: A very big temple made by 100% white marble.

attractions.name: Hanuman Garhi Temple
attractions.description: Visitors to Ayodhya must make a move towards Hanuman Garhi. It is a massive structure in the shape of a four-sided fort with circular bastions at each corner. The temple is highly revered for its imposing architecture and its religious value.

attractions.name: Kanak Bhawan
attractions.description: The Bhawan is frequented by scores of visitors every year. The temple is widely known for the images of Sri Rama and Sita wearing gold crowns and because of this the Bhawan is also referred to as Sone-ka-Ghar.

attractions.name: Nageshwarnath Temple
attractions.description: It is said to be built by Kush, Lord Rama's son. Legend has it that he almost destroyed the water-living Nagas (semi-divine snake people) because he suspected them of stealing his amulet. Only Lord Shiva's intervention saved the semi-divine snakes. Khush then established this temple showing the Nagas worshipping Lord Shiva, his father's favourite deity. Another version of this legend states that the lost amulet was found by a Nag-kanya (young girl from the Naga tribe), who fell in love with him, and as she was Lord Shiva's devotee he constructed this temple for her.

attractions.name: Treta ke Thakur
attractions.description: It is a temple that stands at the place where Rama is said to have performed the Ashwamedha Yagna. The Raja of Kulu is said to have built a new temple here about 300 years ago called Kaleram ka Mandir, where the idols of Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshman and Bharat have reportedly been carved out of a single block of black sandstone. These idols are supposed to be from the original Rama temple, which once stood on the banks of the River Sarayu.

attractions.name: Vijayraghaw temple
attractions.description: It is one of the best temple in Ayodhya, build in 2008. In this temple god Ram presented in 12 faces called Viswa-virat(world's big). This temple made by red marbles and stainless steel.

attractions.name: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar International Sports Stadium
attractions.description: A multi-purpose stadium with a capacity of 30,000.

attractions.name: Chaturdashkoshi Parikrama
attractions.description: Constitutes a circular journey of 28 miles made once a year on the occasion of Akshainaumi, which is completed within 24 hours.

attractions.name: Ram Lila
attractions.description: The enactment of the story of Lord Rama is believed to have been started by great Saint Tulsidas. The Ramcharitmanas, written by him till today forms the basis of Ram Lila performances. In some places, Rama Lila is associated with Vijayadashmi celebrations in late September and early October and also with Rama Navami, the birthday of Lord Rama. Ram lila, basically an enactment of a myth, is presented as a cycle-play with the story varying from 7 to 31 days. The Rama Lila performance evokes a festive atmosphere and enables observance of religious rites. It is also rich in performance of crafts such as costume jewellery, masks, headgear, make-up and decoration. The four main Ram Lila styles are the pantomimic style with a predominance of jhankis based style with multi-local staging; the operative style which draws its musical elements from the folk operas of the region and the stage, Ram Lila of the professional troupes called mandalis. Ayodhya is popular for mandali Ram Lila. The perfor

attractions.name: Ram Navmi Mela
attractions.description: Ayodhya, the holy city of the sacred pilgrim centre of Hindus plays host to the Ram Navmi Festival in the month of April. Thousands of worshippers gather to venerate the Lord at Kanak Bhawan.

attractions.name: Sravan Jhula Mela
attractions.description: This mela celebrates the playful spirit of the deities. On the third day of the second half of Shravan, images of the deities (specially of Rama, Lakshman and Sita) are placed in swings in the temples. They are also taken to Mani Parvat, where the idols are made to swing from the branches of the trees. Later the deities are brought back to temples. The mela lasts till the end of the month of Shravan.

attractions.name: Parikramas
attractions.description: Ayodhya is perhaps the most noted place in the northern India where parikramas are undertaken by Hindu Pilgrims. These are circumambulations of important religious places and are of varying duration, shortest being the `Antargrahi Parikrama’ which has to be completed within a day. After taking a dip in the Saryu, the devotee commences the parikarma from the Nageshwarnath temple and passes through Rama Ghat, Sita Kund, Manipuravata and Brahma Kund, finally terminating at Kanak Bhawan. Then there is the `Panchkoshi Parikrama’ circuit of 10 miles, which touches Chakratirtha, Nayaghat, Ramghat, Saryubagh, Holkar-ka-pura, Dashrathkund, Jogiana, Ranopali, Jalpa Nala and Mahtabagh. On the way the people pay homage to deities in the shrines which are situated on the route.

restaurants.name: Gokul Restaurant
restaurants.description: An open air restaurant, serving vegetarian, non-vegetarian and continental food.

restaurants.name: Mezaban Restaurant
restaurants.description: Good meals and accommodation

restaurants.name: Trimurti Restaurant
restaurants.description: The best place serving vegetarian, non-vegetarian‚ Indian Cuisines and continental food in Faizabad.

attractions.name: Sri Ramanathaswamy Temple
attractions.description: Renowned for its magnificent prakaras or corridors with massive sculptured pillars on either side. The longest corridor in the world is here, 197 m (646 ft) long and 133 m (436 ft) wide. The temple has a gopuram 38.4 m (126 ft) tall. Different rulers built the temple as it stands today, at different periods from the 12th century CE. There are many guides who will attack as soon as you enter the temple premises; negotiate the deal of how much to pay them if you need their services. The history of the temple is linked with the Ramayana and it is believed that the deity was installed by Lord Rama after the war with Ravana at the instance of the great saints to get rid of the "Brahma Dosham".

attractions.name: House of Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
attractions.description: The house of former President Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam is an interesting place to visit. His residence has been converted into a museum that stocks his childhood memoirs. The place is ideal to get a glimpse into the extraordinary life of this simple man, right from childhood to his research days. Several pictures and awards of Dr Kalam are kept on display in this two-storey building, which is maintained by his elder brother. Moreover, a section of the house has been turned into a store that sells a variety of merchandise.

attractions.name: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Memorial
attractions.description: A very beautiful and grand building. It was inaugurated on the second death anniversary of Dr Kalam. A symbol of national integration, the memorial is an amalgamation of Mughal and Indian architectures. A must-visit.

attractions.name: Badrakaliamman Temple
attractions.description: A temple for Devi Durga.

attractions.name: The Five-faced Hanuman Temple
attractions.description: the deity of Hanuman drawn withsenthooram. Idols of Lord Rama, Sita and Hanuman brought from Dhanushkodi during the 1964 cyclone were placed here. The floating stone, used to build the SethuBandanamor, the bridge between India and Lanka, can be found in this temple.

attractions.name: Gandamadana Parvatham
attractions.description: is a hillock situated 3 km away and is the highest point on the island. Here one can see the imprint of Lord Rama’s feet on a chakra. The entire island of Rameswaram is visible from this point. thumb|Gandamadana Parvatham Panorama

attractions.name: Jada Theertham
attractions.description: legend has it that Lord Rama, on his way back after killing Ravana, Worshipped SriRamalinga (believed to be installed by him). Before doing so, he washed his hair in this theertham to purify himself.

attractions.name: Nambu Nayagiamman Temple
attractions.description: Greatly venerated by the people of Ramnad District.

attractions.name: Satchi Hanuman Temple
attractions.description: A very small roadside temple. It is considered to be the place where Hanuman delivered the good news of finding Sita to Rama with satchi or evidence, Choodamani or the jewel that belonged to Sita

attractions.name: Villoondi Theertham
attractions.description: It is found inside the sea like a well where freshwater is available.

attractions.name: Glass boat ride at Pamban Bridge
attractions.description: There is one glass boat at the government boating centre on the other end of the bridge. That boat too is not in order, as water has entered between the two layers of glass through which you are supposed to see the corals. The boatman will tell you that the glass is not in order only when you reach the point where you are supposed to see the corals. The water is shallow there, but you won't be able to see the corals with the glass in that condition. As such, it is an utter waste of money till the government officials fix the boat. Before boarding that single boat, check the glass and ask the boatman if it is in proper condition. (April 2012) One can enjoy the wonderful glass boat ride near Pamban Bridge to see coral reefs in the Sea. The boat has a glass bottom which enables you to see corals through it. To reach this place, you need to catch a local bus from Rameswaram bus stand to Pamban bridge. From there you have to take an auto to the boat centre (₹40-50) (minimum ₹400 per boat of

restaurants.name: Gujarat Bhavan
restaurants.description: Excellent homely meals, but be prepared for a long wait time. When you exit the temple from the East gate and walk straight, around 200 metres towards the seashore you will find this place on the right-hand side.

restaurants.name: Ram Nivas
restaurants.description: They specialise in Indian Chinese food. Service is a little slow but the food is worth the wait. To get there, turn right at the temple when coming from the Bus Stand and walk about 50 metres.

attractions.name: Varkala beach
attractions.description: Varkala beach is as beautiful as, if not more beautiful than Kovalam beach. Laterite cliffs drop sharply into the sea, with a small strip of sandy beach at the base. The beach is less frequented by the tourist crowd and is an ideal location if you want a quiet getaway.

restaurants.name: Eden Restaurant
restaurants.description: In the front garden of Mohan's Inn on the helipad. European owned and managed with European cook. Continental menu.

restaurants.name: Respiro Healthy Food
restaurants.description: International restaurant, Indian and Italian food, Chef from Nepal and chef from Italy. Tasty food in an artistic, colourful, ambient environment.

restaurants.name: Chill out lounge
restaurants.description: a chilled out atmosphere for food, drinks and music.

restaurants.name: Cafe del mar
restaurants.description: Famous for their grills and steaks.

attractions.name: Lepcha Museum
attractions.description: A museum with a small collection of belongings of the native Lepcha tribe.

attractions.name: Mangal Dham
attractions.description: A tribute to Guru Mangaldasji, whose samadhi lies in the ground floor of the dham.

attractions.name: Lepcha Bong Gumpa
attractions.description: Contains a museum.

attractions.name: Buddha Pada
attractions.description: An institute built in the Japanese minimalist style. Conducts workshops and classes in meditation, classical Indian dance, cinema, and other wisdom-based art forms. Accommodation available. Cafe and dining hall.

attractions.name: Triveni Camping
attractions.description: A confluence of two rivers, the river Rangeet with its deep green and crystal clear water, meets with the forceful mountain stream Teesta at a point called Teesta Triveni.

attractions.name: Bimbisara's jail
attractions.description: This archeological site is believed to be the jail in which King Ajatshatru imprisoned his father Bimbisara. From his prison cell, Bimbisara could see Buddha meditating on the Vulture Peak (Gridhakuta).

attractions.name: Chariot Tracks
attractions.description: The Chariot Route and shell inscriptions consist of two parallel furrows cut deep into the rock ground for about thirty feet and are believed to have been made by Lord Krishna's Chariot. Several undeciphered shell inscriptions are engraved in the rock around the chariot marks.

attractions.name: Cyclopean walls
attractions.description: Believed to be 2500 years old, these Cyclopean walls are a 40 km long and 4 metres wide fortification running around the city.

attractions.name: Gridhakuta
attractions.description: The place is atop a small hill and believed to be a meditating place of Buddha. You can continue on to the top of Ratnagiri hill, there is a Viswa Shanti Stupa (Peace Stupa) built by the Buddhist school Myohosan of Japan. One can reach the stupa by using the ropeway or the flight of more than 600 stone steps leading to the top of the hill.

attractions.name: Makhdum Kund
attractions.description: This is the shrine of a Muslim Sufi Saint Makhdum Shah and has warm springs similar to Tapodharma.

attractions.name: Maniar Matth
attractions.description: Dating 1st century CE, the Maniar Matth is said to be a monastery of a cult which worshipped snakes. Several snake and cobra figurins have been found in the vicinity in excavations.

attractions.name: Rajgir Heritage Museum
attractions.description: It has 49 rare items of archaeological and sculpture finds. It also has a collection of antiques along with several Buddhist and Hindu stone sculptures, bronze images of the Gupta and Pala period and terracottas.

attractions.name: Saptaparni Caves
attractions.description: These caves hosted the First Buddhist Council and were used by early Buddhist monks as resting places as well as centers of debates.

attractions.name: Sonabhandar
attractions.description: This ancient structure is said to be the treasury of Magadha.

attractions.name: Tapodharma/Lakshmi Narayan Mandir
attractions.description: Tapodharma was the site of an ancient Buddhist monastery over which a Hindu temple is built today. The place has hot water springs which are rich in sulfur and said to have a curative effects.

attractions.name: Venuvana
attractions.description: It is said to be a bamboo grove gifted to Lord Buddha by Bhimbisara, the then king of Magadha.

attractions.name: Hot springs
attractions.description: Take a deep bath in a hot spring (Kund).

attractions.name: Ropeway
attractions.description: Enjoy the ride on the ropeway.

attractions.name: Dwarkadhish Temple
attractions.description: The over 2000-year-old, 5-storied Hindu temple is the main sight of the holy town. The temple is dedicated to the god Krishna, who is also believed to have been King of Dwarka for 100 years.

attractions.name: Bet Dwarka
attractions.description: This is supposed to be the place where Krishna lived, met his friend Sudama and blessed him, and there is a Peetha (Seat) where Krishna is said to have met Sudama. The temple also has the main Dwarkadish deity which was believed to have been made by Krishna's chief Queen Rukmini and in which Meera bai is said to have merged and disappeared from the material world. There are boats available from Okha Jetty from where people are ferried to the island which is approximately 30 km from Dwarka.

attractions.name: Rukmini Mandir
attractions.description: This temple is 8 km from Dwarka. This is in the outskirts of the city and this is a lonely temple and there is an interesting story of Rukmini being cursed by sage Durvasa because of which the temple is outside the city and its because of this curse only that the water in Dwarka city is salty.

attractions.name: Shivrajpur Beach
attractions.description: Shivrajpur Beach is another notable beach located near Dwarka. It has been awarded the prestigious Blue Flag beach certification for its cleanliness and eco-friendly initiatives. The beach is known for its crystal-clear waters and pristine surroundings, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists.

restaurants.name: Amrutras
restaurants.description: Known for its vegetarian Gujarati thalis. While they serve non-Gujarati food too, it is not particularly tasty.

attractions.name: Mahabodhi Temple
attractions.description: The site where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment. This complex is large and contains a number of major attractions within it. One common way of visiting the statue is to "walk in the steps" of the Buddha. It is said that, after attaining enlightenment, the Buddha spent seven weeks in what is now Mahabodhi temple meditating on the nature of what he had discovered.
