attractions.name: Vir Bahadur Singh Planetarium
attractions.description: A good place to spark children's interest in astronomy and physics. The planetarium runs 45-minute long shows at 1pm, 3pm and 5pm daily.

attractions.name: Gorakhpur Zoo
attractions.description: The second largest zoo in the state with several big cats, deer, monkeys, bears, reptiles, birds and fish in the aquarium section.
attractions.address: Buddha Vihar Rd, Rail Vihar Colony Phase 3rd, Phase 3rd

attractions.name: Gita Vatika
attractions.description: Beautiful temple of Lord Krishna and Radha

attractions.name: Gorakhnath Math
attractions.description: A temple named after Yogi Gorakhnath.

attractions.name: St. John's Church
attractions.description: 200-year old church with rich history.

attractions.name: Lord Buddha Museum
attractions.description: Nice and quiet place to visit.

attractions.name: Railway Museum
attractions.description: There are the lots of collections related to Indian railway and Gorakhpur railway station.. The Rail museum is also a very good picnic place.

attractions.name: Taramandal
attractions.description: You can go Taramandal for boating

attractions.name: Neer Nikunj Water Park
attractions.description: The only water park in Gorakhpur, it has a number of water slides, pools, wave pools and a few non-water related amusement rides like a merry-go-round and Ferris wheel.

restaurants.name: Bobi's Restaurant
restaurants.description: Affordable restaurant serving a variety of cuisines. In-house bakery for cakes and pastries.

restaurants.name: 10 Park Street, Cafe & Kitchen
restaurants.description: serving Indian, Oriental and Continental cuisines.

restaurants.name: Choudhry Hotel
restaurants.description: Good and clean Indian food. Agreeable service with reasonable rates. Can get everything from typical Punjabi dishes to South Indian with variety of sweets.

restaurants.name: Hotel Ganesh
restaurants.description: Good and clean Indian food. South Indian dishes like Dosa, Masal Dosa, and Idly Sambar are available here at reasonable rate.

restaurants.name: Tandoor Food - Take away
restaurants.description: Most famous food joint in the city specializing in Mughlai non-vegetarian foods like authentic biryani, kababs, tandoori chicken. The prices are reasonable and the quality is great. Open for dinner only. A busy place.

attractions.name: Jinnah Tower
attractions.description: Guntur's landmark tower, named after the founder of Pakistan. According to a legend, Liaquat Ali Khan, a representative of Jinnah, visited Guntur in the pre-Independence era. Khan was felicitated by Lal Jan, who is said to have built a tower to commemorate the leader of the Muslim League. It was erected on six pillars which open to a dome, typical of the then-Muslim architecture in the early 20th century. Originally unpainted, the tower was later painted in Indian tricolour in February 2022 by MLA Mohammad Musthafa.

attractions.name: Kondaveedu Fort
attractions.description: This historical fort was built during the reign of the Reddy kings in the 14th century CE. There are 21 structures in the fort. The ruins of the fort located on the hilltop offer unravelled mysteries to the tourist. A place of natural scenic beauty with natural wonders it is an ideal place for trekking. The Gopinatha temple and Kathulabave at the foot of the hillock, numerous temples, residential structures, pillared halls on the hill and the entrance gateways on the east and west sides are the attractions at Kondaveedu.

attractions.name: Uppalapadu Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: The water tanks in the village are unique as they provide refuge to many species birds including endangered Spot-Billed Pelicans and Painted Storks. The bird population in these tanks used to be around 12,000, although lately only about 7,000 birds roost in this dwindling habitat through the year.

attractions.name: Viswa Nagar
attractions.description: This is the place of Sri Viswayogi Viswamji and the Universal Integration Pillar. It is an envisioned symbol of oneness of humanity. Also located here is the VIMS/Viswayogi Institute of Medical Sciences (Mother and Child Care Hospital).

attractions.name: Agasthyeswara Swamy Temple
attractions.description: The oldest temple in Guntur, dedicated to Shiva. As the legend goes, the sage Agastya built this temple during the Treta Yuga, centring around a naturally-occurring Swayambhu Lingam. Other than the legend, the temple has inscriptions in the ancient Naga script from 1100.

attractions.name: Manasa Sarovaram
attractions.description: Often called the "Central Park of Guntur".

restaurants.name: Ananda Bhavan Hotel
restaurants.description: Well-known for tasty and delicious vegetarian meals, and tiffins. Andhra style meals are famous.

restaurants.name: Hotel Surya Mahabodhi
restaurants.description: Famous for its delicacies. Especially the Vada Sambar variety they serve is a feast for your appetite. Also don't forget to taste Guntur Mirchi Bajji. You may get it elsewhere in AP also but the taste that you get in Guntur is absolutely matchless. Two more restaurants namely Nakshatra (a 3-star hotel, located at Lakshmipuram main road) and Grand Nagarjuna are very famous in Guntur.

restaurants.name: Bismillah Biryani Point
restaurants.description: This hotel serves authentic Guntur biryani. Its mutton biryani is special and its chicken biryani is also worthwhile. Also try side dishes of mutton and chicken.

restaurants.name: Hotel Madras Bilal
restaurants.description: Hotel Madras Bilal serves authentic Guntur mutton and chicken biryani.

attractions.name: Ambadevi Temple
attractions.description: This temple is in the heart of Amravati city. It is believed that Shri Krishna abducted Rukmini from this temple, and married her. Goddess Amba attracts devotees from different parts of Vidarbha.

attractions.name: Chatri Talao
attractions.description: 1 km away from Dasturnagar Square on the Malkhed Railway Road. Built in the year 1888 on a small spring called Kali Nadi, this small reservoir was built to supply drinking water to Amravati city. However, Amravati gets water from Upper Wardha Dam now. A small garden and boating facility is also available here.

attractions.name: Sai Mandir
attractions.description: it lies on Badnera road. It has very calm surrounding. Gives mental piece & relief.

attractions.name: Satidham Temple
attractions.description: Located in the heart of the city at Rallies Plot. This temple has beautiful idols of Lord Krishna and Radha, Lord Ram and Sita, Lord Ganesh, Lord Shiva and Rani Satiji. A fair is organized on the occasion of Janmashthami every year. Huge devotees attend the fair.

attractions.name: Shri Bhakti Dham Temple
attractions.description: This temple has beautiful idols of Lord Krishna and Radha. There is also an idol of Shri Sant Jalaram Bappa. There is a small park for children behind this temple.

attractions.name: Wadali Talao
attractions.description: This was built to deliver a clean and fresh water supply to Amravati Camp. There is a small garden with a zoo here. People usually come here during weekends and enjoy boating. This is one of the best places for kids.

attractions.name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
attractions.description: It is a modern construction, but don't miss visiting it.

attractions.name: Takhteswar Temple
attractions.description: White marble temple built on hill, gives Aerial View of City. Crafting work on marble stone is pretty good.

attractions.name: Top 3 Multiplex
attractions.description: One of the multiplex in Bhavnagar.

attractions.name: Adhyatmik Sadhana Kendra
attractions.description: Spiritual Study Centre where more than 500 true seeker are doing their sadhana.

attractions.name: Play Chopat with the locals
attractions.description: The people of Bhavnagar are some of the friendliest in India. Mixing with them will be a memorable experience. Look for people playing Cross and Circle game in public places. You can join them and make friends for a lifetime. Chopat is also called Aman Chache and it is a variation of the dice game in Indian epics.

restaurants.name: Saffron
restaurants.description: Panjabi veg. cuisine
restaurants.address: Waghawadi Road, opp. Swaminarayan Axarwadi Temple

restaurants.name: Red Chilli Garden Restaurant
restaurants.description: One of the best restaurants for Punjabi, Kathiyawadi, South Indian and Paw Bhaji.
restaurants.address: 150 ft Ring road, Top3 to Ghogha road,

attractions.name: Balahanuman Temple
attractions.description: This is where Ramdhun Sri Ram Jay Ram Jay Jay Ram is being chanted non-stop since the last 51 years. And it is a world record registered with The Guinness Book of World Records. This temple faces the Lakhota Lake (man made) which is a nice place to spend ones time. At the center of the Lakhota lake is a small museum that has (among other things) photos of Kumar Ranjitsinhji who played Test cricket (for England).

attractions.name: Shantinath & Adinath Mandir
attractions.description: The two Jain temples in the Chandi Bazaar area are worth visiting. They are historic temples built around 1564-1622.

attractions.name: Darbargadh Palace
attractions.description: A historical palace with Rajput and European style architecture.

restaurants.name: Flavours Restaurant
restaurants.description: Veg. restaurant
restaurants.address: first Floor, City Arcade, Pandit Nehru Road,

restaurants.name: Madras Cafe
restaurants.description: Madras Cafe at Teen Batti is a very good restaurant for Vegetarian fare (especially South Indian).

restaurants.name: Maruti Restaurant
restaurants.description: Veg. restaurant

restaurants.name: Paramount Restaurant
restaurants.description: Non-veg restaurant

restaurants.name: 7 Seas Restaurant
restaurants.description: It serves veg and non-veg cuisine (Indian, Continental & Chinese) - operates 24 hours.

attractions.name: Aaiyappa Mandir
attractions.description: It is an important social, cultural and religious meeting place for people from the south.

attractions.name: Babudih
attractions.description: A village in Chas Block famous for 75 foot (23 m) high tower.

attractions.name: Bokaro Ispat Pustakalaya
attractions.description: Has a collection of over 40,000 books (including some valuable manuscript) that meets the reading requirements of the people in the township. It is managed by the management of the steel plant.

attractions.name: Bokaro Steel Plant
attractions.description: One of the largest steel mills in the country, with an output capacity of more than five million tonnes of salable steel. It's a fully integrated steel plant; hence, a visit here will give you a first hand experience of steel-making from raw material handling, coke ovens, blast furnace to steel melting shops and rolling mills where you see the finished product.

attractions.name: Bokaro Thermal
attractions.description: This is the home of the oldest thermal power plant in Asia, started in 1952 in collaboration with USA and West Germany by the then Prime Minister of the country Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.

attractions.name: Chandrapura
attractions.description: A town famous for Chandrapura Thermal Power Station, a unit of Damodar Valley Corporation. It was a big source of pollution for the adjoining areas owing to the coal based generators, but things changed after electrostatic precipitators were installed in the chimneys, and large scale afforestation was carried out. The town lies on the northern edge of the Damodar river. The Chandrapura Railway Station is a small but beautifully designed Railway Station.

attractions.name: Chas
attractions.description: Once a small grain trading hub of the region, this town first became famous during the Second World War when the British Government used it as a base to supply soldiers fighting on the eastern front against the Japanese. After the decision of Government of India to establish the Bokaro Steel Plant it gained in stature. It was the administrative headquarters of the area when Bokaro was a part of Dhanbad district, and later when Bokaro became a district. The headquarters have been moved to the steel township. Chas continues to be a trading hub, but has declined in importance after the rise of the township to the west.

attractions.name: Chira Chas
attractions.description: This area is real estate hub for the City. Many New colonies came up at this place.

attractions.name: City Centre, Sector 4
attractions.description: The city centre is the main shopping district of the city. The difference of this market and most other major markets in Indian cities happens to be the planning of the market. There is ample parking space, and the approach roads, as well as those inside the market are wide. The place houses almost all major Indian banks, has the best shops in the city for clothing, electronics, and the best food joints. You can find anything from a needle to a car in the market. It used to be home for the only cinema theaters in the city, but only two of them (Jeetendra and Pali Plaza) is operational now. The latest comers to the market are coaching institutes, small clinics, and hospitals. Their rate of growth shows the demand these services have in the city.

attractions.name: City Park
attractions.description: Bokaro has a well maintained City Park with an artificial lake. Three artificial islands have been added. These islands were designed in Japanese style. The park used to have some small animals but they were all transferred to the Jawaharlal Botanical Garden in the early 90s. There is a small guest house that is used to host parties for visiting dignitaries. A small restaurant also stands at the eastern edge of the lake. There is a small toy train that is run for some time early every year. The park hosts an annual Basant Mela (Spring Fiesta) in early February. The southern part of the park is used by thousands during the annual Chhatth puja in October/November. A new small beautiful park was opened in 2007 to make city park more beautiful and make people more enjoy chat new year picnic.

attractions.name: Garga Dam
attractions.description: It is a famous picnic spot for the denizens of Bokaro. Lustrous green surroundings and variety of aquatic habitat residing in and around Garga Dam lures the school excursions and biological expeditions to this place. This dam is constructed for the use of steel plant as well as for the water supply for its people.

attractions.name: Gayatri Mandir
attractions.description: People use to visit the place during the morning and evening time for the daily prayer. Navmi puja at Gayatri mandir is also famous. Khichri is distributed as the prasad on the occasion of Navmi puja.

attractions.name: Gawai Dam
attractions.description: A good picnic spot near Pindrajora on Purulia road. It is 15 km from the city. The picnic spot is likable because of the flow of a stream due to leaving of water from the dam.

attractions.name: Ghaus Nagar
attractions.description: This area is a suburb where people from different part of Bihar living and working in Bokaro Steel Plant. Some people who are retired from Bokaro Steel City are also settled permanently.

attractions.name: Jainamore
attractions.description: One of the 42 villages in Jaridih block of Bokaro. It is on the NH-23 at a distance of around 7 km away from the Bokaro Steel City Railway Station. Close to Jainamore is the Garga Dam on the river Garga which passes through Bokaro. The dam is a popular tourist and picnic spot and known for its scenic surroundings.

attractions.name: Jagannath Temple
attractions.description: The newly built Jagannath temple is another attraction. The temple is a replica of the famous temple in Puri, Odisha.

attractions.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Biological Park
attractions.description: The biggest zoological garden in Jharkhand was built in the late 1980s and early 1990s. It has animals and birds from different parts of the world, with the big cats being the biggest attractions. The zoo came into limelight after multiple breedings of white tigers, Royal Bengal tigers, and the Asiatic lion over a short span of time. The cubs were sent to different zoos in India and abroad, since the available resources were not good enough to cater to the needs of so many big cats. Boating is allowed in the artificial lake created within the park. There is also a kids corner near bear cage and adjacent to it is a small dam. Now the facility of toy train is also available inside.

attractions.name: Kali Mandir
attractions.description: Located in sector 8, it is one of the oldest temples of the city. As the name suggests, the temple is dedicated to one of the incarnations of Shakti, Goddess Kali. Besides the religious activities it is also a major socializing place for the Bengalis of the city. The temple organizes an annual painting competition attended by hundreds of students from the schools of the city.

attractions.name: Mohan Kumar Mangalam Stadium
attractions.description: It is a very well maintained stadium by SAIL having a capacity of 30000. It is also the training centre and headquarters of SAIL football academy. It comes lively on 14th November when Children's Day function is celebrated on its grounds with colourful dance and cultural programmes from the various schools of Bokaro.

attractions.name: Noori Masjid
attractions.description: It is the biggest mosque in the city where the Muslims come for tubliq.

attractions.name: Pupunki Ashram
attractions.description: The last Kasba in the Bokaro Dhanbad route is Pupunki. The village, along with its fields and captive fishery ponds is squeezed between NH-32, Bokaro-Chandrapura Railway line and the Damodar river. Opposite to this village across the NH-32 is the pious Pupunki Ashram "The Multiversity". Established by Akhanda Mandaleshwer Sri Sri Swami Swarupananda Paramhansha Deva, popularly Known as Babamani. This Ashram was an age old home for Gurus who used to harbour Gaushalas with 100s of students being imparted scientific and spiritual knowledge in the past. One can still see the remnants of the past with many rituals still intact in this Ashram. This place is also a popular picnic spot these days.

attractions.name: Ram Mandir
attractions.description: It is the most famous mandir dedicated to Lord Ram and other smaller mandirs. Other gods and goddesses include Hanuman Mandir, Radha Krishna Mandir, Shiv Parivar Mandir, Durga Mandir, Surya Mandir, Kali Mandir, Lord Venkateshwar Mandir, Shiv Mandir, and Sheetala Mandir. Ram Mandir was established in 1967-68 by the late Founder Secretary Pt. Parma Nand Tripathi, a great labor leader. The mandir houses a rich Dharmik library and Rishi Niwas. All festivals, pravachan, Kirtan, functions, and celebrations are organized by the Shree Ram Mandir Trust. Also, the poor arrange more than 250 marriages in a year in the Ram Mandir campus at a very low cost. The Ram Mandir market is also famous for its coffee house, batata poori, chat, samosa, phuchka, and famous egg-rolls. Ram Mandir houses one of the oldest markets of Bokaro. The airport is one kilometer from Ram Mandir.

attractions.name: Siwandih
attractions.description: A suburb which houses a large number of migrants from Bihar living and working in the Steel mill. The area is situated in western part of Bokaro near the Bokaro Railway Station. The Garga Dam is nearby to this place. Azad Nagar is an area in Siwandih two mosques are there in this area. Two of big Idgah one in Millat Nager is also in this area for Muslims prayer for ID and IDU'L Zuha. Popular neighborhoods in Siwandih are Bansgora, Islampur, Makhdumpur,Millat Nager and Haisabatu.

attractions.name: Tenughat
attractions.description: Tenughat is famous for Tenughat Dam and Tenughat Thermal Power Station. A canal too runs through the region.

attractions.name: Sri Talpagiri Ranganadha Swamy Temple
attractions.description: The most famous temple on the southern bank of the River Pennar, the Galigopuram of the temple is 29 m high and has seven gold Kalasams. The most beautiful chamber of the temple is the Addalamantapam (mirror parlor), walled with high-class mirrors arranged at proper angles to reflect only the deity seated in an elevated ornate seat for the Lord in the centre.

attractions.name: Bara Shaheed Dargah
attractions.description: Located on the banks of the Swarnala Cheruvu lake. The shrine is dedicated to twelve martyrs (Sufi saints/warriors) who are believed to have sacrificed their lives in battle centuries ago. It stands as a profound symbol of communal harmony, drawing millions of devotees across all faiths, backgrounds, and nationalities.

attractions.name: Gulbarga Fort
attractions.description: The fort dates back to the time of the Kakatiya dynasty. Later, the fort was turned into a mighty citadel under the Bahmani Sultanate. Today it is mostly in ruins but contains several structures from the Bahmani period. Contains several structures inside

attractions.name: Gate of Gulbarga Fort
attractions.description: Entry to the Gulbaraga Fort is through the north-west. The arched gateway is flanked by bastions and topped with battlements.

attractions.name: Bala Hisar
attractions.description: Bala Hissr is a dojon (heavily fortified central tower of a fort) located inside the Gulbaraga Fort. It was added by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, the founder of the Bahmani dynasty. Three large cannons rest atop the tower.

attractions.name: Jama Masjid
attractions.description: The mosque was built in 1367 by Bahmani Sultan Mohammed Shah I to commemorate the establishment of the capital in Gulbarga following the defeat Kapaya Nayaka of Warangal.

attractions.name: Choti Masjid
attractions.description: This small three domed mosque is located north of the Jami Masjid

attractions.name: Haft Gumbaz
attractions.description: A group of tombs of the Bahmani dynasty built during the 14th and 15th centuries. The tombs are examples of early Indo-Islamic architecture. The complex houses a total of 7 tombs out of which 4 belong to the rulers of the Bahmani sultanate. A unique feature seen only in the Haft Gumbaz is the double-chambered tomb, with one chamber for the king and the other for his family members.

attractions.name: Dargah of Banda Nawaz
attractions.description: Banda Nawaz was a Sufi saint of Chishti Order. He was invited by the Bahmini Sultan Firoz Shah to settle in Gulbaraga (Kalaburagi) in 1399/1400. He later had a conflict with the Sultan but continued staying and preaching in Gulbarga. He died in 1422 and was laid to rest in the dargah. His death anniversary (ur) is celebrated on 15, 16 and 17 Dhu al-Qadah (11th month of the Islamic calendar).

attractions.name: Chor Gumad
attractions.description: This single-domed structure stands on the north-western corner of the citadel next to the fort walls. The structure probably doubled up as a watch tower. Nothing much is known about the history of the tomb or its occupants. According to legend, once a thief used to store his loot in the tomb and hence the name. The other name, Shor Gumbad, literally translates into noisy dome. The interiors of the tomb have unique acoustic properties, allowing the sound to echo through the interiors of the tomb.

attractions.name: Sharana Basaveshwara Temple
attractions.description: The temple houses the Samadhi of Sharana Basaveshwara, a 12th century Indian philosopher, poet, Lingayat social reformer of bhakti movement. The temple has a towering spire and consists of a series of pillars and arches. The temple is known for its intricate carvings of Hindu gods, goddesses, demigods, damsels, animals and events from local lore. The temple is also known for its chariot festival, which happens in March.

attractions.name: Buddha Vihar
attractions.description: A Buddhist temple and spiritual centre. Opened in 2007, it is a new addition to the medieval city. The architecture blends with the architecture of famous Buddhist pilgrimage like Sanchi, Sarnath, Ajanta, etc. It is an oasis of peace.

attractions.name: Bhavani Sangameshwarar Temple
attractions.description: Sangameshwarar Temple, Bhavani is about 12 km. from Erode. The famous Sangameshwara Temple is on the shores of the Bhavani river. Three rivers by name Cauvery, Bhavani and invisible Amudha merge at this pilgrimage place.

attractions.name: Birds Sanctuary
attractions.description: Birds Sanctuary, Vellode - is about 15 km from Erode

attractions.name: Chennimalai
attractions.description: Chennimalai - is about 30 km. from Erode and 12 km from Perundurai

attractions.name: Government Museum
attractions.description: Government Museum, was opened to the public in 1987. The important exhibits are inscription of Kongu Chola, hero stones from Bargur, Tanjore paintings, manuscripts, coins, geological objects, Kodumanal antiques and other pre-history items. It has both botanical and zoological specimens also. The Museum is known for its collection of palm-leaf manuscripts and coins.

attractions.name: Kodiveri Dam
attractions.description: Kodiveri Dam is about 10 km from Gobichettipalayam and 55 km from Erode

attractions.name: Periyar Memorial House
attractions.description: a museum depicting the life history of Periyar E. V. Ramasamy

attractions.name: Sangameswarar Temple
attractions.description: IHindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva located approximately 15 miles from Erode.

attractions.name: Sivanmalai
attractions.description: Sivanmalai - is about 50 km. from Erode and 5 km to Kangayam

attractions.name: Thindalmalai
attractions.description: Thindalmalai - is 5 km from Erode

attractions.name: Vattamalai
attractions.description: Vattamalai - is about 5 km from Kangayam

attractions.name: Bhabani Pathak’s Tilla
attractions.description: Made famous in the novel Devi Chaudhurani by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. An unbelievable network of tunnels starting near the City Centre region right up to the Damodar river. Nowadays, it is a protected monument (the entrance of the cave). But you would be able to visit the place.

attractions.name: Bhiringi Shmashankali Temple
attractions.description: A Kali temple established in 1852. People from different places arrive at the temple during Kali Puja.

attractions.name: Durgapur Barrage
attractions.description: Definitely one of the best places to see, if you are interested in one of two things: nature and man's effort to control its fury. And if you really are game, you should be there at the height of monsoons. Try peering over the railings to watch water being let out of the lock-gates. It is a phenomenal sight. A few yards away from the main barrage is the canal. There is a short foot bridge over it. Try crossing with a lock gate open. It is dizzying. And finally, get down by one of the sides (Bankura or Durgapur - prefer Durgapur), the beaches. It is really pretty. Finally, there are a few fishermen who fish in those waters. Pay a few bucks and ask them to give you a ride. Earlier it used to be a great spot for bird-watching in the winters. But the birds have decreased although if you go in the early morning you can still see lots of birds. One bit of advice: Wear warm clothes.

attractions.name: Durgapur Steel Plant
attractions.description: The steel plant is one awesome thing to see. It is hard to imagine the scale of things that happen and how the heck all of this works together. You need a permit to visit, which is easily obtained from the Administrative building, outside the plant, near the main gate of the plant.

attractions.name: Rarheswar Shiva Temple
attractions.description: According to the Archaeological Survey of India, this temple is more than 800 years old, with a unique architectural style. It is built in the style of Rathas of Southern India.

attractions.name: Durgapur Club
attractions.description: It is a fraction of its former colonial self. Yet, with swimming pools and the who’s who of the Durgapur Steel Plant, complete with its British era high-nosedness, is still a hotspot.

attractions.name: Kumaramangalam Park
attractions.description: This was one of the most beautiful parks around, being the first park in the entire Paschim Bardhaman district to have a musical fountain. Then due to neglect the entire infrastructure started falling apart. Durgapur Steel Plant, which oversaw its maintenance outsourced it to a private company. The musical fountain is now back and the park is back to its good old days again. Boating facilities are also available.

attractions.name: Troika Park
attractions.description: It is a fun place for kids near City Centre. It has a toy-train, a few rides and a bunch of other attractions. Adjacent to it is a deer park. You can actually walk in and touch a few of the deer. You can also find a leisure boating lake close by.

attractions.name: Birla Mandir
attractions.description: One of the most beautiful temples, dating back centuries and a must visit, which is maintained by the Birla Group.

attractions.name: Swami Shanti Prakash Ashram
attractions.description: A Sindhi religious and spiritual center known for its architecture and carvings.

attractions.name: Bishnu Temple
attractions.description: This stone temple is built over a platform with a Bengal hut-shaped roof and arched entrance. The temple dates to about the 14th century CE. A stone, called "Narayan shila", is worshipped here as the deity of the temple. Earlier, a 12 armed Lokeswar Vishnu idol was being worshipped as deity, which has been stolen long before. The temple is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

attractions.name: Ghaghar Burhi Temple
attractions.description: A small shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali, it is the oldest temple of Asansol.

attractions.name: IISCO Steel Plant
attractions.description: Operated by Steel Authority of India (SAIL), the IISCO Steel Plant is one of the major steel plants in West Bengal.

attractions.name: Manoj Talkies
attractions.description: You can watch all newly released movies here. Good cinema hall; one of the biggest with a seating capacity of almost 1800.

attractions.name: Nehru Park
attractions.description: A beautiful park on the banks of the Damodar River. A cast iron statue of Nehru, casted by IISCO, is in the park. There is an eatery in the park. There's a big pond inside the park with boating facilities. You can get great views of the Biharinath Hill from the park.

attractions.name: Panifala
attractions.description: A picnic spot with a lake for boating and beautiful garden of flowers.

attractions.name: Satabdi Park
attractions.description: There are facilities for paddle boating and a few rides for children. Nice place to spend the evening.

restaurants.name: Gangar Hotel
restaurants.description: Dhaba type. No pretensions of luxury. Delicious Bengali food - dal-aloobhaja must try; fish range from rui and chital maachh to ilish and varieties of chhoto maachh; those who like can also order mangsho or dimer dalna.

restaurants.name: Garam Masala
restaurants.description: Bombay Hotel presents a complete vegetarian AC restaurant in the market place.

attractions.name: Killa Lake
attractions.description: A large lake in front of the fort.

attractions.name: Mahipalgad
attractions.description: A fort on a mountain ridge amidst dense evergreen forest.

attractions.name: Suvarna Vidhana Soudha
attractions.description: Largely identical in design to Bangalore's Vidhana Soudha, the winter session of the Karnataka Legislature is held here.

attractions.name: Kamal Basadi
attractions.description: A splendid Jain temple, built by the Ratta dynasty in c. 1204 under the guidance of a Jain monk.

attractions.name: Chikki Basadi
attractions.description: A ruined Jain temple near Kamal Basadi.

restaurants.name: Aadinarayan
restaurants.description: Famous for fish.

restaurants.name: Hotel Aadinarayan
restaurants.description: Famous for fresh seafood.

restaurants.name: Tatte Idli
restaurants.description: Tatte Idli & Masala Dosa with delicious Chutney & Sambar

attractions.name: Nau Gaja Peer Shrine
attractions.description: Nau Gaja Peer roughly translates to the "Nine Gaja Saint" (Gaj is a traditional unit of length in India equivalent to about 0.91 metres or 3 feet). This makes the legendary saint the shrine is dedicated to more than 8 metres or 27 feet. The shrine also houses a Hindu Shiva temple. As such, it is a pilgrimage site visited by both Muslims and Hindus.

attractions.name: Amirthi Forest
attractions.description: A large forested area near Javathu mountain. Amirthi Falls and Amirthi Zoo can be found here. Animals at the park include spotted deer, mongoose, hedgehog, foxes, reason monkeys, red headed parrots, love birds, tortoises, peacock, crocodiles, wild cats, eagles, ducks, pigeons, wild parrots, rabbits, and pythons.

attractions.name: Golden Temple, Sripuram
attractions.description: Dedicated to Sri Lakshmi Narayani or Maha Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, in 2007. The temple has covered in intricate work done by artisans specialising in temple art using gold. Every detail was manually created and has significance from the Vedas. Sripuram's design features a star-shaped path (Sri chakra), positioned in the middle of the lush green landscape, with a length of over 1.8 km. You walk along a 'starpath' to reach the temple in the middle, past spiritual messages.

attractions.name: Jalagandeswarar Temple
attractions.description: This temple to Lord Shiva is a fine example of Vijayanagaram Architecture. The temple has exquisite carvings on its gopuram (tower), richly carved stone pillars, large wooden gates and stunning monoliths and sculptures.

attractions.name: Theertagiri Murugan Temple
attractions.description: Temple dedicated to Lord Murugan with a huge statue of him also nearby

attractions.name: Sajra and Gojra Forts
attractions.description: These are abandoned cliff top remains of forts built by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. This is recommended only for those with strength as it's accessible only via foot. You also need to be aware of when and how you plan to climb them.

attractions.name: Palamathi Murugan Temple
attractions.description: Murugan Temple on Palamathi Hill

restaurants.name: The Vellore Kitchen
restaurants.description: Good place for South Indian chicken and mutton dishes. They also have seafood and other cuisines.

restaurants.name: Zaitoon Katpadi
restaurants.description: Good Middle Eastern style restaurant.
restaurants.address: 1st floor, Selvam Square, Tiruvalam Rd, Selvam Nagar, Katpadi

attractions.name: Panch Mandir
attractions.description: It consists of two nine-pinnacled temples and two five-pinnacled temples.

attractions.name: Aryan Park
attractions.description: Boating, You can see rabbit, ostrich, sunflower garden.

attractions.name: Gandhi Research Foundation
attractions.description: A museum and research institution dedicated to the life and achievements of Mahatma Gandhi.

attractions.name: Anjanaya Statue, Jagannatha Hill
attractions.description: Located in the outskirts of Kurnool (5 km).

attractions.name: Konda Reddy Fort
attractions.description: Remains of old Kurnool Fort.

attractions.name: Kotla Vijaya Bhaskar Reddy
attractions.description: Ghat on the banks of Hundri River in Kurnool Town, named after the former Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh state.

attractions.name: Orvakal Rock Garden
attractions.description: Small park with igneous rock formations and a cave museum. This site was used in the making of several Indian movies.

attractions.name: Tungabhadra River Banks
attractions.description: There are many temples along the banks of the Tungabhadra River. This river is heavily polluted. It flows through three states: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

attractions.name: Bhukailash Rajbari
attractions.description: One of the few zamindar palaces in South Kolkata, built by Joynarayan Ghosal in 1781. He had an estate at Gobindapur, which later became Fort William (present-day Vijay Durg). He got a new estate of 108 bighas (1,44,720 m²) at Kidderpore during the construction of Fort William. After clearing the forest, he built a palace as well as temples dedicated to Shiva and family deity Patitapavani. Since then, the whole property has been endowed for worship of Patitapavani.

attractions.name: BNR House
attractions.description: Once the residence of Indologist Sir William Jones, now the official residence of the General Manager (GM) of South Eastern Railway (SER).

attractions.name: Choto Rasbari
attractions.description: A temple built in 1846-47 by Pyarilal Mondal and Monimohan Mondal, both members of the Bawali zamindar family of Budge Budge, once served as a major pilgrimage site. The temple complex also has a ghat along the Adi Ganga River with four columns, now in shambles. Even the river faces similar condition, being neglected for decades.

attractions.name: India Government Mint
attractions.description: Though the mint dates back to 1757, the present building was built in the 1930s.

attractions.name: Tollywood
attractions.description: From an early beginning in the silent era in 1919 to the talking era in the 1930s to the golden days of 1950s to 1970s has been a chequered history. It has seen such greats as Satyajit Ray, Bimal Roy, Ritwik Ghatak and Mrinal Sen. Tollygunge produces about 70 films annually.

attractions.name: Indenture Memorial
attractions.description: A memorial dedicated to the 1.6 million Indian workers who were transported to labour in European colonies. The indenture system was a substitute for slavery, which was abolished in many European countries by the 19th century. This resulted to the increasing presence of Indians abroad, especially in Africa, Southeast Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific.

attractions.name: Suriname Ghat Memorial
attractions.description: A memorial commemorating the indentured migration of Indian workers from the ghat to the South American country of Suriname, then a Dutch colony. A total of 64 sailing ships carried 34,300 workers to the country from 1873 to 1917. The memorial contains an aluminium statue of a plainly-dressed couple carrying a potli, symbolising the first Indian man and woman to set foot on Suriname, resembling the Baba and Mai monument in Paramaribo.

attractions.name: Gurusaday Museum
attractions.description: The outcome of a lifetime collection of traditional folk arts in Bengal by Sir Gurusaday Dutta. On his death in 1941, the collection was handed over to the Bratachari Society founded by Sir Gurusaday Dutta to preserve and protect Bengal folk arts. It was opened as a museum to the public with the help of the union government in 1963. It contains, among other fine handicrafts, terracotta panels, kantha (folk quilt work) and patas (hand-painted scrolls), notably of the Kalighat School.

attractions.name: Sabarna Sangrahashala
attractions.description: The only family museum of Kolkata. It was established in 2005 by the Sabarna Roy Choudhury Paribar Parishad and is a popular tourist attraction, especially for those who want to know more about the history of Kolkata. It is also a research institute in the making. The museum possesses some of the rarest Kabulatipatras, documents and articles of historical importance besides several artifacts dating back to the 17th century. The museum is dedicated to students for creating an awareness of history, heritage, and culture of the land. Every year in the month of February, the museum organises the International History and Heritage Exhibition which is only of its kind in Eastern India.

attractions.name: SER Headquarters
attractions.description: Contains a heritage gallery.

attractions.name: State Archaeological Museum
attractions.description: The museum has a wide collection of antiques from the bronze age and various artefacts collected from excavations across West Bengal.

attractions.name: Sibtainabad Imambara
attractions.description: A major centre of Shi'a Islam in West Bengal. It was founded in 1864 by Wajid Ali Shah. He was buried within the imambara after death.

attractions.name: Tipu Sultan Masjid
attractions.description: Builtby the Waqf Committee at Tollygunge, with the same design and look as the Tipu Sultan Mosque in Esplanade.

attractions.name: Jagannath Temple
attractions.description: One of the major Jagannath temples in West Bengal, and Ratha Yatra is the major crowd-puller of this temple.

attractions.name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
attractions.description: One of the many Swaminarayan temples in India, built by Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) in 2013. It has been said that Shri Swaminarayan (1781–1820) once visited the Kapil Muni Temple in Sagar Island. There is a 1,400-foot pathway (parikrama) in the temple.

attractions.name: Royal Calcutta Golf Club
attractions.description: The oldest golf club in India, established in 1829. Exclusively for members and guests.

attractions.name: Tollygunge Club
attractions.description: Exclusively for members and guests. Founded in 1895, and popularly known as the Tolly Club, the club is spread over a hundred-acre campus, and is acknowledged as one of the top clubs in the world. Even though the club has been more Indianised since 1947, the old elite colonial vibe is still there. It has been a popular choice to host events like weddings. As a sports club, it offers facilities for golf, tennis, squash, indoor and outdoor swimming, riding and amateur equestrian sports. The club also offers 67 well-furnished rooms, including air conditioned suites and residential rooms for the members and guests. Both AC and non-AC restaurants are available, serving continental, Indian and Chinese meals along with snacks and drinks.

attractions.name: Benuban Chhaya
attractions.description: A public park built around a lake and has a tree lined path flanked by lakes on either side. The park is a peaceful destination to spend time with family and friends. You can also take a boat ride and visit a tram restaurant inside the park.

attractions.name: Patuli Lake
attractions.description: A long waterbody along EM Bypass, attracting hundreds on weekends. The lake is lined by roadside stalls, as well as various sculpture portraying some of Kolkata's wonders, including a replica of the Dakshineswar Kali Temple, a Durga idol, a replica of the Howrah Bridge across the lake, a sculpture representing the football rivalry between Mohun Bagan and East Bengal (Kolkata Derby), and a sign of the iconic Floating Market that sadly has been closed since December 2023.

restaurants.name: Arsalan Restaurant & Caterer
restaurants.description: Biryani and Mughlai food. Popular items: firni, mutton kosha, mutton boti kebab, chicken chatpata, mutton biryani, egg chicken roll.

restaurants.name: Fiya the Zayka
restaurants.description: Cooking the Royal Biryani is the profession of Fiya the Zayka’s; they serve Mughlai food, developed under the patronage of the Mughal Kings and Queens using the spices of the Mughals' adopted Indian homeland.
restaurants.address: 44/1 Adi Ganga, Bansdroni Post Office Road, Bansdroni 700070

restaurants.name: Foodpath
restaurants.description: A row of roadside stalls attracting hundreds during weekend.

restaurants.name: Beans and Cream Cafe
restaurants.description: A cosy café with outdoor seating. Offers a variety of breakfast options, as well as coffees and teas.

restaurants.name: Bhooter Raja Dilo Bor
restaurants.description: A Feluda-themed restaurant with 10 outlets in Kolkata, literally meaning "the king of ghosts has given a boon". It is famous for its hilsa (iliś) dishes.

restaurants.name: Double Daker's Lane Café
restaurants.description: A café with an old-house vibe, with familiar menu like pastas, burgers, wraps and rolls, along with a variety of hot and cold drinks.

restaurants.name: Koshe Kosha
restaurants.description: Famous for its mahabhoj thali with mutton curry, as well as whole bhapa ilish.

restaurants.name: Drop In
restaurants.description: Vegetarian restaurant. Indian and Chinese cuisine. Popular items: lassi, naan, paneer tikka masala, roti, thali.
restaurants.address: Ground Floor, Ideal Towers, 57, Block A, Diamond Harbour Road

restaurants.name: Chakhna Shakna Punjabi Dhaba
restaurants.description: Specialist in Punjabi, tandoori & North Indian cuisine. Free home food delivery or sit 'n' dine service.

restaurants.name: Domino's Pizza
restaurants.description: Pizzas, garlic bread.

attractions.name: Brahmamoyee Kali Temple
attractions.description: A temple complex consisting of a nine-pinnacled temple and three Shiva temples. It was built by Gopimohan Tagore, a relative of Rabindranath Tagore, in May 1813. It is said that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar used to visit the temple and the adjoining Sanskrit College in Shyamnagar.

attractions.name: Ancestral house of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose
attractions.description: Janakinath Bose, father of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, used to live in Cuttack most of the time and come to this house during Puja times. The area where the house is located was originally known as "Kodalia" before being later renamed to "Subhasgram" to honour the freedom fighter. Although the Bose family later moved to Bhowanipore further north, Durga Puja still brings the family together at Subhasgram.

attractions.name: Bhaskar Bhawan State Museum
attractions.description: A museum with numerous sculptures of sculptor Chintamoni Kar.

attractions.name: Chintamoni Kar Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: Famous for its wide variety of birds, butterflies, ferns and orchids. The best time to visit is winter or spring, when maximum variety of birds are present in this sanctuary.

attractions.name: Ramakrishna Mission Ashrama
attractions.description: Arranges several cultural programmes, not just religious ones.

attractions.name: Chaithurgarh
attractions.description: It was constructed by Raja Pratwidev First. Archeologists consider it as one of the strongest natural fort. Since it is protected by strong natuaral walls, only at some places walls have been built. The fort has three main entrances which are named as Menaka, Humkara, and Simhadwar.

attractions.name: Barua sagar
attractions.description: Baruasagar is around 24 km from Jhansi. It is a small town on the bank of Betwa river. It has a large lake which is called Barua sagar tal. Places to see here are the fort, Jarai-ka-Math, and the lake. It lies on Jhansi-Varanasi route and all the buses that go to Khajuraho pass through this town.

attractions.name: Chirgaon
attractions.description: Chirgaon is 30 km from Jhansi, It is on the banks of Betwa river. It is on National Highway 25. It is famous for National Poet Maithili Sharan Gupt who was from Chirgaon. Hindi authors generally describe this Triveni of poets from Chirgaon by comparing them with Triveni of Ganges.

attractions.name: Fort of Jhansi
attractions.description: The fort of Jhansi was built in 1613, by Raja Bir Singh Judao (1606-27) of Orchha. This fort is built on a rocky hill and the city of Jhansi is around this fort. During the earlier days, the wall of the fort was all around Jhansi city. This wall had ten gates. Some of these gates are still existing and some vanished with time. But places around these gates are still identified with name of gates. Some of the gates are Khandero Gate, Datia darwaza, Unnao gate, Jharna Gate, Laxmi Gate, Sagar Gate, Orchha Gate, Sainyar Gate and Chand gate. Timings: dawn to dusk daily.

attractions.name: Government Museum
attractions.description: The Government Museum is in a very picturesque location in the heart of the city. The surrounding area has some beautiful parks. At one side, is Deen Dayal Sabhagar (city auditorium). Nearby you can see Vrindavan Lal Verma park, Open-air theatre, Rani Lakshmi Bai Park, and a magnificent view of Jhansi fort. There is 1857 Mutiny Memorial on the way to the fort. It is a small park where 1857 mutiny has been depicted with statues that are made by metal scrap! The museum has a rich collection of sculptures, paintings, documents, etc. from different eras. A must see attraction during your visit to Jhansi, it will acquaint you with the history of the region.

attractions.name: Nag Mandir
attractions.description: This temple is in Jhansi cantonment. The beauty of this place is to visit it during sunrise. The spectacular view includes beautiful tree groves and beautiful aura of Jhansi. It shows the beauty is to be searched out in every thing.

attractions.name: Rani Mahal
attractions.description: Rani Mahal was built by Raghunath II of Newalkar family (1769-96). Rani Mahal is decorated with multicoloured paintings and art forms. Rani Mahal has been converted to museum with artefacts from 9th and 12th century AD. The best way to reach Rani Mahal is to take an auto from Elite crossing to the city..

attractions.name: St Jude's Shrine
attractions.description: This shrine of great imortance among Catholic Christians. St. Jude's bone is buried in the foundation of the cathedral. Devotees come from as far as Goa, on the St Jude's feast day on October 28, every year. Feast day is marked by a week long fair and a procession on the last day of the fair. This fair attracts people of all the faiths and religions.

attractions.name: Our Lady of Snows Basilica
attractions.description: The church dates back to the 16th century. The basilica is dedicated to Lady of Snow a title given to St. Mary.

attractions.name: Holy Trinity (CSI) Church
attractions.description: Built by the Dutch East India Company (VOC) the church dates back to 1750. The VOC monogram and the year 1750 (in Roman numerical) are displayed above the main entrance. The floor plan of the church represents a Greek cross with equal arms.

attractions.name: Ballari Fort
attractions.description: This is a big fort sitting on a huge monolithic rock mountain at the center of the city. There is only one way upwards mainly consisting of a rocky trail and steps. It gives a great view of the city from top as it is the highest point in the city, and is good for a trek (should take about 3 hr) in the mornings.

attractions.name: Durgamma (Ballaramma) temple
attractions.description: This is a 350-year-old temple of the Goddess Durga, which is held in high regard. You can visit it in the mornings or evenings when the aarti (a worshiping ritual) takes place.

attractions.name: Radha Krishna Temple
attractions.description: It is the quiet heaven in the middle of the bustle hardly known by anyone but the spiritual. This temple was established by the migrant traders in the city about 50 years ago. It falls on the path the ascetics have to travel from Kanyakumari/Rameshwaram to Haridwar. These traveling mendicants are provided food and shelter here. Often, one can witness religious debates and discussions amongst these travelers here. It also has a beautiful external courtyard and an internal courtyard. Tiled mosaic work lace the entrance room. Frescoes decorate the walls. Monkeys and cats wander about peacefully.

attractions.name: Human Face hill
attractions.description: This hill has been said to look like the face of a sleeping human.

attractions.name: Neolethic art on boulders near Sanganakallu
attractions.description: The exact location is not very clear, but you can ask the locals there to guide you. The said hills are most probably called Hiregudda or Kupgal hill.

attractions.name: Bible Museum
attractions.description: This beautiful shrine which has 14 Stations of the Cross separately erected outside and a Bible Museum on the ground floor is an architectural landmark in the City of Ballari. It is erected in gratitude for the many blessings of God, through the loving and powerful intercession of Our Lady, showered on our Bishop, Most Rev. Dr. Joseph D’silva and the Diocese of Bellary. The Bellary Arogya Mathe Shrine is a place of pilgrimage, prayer and spiritual enrichment, open to all people irrespective of caste and creed. A very good attraction of this church is the model of Bible is presented in the forms of art.

attractions.name: Rajkumar Park
attractions.description: This is park surrounds a natural pond. Boating is a main attraction here, but people do come here for a pleasant walk or feeding the fishes (puffed rice is available just outside the gate). There is also a play area for children.

attractions.name: Ballari exhibition
attractions.description: Visit the exhibition-cum-tradefair which is setup for around two months in the Municipal high school grounds. It has interesting amusement rides and games for both kids and adults.

restaurants.name: Ashraya Cafe
restaurants.description: Rs.70 for vegetarian lunch with chapathi/parotta, rice, rasam, sambar and curd.

restaurants.name: New Madeena Cafe
restaurants.description: Parotta and Kerala chicken curry for ₹200.

restaurants.name: Dwaraka Vegetarian
restaurants.description: Rs.300 for lunch.

restaurants.name: Shahi Durbar Cafe
restaurants.description: Rs.50 for vegetarian lunch.

restaurants.name: Azeem Fast Food
restaurants.description: Rs.140 for Chicken BiriyaniRs.200 for Mutton Biriyani.

restaurants.name: Mayura Cafe
restaurants.description: Vegetarian food of good quality. No seats. Pay and collect from the counter and eat by standing near the tables provided.

attractions.name: The Jain temple at Nathnagar
attractions.description: It is an important pilgrimage centre for Jains.

attractions.name: Budhanath Temple
attractions.description: It is an ancient Shiva Temple on the bank of Ganges.

attractions.name: Sultanganj
attractions.description: It is an important religious center for Hindus from where holy water of Ganges is carried and offered at Deoghar.

attractions.name: Dargha of Shawaz Rahmat-ulla
attractions.description: One of the most popular place of Muslims.

attractions.name: Mandar Parvat
attractions.description: It is supposed to have concurrent to Patliputra or Patna. Bhagdattpuram fin the gods to churn the ocean to procure amrit. The serpent, Vasuki offered to serve as the rope and has left behind an impression of the coil on the granite hill. It is believed that Panchjanya, the conch shell used in the Mahabharat was discovered here in the "Shankh Kund". The Puranas also refer to the hill. It is believed to have been visited by Vishnu as Madhusudana (the destroyer of Madhu the Demon). It is said that Vishnu covered Madhu under the hill after defeating him to death. Kalidasa's Kumarasambhava refers to foot marks of Vishnu on the slopes of Mandara. The hill is replete with relics of bygone ages. Apart from inscriptions and statues, there are numerous rock cut sculptures depicting various images of Hindu Gods. The hill is equally revered by the Jains who believe that their 12th Tirthankara attained nirvana at the summit. The area around Mandara Hill is laced with a landscape of extraordinary sp

attractions.name: Ancient cave sculpture
attractions.description: Ancient cave sculptures from Emperor Ashoka's reign, from 274 to 232 BC are found in the neighbourhood and at Sultangunj, 20 km west of Bhagalpur,

attractions.name: The Tomb of Suja
attractions.description: The tomb of Suja, brother of Moghul emperor Aurangzeb, in the heart of the town is reminiscent of the city's association with the Mughal period

attractions.name: Vikramshila University
attractions.description: The royal university ranks next to Nalanda, and owes its origin to Dharmapala, the devout Pala king who called himself Paramasaugata (chief worshipper of the Buddha) and was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism. It was the medieval center to the conservation and propagation of Buddhist education, established by King Dharmapala of Bengal at the end of the 8th century.

attractions.name: Participate in "Vish-hari Puja"
attractions.description: The religious festival of "Vish-hari Puja" or "the worship of the Snake Queen" or "Manasa Devi, said to be a daughter of lord Shiva and Queen of Snakes" traces its roots back hundreds of years and is still celebrated every year with thousands of believers and snake charmers offering milk to the Nag (the Snake King) and Nageen (The Snake Queen).

attractions.name: Annavaram Satyanarayana Swamy Temple
attractions.description: A religious site growing in popularity. This temple has great architectural features and sits on a hill top that offers a panoramic view of the surrounding fields and villages.

attractions.name: Bhimeswara Swamy Temple
attractions.description: an important Siva temple located in Draksharama

attractions.name: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: is a large stretch of mangrove forests in India that is home to more than 120 bird species and a few endangered bird species. The sanctuary is very well maintained and lush green. There is a boat service by APTDC into the waters.

attractions.name: Kukkuteshwara Swamy Temple
attractions.description: at Pithapuram (12 km)

attractions.name: Hope Island
attractions.description: in the Bay of Bengal and is around 7km east of Kakinada

attractions.name: Kotipalli Kotilingeswara Temple
attractions.description: on the banks of the Godavari River

attractions.name: Konaseema
attractions.description: offers scenic locations of delta islands and boat rides on the Godavari River. This area is known for its scenic greenery and hospitality. There were traditional festivals held here during the year such as Nagula Chavathi (snake worship) and Bhogi (harvest festival)

attractions.name: Rajiv Gandhi Beach
attractions.description: on the banks of the Godavari River in Yanam

attractions.name: Sri Bhava Narayana Swamy Temple
attractions.description: at Sarpavaram (5 km)

attractions.name: Sri Bhimeswaraswamy Vari Temple
attractions.description: one of the Pancharama Kshetras and a National Heritage Site)(10km) Samalkota

attractions.name: Vakalpudi beach
attractions.description: a short distance from the Kakinada Beach Park on the banks of the Godavari River in Yanam.

restaurants.name: kottaaya
restaurants.description: kakinda is very famous for this special dish name as kottaya khaja

attractions.name: Kharosa Caves
attractions.description: Twelve caves featuring sculptures of a Jain tirthankara, Narasimha, Shiva-Parvati, Kartikeya and Ravana.

attractions.name: Baro Mandir Ghat
attractions.description: A row of 12 Shiva temples along the Hooghly River.

attractions.name: Gandhi Memorial Asram
attractions.description: Founded in 1921 by Satish Chandra Dasgupta, a close aide of Mahatma Gandhi. The institution occupies an important place in Indian independence movement and which Gandhi himself called it his second home like Sabarmati Ashram. He visited the place several times during the period of 1939 to 1947.

attractions.name: Giribala Dasi Thakurbari
attractions.description: A "pancharatna" (five-pinnacled) temple dedicated to Radha-Krishna. The temple premise resembles that of Dakshineswar with a row of Shiva temples at riverside and a ghat at the middle, but without the crowd. The temple was built by Giribala Dasi, a granddaughter-in-law of Rani Rashmoni, who constructed the Dakshineswar temple.

attractions.name: Gobinda Kumar House
attractions.description: One of the elegant edifices on the Hooghly River. It originally belonged to Asutosh De or Chatu Babu, one of the figures of the 19th-century Bengali Renaissance. In 1873, during a dengue outbreak, Debendranath Tagore took refuge at this house with his family. This is where his son Rabindranath had his first encounter with nature, away from the busy life in Kolkata, something he later vividly recalled in his autobiography My Reminiscences. He revisited the house in 1919 after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Punjab, and it was here where he decided to renounce his knighthood in protest. As the home eventually passed on the hands of Mymensingh zamindar Gopal Das Choudhury, he opened a home for destitute girls after his father, which is still active.

attractions.name: Laling Fort
attractions.description: Laling is an ancient place and the fort was built up 14th century in the regime of first Faruki king, but the fort is in broken condition in these days. Also, there are two temples of 'Hemadpanthi' styles and are also in very much frayed condition.

attractions.name: Ekvira Temple
attractions.description: This temple belongs to Ekvira mata, which is as Shaktipeeth famous in whole Maharashtra. It is 5 minutes away from the bus station.

attractions.name: Shiva_tirtha
attractions.description: It was built by Anil Anna Gote who is the MLA of Dhule. There is a garden along with a massive monument of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. People go there in the evening to hang out.

restaurants.name: Misal pao
restaurants.description: It is available in cheap rates and famous for the breakfast of Dhule people.

attractions.name: Tilyar Lake
attractions.description: The Tilyar lake is spread over 132 acres. To attract people, there's a restaurant and a mini zoo with bears, tigers, panthers, deer, birds monkeys etc, a toy train for children, a small Columbus swing for adults, a wide lake for large green lawns to play and sit.

restaurants.name: Bikaner Sweets
restaurants.description: Great pani puri (Gol Guppa).

restaurants.name: Madras Hotel
restaurants.description: They serve the best of South Indian food with much much variety.

restaurants.name: Nagpal
restaurants.description: One of the best chhola bhaturas in the city and great dosas too.

restaurants.name: Pappu Bakery
restaurants.description: You can try the cake and pastries, cold drinks.

restaurants.name: Sagar Villa Restaurant
restaurants.description: Great food.

attractions.name: Eco Park
attractions.description: The park is home to a variety of local wildlife. The sunsets here in the natural surroundings are pretty.

attractions.name: Biju Patnaik Park
attractions.description: A great place to visit with family and friends

attractions.name: Gautam Buddha circle
attractions.address: Top Floor 253/2204, Saliabandha street, Gosani Nuagam

attractions.name: Ramaguda Reservoir
attractions.description: An old abandoned reservoir

attractions.name: Selfie Point
attractions.description: Popularly known as the selfie point, it is a garden with a beautiful fountain. People usually come here to relax and take selfies obviously!

attractions.name: Dakhinapura Ghai
attractions.description: A waterbody which is not too big to be called a lake. It has a very soothing and beautiful view.

attractions.name: Maa Taratarini Shaktipeeth
attractions.description: Set atop a hill, this legendary temple is a major pilgrimage centre for the Shakta sect of Hinduism.
attractions.address: Temple Road Dt, near Rushikulya River, Raipur

attractions.name: Maa Sidhhabhairabi Temple & Jagannath Temple
attractions.description: Tourists from almost all parts of southern Odisha as well as northern Andhra Pradesh visit this holy shrine every day. The holy days on which most of the devotees assemble before the deity to offer their prayers are on Sankranti days of the Hindu calendar and on all Tuesdays.

attractions.name: Taptapani
attractions.description: As the name suggests, is famous for its hot springs. Nestled at about 1,800 feet (550 m) above sea level, this spot is 56 km away from the city's railway station. The sprawling Panthanivas is the only shelter for tourists at Taptapani.

restaurants.name: New Biryani Centre
restaurants.description: Informal biryani, tandoori & Chinese chicken recipes dished up in a down-to-earth location.
restaurants.address: Corporation Rd, Infront Of Biju Patnaik Park, Triveni Nagar

restaurants.name: Calcutta Roll
restaurants.description: Get some great Egg-Roll and Chicken-Roll from this pretty busy store.

restaurants.name: Girija Restaurant
restaurants.description: Great food can be found here.

restaurants.name: Vizag Juice Center & Lassi
restaurants.description: It's a small store but it serves some great juice and lassi.

restaurants.name: Pidha Hotel
restaurants.description: Some traditional food in pure traditional style

attractions.name: Ambara Chowk
attractions.description: About 40 km from Muzaffarpur, Ambara Chowk is situated in Saraiya Block on the Muzaffarpur - Rewa road. It is believed to be the home village of Amrapali, the famous Nagarvadhu (courtesan) of Vaishali. Amrapali was known for her beauty.

attractions.name: Baba Garibnath Temple
attractions.description: Baba Garibnath Temple situated in the center of the Muzaffarpur town is undoubtedly one of the most famous "Lord Shiva" temples. Its history goes like this-There was a landlord in ancient times who owned the land where the present temple is. There was a huge Banyan tree in the premises of the temple which provided shade and relief to many people. Due to bad financial condition the landlord had to sell his house to another person. The new owner seemed not too interested in Banyan tree so he ordered it to be cut down to clean the premises. While cutting the tree a "Shivling" was found within it, which got partly damaged due to the swing of the axe, and red water started oozing out from the "Shivling"! The Landlord was quite disturbed after seeing this and was not able to sleep for the entire night. In the morning "Baba Garibnath" appeared in his dreams and said that he was Baba Garibnath-one who has great sympathy for poor. He ordered him to establish the "Shivling" at the same place and

attractions.name: Mata Banglamukhi Temple
attractions.description: This temple, which is almost 300 years old, attracts many Tantric Hindus, especially on Navratri.

attractions.name: Chaturbhuj Asthan Temple
attractions.description: This is a temple with an interesting back story. It is said that in 1303, in a village called Turki, a big idol of Lord Chaturbhuj was found. We are told that there was a saint who was a great worshipper of Shiva and was also responsible for establishing a "Shivling" at the present Muzaffarpur (which was a village at that time). Lord Chaturbhuj came in his dreams and asked him to place him near "Lord Shiva", as he was not comfortable at Turki. The saint brought the idol all the way from Turki to Muzaffarpur on foot. Lord Chaturbhuj was established beside Lord Shiva under a tree and since then his regular worship started. It is also retold that there was a man from Patna who was another great worshipper of Shiva. Shiva came in his dreams and asked him to build a temple for him, saying he would get lots of fame and that he would be blessed with a child. As a result, he had the beautiful Chaturbhuj Temple built.

attractions.name: Hathilwa-Mathh
attractions.description: About 40 km from Muzaffarpur is the famous temple, Hathilwa-Mathh dedicated to Radha-Krishna. While the Badi Masjid at Company Bagh and the Gurudwara at Ramna are definitely worth a visit.

attractions.name: Kali Mata Temple Of Sikandarpur
attractions.description: This great temple is an icon of faith, worship and belief on Ma. It is situated on the south coast of "Gandak" river. Possibly, it was made in the year of 1932 by Darbhanga Maharaj Kamlesh Singh. Devotees come in masses to worship Ma.

attractions.name: Katra Garh
attractions.description: The place is situated nearly 35 km northeast of Muzaffarpur. Katra Garh was one of the states of the Mughal Empire during the reign of Akbar. It was then named as Akbarpur. Several idols, ornaments, earthen pots and other articles of historical importance have been found here in course of excavations.

attractions.name: Khudi Ram Bose Memorial
attractions.description: A memorial tablet has been raised in the memory of Khudi Ram Bose & Prafool Chaki who was executed at Muzaffarpur Jail in the year 1908 on the charge of throwing a bomb on Kingsford, the then British District & Sessions Judge of Muzaffarpur. The memorial tablet is situated opposite the present residence of the District and Sessions Judge, and the road where they threw the bomb was named as Prafool Chaki Marg. As a proof, a sign board is there just in front of the Red Cross building.

attractions.name: Rajkhand
attractions.description: It is situated about 5 km from headquarters of the Aurai block on Aurai-Saidpur road. There is an old temple of Bhairav Nath. A big cattle fair is held here every year on the occasion of Shivaratri festival.

attractions.name: Ram Chandra Shahi Museum
attractions.description: Ram Chandra Shahi Museum at Muzaffarpur was established in the year 1979. It has got its own building in the campus of Jubba Sahni Park. The museum possesses a very good collection including artifacts and numerous art-objects of varied nature. The museum is famous for its rich collection of rare postage stamps.

attractions.name: Ramna's Tripur Sundari Temple
attractions.description: Ramna's Tripur Sundari Temple attracts millions of Devotees Due to its aesthetic beauty and richness. A wealthy man, Shri Umashankar Prasad built this Beautiful and magnificent temple on 28th June 1941. It is said that it is really surprising to see that a man made temple attracts such big gathering of Devotees. This temple is also famous by the name of "Devi Temple" and Ma's beautiful idol mesmerizes one and all.

attractions.name: Shri Ram Temple
attractions.description: Shri Ram temple is one of the famous religious places. Situated at "Sahu Pokhar" in Muzaffarpur, its status was kept as one of the "Navratna" temples. It is said that it was made by artists from Rajasthan. Later Shri Shiv Prasad Sahu of Sahu family took over the order and care taking of the temple and still Sahu family is doing the same. Within the premises the biggest temple is of "Shri Ram and Mata Janaki". Beside that "Mahadev" temple is there whose Shivling is India's third largest Shivling. Devotees come in masses to offer their prayers in this sacred temple.

attractions.name: Simri Mai Temple Of Police Line
attractions.description: Near Muzaffarpur Engineering College in Avaas Nagar there is a famous "Devi Peeth", it is called Simri Mai. It is said that here to please "Bhagwati" coconut is broken. History tells that long ago there was an old lady who used to live in a hut near this place. During night she used to medidate for long hours. She took "Samadhi" on the 17th day of Navratra here. From that day this place has got a status of "Lokpeeth" and is famous by the name of "Simri Mai".

attractions.name: Balaram Mandir
attractions.description: Once a residence of Balaram Bose, a disciple of Sri Ramakrishna, the house hosts various events under the auspices of the Ramakrishna Mission, including the birthday celebrations of Ramakrishna, his wife Sarada Devi, and Swami Vivekananda. The house also has a collection of 1,800 books.

attractions.name: Belgachia Villa
attractions.description: A large garden house. Prince Dwarkanath Tagore bought it from an Italian around 1823. In 1846, when he died in England, it was discovered that he was heavily in debt due to his extravagant spending. To pay off his debts, his son Debendranath sold Belgachia Villa and other properties.

attractions.name: Clive House
attractions.description: Considered to be the first pucca brick and cement building in West Bengal, possibly built by the Dutch or Portuguese. What is known is that it was used by British soldiers when they first entered the country. Later, Robert Clive took the area over, renovated it, added a floor to the single-storey building, and made it his country house around 1757-60. The house is on a raised mound in otherwise flat surroundings. When Clive House was excavated, a variety of artefacts were recovered, including coins, terracotta figures, sculptures, pottery and intelligence on a Portuguese fort. The articles found could be of the Sena period or may alternatively have links with the ancient Chandraketugarh civilisation. The name "Clive House" also refers to the surrounding neighbourhood.

attractions.name: Cossipore Burning Ghat
attractions.description: Another major Hindu crematorium along the Hooghly River after Nimtala Ghat. It is where Sri Ramakrishna was cremated in 1886, and his remains are kept at "Sri Ramkrishna Paramhanshadev Samadhiprangan", literally the "burial ground of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa".

attractions.name: G.T.S. Tower
attractions.description: A masonry tower, built in 1831 for the Great Trigonometrical Survey conducted by George Everest, the namesake of Mount Everest. The tower is still maintained in good condition by the KMC, as a relic of the history of geographic survey in India.

attractions.name: Tala Tank
attractions.description: One of the largest overhead water reservoirs in the world, as well as the major water supplier to Kolkata for more than 110 years since its inauguration in May 1911 by Edward Norman Baker, the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal. Owned by the KMC, the reservoir is fed by Palta Water Works near Barrackpore and to send the water supply to the city. It covers with a capacity of {{convert|9.9|e6impgal|e6L

attractions.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
attractions.description: The famous Hindu navaratna (nine-pinnacled) temple dedicated to Goddess Kali, who is worshipped here as Ma Bhavatarini. The temple was inaugurated by Rani Rashmoni in 1855, and Ramakrishna Paramahamsa was the head and only priest of it from 1856 to 1886. He spent most of his life in the nahabat khānā (corruption of naubat xānā, meaning "drum house") chamber of the temple complex. After Ramakrishna's death, the temple complex had been taken over by the then-Government of Bengal, later the Government of West Bengal. It attracts thousands of worshipers around the year, especially on the day of Shyama Puja, Shiva Chaturdashi, Poyla Boishakh, Akshaya Tritiya, New Year's Day and Kalpataru Utsava. Beside the main temple, there are twelve shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva along the Hooghly River and a bathing ghat.

attractions.name: Panchavati
attractions.description: A complex of trees consisting of banyan (বট boṭ), peepal (অশ্বত্থ oshwottho), neem (নিম nim), amla (আমলকী āmlokī) and woodapple (বেল bel) trees. This is where Ramakrishna performed his advaitic sādhonā in 1865.

attractions.name: Rani Rashmoni Temple
attractions.description: The shrine dedicated to Rani Rashmoni, the founder of the temple.

attractions.name: Indian Statistical Institute
attractions.description: Founded by the statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1932, the institute is often considered one of the foremost centres in the world for training and research in statistics.

attractions.name: Geology Museum
attractions.description: Houses the fossil of the dinosaur species Barapasaurus tagorei native to India, with a life-sized replica skeleton on display.
attractions.address: Geological Studies Unit, Platinum Jubilee Auditorium

attractions.name: P.C.M. Memorial Museum & Archive
attractions.description: A museum hosted in the former residence of statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. It has five galleries dedicated to his life, along with 752 exhibits. It also has a preserved study room and living quarters of the statistician for their historical value.

attractions.name: Alambazar Math
attractions.description: Second monastery of Ramakrishna Order. Swami Vivekananda first put up here after coming back from abroad.

attractions.name: Baranagar Math
attractions.description: First monastery of Ramakrishna Order. After the death of Sri Ramakrishna, Swami Vivekananda and some of his other disciples permanently started to live here. Here, they decided to establish Belur Math for the first time.

attractions.name: Baranagore Ramakrishna Mission
attractions.description: Founded by Yogindranath Tagore (the disciple of Swami Brahmananda) in 1912. This institution celebrates many cultural programmes throughout the year. Many people come to watch those cultural events every year.

attractions.name: Sri Sarada Math
attractions.description: Daily ritual worships are performed here by the nuns. The birthdays of Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi, Swami Vivekananda, and other personalities are celebrated in this nunnery, besides the Hindu festivals. Religious discourse and lectures are also done regularly.

attractions.name: Udyan Bati
attractions.description: A monastery where Sri Ramakrishna lived from 1885 till his death in 1886. Kalpataru Utsav is celebrated every year at 1 January.

attractions.name: Nivedita Setu
attractions.description: A multi-span extradosed bridge, named after a disciple of Swami Vivekananda. See the Bally listing for details.

attractions.name: Vivekananda Setu
attractions.description: A long rail-cum-road bridge, commonly known as Bally Bridge (বালি ব্রিজ Bāli Brij). See the Bally listing for details.

attractions.name: Basri Shah Mosque
attractions.description: The oldest mosque in Kolkata, dating back to 1804. It has three domes and four minarets, and is affiliated with the Hanafi school of worship.

attractions.name: St. James Church
attractions.description: The only church serving Baranagar.

attractions.name: Adyapeath Temple
attractions.description: A three-pinnacled temple dedicated to goddess Adya, and the centre of a major religious controversy. It is said that Annada Thakur received a divine command that goddess Adya was buried under the Eden Gardens for thousands of years. He went there in 1928 and allegedly saw the statue of the goddess coming out from the ground. He consecrated the statue as the idol of this temple. But archaeologist Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay found that the statue was sculpted recently and not thousands of years ago, as Annada Thakur claimed. Later, many people got enraged to Thakur's deception, and the devotees of the goddess decided to immerse the statue to the Ganges to prevent further fury. The sanctum of the temple remained void till the consecration of the present idol.

attractions.name: Bamondas Mookerjee Kali Mandir
attractions.description: Bamondas Mookerjee is considered a leading industrialist of his time in brickfields and colliery. After purchasing 35 bighas (46,900 m²) of land at Cossipore from British attorney John Hart in 1894, he built a Kali temple in 1904. Daily worship and all rituals are practised here, although animal sacrifice is prohibited.

attractions.name: Kripamayee Kali Temple
attractions.description: A navaratna (nine-pinnacled) temple of Goddess Kali worshipped as Kripamayee (she who is merciful). There are twelve shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva.

attractions.name: Mahamilan Math
attractions.description: The Annapurna Temple and the Omkarnath Temple are two attractions here.

attractions.name: Parshwanath Jain Temple
attractions.description: Considered one of the most sacred Jain temples of worship in Kolkata. The temple also has a dharamshala equipped with modern facilities.

attractions.name: Pathbari Temple
attractions.description: A place where Chaitanya Mahaprabhu set his foot on his way to Puri in the early 16th century.

attractions.name: Sinthee More Ground
attractions.description: Hosts various local events throughout the year, including "Ajanta Circus" every winter.

attractions.name: Tala Lake Park
attractions.description: A parcel of greenery within the area's hustle.

restaurants.name: Arsalan Restaurant & Caterer
restaurants.description: Biryani and Mughlai food. Popular items: firni, mutton kosha, mutton boti kebab, chicken chatpata, mutton biryani, egg chicken roll.

restaurants.name: Food Plaza
restaurants.description: Vegetarian meals such as chole bhature.

restaurants.name: Haldiram's
restaurants.address: P420, Kazi Nazrul Islam Sarani, Kaikhali

restaurants.name: Sher-e-Punjab
restaurants.description: Quality Punjabi dhaba food. Chinese & Thai dishes also available. AC or open-air seating. Drinks served.

restaurants.name: Anandamayee Sweets
restaurants.description: Traditional Bengal sweets, curd (in Bengali "doi"), ice cream, dhokla, lassi.

restaurants.name: The Cric World
