restaurants.description: Multi-cuisine restaurant.

restaurants.name: Mahua
restaurants.description: The 40-year-old shop is known for creamy dahi (দই dai), and it often runs out of dahi every day.

attractions.name: Gol Gumbaz
attractions.description: It is the second-largest dome and largest unsupported dome in the world. It is the mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah and his family. It houses 5 cenotaphs (the original graves are located in the crypt below). Apart from Mohammed Adil Shah the cenotaphs belong to two of his wives, a mistress, a daughter and a grandson. It was built in 1659. At the top, the whispering gallery is a wonder where a tick of a watch can be heard from the opposite side of the dome over 200 feet away. It has a clock room for storing luggage.

attractions.name: Gol Gumbaz Mosque
attractions.description: The mosque is located on the western end of the Gol Gumbaz complex. The mosque is best viewed from the top of Gol Gumbaz. It is not accessible to visitors.
attractions.address: West side of Gol Gumbaz complex

attractions.name: Gol Gumbaz Site Museum
attractions.description: The Gol Gumbaz Site Museum is housed inside the Maqar Khana (drum house). It houses 8 galleries spread over two floors.

attractions.name: Jumma Masjid
attractions.description: A Mosque built by Ali Adil Shah I over 300 years ago for the entire city (jumma = public gathering). The Kuran inscriptions in gold is the main attraction. It can contain 2250 devotees. The intricately carved mihrab (the niche that points the direction to Mecca) is absolutely brilliant and is in stark contrast to the generally simple and bare architecture of the mosque itself (which is quite typical for the Deccan monuments)

attractions.name: Taj Bawdi (Tasabavadi)
attractions.description: A stepwell built by Ibrahim Adil Shah II in honour of his wife, Queen Taj Sultana, in the year 1620. The stepwell complex is approached through a large arched gateway. The complex also houses a hammam.

attractions.name: Jod Gumbaz
attractions.description: The tombs date back to the late Adil Shahi period and house the mortal remains of Khan Muhammad (octagonal tomb) and his spiritual advisor, Abdul Razzaq Qadiri (square tomb). Khan Muhammad was a commander of the Adil Shahi army. He betrayed them and favoured the Mughals. He was executed. The tomb was founded by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. The tomb complex also houses another smaller tomb. The complex is an active dargah and is visited by a large number of devotees.

attractions.name: Bara Kaman
attractions.description: Ali Adil Shah II began building a beautiful structure in 1627 with 12 arches in 12 rows, 12 columns, and 12 storeys tall, so that its shadow would fall on Golgumbaz in the evening. He died before it got completed. Nowadays, the unfinished monument can be visited.

attractions.name: Upali Buruj
attractions.description: This is a large structure around 80 feet tall built in 1584. Approachable by a long flight of stairs. Has 2 cannons at the top. You can get a 360-degree view of Bijapur town from the top.

attractions.name: Malik E Maidan
attractions.description: Translated as the king of the field, this is a huge cannon made of "Panchaloha" or five metals. It weighs 55 tons. This cannon helped Bijapur to defeat mighty the Vijayanagar empire in the battle of Rakkasatangadi (Talikot) in 1565. Today, it stands atop a bastion on the western wall of Bijapur Fort. It is located just north of the Mecca gate.

attractions.name: Ibrahim Rauza mausoleum
attractions.description: Ibrahim Rauza mausoleum is located outside the citadel walls but within the city limits. It houses the mausoleum of Ibrahim Adil Shah II. The complex is accessible via a gateway in the north. It houses the mausoleum on the east and a mosque on the west. Both the mosque and the mausoleum stand on an elevated platform with a water cistern in the middle. The mausoleum houses several graves. It was constructed in 1626.

attractions.name: Asar Mahal
attractions.description: This building was constructed in 1646 by Sultan Mohammed. It served as a justice hall. On the eastern side lies a large water body. There are several ruined structures in the complex. The Asar Mahal functions as a mosque.

attractions.name: Anand Mahal
attractions.description: This was private residence of the king with the queen, used for relaxing and pleasure, hence the name Anand Mahal. Today it houses several state government offices.

attractions.name: Gagan Mahal
attractions.description: Built by Ali Adil Shah I, the fifth ruler of Adil Shahi dynasty, in 1561. Gagan Mahal has two floors. The ground floor of Gagan Mahal was the place for the audience hall or durbar hall. The second floor of Gagan Mahal was used as a residence for the royal family. The front facade consists of a wide arch flanked by smaller arches. Today, the Gagan Mahal is beautifully restored with a large open space, which serves as a socializing place for locals and tourists.

attractions.name: Sat Mahal
attractions.description: A seven-storeyed palace. It is built by Ibrahim Adil Shah II around 1583 as a corner structure within the citadel, which also served as a watchtower. It is in ruins and only 5 of the seven stories survive.

attractions.name: Jal Mahal
attractions.description: The slender domed structure stands in the middle of a small water tank, which has dried up

attractions.name: Andu Masjid
attractions.description: The mosque was built in 1608/09 CE by I'tibar Khan, a noble in the court of Ibrahim Adil Shah II. It is a two-story building following the Indo-Islamic style of architecture. The mosque occupies the first floor and part of the ground floor. The remaining part of the first floor probably served as a sarai. The first floor contains an open terrace surrounded by low parapet. The structure is topped with a central ribbed dome and is flanked by four minarates.

attractions.name: Mehtar Mahal
attractions.description: Mehtar Mahal is a three-storied palace located on the southern side of the Bijapur citadel. It was constructed in the early 17th century under the rule of Ibrahim Adil Shah II. It follows the Indo-Saracenic style of architecture and is complete with slender minarates and ornate oriel windows. The palace is accessible through a giant, decorative teakwood door. The complex also houses an active mosque dating back to the sultanate period.

attractions.name: Fateh Darwaza
attractions.description: Southern gateway. Complete with bastions and guardhouses. Today traffic passes through this gateway.

attractions.name: Mecca Gate
attractions.description: Western Gateway. Totally encroached and not accessible.

attractions.name: Shahapur Gate
attractions.description: North-western Gate

attractions.name: Alapur Gate
attractions.description: Located near Gol Gumbaz next to the railway line. The gate is encroached.

attractions.name: Bahamani Gate
attractions.description: Northern Gate

attractions.name: Jahan Begum's Tomb
attractions.description: Jahan Begum was the wife of Muhammad Adil Shah. The tomb is unfinished and lies in ruins. The tomb, made of black, polished granite, is enclosed inside an arched pavilion, whose roof has long since collapsed. The four ruined minars stand at the corner of the enclosure. The entire area is a walled complex with a mosque on the southern side.

attractions.name: Ain-ul-Mulk's Tomb
attractions.description: The tomb contains the mortal remains of Ain-ul-Mulk, a nobleman in the court of Ibrahim I. He rebelled against the sultan and was killed in 1556. The structure stands on a square base and is topped with a hemispherical dome. Each of the four corners is provided with a domed pavilion. The outer walls are decorated with intricate stucco work. The facade has two tiers of three recessed arches on all its sides. The huge complex also houses a mosque and several other ruined structures.

attractions.name: Jahan Begum Palace
attractions.description: The palace consists of a single-storied structure. It is in ruins. A few arches and jalis are all that remains of the grand palace.
attractions.address: Located south-west of the Jahan Begum Tomb complex

attractions.name: Shivgiri
attractions.description: This is a new structure. At tall, it is the largest statue of Lord Shiva in the world.

attractions.name: Sangeeth Nari Mahal
attractions.description: It is a mystery how this great theater of music remained undiscovered until 1990, but when it was found the scientists were amazed about the acoustics used. In the memory of this find, Bijapur celebrates "Navarasapur Utsav" every 5 years where renowned musicians from across India come to perform

attractions.name: Saat Kabar
attractions.description: Saat Kabar (Literally meaning 60 graves) is believed to house the 63 graves of the wives of Afzal Khan, a general under Adil Shah II. According to legend, Khan had his wives murdered out of jealousy to prevent them from remarrying after he died in battle with Shivaji. The graves are arranged in a rectangular formation, with a mosque on the western side. To the west of the grave complex lies a small step well.

attractions.name: Bijapur Market
attractions.description: You can wander around this crowded and noisy market and see the vegetables and spices which are sold there.

restaurants.name: Kamat restaurant
restaurants.description: Excellent veg Indian food.

restaurants.name: Mysore Restaurant
restaurants.description: A nice vegetarian restaurant which is usually crowded for lunch. At the last floor, it offers a nice view of the market.

attractions.name: Shivappa Nayaka Palace
attractions.description: Situated on the banks of the River Tunga in the busy lanes of Shimoga is a 16th-century place built by Shivappa Naik of Keladi. A good architectural piece built with rose wood. The palace has a museum which has several interesting and rare archaeological collections of stone carvings and antiques from the Keladi period. Recovered idols of the Hoysala and Chalukya periods from the early 16th century to late 18th century are displayed here.

attractions.name: Shimoga railway station
attractions.description: Known for being one of the earliest railway stations in Karnataka. The second railway line of the Mysore Kingdom was a meter gauge line between Shimoga and Birur. Birur to Shivamogga line was launched on December 1, 1889, and the Shivamogga railway station received the first passenger train after it covered a distance of 37.92 miles on its inaugural run.

attractions.name: Sacred Heart Church
attractions.description: Situated in the heart of city, the church was renovated and is said to be second largest church in India with an area of 1800 m² (18000 square feet). Also equipped with a prayer hall with a capacity to hold up to 5000 people at a time.

attractions.name: Tyavarekoppa Lion and Tiger Safari
attractions.description: This place comprises a zoo and animals in the wild. Not a safari in the true sense of the word because the lions and tigers are housed in fenced enclosures and a sighting is guaranteed. The buses are well covered and take you into the wild every 30 min. All cameras are allowed at a cost of ₹150-400 depending on the type. The park also has a mini zoo housing hyenas, bears, porcupines, pythons, and alligators. You can see animals like lion, tigers, and deer. The zoo is also great, highlights being cheetahs, bears and peacocks.

attractions.name: Elephant Training Camp-Sakrebylu
attractions.description: On the way to Thirthahalli from Shimoga, you can hear elephants reciting their lessons. Yes, it's not a joke, in fact, here, you can find many elephants being tamed by professionals, for log lifting and other such work. Elephants from the adjoining forests bathe at this spot, before they re-enter their forest abode. Every morning these majestic creatures waddle down to the waters, and after having cleansed their bodies and having satiated their thirst, they leave the waters before the rays of the sun get stronger. They are off to deal with their day's routine, only to return the following day. To catch a glimpse of these elephants at play in the waters, get there before 9AM.

attractions.name: Mandagadde Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: you can hear the birds chirping. This place is a spot for birds migrating from places around the world. The place is surrounded by dense lush green forest and the flow of river Tunga has created a small island which adds to the beauty. The dense trees on the island provides shelter to migrating birds. Birds like Egrets, Bellakki Cormorant, Darter, Snake bird etc immigrate from different parts of the world during may season for breeding A high platform is built on the edge of river Tunga for bird watching. Boats are available for a closer watch.

attractions.name: Kudli Hoysala Rameshwara Temple
attractions.description: a 12th-century Shiva temple in early Hoysala construction in simple Vesara style.

attractions.name: Kuppalli
attractions.description: Birthplace of the renowned Kannada poet Kuvempu (Jnanapitha award winner). 18 km from Thirthahalii, it is a must-see place for its natural surroundings and well-kept house of Malnad architecture.

attractions.name: Ambuthirtha
attractions.description: Birthplace of the River Sharavathi. This river forms a beautiful waterfall at Jog. Sharavathi River is the major source of hydro electric power in Karnataka.

attractions.name: Kavaledurga Fort
attractions.description: Fort of Shivappanayaka, very close to Thirthahalli.

attractions.name: Nagara
attractions.description: A 16th-century place situated which was also known as "Beendanoor" in the 16th century. This place was the capital of the Keladi rulers and later on, was captured by Hyder Ali. Other places of interest are Shivappanaika Palace, Neelakenteshwara Temple, Devagana tank and Gudde Venkataramana Swamy Temple.

attractions.name: Agumbe
attractions.description: the 'Cheerapunji of Karnataka' gets the state's highest rainfall, is around 2 hours away from Shimoga, is an amazing village known for its forest resource, sunset spots, trekking passes, lakes, mountains. This one is a must see.

attractions.name: Honnemaradu
attractions.description: a small town alongside a reservoir, is tucked away in the lush greenery of the Western Ghats along the Sharavati backwaters near Sagar. Encompassing an area of 50 km by 80 km, this reservoir stretches as far as the eye can see. Honnemaradu, or “Golden Lake”, has some of the most spectacular views of the sunrise and sunset. Deep in a forest, without the slightest trace of civilisation, Honnemaradu is a haven for die-hard outdoors fanatics as well as those who want a complete break from the city. Hiking is permitted along roads only, and boats are available with a hired guide. Honnemaradu is 8km outside of Talaguppa. Some of the water sports activities here include coracling, canoeing, kayaking, and wind rafting. There are many travel groups who organise island camping and water sports.

attractions.name: Sri Shigandur Chaudamma Temple
attractions.description: The Chaudamma/Chaudeshwari temple in Sigandur in Sagara Taluk. Of note is the "launch" which is used to get across the backwaters of the Sharavathi river. This launch also transports vehicles, including cars and buses, and even people.

attractions.name: Guduvi Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: This bird sanctuary is unique for many reasons, but is the only sanctuary located in the midst of the dense forest. Guduvi is one of the 5 famous bird sanctuaries of Karnataka. The place is 16 km from Soraba taluka of Shimoga district. This bird sanctuary is spread over an area of 73.68 ha. As per 1993 survey, it is told that 191 varieties of birds are found at this place. A natural lake and the trees gives shelter to this birds. Some important birds found are White Pebis, Stone Bill, Egret, Cormorant, Snake bird, Heron. Different birds immigrate from other parts of the world in different seasons for breeding. A platform is built for a closer look of birds.

attractions.name: Kodachadri
attractions.description: A glorious and enchanting mountain provides the perfect escape from the hectic pace of everyday life. A paradise for trekkers, the place attracts lot of trekkers around Karnataka state. Kodachadri is situated at 435 m (1411 ft) above sea level and 115 km from Shimoga. A beatific hill abode that overlooks the panoramic Western Ghats. It is clothed with splendid evergreen forests. The first portion of the hill is very steep and difficult to ascend. On the west, the hill descends almost perpendicular for about 1300 m (4026 ft), meeting the Dakshina Kannada forests that lie below. The sea appears quite close, and on a clear day, you can also see the ships go by. The famous temple town of Kollur is 12 km away. The steep hills challenge the trekkers for an adventurous trekking experience. If you want to stay, you can go to Kalyani Chowka in Nittur and from there to Nisarga Dhaama. Manjanna always will be there for your help.

attractions.name: Bala Quila Fort
attractions.description: One of the few forts built in Rajasthan prior to the rise of the Mughals. Permission from the superintendent of police is required prior to visiting (however this is easy to get). As of Oct 2022, it is closed until 2023.

attractions.name: Bhartrihari Temple
attractions.description: A famous TapoBhumi of Raja BhartriHari

attractions.name: Government Museum
attractions.description: At former city palace.

attractions.name: Pandupol
attractions.description: A place where "Pandvas" stayed at the time of agyatvaas. There is a Hanuman temple which have the unique Hanuman idol (in the form of relax). It is placed in the middle of Sariska jungle.

attractions.name: Jaisamand Lake
attractions.description: It is a lake constructed by King of Alwar.

attractions.name: Sariska Reserve and National Park
attractions.description: One of the most famous national parks in India designated as a tiger reserve.

attractions.name: Silliserh lake
attractions.description: A decent lake named Siliserh lake along with government hotel (RTDC hotel) also named as Silliserh Hotel with restaurant and boarding facility except during rainy season boating facility is available round the year.

restaurants.name: Prem Pavitra Bhojnalaya
restaurants.description: Serves pure-veg food from ₹60-100.

restaurants.name: Inderlok Classic
restaurants.description: Veg dining.

attractions.name: Nizamabad Fort
attractions.description: Built in 10th century by the Rashtrakuta dynasty.

attractions.name: Sri Siddaganaga Mutt
attractions.description: Sri Siddaganaga Mutt is a main attraction of Tumkur, where around 8000 students are provided education, boarding and lodging free of cost.

attractions.name: Devaraayana Durga
attractions.description: Devaraayana Durga is a famous hill station and a religious place about 15 km from the City of Tumkur. Naamadachilume on the route to Devaraayana Durga is a protect forest area which has a deer park.

attractions.name: KaidaaLa
attractions.description: KaidaaLa has a famous Sri Chenna Keshava Swamy temple which dates back to the hoysalas. The temple was carved by Jakanaachari, who was the chief architect of belur temple. And Kaidala is the birth place of Jakanaachari.

attractions.name: Goravanahalli
attractions.description: Goravanahalli is one of the popular pilgrim centres located in the Koratagere taluk of Tumkur district.The temple here is dedicated to goddess Mahalakshmi. It is believed that the idol of Shri Mahalakshmi is self originated.

attractions.name: Hebbur
attractions.description: Shri Kamakshi Sharada Temple managed by Shri Kodandashrama Mutt of Hebbur, is situated in Tumkur Taluk, Tumkur district of Karnataka.

attractions.name: Siddara Betta
attractions.description: Siddara Betta Sacred Place where 9000 siddaru (holy spiritual men) made meditation and worship of Lord Shiva, They got mooksha (freedom) from this eternal world. It is extraordinary place for trekking. There are many useful ayurvedic herbs found here.

attractions.name: Kunigal Lake Temple
attractions.description: Two beautiful temples with a promenade on the lake.

restaurants.name: Pavithra Idly Hotel
restaurants.description: Idly at Kyatsandra is very famous all over Karnataka. Pavitra Idly Hotel offers delicious idlys as does Ravi Darshan Idly Hotel adjacent to Pavithra Idli Hotel. Both hotels are famous for serving hot tatte idlis throughout the day.

restaurants.name: Ashoka Restaurant
restaurants.description: South Indian vegetarian lunchː ₹70.

restaurants.name: Ganesh Upahar
restaurants.description: Good ambience.

attractions.name: Firoz Shah palace complex
attractions.description: Built by the Tughlaq Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1394, the palace is made from red sandstone and is an example of Seljuk architecture.

attractions.name: Rakhigarhi
attractions.description: A village and Indus Valley Civilisation archeological site. Although only 5% of the site has been excavated, many interesting artifacts have been found so far, including fire altars, toys, hunting and fishing tools, statues, a granary and a drainage system.

attractions.name: Blue Bird Lake
attractions.description: An important point for several migratory birds.

attractions.name: Deer Park
attractions.description: A 19-hectare (48-acre) park containing 20 blackbucks, 16 chital spotted deer and six sambar A part of the park is reserved for fodder.

attractions.name: Shatavar Vatika Herbal Park
attractions.description: A park which preserves many endangered species of herbs used in Ayurvedic medicine.

attractions.name: Bishnu Temple
attractions.description: This stone temple is built over a platform with a Bengal hut-shaped roof and arched entrance. The temple dates to about the 14th century CE. A stone, called "Narayan shila", is worshipped here as the deity of the temple. Earlier, a 12 armed Lokeswar Vishnu idol was being worshipped as deity, which has been stolen long before. The temple is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

attractions.name: Ghaghar Burhi Temple
attractions.description: A small shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali, it is the oldest temple of Asansol.

attractions.name: IISCO Steel Plant
attractions.description: Operated by Steel Authority of India (SAIL), the IISCO Steel Plant is one of the major steel plants in West Bengal.

attractions.name: Manoj Talkies
attractions.description: You can watch all newly released movies here. Good cinema hall; one of the biggest with a seating capacity of almost 1800.

attractions.name: Nehru Park
attractions.description: A beautiful park on the banks of the Damodar River. A cast iron statue of Nehru, casted by IISCO, is in the park. There is an eatery in the park. There's a big pond inside the park with boating facilities. You can get great views of the Biharinath Hill from the park.

attractions.name: Panifala
attractions.description: A picnic spot with a lake for boating and beautiful garden of flowers.

attractions.name: Satabdi Park
attractions.description: There are facilities for paddle boating and a few rides for children. Nice place to spend the evening.

restaurants.name: Gangar Hotel
restaurants.description: Dhaba type. No pretensions of luxury. Delicious Bengali food - dal-aloobhaja must try; fish range from rui and chital maachh to ilish and varieties of chhoto maachh; those who like can also order mangsho or dimer dalna.

restaurants.name: Garam Masala
restaurants.description: Bombay Hotel presents a complete vegetarian AC restaurant in the market place.

attractions.name: Atal Park
attractions.description: Well maintained park with gardens and fountains. Travelers and local populace enjoy this park for picnics and leisurely strolls.

attractions.name: Cantonment Church Tower
attractions.description: The Cantonment Church Tower is a church tower in Karnal city of Haryana, India. It stands near National Highway 1 of India. It has been declared as a historical monument by Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage. It was the tower of St. James' Church, Karnal, dedicated to St. James, one of disciples of Jesus Christ. The tower is 35m tall, and is surmounted by an ornamental cross.

attractions.name: Dargah Nuri
attractions.description: There is a Dargah Nuri at village Newal on Karnal-Kunjpura road. This Dargah was built in memory of Hazrat Sufi Shah Alama Nur Mohd of Delhi, and is managed by Managing Committee, village Newal.
attractions.address: Karnal-Kunjpura road, Village of Newal (10km NE of Karnal)

attractions.name: Kalander Shah's Tomb
attractions.description: A shrine of famous Sufi saint Baba Bu Ali Shah kalander. An enclosure with mosque and a reservoir with fountains.

attractions.name: Karn Taal
attractions.description: A park

attractions.name: Miran Sahib's Tomb
attractions.description: A tomb for the memory of a saint, Sayad Mohd AKA Miran Sahib, a saint who died in 899 AD.

attractions.name: Old Fort
attractions.description: Constructed in 1764. Now the office and residence of the Tehsildar (Tax Inspector).

attractions.name: Sita Mai Temple
attractions.description: A temple dedicated to the Nepali Hindu Goddess Sita.
attractions.address: Village of Sitamai (25 km NW of Karnal)

restaurants.name: Jhilmil Dhaba
restaurants.description: North Indian and Indo-Chinese cuisine.

restaurants.name: Pizza Hut
restaurants.description: Delivery.

attractions.name: Bardhaman Science Centre
attractions.description: Founded in 1994, the Science Centre aims at promoting the amazing facts and mechanisms of science through various models and displays. Some of the popular exhibits include the mystery behind flying objects, a game of energy balls, the wonders of chemistry show and many more very interesting exhibits. The main attractions of the centre are 3D Theater, Science Shows, Science Magic & Miracle shows, Taramandal Shows and Sky Observation through Telescope. The centre has galleries on Fun Science, Human Performance and Life Science Corner. The science centre also organises daily shows (with separate tickets), which includes a 3D show (₹25), a Science show (₹10) and a Taramondal show (₹10).

attractions.name: Golapbag
attractions.description: Literally "rose garden", Golapbag is a botanical garden built in 1883 by Raja Bijoy Chand Mahtab. Once a place of retreat for the Rajas, Golapbag later became the main campus of the University of Burdwan. It contains several ancient structures including the Hawa Mahal, a domed pavilion located on an island.

attractions.name: Ramnabagan Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: Originally a botanical garden, Ramnabagan became a deer park with spotted deer in 1978. It was declared a wildlife sanctuary by 1981. The sanctuary consists of animals from different parts of erstwhile Bardhaman district. Ramnabagan forest, with its tall and stately teak and sal forest having mesophytic associates like kadbels, dumur and jam, is a solace from the din and bustle of urban life.

attractions.name: Bardhaman Clock Tower
attractions.description: Built by Burdwan Development Authority (BDA), the clock tower resembles the Big Ben of London.

attractions.name: Curzon Gate
attractions.description: Officially known as Bijoy Toran (বিজয় তোরণ Bijaẏ Toraṇ), literally the "victory gate". The ceremonial gateway was built to commemorate the visit of Lord Curzon, the viceroy of India, to Bardhaman in 1903. It was constructed by Bijoy Chand Mahtab, the head of Bardhaman Raj. The arched gateway is supported by eight columns and has two side arches. The side arches are topped with sitting lions and the central arches are crowned with three female figurines, with swords, boats, and sheaves of corn in their hands. On either side of the female figurines atop the eight columns are eight urs. After independence in 1947, the gateway came to be known as Bijoy Toran and the new name is inscribed in Bengali atop the arch. There are a pair of statues in front of the gate.

attractions.name: Krishak Setu
attractions.description: A bridge on the Damodar River connecting Bardhaman to Bankura and Arambagh. It was built in 1978.

attractions.name: Bardhaman Railway Overbridge
attractions.description: One of the longest cable-stayed bridges in West Bengal, the four-lane railway overbridge connects Bardhaman to Katwa. It was constructed by Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) and was inaugurated in 2019, replacing the century-old two-lane railway overbridge. It takes after the iconic Vidyasagar Setu in Kolkata.

attractions.name: Bardhaman Rajbati
attractions.description: Built by Mahtab Chand Bahadur in the 19th century, on a site of a Mughal fort. It was constructed by Burn and Company. Later, Uday Chand Mahtab handed over the building to the state government, and now it houses an administrative department of the University of Burdwan.

attractions.name: Mazhar of Pir Baharam
attractions.description: It houses the tomb of a Persian Sufi saint Pir Bahram Sakka. He was known for providing water to thirsty travellers and was called Sakka (Persian word for one who gives water). He spent his last days in Bardhaman and died in 1663 or 64. However, the place is more known for the resting place of Sher Afghan Khan, the first husband of Noor Jahan (then known as Meherunissa), who later on went on to become the wife of Mughal Emperor Jahangir. Buried next to Sher Afghan is Qutubuddin Koka. They both died fighting each other in a battle at Bardhaman in 1610. Sher Afghan (originally known as Ali Quli Khan Istajlu) was a jagirdar under Akbar and then under Jahangir. In 1594, he married Meherunissa. In 1610, Sher Afghan revolted against Jahangir and Jahangir sent Qutubuddin Koka to control the rebellion. The rebellion was brought under control but both Sher Afghan and Qutubuddin Koka died in the battle. Their tombs are next to each other. The tomb of Pir Baharam predates that of Sher Afghan and

attractions.name: Nawab Bari
attractions.description: A Mughal-era tomb complex housing the grave of Khaja Anwar, the amir of Azim-us-shaw. Khaja Anwar was killed in an ambush in 1698. Later in 1715, Mughal Emperor Farrukhsiyar built a huge tomb in over for Khaja Anwar. Today walled tomb complex along with a mosque and several structures still stands and is popularly known as the Nawab Bari. The complex is centred around a huge tank, which has long dried up. At the centre of the dry tank is an arched pavilion popularly known as Hawa Mahal. The Hawa Mahal is connected to the mainland by an arched causeway. The entrance is through a two-storied gateway in the north. On the western side of the complex is a mosque. The triple dome mosque, which is still functional, has beautiful stucco works on its walls. The star attraction of the complex, the magnificent tomb, lies on the southern end of the complex. The single domed square structure is flanked on the corners by slender minarets. The square structure on the other hand is flanked by two rect

attractions.name: Sainbari
attractions.description: Aged mansion and the site of the infamous Sainbari murder of 1970.

attractions.name: Sarbamangala Temple
attractions.description: Established by Maharaja Kirtichand Ray, the temple is dedicated to Ma Sarbamangala, the family deity of the Bardhaman royal family. The temple followed the navaratna (nine-pinnacled) plan. Over the years the temple has largely been modified but many of the temple's beautiful terracotta panels have survived. It is an active temple with several other structures.

attractions.name: 108 Shiva Temples
attractions.description: The complex consists of 108 temples dedicated to Lord Shiva and they are arranged in a rectangular formation around two ponds. The temples follow the at-chala style of architecture, the four corner temples are octagonal. The Shivalingas in all the temples are made of black stone. The temple complex was constructed in 1788 by Maharani Bishnu Kumari Devi, wife of Tilak Chandra Bahadur of the Bardhaman royal family. The temples were repaired in 1965 by Birla Jana Kalyan Trust. The unscientific repair leads to the temples losing their antiquity along with their grace and beauty. The temple complex is under the control of the 108 Shiv Mandir Trust Board. The complex also houses two statues of Nandi Bull. one white and another black. There is also a waiting shed for pilgrims and devotees. There is also a set of 108 bells near the entrance.

attractions.name: Christ Church
attractions.description: The oldest church in Purba Bardhaman district, built in 1816 under the auspices of Charles Stuart. It is a small church with a brick-red facade. The church is crowded during Christmas.

attractions.name: Bardhamaneswar Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple housing a huge Shivalinga. The Shivalinga is not very high but has a huge circumference and is often referred to as Moṭā Śib Mandir (মোটা শিব মন্দির). According to legend, the temple was founded by the legendary trader Chand Sadagar of Mansamangal fame. Today it is an active temple with modified and added structures hardly anything remains of its history.

attractions.name: Kankaleshwari Temple
attractions.description: A navaratna (nine-pinnacled) temple with terracotta reliefs. Although the temple is said to be ancient, the idol of Goddess Kali was found in 1913 from the Damodar River. The idol has eight hands with four at each side.

attractions.name: Sri Guru Nanak Gurdwara
attractions.description: The sole gurudwara of Bardhaman, and one of the few Sikh places of worship in West Bengal. The gurudwara was built by Civil Surgeon Lt. Col. Harikishan Singh between 1930-35 in memory of his parents.

attractions.name: Krishnasayer Park
attractions.description: One of the most famous natural attractions in the city. It is surrounds by an artificial lake, which was dug way back in 1691 by Raja Krishnaram Ray. The ancient garden surrounding the 33-acre lake only exists in bits and pieces. The lake offers boating facilities. the lake is a venue for several fairs and carnivals.

attractions.name: Meghnad Saha Planetarium
attractions.description: Named after the famous scientist Meghnad Saha, the planetarium came up in 1994 with the major instruments being gifted from Japan. The planetarium has a capacity of 90. Six shows of 35 minutes duration are held daily. The show happens when there are at least 10 people.

attractions.name: Sadarghat
attractions.description: Literally "primary ghat", Sadarghat provides an amazing view of the Damodar River. A lot of people arrive at the sandy area to enjoy picnic.

attractions.name: Town Hall
attractions.description: It was built somewhere between 1890 and 1894. It preserves the legacy of Lala Bansogopal Nandey. It was handed over to the Bardhaman Municipality in 25 May 1984. The original structure occupied an area of . In 1990, the building was restored and extended. The present sitting capacity of the hall is 485 people. There is a children's park in front of the Town Hall.

attractions.name: Barasat Stadium
attractions.description: This football stadium is used mostly for Calcutta Football League matches. It is also used for several district-level, state-level and sometimes national level tournaments.

attractions.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Uddyan
attractions.description: This is a renovated amusement park containing lakes, gardens, fountains, monuments, and statues. Contains boat rides and toy train rides. There is also a light and sound show from 6:00 pm to 7:00 pm .

attractions.name: Bangpur Durga puja
attractions.description: Celebrated widely.

attractions.name: Mosque of Makhdum Shah Sharif-ud-din
attractions.description: Named after a Muslim saint of 14th century.

attractions.name: Pawapuri
attractions.description: Sacred place for the Jain community. Famous for beautiful temples of God Mahavir.

attractions.name: Tomb of Malik Ibrahim Vaya
attractions.description: A beautiful ancient tomb constructed on top of the rocky hill. Nearby are the ruins, which are believed to be ruins of Jarasandh Jail. The beautiful natural view from the top of the hill is very attractive.

attractions.name: Tomb of Saint Baba Maniram
attractions.description: The scene around the temple is very calm and beautiful.

attractions.name: Fulwari
attractions.description: The orchard of the old Darbhanga dynasty, located in Chatariya village about a kilometer away from Kadirabad at the banks of Adhwara river. An ancient village of rich cultured of Mithila is known as Purushottampur alias Chataria. Later on the nick name Chataria was popularly accepeted by the region. The Unique geographical condition provides natural safety for the village .It is almost surrounded by the river Choti Baghmati & It is the boundary of river which separates the village from Dist H.Q Darbhanga. In its thousand mts of surroundings the village enjoys the locality of followings:- LNM University, KSS University, Bus stand DBG, Agricultural Market, Eng College & main market of Darbhanga Tower.

attractions.name: Ahilya Asthan
attractions.description: It is famous historical temple dedicate to gautam rishi's wife ahilya. This temple is situated about 3 km. South of Kamtaul Railway Station in Jale Block; and around 18 km from darbhanga.you must go there Pankaj Jha

attractions.name: Rajnagar
attractions.description: Rajnagar is the very important historical place of Madhubani District. But it is erasing its beauty in lack care. There is the ruins of place, Hathi Ghar, Girza Mandir, Shiv Mandir, Hanuman Mandir, Kali Mandir, Kamakhya Mata Mandir, Rani Ghar, Rani Pokhar, Naulakha etc. The Kali Mandir of Rajnagar is very famous because of its beauty. It is made from white Marbles (Sangmarmar) in 1929. There is a Ghanta also in the Rajngar. pankaj jha

attractions.name: Kala Amb
attractions.description: The site of the Third Battle of Panipat between the Marathas and Afghans. According to legend, it was marked by a black mango tree which has since disappeared.

attractions.name: Kabuli Bagh
attractions.description: A mosque and garden built by first Mughal emperor Babur to commemorate his victory over Ibrahim Lodi.

attractions.name: Tomb of Ibrahim Lodi
attractions.description: The last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, Ibrahim Lodi's tomb is quite a simple looking rectangular tomb with a small flight of steps.

attractions.name: Hemu's Samadhi Sthal
attractions.description: A memorial to 16th century King Hemu, who defeated the Mughals in October 1556 and briefly took control of Delhi before being defeated in a repeat battle around a month later.

attractions.name: Gautam Buddha University
attractions.description: A landmark educational institution known for its architecture, cultural events, and open green spaces.

attractions.name: Surajpur Wetland and Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: A protected nature reserve, home to over 180 species of birds. Best for bird watching and eco-tourism.

attractions.name: Buddh International Circuit
attractions.description: India’s first Formula One race track, hosting motorsports events, karting, and driving experiences. Since 2023, it has been the home of the MotoGP Grand Prix of India.

attractions.name: Shaheed Vijay Singh Pathik Sports Complex
Noida Film City
attractions.description: A hub for films and television in India. It has been the location for many Bollywood and Indian films.

attractions.name: Kiran Nadar Museum of Art
attractions.description: Established in January 2010, it is India's first private museum of art exhibiting modern and contemporary artworks.

attractions.name: Stupa 18 Gallery
attractions.description: An art gallery where you can see and buy art pieces by various new as well as established talented artists. Open to public, this gallery has interesting exhibitions every month.

attractions.name: Rashtriya Dalit Prerna Sthal and Green Garden
attractions.description: The green expanse along the banks of river Yamuna includes a mini-museum called the Rashtriya Dalit Smarak (National Dalit Memorial). It includes the idols consecrated for the people who devoted their life for humanity, equality and social justice, including Buddha, Kabir, Birsa Munda, Jyotirao Phule, B.R. Ambedkar, Periyar etc.

attractions.name: Shivalik Park
attractions.description: The garden that hosts the annual Noida Flower Show.

attractions.name: Okhla Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: A haven for over 300 bird species, especially waterbirds.

attractions.name: Worlds of Wonder
attractions.description: There are three sections within the modern theme park complex: a water park, an amusement park and a go-karting track.
attractions.address: Sector 38A, Entry Gate No. 11, Entertainment City

restaurants.name: The Yellow Chilli
restaurants.description: One of celebrity chef Sanjiv Kapoor's restaurants. The food is varied and is inspired by dishes from all over India though there is an emphasis on Punjabi and Mughlai cuisine.
restaurants.address: 1 A/31 H Block. Commercial Market, Sector 63

restaurants.name: Punjabi by Nature
restaurants.description: P-19, Sector 18 (Atta Market). The local outlet of the exuberantly hip Punjabi chain, serving up tandoori lobster and vodka golgappas next to crazy decor that's half dhaba, half crystal chandeliers and indoor waterfalls. While there's a premium to pay for the surroundings, the food is solid and the makki ki roti with sarson ka saag is worth the price tag. ₹500, more if you sample the booze or seafood.

attractions.name: Akshardham Temple
attractions.description: One of the biggest religious attractions in Central Gujarat, this temple has pink stones with beautiful carvings and is surrounded by beautiful gardens and awesome fountains. A laser water show, the first of its kind in the world, is a must to see. Spread over nine hectares.

attractions.name: Capitol Complex
attractions.description: A magnificent domed building.

attractions.name: Children's Park
attractions.description: An attraction for children and tourists, the Children's Park in Sector 28 has a mini train and a lake with boating facilities.

attractions.name: Deer Park
attractions.description: Near Sarita Udyan, at Indroda village, nice place to visit for both children and adults.

attractions.name: Sarita Udyan
attractions.description: In sector 9 and along the river front is the lovely Sarita Udyan, a great spot for picnickers. The entire area is being developed to provide full recreational facilities.

attractions.name: Indroda Nature Park
attractions.description: A nature park having a dinosaur fossil park, a botanical garden, a deer park, a blue whale skeleton on display, a cactus garden, a bird cage and places for family picnic.

attractions.name: Mahatma Mandir
attractions.description: A museum dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi.

attractions.name: GIFT City
attractions.description: Business district with world class hotels and facilities.

attractions.name: Dindigul Fort
attractions.description: This 280-foot-tall fort was constructed in 1605 by Madurai King Muthi Krishna Naicker and Thirumalai Naicker. It was a witness to many wars between rulers like Tipu Sultan and the English men.

attractions.name: Sirumalai - Hill Resort
attractions.description: This is an economical Hill resort and a picnic spot for weary travellers. This is on the way to Natham 25 km from Dindigul city. This place is accessible from Madurai also. Though the uphill journey is for a brief time, the 18 hair-pin bends provide the real thrilling experience, characteristic of a trip to a hill station. The entire locale is green and lush and the climate is cool/warm. Sirumalai provides an opportunity to go on trekking and hiking. Beautiful scenic view of saathiyar river basin and Dindigul town delight the visitors. Vellimalai Temple is the famous destination for devotees. Sanjeevi Hills, famous in Indian Epic Ramayana is also in the vicinity. Bus service and private cabs are available from Dindigul city.

attractions.name: Gandhigram Rural Institute
attractions.description: Established in 1956, Gandhigram Rural Institute was founded by two Gandhians; Dr.T.S.Soundaram and Dr.G.Ramachandran. They followed the Mahatma Gandhi’s ‘Nai Talim’ system of education. Gandhigram Rural Institute has developed academic programmes in Rural Development, Rural Economics and Extension Education, Rural Oriented Sciences, Cooperation, Development Administration, Rural Sociology, English and Communicative Studies, Tamil and Indian Languages. The Gandhigram Rural Institute has a campus of nearly 200 acres in a rural setting, nestling in one of the enclaves of the beautiful Sirumalai range. To its west are chains of mountains including the beautiful Kodaikanal Hill Station. Lying North of Madurai, Gandhigram is easily accessible by rail and road. The climate of the place is pleasant all through the year and the panorama of nature surrounding Gandhigram is pleasing. The nearest railway station is 2 km away in Ambathurai, the nearest railway junction is 11 km away from Dindigul a

attractions.name: Thadikombu - Perumal Temple
attractions.description: It is 5 km from Dindigul on the way to Karur. The main deity is Lord Alagar and the main festival is during the Tamil month of Chitrai.(April–May)

attractions.name: Begambur Big Mosque
attractions.description: This is a famous mosque in Begambur and is around 200-300 years old.

attractions.name: Sri Kottai Mariamman Kovil
attractions.description: This is an ancient temple believed to be 200 years old and the idol is believed to have been installed by the King Tipu Sultan. There are many deities in this temple like Mariamman which is the main deity, Vinayaka, Muruga, Madurai Veeran, Kali and Durga. The temple structure is in the form of a square. The temple is run by a board of Trustees.

attractions.name: Kasi Visalakshi-Vishwanathar Temple
attractions.description: In Kunnuvarankottai or Kunnapatti (Pronounced as "Kannapatti") is 8 km from Batlagundu on the Batlagundu-Usilampatti road. (It is to be noted that locals pronounce the village name as Kunnuvarankottai or Kannapatti (Tamil:கண்ணாப்பட்டி. This area is also referred to in the biography of Sri Sacchidananda Bharathi-I). This is the birthplace of the 25th Pontiff of the Sringeri Sarada Peetam Sri Sacchidananda Bharathi I. There are regular buses every 30 minutes from Batlagundu bus stand to Usilampatti (the bus stop is better known as Kannapatti(Tamil:கண்ணாப்பட்டி)). It is advisable to visit the temple in the mornings from 7:30AM- 11:30AM. Shri V.Viswanathan is the priest of this temple. One main advantage of this temple is that it is just very close (walkable distance) to the main Batlagundu- Usilamapatti road and is easily accessible to devotees. There are budget restaurants in Batlagundu that serve South-Indian dishes. An added attraction is the point of confluence of the three rivers Vai

attractions.name: Kamakshiamman Temple
attractions.description: In Devadanapatti is 8 km away on the Batlagundu-Peryakulam road. The deity here is called as Moongilanai Kamakshi. There are regular buses from Batlagundu bus stand (every 10 minutes) to Periyakulam. (the bus stop is Devadanapatti).

attractions.name: Athoor: Kamarajar Lake
attractions.description: The Kamarajar Lake is in the western part of Athoor Village located in the Kamarajar Valley in Western Ghats. There are places to stay near the lake. They are 'Candle House Resort' a family home stay, 'Double Dutch Resort' and 'Cardamom House' on the shore of Athoor Kamarajar Lake. Athur is a village 3 km west of Sempatti in between Dindigul and Batlagundu. Sembatti is 12 km south-west of Dindigul and 48 km north of Madurai. The Kodaganar River, a tributary of river Kaveri runs through the village. There is a cave temple here for Lord Sadayandi, another ancient Kasi Viswanatha temple and a 50-year-old, beautiful Catholic church.

attractions.name: St.Joseph Church
attractions.description: This 100-year-old church was constructed between 1866 and 1872. This is the head church of all other Roman Catholic churches in Dindigul District.

attractions.name: Dindigul - Nagal Nagar perumal Temple
attractions.description: This is a Vishnu temple which is in Nagal Nagar near the railway station.

attractions.name: Soundararaja Perumal Temple - Vadamadurai
attractions.description: On the busy Dindigul – Trichy National Highway, at about 18 km from Dindigul, a road branches out in the right side. Vadamudarai is the name of the village, where the famous Soundararaja Perumal Temple is situated. The famous temple is situated at the heart of the small village. The temple has been renovated and has separate sanctum sanctorum for Perumal and Soundaravalli Thayar, Chakkarathalvar, Lakshmi Narasimar, Baktha Anjaneyar, Andal, Vishvaksena and Garuda are the other deities to be worshiped in the temple.

attractions.name: Vedasandur
attractions.description: Vedasandur is 20 km from Dindigul (on south), 75 km from Madurai (on South), 60 km from Karur (on north), 85 km from Trichy (on east, and 45 km to Palani (on west). This was a place where hunters used to sell their goods in the olden days - Vedasandur means "Hunter's open market". The Kudakanar river, a tributary of Cauvery river goes through the centre of town. Another attraction is a very tall 51 feet idol of Lord Anjaneyar in the temple that is situated in the campus of Seethamaram Nalroad -(ARR Engineering India (P) Ltd. There are many other places of worship and also a tobacco research center in this town.

attractions.name: 7 Dollar church
attractions.description: A famous Mother Mary Church. Got to visit during the Christmas celebration. Also famous for the Thursday Infant Jesus Fellowship. A very famous Paska (passover) is celebrated for three days by the entire area.

attractions.name: Anjaneyar Temple
attractions.description: This is said to be 300-year-old temple built by Queen of Madurai Rani Mangamma. The idol will be half buried when the water is in full flow here. This temple is near the Peranai bridge (see site below) and regulator constructed by the British.

restaurants.name: Venu's Briyani
restaurants.description: The most popular restaurant that serves this unique dish

restaurants.name: Thalappakatti
restaurants.description: Equally famous and has a longer history

restaurants.name: Koli Nadar
restaurants.description: A non-veg restaurant that offers a wide variety

attractions.name: Elgandal Fort
attractions.description: Elgandal Fort is a historic hilltop fortress situated on the banks of the Manair River in the Elgandal village near Karimnagar. It serves as an architectural testament to the Deccan region's multi-dynastic past, having changed hands across five different empires over several centuries

attractions.name: BB Zarda Co
attractions.description: It has a very famous history been there since Nizams. It was established in 1935 by Bhoga Mallaiah.

attractions.name: Garshakurthy Village
attractions.description: Garshakurthy is famous for Nizam's Khila. Temples: Sri Venkateswara temple, Markandeya temple, Hanuman temple. Parvati Lake is famous for boating and is a joyful place for friends.

attractions.name: Devi ki Tekri
attractions.description: The Tekri can be climbed by two ways one through steps and another through slope. We took the slope way which was more lengthy but easier to climb.In the south of the tekri is the temple of Tulja (Elder) Mata. According to historians it is contemporary to the temple of Chamunda Mata. In the temple is the half statue (upper portion) of the Goddess Tulja. Goddess Tulja and Chamunda are both sisters.

attractions.name: Mitha Talab
attractions.description: Lake.

attractions.name: Baba dham'
attractions.description: Baba dham' is the main attractive religious temple and status symbol of Sonipat. It is a very neat and clean temple with many small temples within such as Sani Mandir, Sai Mander, Radha Kirshan Mandir, and more. This temple is found in the outskirts of Sonipat near the Kami-Bhuri road.

attractions.name: Khwaja Khizr Tomb
attractions.description: Red sandstone and 'kankar' block monument with highly decorated floral ceiling.

attractions.name: Mata Chintpurni Mandir
attractions.description: Religious followers have visited here for centuries in order to pray at the lotus feet of Mata Shri Chhinnamastika Devi.

attractions.name: Mughal Buildings
attractions.description: At the outskirts of the city one can enjoy the site of Mughal Buildings which lie unprotected. Among them is the Mosque of Abdullah Nasir-ud-din, who was a descendant from Mushid of Iran kijjar makkbara. In Sonipat Kijjar Makkbara is the most beautiful garden having very rich historic legend associated with it. When visiting Sonipat, one must see this site. It is reserved heritage and open to the public during the whole year. It is very beautiful with green grass and beautiful plants. It is situated in outer part of the city in village Jatwada.

attractions.name: Sai Dham
attractions.description: A very religious site as well as a popular tourist destination.

attractions.name: Shankar Kui
attractions.description: One of the oldest temples in Sonipat.

attractions.name: Shri Ram Temple
attractions.description: One of the oldest, if not the oldest temples in Sonipat.

attractions.name: Yamuna River
attractions.description: The river flows besides the rural belt of the city with its holy waters which turn into a Black Nullah after entering the National Capital Delhi. It also acts as a natural boundary also between state of Haryana and the state of Uttar Pradesh.

attractions.name: Mojoland
attractions.description: Mojoland is a picnic destination with a lot of adventures, such as a water park, amusement park, aero sports park, snow park, and theme park.

attractions.name: Industrial areas and textile clusters
attractions.description: Ichalkaranji’s identity is deeply tied to its textile industry, and many visitors come specifically to observe the city’s power loom clusters and cooperative mills. While most factories are not formal tourist attractions, some owners may allow guided visits if arranged in advance. The buzzing sound of looms and the dense network of workshops offer a unique glimpse into one of India’s most productive textile hubs.

attractions.name: Shri Siddheshwar Temple
attractions.description: Dedicated to Lord Shiva, known for its peaceful atmosphere and traditional architecture. It’s a popular spot for morning and evening visits, especially during festivals like Mahashivaratri.

attractions.name: Shri Datta Mandir
attractions.description: Dedicated to Lord Dattatreya, an important spiritual centre for locals. The temple complex becomes especially lively during Datta Jayanti.

attractions.name: Shahu Stadium
attractions.description: A local sports ground that hosts athletic events, kabaddi matches, and community gatherings.

attractions.name: Qila Mubarak
attractions.description: Constructed by Raja Dab during the period 90-110 AD.

attractions.name: Gurudwara Hazi Ratan
attractions.description: Grain Market, Bhatinda

attractions.name: Chitrakoot
attractions.description: The place where Ramcharitra Manas was written. Very nice place to visit for greenery and to see ancient caves where Lord Ram spent around 12 years with his wife Sita and brother Lakshman. Here you can see River Mandakini Ramghat, Tulsi Mandir, Bharat Milap, Bharat Koop, H Dhara Mountain, Kamadgiri mountain etc. Very nice place for pilgrims. On Amavasya and Purnima you'll get heavy crowd in Chitrakoot.

attractions.name: Maihar
attractions.description: Sharda Mata temple.

attractions.name: Dharkundi
attractions.description: Not many people know, but it is a wonderful place with greenery all around and a peaceful meditative atmosphere.

attractions.name: Ramban
attractions.description: Ancient remains of temples and Hanumanji Mandir
attractions.address: 15 km from Satna on Rewa Road

attractions.name: Matha Kuar Shrine
attractions.description: Matha Kuar Shrine is the place of Buddha's last sermon. After having a meal of pork (some say mushroom) in a nearby place (present-day Fazilnagar) Buddha fell severely ill. The meal was provided by a blacksmith named Chunda and is considered as Buddha's last meal. Despite his illness, he travelled to Kushinagar to deliver his last sermon. After the sermon, he told his disciples to prepare his deathbed in the nearby sal forest. Over the years and centuries, several kings and nobles have paid tribute to Buddha by creating several structures. Today it is a protected site under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). It follows a typical plan of a Buddhist Vihar complete with a central courtyard surrounded by cells or small rooms. On the western end of the vihar is a small white temple like structure complete with a porch supported by pillars. It houses a 3-metre-tall statue of Buddha in bhumisparsha (earth touching). The monolithic statue was made of Gaya blue stone and was excavated du

attractions.name: Mahaparinirvana Temple
attractions.description: This site marks the exact location of Buddha's death. A 1965 built temple stands above the ancient ruins, The temple consists of a shrine and stupa was built to commemorate the 2,500th anniversary of the death of Buddha. The shrine houses a 6.1-metre-long Buddha statue in reclining posture, with the head towards the north. It is made out of a single stone and rests on a stone couch. The statue was discovered in 1877 in a heavily damaged state and fragmented parts. The fragments were joined to create the statue. The temple stands on the ruins of a Buddhist vihar. The ruins were part of century-old structures constructed by various kings as a tribute to the Buddha. These structures have been excavated by various archaeological digs. The earliest part of the excavated ruins dates back to the time of Asoka with subsequent additions by the Kushans (50 -241 CE) and Guptas (320 – 647 CE). Today the Mahaparinirbab site is the main attraction for pilgrims and tourists. Throughout the day thousa

attractions.name: Ramabhar Stupa
attractions.description: This is the site of the cremation of Buddha. After his death, his mortal remains were cremated about a km east of his death place. Later a giant stupa was built at the location which was unearthed during an archaeological dig in 1910. The central stupa is surrounded by smaller votive stupas and several vihar like structures. Devotees frequent the place and do the parikrama of the stupa and perform various other rituals.

attractions.name: Relic Distribution Site
attractions.description: After the cremation, the mortal remains of Buddha were kept as relics and distributed among eight kings of north India. There are no historical remains at the site but it is believed that the distribution happened at this very place. Today a small shrine housing a statue of Buddha marks the site. It is located off the main road and barely visited by pilgrims and tourist.

attractions.name: Museum
attractions.description: The site museum displays artifacts collected from the different archaeological sites of Kushinagar. Over 1,300 artifacts are on display, including those made of stone, terracotta and bronze items along with coins and other artifacts.

restaurants.name: Yama Cafe
restaurants.description: The owner, Mr. Roy, is an old-timer at Kushinagar and can advise on many things there.

attractions.name: Khandadhar Waterfall
attractions.description: This is the highest waterfall of Odisha and among the highest of India. Khandadhar means the edge of a sword. The fall looks like a hanging sword from a distance. The water falls from a height of . Pauri Bhuiyas are the tribal people who inhabit the place . The folklore says, Goddess Kankala Devi ate everything that comes across her . Be it soil, trees or stones. Pauri Bhuiyas placed her on a rock, which she ate as well. A hole was created on that rock and the water started falling from that hole. The falling water resembles a sword, hence came the name Khandadhar.

attractions.name: Balod
attractions.description: Balod houses Prachin Kila or oldest Palace, Mandir and Sati Chabutra.

attractions.name: Devbaloda
attractions.description: Famous for its ancient Shiv Mandir.

attractions.name: Kharkhara
attractions.description: Its major attraction is a Dam which is 1,128 m long and is located on the Kharkhara River.

attractions.name: Maitri Bagh
attractions.description: It features landscaped garden which is a joint initiative of Indian and Russian government and a Zoo. The highlights of Zoo are exotic animal and avian species, lake, toy trains and others. The musical fountain on the island in the artificial lake is a dynamic spectacle which responds to the music in a way that interprets the style and rhytmm of the musical performance. As the music plays, jets of water shoot in the air, twist, sway, pirouette, pulse, drum and skip with the beat - each movement lit by brilliant colours.

attractions.name: Nagpura
attractions.description: It is a site to visit exquisite Jain temples and Pasharwanath Tirth.

attractions.name: Tandula
attractions.description: The prime attraction of this place is a Dam on Tandula River. It is an exciting picnic spot also.

attractions.name: Clock Tower
attractions.description: The Clock Tower is a historic structure at the centre of Anantapur town, built in memory of martyrs of the Indian freedom movement by the initiative of M. Ramachandra Naidu (then district judge) and other citizens. The height of the Clock Tower is which signifies the year 1947. The Tower's radius is which signifies the date 15th. The Tower has 8 faces which signifies August, the eighth month of the year.

attractions.name: Arts college
attractions.description: to see ancient architecture.

attractions.name: ISKCON Temple
attractions.description: 7 km from town. Built by ISKON in 2008.
attractions.address: Hare Krishna Land, Somuladoddi, National Highway No.7

attractions.name: Cheruvu Katta
attractions.description: This is holy place both for Hindus and Muslims. All the temples are located at one place (Shirdi Sai Baba, Ayyappa, Ganesh & Hanuman Temples)

attractions.name: Sarada Temple
attractions.description: It's a peaceful place and very famous.

attractions.name: BlooMoon Restaurant
attractions.description: An outdoor restaurant.

restaurants.name: Bajjis
restaurants.description: Famous restaurant in 1st road, near Police Training College

restaurants.name: Biriyani
restaurants.description: Spice touch

restaurants.name: Dosa
restaurants.description: Famous restaurant in I-Road Gurukrupa hotel, Sujatha Hotel, Indira Priyadarshini Hotel-near Clock Tower.

restaurants.name: IDLY
restaurants.description: Famous restaurant in Oldtown near to Krishna theatre, near Srikantam Circle.

restaurants.name: LASSI
restaurants.description: Famous restaurant near Medinova Hospital.

restaurants.name: Oaligalu
restaurants.description: In old town.

restaurants.name: Poori
restaurants.description: Opposite Emrald Restaurant..

restaurants.name: Gongooras
restaurants.description: At national highway towards Bangalore.

restaurants.name: Spice Touch
restaurants.description: near Hotel Sapthagiri Balla is also good.

restaurants.name: Adi Murthi Tiffin Center
restaurants.description: Famous for varieties of dosas.

restaurants.name: Madhu Restaurant
restaurants.description: Famous for North Indian dishes.

attractions.name: Cactus Garden
attractions.description: The garden is not very big but well maintained and is quite different from most other gardens you are likely to come across. There are a staggering number of cactus varieties, many of which tower over you.

attractions.name: Bibrod Tirth
attractions.description: A major Jain temple centred around the first tirthankara (spiritual teacher) of Jainism, Adinath.

attractions.name: Shwetambar Temple
attractions.description: A Jain temple dedicated to Lord Parshvanath, the 23rd tirthankara (saviour) in the religion. In the middle of the temple is an over 13 foot high statue of Parshvanath, made out of a single emerald stone.

restaurants.name: Checkers Café
restaurants.description: Sandwiches, burgers, pasta, pao bhaji, Chinese, sundae ice cream and other snacks.

attractions.name: Kathiyavadi Panchapandavar Ancient Jain Hill and Caves

restaurants.name: Arcot Chairman Sweet
restaurants.description: It's the most famous for its Makkan Peda, a sweet unique to Arcot.

restaurants.name: Sri Durga Bhavan
restaurants.description: Vegetarian Restaurant that serves South Indian dishes.

attractions.name: Balaram Mandir
attractions.description: Once a residence of Balaram Bose, a disciple of Sri Ramakrishna, the house hosts various events under the auspices of the Ramakrishna Mission, including the birthday celebrations of Ramakrishna, his wife Sarada Devi, and Swami Vivekananda. The house also has a collection of 1,800 books.

attractions.name: Belgachia Villa
attractions.description: A large garden house. Prince Dwarkanath Tagore bought it from an Italian around 1823. In 1846, when he died in England, it was discovered that he was heavily in debt due to his extravagant spending. To pay off his debts, his son Debendranath sold Belgachia Villa and other properties.

attractions.name: Clive House
attractions.description: Considered to be the first pucca brick and cement building in West Bengal, possibly built by the Dutch or Portuguese. What is known is that it was used by British soldiers when they first entered the country. Later, Robert Clive took the area over, renovated it, added a floor to the single-storey building, and made it his country house around 1757-60. The house is on a raised mound in otherwise flat surroundings. When Clive House was excavated, a variety of artefacts were recovered, including coins, terracotta figures, sculptures, pottery and intelligence on a Portuguese fort. The articles found could be of the Sena period or may alternatively have links with the ancient Chandraketugarh civilisation. The name "Clive House" also refers to the surrounding neighbourhood.

attractions.name: Cossipore Burning Ghat
attractions.description: Another major Hindu crematorium along the Hooghly River after Nimtala Ghat. It is where Sri Ramakrishna was cremated in 1886, and his remains are kept at "Sri Ramkrishna Paramhanshadev Samadhiprangan", literally the "burial ground of Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa".

attractions.name: G.T.S. Tower
attractions.description: A masonry tower, built in 1831 for the Great Trigonometrical Survey conducted by George Everest, the namesake of Mount Everest. The tower is still maintained in good condition by the KMC, as a relic of the history of geographic survey in India.

attractions.name: Tala Tank
attractions.description: One of the largest overhead water reservoirs in the world, as well as the major water supplier to Kolkata for more than 110 years since its inauguration in May 1911 by Edward Norman Baker, the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal. Owned by the KMC, the reservoir is fed by Palta Water Works near Barrackpore and to send the water supply to the city. It covers with a capacity of {{convert|9.9|e6impgal|e6L

attractions.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
attractions.description: The famous Hindu navaratna (nine-pinnacled) temple dedicated to Goddess Kali, who is worshipped here as Ma Bhavatarini. The temple was inaugurated by Rani Rashmoni in 1855, and Ramakrishna Paramahamsa was the head and only priest of it from 1856 to 1886. He spent most of his life in the nahabat khānā (corruption of naubat xānā, meaning "drum house") chamber of the temple complex. After Ramakrishna's death, the temple complex had been taken over by the then-Government of Bengal, later the Government of West Bengal. It attracts thousands of worshipers around the year, especially on the day of Shyama Puja, Shiva Chaturdashi, Poyla Boishakh, Akshaya Tritiya, New Year's Day and Kalpataru Utsava. Beside the main temple, there are twelve shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva along the Hooghly River and a bathing ghat.

attractions.name: Panchavati
attractions.description: A complex of trees consisting of banyan (বট boṭ), peepal (অশ্বত্থ oshwottho), neem (নিম nim), amla (আমলকী āmlokī) and woodapple (বেল bel) trees. This is where Ramakrishna performed his advaitic sādhonā in 1865.

attractions.name: Rani Rashmoni Temple
attractions.description: The shrine dedicated to Rani Rashmoni, the founder of the temple.

attractions.name: Indian Statistical Institute
attractions.description: Founded by the statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1932, the institute is often considered one of the foremost centres in the world for training and research in statistics.

attractions.name: Geology Museum
attractions.description: Houses the fossil of the dinosaur species Barapasaurus tagorei native to India, with a life-sized replica skeleton on display.
attractions.address: Geological Studies Unit, Platinum Jubilee Auditorium

attractions.name: P.C.M. Memorial Museum & Archive
attractions.description: A museum hosted in the former residence of statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis. It has five galleries dedicated to his life, along with 752 exhibits. It also has a preserved study room and living quarters of the statistician for their historical value.

attractions.name: Alambazar Math
attractions.description: Second monastery of Ramakrishna Order. Swami Vivekananda first put up here after coming back from abroad.

attractions.name: Baranagar Math
attractions.description: First monastery of Ramakrishna Order. After the death of Sri Ramakrishna, Swami Vivekananda and some of his other disciples permanently started to live here. Here, they decided to establish Belur Math for the first time.

attractions.name: Baranagore Ramakrishna Mission
attractions.description: Founded by Yogindranath Tagore (the disciple of Swami Brahmananda) in 1912. This institution celebrates many cultural programmes throughout the year. Many people come to watch those cultural events every year.

attractions.name: Sri Sarada Math
attractions.description: Daily ritual worships are performed here by the nuns. The birthdays of Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi, Swami Vivekananda, and other personalities are celebrated in this nunnery, besides the Hindu festivals. Religious discourse and lectures are also done regularly.

attractions.name: Udyan Bati
attractions.description: A monastery where Sri Ramakrishna lived from 1885 till his death in 1886. Kalpataru Utsav is celebrated every year at 1 January.

attractions.name: Nivedita Setu
attractions.description: A multi-span extradosed bridge, named after a disciple of Swami Vivekananda. See the Bally listing for details.

attractions.name: Vivekananda Setu
attractions.description: A long rail-cum-road bridge, commonly known as Bally Bridge (বালি ব্রিজ Bāli Brij). See the Bally listing for details.

attractions.name: Basri Shah Mosque
attractions.description: The oldest mosque in Kolkata, dating back to 1804. It has three domes and four minarets, and is affiliated with the Hanafi school of worship.

attractions.name: St. James Church
attractions.description: The only church serving Baranagar.

attractions.name: Adyapeath Temple
attractions.description: A three-pinnacled temple dedicated to goddess Adya, and the centre of a major religious controversy. It is said that Annada Thakur received a divine command that goddess Adya was buried under the Eden Gardens for thousands of years. He went there in 1928 and allegedly saw the statue of the goddess coming out from the ground. He consecrated the statue as the idol of this temple. But archaeologist Rakhaldas Bandyopadhyay found that the statue was sculpted recently and not thousands of years ago, as Annada Thakur claimed. Later, many people got enraged to Thakur's deception, and the devotees of the goddess decided to immerse the statue to the Ganges to prevent further fury. The sanctum of the temple remained void till the consecration of the present idol.

attractions.name: Bamondas Mookerjee Kali Mandir
attractions.description: Bamondas Mookerjee is considered a leading industrialist of his time in brickfields and colliery. After purchasing 35 bighas (46,900 m²) of land at Cossipore from British attorney John Hart in 1894, he built a Kali temple in 1904. Daily worship and all rituals are practised here, although animal sacrifice is prohibited.

attractions.name: Kripamayee Kali Temple
attractions.description: A navaratna (nine-pinnacled) temple of Goddess Kali worshipped as Kripamayee (she who is merciful). There are twelve shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva.

attractions.name: Mahamilan Math
attractions.description: The Annapurna Temple and the Omkarnath Temple are two attractions here.

attractions.name: Parshwanath Jain Temple
attractions.description: Considered one of the most sacred Jain temples of worship in Kolkata. The temple also has a dharamshala equipped with modern facilities.

attractions.name: Pathbari Temple
attractions.description: A place where Chaitanya Mahaprabhu set his foot on his way to Puri in the early 16th century.

attractions.name: Sinthee More Ground
attractions.description: Hosts various local events throughout the year, including "Ajanta Circus" every winter.

attractions.name: Tala Lake Park
attractions.description: A parcel of greenery within the area's hustle.

restaurants.name: Arsalan Restaurant & Caterer
restaurants.description: Biryani and Mughlai food. Popular items: firni, mutton kosha, mutton boti kebab, chicken chatpata, mutton biryani, egg chicken roll.

restaurants.name: Food Plaza
restaurants.description: Vegetarian meals such as chole bhature.

restaurants.name: Haldiram's
restaurants.address: P420, Kazi Nazrul Islam Sarani, Kaikhali

restaurants.name: Sher-e-Punjab
restaurants.description: Quality Punjabi dhaba food. Chinese & Thai dishes also available. AC or open-air seating. Drinks served.

restaurants.name: Anandamayee Sweets
restaurants.description: Traditional Bengal sweets, curd (in Bengali "doi"), ice cream, dhokla, lassi.

restaurants.name: The Cric World
restaurants.description: Multi-cuisine restaurant.

restaurants.name: Mahua
restaurants.description: The 40-year-old shop is known for creamy dahi (দই dai), and it often runs out of dahi every day.

attractions.name: Etawah Safari Park
attractions.description: One of the main attraction of the city, with a breeding centre for the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo leo). Here, you walk through the cage paths where the lions and other animals are moving freely in the jungle.

attractions.name: National Chambal Sanctuary
attractions.description: Home to various endangered species like the gharial, Gangetic dolphin, red-crowned roof turtle and various species of birds.

attractions.name: Durgadi Fort
attractions.description: A fort Which was built by Shivaji Maharaj near Ganesh Ghat at Kalyan, on the Ulhas river bank. Built in Under the Marathas reign (1760-72), a new gate about 70m to the south of the Ganesh gate was opened near the mansion of Ramji Mahadeo Biwalkar. Also here is the 'Eidga' Mosque.
attractions.address: Kalyan-Ahmednagar Hwy, Annabhau Sathe Nagar, Tilak Nagar

attractions.name: Kala Talav
attractions.description: A famous & historical lake.

attractions.name: Lonad Caves & ancient Sun Temple
attractions.description: Caves as old as the ones at Ajanta and Ellora, on a hill near Lonad village. The Sun Temple is in the village.

restaurants.name: Hotel Relish
restaurants.description: Hotel Relish is a family restaurant and bar serving Indian, Chinese, Punjabi & Mughlai dishes.

restaurants.name: Gurudev Hotel
restaurants.description: AC/non AC

restaurants.name: Kokan King Family Garden Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: Konkan King also has a resort and water park to chill out with your family and friends. When it's the season, you can enjoy boating with a mini-train for your children, bird sanctuary and lots of amusement games. Specialists in Chicken Handi and fresh seafood. Grab some vadapavs late in the night till the early morning just outside the eastern side of the railway station.

restaurants.name: Metro Junction Mall
restaurants.description: Fast foody. 3rd level of mall is reserved for food court.

restaurants.name: Prasad Hotel
restaurants.description: 3½ star rated with high brand infrastructure and hospitality, service. Prasad hotel is near Katemanivli. Kolhapuri bhaji is most tasty food served here.

restaurants.name: Relax Garden NX
restaurants.description: This is one of the best hotels in town for dinner. 4 km away from the station.

attractions.name: Bamkimanjali Stadium
attractions.description: A football stadium hosting games of Calcutta Football League, Naihati Gold Cup and I-League.

attractions.name: Boro Maa Kali Temple
attractions.description: The most noteworthy religious spot in the city. It came up in 1923, when a young Brahmin built a tall Kali idol after visiting Nabadwip and witnessing the grandeur of the idols there. Every year thousands of devotees from various places in West Bengal flock to the city during Kali Puja.

attractions.name: Rishi Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's Residence and Museum
attractions.description: The birthplace of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, a Bengali novelist known for composing the patriotic song Vande Mātaraṁ.

attractions.name: Jubilee Bridge
attractions.description: A former rail bridge over the Hooghly River.

attractions.name: Lohagarh Fort
attractions.description: Built in by Jat ruler Maharaja Suraj Mal in the 18th century. It's one of the few forts in India not conquered by the British, despite them laying siege to it for six weeks in 1805. The fort is surrounded by a moat, which has remained intact to this day. The approach is through two gates.

attractions.name: Jawahar Burj
attractions.description: It was built by Raja Jawahar Singh in 1765 to commemorate his victory over the Mughals at the Battle of Delhi (1764)

attractions.name: Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: It is also known as Ghana, is a world famous sanctuary developed by Maharaja of Bharatpur. It is also one of the few Natural UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India. The best time to see the park is in October to February when there is a lot of migratory birds, otherwise it can be relatively bird free. The best times for bird spotting are early evening and morning. Admission is ₹200, an optional driver is ₹100 per hr, and an optional guide is ₹150 per hr. Another way to see the park is to hire a bike at your hotel or entrance (approx ₹40/day).

attractions.name: Ganga Maharani Temple
attractions.description: Built by Maharaja Balwant Singh in 1845.

attractions.name: Jama Masjid
attractions.description: The main mosque of Bharatpur. Built by Hindu Jat rulers. Sandstone structure.

attractions.name: Laxman Temple
attractions.description: 400 years old temple.

restaurants.name: Buns and Tins
restaurants.description: Open air restaurant.

attractions.name: Kanwar Lake Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: Contains rare and endangered migratory birds and has a large oxbow lake.

attractions.name: Gandhi Samadhi [Memorial]
attractions.description: The only second place where last remains of Mahatma Gandhi is kept and over that a memorial is built.

attractions.name: Jesal-Toral Samadhi
attractions.description: At nearby town named Anjar, you can visit this legendary temple famous amongst locals.

attractions.name: Kandla Port
attractions.description: One can take permit from Port officials to visit one of the biggest port of India.

restaurants.name: Dabeli
restaurants.description: This food item is very famous around the area. Have it from any food shop or even small time food corner. Its tasty and worth it.

restaurants.name: South Indian Food at Chawla Cafe
