restaurants.description: The oldest restaurant in the city. It serves fabulous south Indian dishes and snacks. Must visit for a foodie.

attractions.name: Raichur Fort
attractions.description: A hill fort surrounded on three sides by a double row of low circuit walls. It was built without the any cementing material. The inner wall has two gateways: the Sailani Darwaza on the west and the Sikandari Darwaza on the east. The outer fortifications contain five gateways: Mecca Darwaza on the west, the Naumngi Darwaza on the north, the Kati Darwaza on the east, the Khanrlak Darwaza on the south and the Doddi Darwaza on the south-west. Inside the fort, there are old buildings and mosques of considerable archaeological interest, several of them containing inscriptions commemorating their erection during the later Bahmani and the Adil Shahi periods.

attractions.name: Maliabad Fort
attractions.description: A town 5 km from Raichur city, known for its historically important fort, Vishnu temple, two life size elephants carved in white granite and other monuments

attractions.name: Cholamandal Artists' Village
attractions.description: Set up by a group of artists to serve as a recluse for artists of all genres. This village offers the ambience needed for creativity to flow and is inhabited only by artists. The village offers guesthouse facilities exclusively for artists from elsewhere so that they could also benefit from the environment provided by the place. A must-visit for those who appreciate the finer things of life.

attractions.name: Lok Bhavan
attractions.description: The official residence of the Governor of Tamil Nadu appointed by the President of India, formerly the Raj Bhavan. The Lok Bhavan complex features a collection of architecturally distinctive buildings, including the spacious Bharathiar Mandapam, along with expansive lawns where state and official functions, as well as meetings, are held.

attractions.name: Pallikaranai Wetland
attractions.description: A Ramsar site and the only surviving wetland ecosystem of the city. The marsh contains several rare or endangered and threatened species and acts as a forage and breeding ground for thousands of migratory birds from various places within and outside the country.

attractions.name: Church in honour of Our Lady of Health
attractions.description: Founded in the 16th century after the three miracles: the apparition of Mary and Jesus to a slumbering shepherd boy, the curing of a lame buttermilk vendor, and the survival of Portuguese sailors assaulted by a violent sea storm.
attractions.address: Beach Rd, Ashtalakshmi Garden, Besant Nagar

attractions.name: St. Thomas Garrison Church
attractions.description: St. Thomas, referred to as Didymus, in the Gospel of St. John is one of the twelve disciples of Jesus Christ. He is one of the prime witnesses to the resurrection of Jesus. St. Thomas Mount is associated with St. Thomas, the apostle of Christ, who is believed to have been martyred here. The mount is commonly called in Tamil Parangi Malai or Bhringi Malai. History says 2000 years ago, a saint Parangi lived here (parangi in Tamil is used to refer to a white person). According to local myth, St. Thomas was one of the first Christians to reach India and to preach Christianity. He is believed to have reached South India in AD 52, and spent the last years of his life in a cave on this hill. Tradition states that Thomas was assassinated by an arrow in 72 CE, by persons hostile to him. Thus, the hillock acquired the name St. Thomas Mount. Over time Anglo-Indians predominated in this area. A small relic-filled Church built in 1523 by the Portuguese stands at the summit of the 300 feet (90m) hig

attractions.name: St. Thomas Church on the Mount
attractions.description: St. Thomas Mount or Parangimalai is a mountain in southern Chennai. It is associated with St. Thomas, one of Jesus's 12 apostles. St. Thomas is believed to have been killed here. At the northern foot of the mount, is a gateway of four impressive arches surmounted by a cross bearing the inscribed date 1547. A flight of 160 steps leads up to the summit of the mount. There are 14 Stations of the Cross on the way to the summit. A small shrine dedicated to "Our Lady of Expectation" (Mother Mary) is built atop the mount. It was built in 1523.

attractions.name: Anjaneyaswami Temple
attractions.description: This temple is very famous because of the deep veneration shown for Lord Hanuman. One amazing fact about this temple is the 32-feet (10-m) idol of Anjaneyar that is moulded out of a single rock.

attractions.name: Ashtalakshmi Temple
attractions.description: The temple is dedicated to Lakshmi, the consort of Vishnu. Astha, in Sanskrit, is the number eight and eight forms of Lakshmi are worshipped in the Ashtalakshmi temple.

attractions.name: ISKCON Temple
attractions.description: The temple of the Hare Krishnas in Chennai.

attractions.name: Marundeeswarar Temple
attractions.description: This temple is believed to have been built in 11th century and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is believed that the temple was also visited by Saint Valmiki, who authored the Hindu epic Ramayana. The temple has two entrances, one from East Coast Road and the other from West Tank Street, both adorned by 5-tiered gopuram (gateway tower). The entrance from the West Tank Street has got three gates whereas the entrance from the East Coast Road has only one gate. The temple occupies an area of about - numerous images adorn the pillars of the temple, while stucco figures adorn the gopurams. The Mandapam (hall) housing the Somaskanda form of Shiva has 36 massive pillars adorned with carvings.

attractions.name: Madhya Kailash
attractions.description: Very popular for locals. Ananda Vinayagar Lord Ganesha, the bestower of happiness, sits right in the centre of Parameshwar, Ambikai and Thirumal.
attractions.address: Sardar Patel Rd, Rajiv Gandhi Salai, Adyar

attractions.name: Prathyangira Devi Temple
attractions.description: A magnificent temple built for Goddess Prathyangira, in her incarnation of Shri Maha Prathyangira Devi. She is considered to be a powerful repellent of the influences generated by witchcraft, and is said to have the power to punish Adharma. This is one of the few temples of Prathyangira and the only temple for Shri Maha Prathyangira Devi, the Shanta form. Regular pujas are offered every day and special pujas during festive season.

attractions.name: Shirdi Sai Baba Temple
attractions.description: Built in the memory of the revered saint Sai Baba of Shirdi, this temple is among the two shrines dedicated in Sai Baba's name in the city.

attractions.name: Birla Planetarium
attractions.description: Built in memory of B.M. Birla, the well known industrialist and visionary. Adjoining the planetarium is a Periyar Science and Technology Museum which will be of interest to students and other science scholars.

attractions.name: Kart Attack
attractions.description: A centre dedicated to fulfilling the speed maniac's desire for a thrill in a safe and secure environment. The first go-karting centre of Chennai, this has placed Chennai on the go-karting map of India and has been instrumental in creating a few go-karting champions also.

attractions.name: Breezy Beach
attractions.description: It is smaller and less popular than Elliot's Beach. This beach is not as commercialised as Elliot's Beach and is hence more quiet and peaceful. Evenings are delightful and with gentle breezy here, Lots of tourists are attracted towards this beach. Since the residential area around this beach is occupied predominantly by young professionals working in the IT/ITES industries (that thrive in the area), this beach has turned into a hot spot for them. It is less polluted and eco-friendly. For those who look for a calm, cool and breezy place to relax, this beach is the best place in Chennai.
attractions.address: Water Land Drive Rd, Lakshmana Perumal Nagar, Valmiki Nagar

attractions.name: Edward Elliot's Beach
attractions.description: This is spread along the coast down south from the Marina Beach. It is also the night beach for Chennai youth. This beach is comparatively quieter. At the end of this beach are the Velankanni church and the Ashtalakshmi temple. Good roads, pavements, walking tracks illuminated sands make visiting this beach a real pleasure.

attractions.name: Golden Beach
attractions.description: The first amusement park in Chennai, just about 11 km away from Adyar. Still a landmark of Chennai, this park offers over 40 odd rides for the fun seeker.

attractions.name: Guindy National Park
attractions.description: The park area stands close to 280 hectares. Guindy Park is probably the smallest national park in the country and one of the few Indian national parks within the city limits. The park is inhabited by more than 20 species of trees, about 14 varieties of shrubs and more than 14 species of woodland mammals. The place also houses many species of rare birds and amphibians. The dry deciduous forests of Guindy are lined with tree species like Amona Squamosa, Atlanta Monophylla, Feronia Limonia and Azadirachta India. The popular park animals include species like antelopes (blackbucks), elephants, spotted deer, Indian civets, jungle cats, hedgehogs, pangolins and golden jackals. Some rare bird species found in the park include black-winged kites, honey buzzards and pariah kites. The park is also home to many reptile and amphibian species.

attractions.name: Guindy Snake Park
attractions.description: Founded by one of the prominent wildlife conservationists Romulus Whitaker. The park houses a number of snake species, lizards, crocodiles and turtles. The park breeds more than 30 species of Indian snakes. Some of the most sought-after species include King Cobra, Indian Rock Python, Reticulated Python, Adders and Vipers. In addition to the snakes the park also breeds species of lizards, crocodiles and turtles. The museum in the park premises contains preserved specimens of many reptiles and amphibians. They have a snake display show 4 times daily, and live snakes of different species are shown to the audience with a voiceover in 3 languages (English, Tamil and Hindi).

restaurants.name: Bella Ciao
restaurants.description: Italian-owned and run, authentic Italian food. The famous wood fired oven pizza, home made pastas, steaks and salads.
restaurants.address: Lounge Beach Garden, #4, Shri Krishna Enclave, Kottivakkam

restaurants.name: The Good Spot
restaurants.address: 30/31, Second Main Road, Kasturibai Nagar, Adyar

restaurants.name: The Great Kabab Factory
restaurants.description: Specialities: Galoutti Kabab, Tangri and Murgh Malai Kababs, Fish and Mutton Kababs. They serve alcohol and have valet parking.
restaurants.address: Radisson G R T Hotel, G.S.T. Road, St Thomas Mount

restaurants.name: Navaratna
restaurants.description: India restaurant serving Royal Indian Cuisine. Live Ghazal performances. A Private dining room is available for up to 12 persons and an intimate bar for pre-dinner drinks.
restaurants.address: 1 GST Rd, Le Royal Meridien, St. Thomas Mount

attractions.name: Bangar Museum
attractions.description: A small museum with a good collection of stone artifacts acquired from different places of Rajasthan. It exhibits ancient, historical and artistic items such as costumes, coins, and arms.

attractions.name: Chandra Choodeswarar Temple
attractions.description: An ancient Shiva temple. The exact history of the temple is unknown. This is the only temple in Northern Tamil Nadu that uses a golden chariot for temple functions.

attractions.name: Rajaji Memorial House
attractions.description: The birthplace of C. Rajagopalachari, fondly called "Rajaji".

attractions.name: Vizianagaram Fort
attractions.description: An early 18th-century square-shaped fort, built by Maharaja Vijaya Rama Raju in 1713. It has two main gates, of which the main entrance is elaborately decorated. There are various temples and palaces within the fort, as well as a victory tower.

attractions.name: Ganta Stambham
attractions.description: The iconic octagonal clock tower of Vizianagaram. Built in 1885, the tower was partly inspired by the Big Ben in London.

attractions.name: Pedda Cheruvu
attractions.description: The central lake of Vizianagaram.

attractions.name: Ramanarayanam
attractions.description: Despite being newer than the Vizianagaram Raj era, Ramanarayanam is one of the most-visited attractions in and around the city, attracting millions of pilgrims. Built by the NCS Charitable Trust on a 15-acre site, the temple is based on the Ramayana and is shaped like a bow and arrow.

attractions.name: Kotla Vijayabhaskara Reddy Botanical Garden
attractions.description: Tents are available for longer visits. The paved walkways take you through the 19 sections (Vanaja) in the Patil. The bamboo and palm sectors are major attractions, with varieties of bamboo trees separated by a 3-metre (10 ft) distance. Special signboards are erected at each bamboo variety indicating its generic and scientific names. The palm sector has diverse species. Here you can find a variety of flowers in abundance, such as yellow and purple cosmos, blue salvia, red raselia, etc.

attractions.name: Shilparamam
attractions.description: Designed as a contrast to the futuristic Cyber Tower that lies across the road, the crafts village of Shilparamam ("sculpture village") guards the entrance road to HITEC City. The intent is to showcase and preserve the old. There is a bazaar where you can buy assorted handicraft and art work. There is also an entire village where you can find realistic-looking sculptures of villagers carrying out their traditional crafts. You can also find a rock museum which contains natural rock formations that allegedly look life-like. Pay by UPI or cash as credit cards are not accepted by most shops. Also next to Shilparamam is Shilpa Sandhya Vedika, a location for eating and shopping.

attractions.name: Aalankritha Art Gallery
attractions.address: 41 A, Kakateeya Hills Ext. of Jubilee Hills Road No. 36

attractions.name: Hussain Shah Wali Dargah
attractions.description: The mausoleum of Hussain Shah Wali, a Sufi saint of Golconda during the Qutb Shahi dynasty. He is best known for the Hussain Sagar in Hyderabad. The dargah was built by Abdullah Qutb Shah in his honour.

attractions.name: Ameenpur Lake
attractions.description: A major sport for birdwatchers, with various resident and migratory birds like flamingos, egrets, herons, cormorants, kingfishers and river terns.

attractions.name: Durgam Cheruvu
attractions.description: A popular lake, often called "Secret Lake" since it's hidden between the Jubilee Hills and Madhapur. Under the rule of the Qutb Shahi dynasty (ca. 1518–1687), this lake served as the drinking water source for the residents of Golconda. Nowadays, it is popular among tech workers to relax after their daily grinds. There is an amphitheatre, and the On the Rocks cafeteria. Boating is also available. A cable bridge with dancing fountain also adorns the lake.

attractions.name: Khajaguda Talab
attractions.description: A small lake brimming with species of birds, snakes, snails, and lizards. Khajaguda Talab has been beautified with shoreside sculptures and floaters in the lake.

attractions.name: Osman Sagar
attractions.description: A large reservoir and a popular tourist destination, especially in the monsoon season when the reservoir is full. The Gandipet Eco Park at Osman Sagar has a 2.5-km long boardwalk, an aquarium, a butterfly garden, an open-air theatre and a sensory park.

attractions.name: Mrugavani National Park
attractions.description: This park has a large variety of plants; animals such as the Indian hare, civet cat, mongoose, cobra, Russel Viper and bird species.

attractions.name: Ocean Park
attractions.description: A water-theme park.

attractions.name: Treasure Island
attractions.description: Theme park with go-karts.

attractions.name: Emaar MGF Boulder Hills Golf and Country Club
G. M. C. Balayogi Stadium
attractions.description: A multipurpose stadium with both indoor and outdoor activities. The outdoor (athletic) stadium is used mostly for football matches and it is the host stadium of Hyderabad FC. The indoor stadium is one of the home arenas for the India's prime basketball league, the UBA Pro Basketball League.

restaurants.name: Ginger Court
restaurants.description: Mughlai and Indian Chinese food.
restaurants.address: H No 1-74/1, Guttala, Hitech City, Madhapur

restaurants.name: Olive Garden
restaurants.description: Do not be misled by the name and expect Italian. It serves passable Mughlai and Punjabi fare.

restaurants.name: Collage
restaurants.description: A good choice for a lunch or dinner buffet in HITEC City. The service is courteous and the spread is tasteful though not extensive. The biryani is flavourful and the rest of the Indian fare is also quite decent.

attractions.name: Nagaraja Temple
attractions.description: The namesake of Nagercoil, with Nagaraja as its principal deity. The devout traditionally offer milk to this "King of Snakes".

attractions.name: St. Xavier's Cathedral
attractions.description: St. Francis Xavier Cathedral, in the Kottar locality, was established in 1600 AD. St.Francis Xavier stayed here and the church was built on the land which St. Xavier was awarded by the Venad king.

attractions.name: Trekking
attractions.description: very scenic village with rivers and hills all around

attractions.name: Ekambareswarar Temple
attractions.description: The highest, largest and most impressive temple in town, spanning 40 acres and dating back to the Pallava period. Represents the earth form of the five form-element abodes of Lord Shiva. Featuring huge quantities of carved stonework, it is one of the most important Shiva temples. The inner sanctum protects a mango tree said to be 3500 years old, embodying the four Vedas and bearing fruits of four different tastes each season. Much of the 40 acres of the temple seems to be closed to visitors, but the central building is impressive enough.

attractions.name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
attractions.description: Abode of Kamakshi (Parvati), consort of Shiva.

restaurants.name: Saravana Bhavan
restaurants.description: This chain is known for good south Indian food with branches all over. You have the choice of self service, a lunch room with fans, or an a/c room that is nicely cool. Food is consistently good and particularly good for Westerners because of high standards for cleanliness. Extensive menu in English. Try the 'fourteen idli' (sambar idli), which is idli swimming in sambar sauce.
restaurants.address: North side of Gandhi road, west a little from the main roundabout by the bus station

restaurants.name: Sri Rama Cafe
restaurants.description: Very long established pure vegetarian restaurant in South Indian style. Sit down, watch a banana leaf get spread in front of you and loaded up with rice, curry and breads. Drinking water is also served. Extra curry and rice were offered to me at no charge, so a meal here is basically "all you can eat".
restaurants.address: Next to the similarly named Sri Rama hotel

attractions.name: Aashbujha Temple
attractions.description: See the scenic beauty of The Vindhyas from this temple.

attractions.name: Budhenaath Temple
attractions.description: See the old stone carving at Pakka Ghat and Budhenaath Temple

attractions.name: The Clock Tower
attractions.description: It is one of its own kind.The stone carving of the tower will make mesmerize you. The clock is very old and is one of the sisters in Big Ben family.

attractions.name: Vindham, Sirsi and other water falls
attractions.description: There are various water falls surrounding the city.Vindham, Sirsi, Sidhnath ki dari being most famous in them

attractions.name: Explore the ghats
attractions.description: Mirzapur is situated at the bank of Ganges. You can enjoy a serene evening at one of the Ganges Gahts. The ghats in Mirzapur are relatively calm and quiet compare to Ganges Ghats of Varanasi and Allahabad. Visit Pakka Ghat to watch some rare and beautiful stone carving. It is situated in middle of the city and you can get Handrikshaw from any of the place in city. Try some boating in the serene Ganges.

attractions.name: BNR Garden
attractions.description: A park and a picnic spot, frequented by people of all ages. It offers toy train rides within the park.

attractions.name: Gole Bazaar Durga Temple
attractions.description: The temple was established in the early 20th century by some Bengali people working on the railways. It is famous for its Durga Puja and is very popular. It also serves as a seat of culture for the city.

attractions.name: Hijli Eco Park
attractions.description: It’s a famous picnic spot in winter. There is a small deer park inside.

attractions.name: Kalaikunda Air Force Station
attractions.description: Built by the British for the Royal Indian Air Force during World War II. It was used to conduct raids against advancing Japanese in Burma and also for operations to transport aid to parts of China. Access to the Air Force Station is restricted to defence personnel and is out of bounds for tourists without special permits.

attractions.name: Khargeshwar Temple
attractions.description: This is one of the oldest temples in the city, a Shiva temple, from which derives the name of Kharagpur.

attractions.name: Salua Air Force Station
attractions.description: An airbase used by the 317th Airlift Squadron of the US Air Force during World War II.

attractions.name: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur
attractions.description: The first Indian Institute of Technology, established in 1951. The IIT attracts visitors throughout the year (especially in the spring academic semester from January to April) on account on the Spring Fest, Kshitij and other departmental and interdepartmental fests and events.

attractions.name: Hijli Shaheed Bhavan
attractions.description: IIT Kharagpur was originally a detention camp during the British Raj to imprison Indian independence activists. The building was later renamed Shaheed Bhavan (and colloquially referred to as the "Old Building" in the institute), and was built on the Neo-Byzantine style of architecture. In 1990, the building was converted into a museum called the Nehru Museum of Science and Technology. The museum has many indoor exhibits, which include technical models collected from various institutes and organisations across India. The park outside the museum contains 14 open-air demonstrations and outdoor exhibits. The outdoor exhibits include a Hawker Hunter Mk 56 and a steam locomotive. The museum has an archive room showcasing documents relating to the history of IIT Kharagpur and Southwest Bengal.

attractions.name: Eluru Buddha Park
attractions.description: 74 feet statue of Abhaya Buddha in a pond.

attractions.name: Brundavan Park
attractions.description: Recreational park with walking track.

attractions.name: Kolleru Bird Sanctuary
attractions.description: A bird sanctuary based on one of the largest freshwater lakes in India

restaurants.name: Banana Leaf
restaurants.description: A Multi Cuisine Restaurant in Manya Guestline - A Star Hotel

restaurants.name: Dosa
restaurants.description: Definitely make sure to eat dosa- a kind of crape at Vasanthamahal center, Hai tea center, or Fire station center.

attractions.name: Bidar Fort
attractions.description: Built in 1427 when Sultan Alla-Ud Din Bahman of the Bahmanid Dynasty shifted his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar. There are over 30 monuments inside fort. The fort was one of the largest and strongest forts in India.It was built in 15th century.

attractions.name: Mahmud Gawan Madrasa
attractions.description: An ancient madrasa (Islamic college) built by the Bahamani empire around 1460 AD. It bears testimony to the scholarly genius of Mahmud Gawan, who first came to Delhi as a Persian trader from Gilan in Iran and moved to Bidar in 1453. The madrasa is a prime example of Indo-Islamic architecture and has been declared as a monument of national importance by the Indian government.

attractions.name: Tomb of Mahmood Shah Bahmani II
Tomb of Ahmed Shah Bahmani II
Tomb of Malika E Jahan Bida
Papnash Temple
attractions.description: It is believed that Lord Sri Rama, on the way to Ayodhya from Lanka after defeating Ravana, visited this place and that resulted in the temple which would wash off his act of killing Ravana who is a Shiva Bhakt.

attractions.name: Narasimha Zarna
attractions.description: The temple virtually runs into a cave waterbody and is one of the unique in the world. The water in the cave will guide the pilgrims to the idol.

attractions.name: Gurdwara Nanak Jhira Sahib
attractions.description: This is a Sikh historical shrine. One of the most popular south Indian historical gurudwaras amongst the Sikh community all over India.

attractions.name: Manik Prabhu Temple
attractions.description: Situated 53 km away from the city of Bidar, Manik Prabhu Temple is a unique architectural beauty and a major spiritual and religious centre. The Manik Prabhu temple is built over a Sanjeevani Samaadhi of a Saint- Shri Sadguru Manik Prabhu Maharaj and his spiritual stature and holy presence is still maintained by his 6th successor Shri Sadguru Dnyanraj Manik Prabhu Maharaj. The temple attracts both Hindu and Muslim devotees. The temple administration is carried out by Shri Manik Prabhu Samsthan which runs a number of social and charitable institutions since 140 years.

attractions.name: Girija B Kudre's Farm House
attractions.description: B. S. Kudre a great visionary & a social reformer from Bidar had developed an Organic Mangoes / Amla plantation in about 65 acres (260,000 m2) of land at Andura. Having developed a cold storage along with it, exporting the Mangoes & Grapes to US, UK & Middle Eastern Countries. By adopting the primitive method of Agriculture / Horticulture, showing the importance of Indian Breed Cow's, their Medicinal values in day to day life, made a benchmark for all the researcher's to visit at least once in lifetime

attractions.name: Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: A wildlife sanctuary in Bihar. There several hot springs located here as well as several places of interest nearby. This area of grasslands and forest contains a mixture of flora. A few of the animals to be found include tigers, wild bears, mongoose, snakes and a wide variety of wild bird species.

attractions.name: Chandika Sthan
attractions.description: Chandika Sthan is a Hindu temple, one of the fifty one Shakti Peethas, places of worship consecrated to the goddess Shakti.

attractions.name: Kharagpur Jheel
attractions.description: This is a pond. The temple is positioned in the middle of the pond. A famous for the tourist attractions. One of the best place for one day travelers. It is wide and open place for family visit.

attractions.name: Machhli talav
attractions.description: This is a temple of Shiva (Shivling). The temple is positioned in the middle of the pond. And is very beautiful. Macchli talav also has a garden.

attractions.name: Munger Fort
attractions.description: This fort; built on rocky hills, traces its history from about 1330 AD. It contains several important monuments.

attractions.name: Sita Kund
attractions.description: It has a very interesting ancient story about this place, which belongs in the period of Ramayana. After being rescued form Lanka, Ram, to satisfy all public opinion, asked Sita to prove her chastity and she gladly agreed to the Agni Pariksha (the fire ordeal). She came out of the fire test unscathed. The hot spring is now an enclosed and grilled reservoir and is visited by a large number of pilgrims on the full moon day of Magh. The water is beautifully clear and transparent and sends up numerous bubbles from its rocky bed. Various explanations of this phenomenon have been suggested, such as “Deep seated thermodynamics action and variation of underground volcanic activities.

attractions.name: Cactus Garden
attractions.description: This is the largest succulent botanical garden of Asia. Situated in the heart of the city of Panchkula, it covers a total area of 7 acres. The Cactus Garden is known for its rare & endangered species of Indian succulents. You can spot nearly 3500 different kinds of species over there. Chandigarh Cactus Garden was set up in the year 1987. This unique garden consists of three green houses. It has been drawing more and more crowds every year, consisting not just of tourists, but botanists also.

attractions.name: Burhanpur Station
attractions.description: The only railway station in Burhanpur. Trains arrive and leave the station regularly.

attractions.name: Dargah-E-Hakimi
attractions.description: Syedi Abdul Qadir Hakimuddin (1665-1730 AD) is the holy dawoodi bohra saint who is buried in Burhanpur, India. His grave is visited by pilgrims from all over the world. The tomb complex 'Dargah-e-Hakimi' includes mosques, gardens, and international class accommodation facilities for visitors.

attractions.name: Amul Dairy
attractions.description: Asia's largest dairy.

attractions.name: Watch a film
attractions.description: There are many cinemas in the city.

attractions.name: Dwarka Baoli
attractions.description: A stepwell discovered in 2011 under the foliage of thick vegetation and undergrowth and hidden behind a large group of tall trees. The Dwaraka Baoli finds a mention in the list of Maulvi Zafar Hasan of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Maulvi Zafar Hasan documented the list of baolis in 1910 and listed over 100 baolis in and around Delhi. It was listed as the Loharheri Baoli or the Blacksmith’s stepwell. It is a 22-step stepwell or baoli, made of rubble masonry. The well, now covered by an iron grill, is situated on the southern end of the baoli. The side wall contains two sets of recessed arches. It is a small baoli with no ornamentation and not much of general tourist interest.

attractions.name: Indian Air Force Museum
attractions.description: The oldest museum of its kind in the country. It houses aircraft, photos, memorabilia, weapons and uniforms of the Indian Air Force.

attractions.name: Rajputana Rifles Regimental Museum
attractions.description: A regimental museum, covering the rich history of the Rajputana Rifles from its inception. The museum exhibits weapons and uniforms and narrates the history through large format images and audiovisual film.

attractions.name: Shri Bharat Kshetra
attractions.description: Jain temple.

attractions.name: Sulabh International Museum of Toilets
attractions.description: A rather unusual museum dedicated to the global history of sanitation and toilets. The objective in establishing this museum was to highlight the need to address the problems of the sanitation sector in India.

attractions.name: Yashobhoomi
attractions.description: The largest convention centre in India and Asia by area, and one of the biggest MICE facilities in the world

attractions.name: The Free Spirit Dance Studio
attractions.description: Dance workshops on Bollywood, Indian folk genres like bhangra and contemporary Western and fusion genres, including jazz, hip-hop and zumba.
attractions.address: J13/69, Basement, Block J, Rajouri Garden Extension, Rajouri Garden

restaurants.name: Barbeque Nation
restaurants.description: Offers an option where customers can make their food on their personal grills, which are embedded in each table. Vegetarian and non-vegetarian BBQ starters, a main course buffet, soups, salads, desserts and a variety of liquors.

restaurants.name: Om Sweets
restaurants.description: Both a sweet shop and casual multi-cuisine restaurant with a strong emphasis on quality and hygiene.

attractions.name: Bansilalpet Stepwell
attractions.description: Nothing much is known about the stepwell and its builder. But architectural features state that it dates back over 300 years and was built during the Nizam rule. The Pharaoh & Co map mentions the well as Naganah Kunta in their 1954 map' Later a Britisher named T.H. Keyes developed the area and the project was funded by local businessman Seth Bansilal, after whom the stepwell is popularly known. In the 1980s two men died falling into the well. After this, the well was abandoned and turned into a garbage pit. In 2020 tonnes of garbage were removed and the stepwell was restored. The surrounding was landscaped and galleries were added. The galleries exhibit the transformation process along with the history of the stepwell.

attractions.name: The Hyderabad Public School
attractions.description: A former Nizam's palace and the Jagirdar's College. This Institution was founded in 1923 and is one of the oldest and largest public schools in the country. The campus is a recognised heritage site.

attractions.name: Osmania Arts College
attractions.description: Built during the period of the last Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan. The imposing façade of the building is a great sight.

attractions.name: Rashtrapati Nilayam
attractions.description: The official retreat of the President of India in Hyderabad, where the President stays for at least two weeks during winter and conducts official business. Like the Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, the retreat's premises include a landscaped garden, seasonal flowering plants and display of potted plants around the main building, natural cascading water falls and seven different types of nutrition gardens.

attractions.name: Secunderabad Clock Tower
attractions.description: The landmark clock tower in Secunderabad.

attractions.name: Shamirpet Lake
attractions.description: Shamirpet has a beautiful lake and a deer park. The peaceful environs make it a great picnic spot. Telangana Tourism offers comfortable cottages facilities for accommodation (under private management), while the forest lodge can be booked with the Telangana Forest Department office at Saifabad.

attractions.name: Sir Ronald Ross Institute Of Parasitology
attractions.description: The medical laboratory where Ronald Ross discovered that malaria was transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes. It is a division of Osmania University, and has been transformed into a museum exhibiting old photos of Roland Ross along with his family members. Also, a set of diagrams and charts explains Ross' research. Outside the building is a bust of Ronald Ross and a marble plaque commemorates the event.

attractions.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Assumption
Musheerabad Mosque
attractions.description: A congregation mosque that was built in 1560 by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah of Golconda. The mosque has five lofty arches and two minarets at the corners, similar to Hayat Bakshi Mosque. After the fall of Golconda, the mosque went into disuse till the area became a jagir of Nawab Arastu Jah, the Prime Minister during the reign of Nizam Ali Khan. Although the mosque was repaired in 1951, it is now dilapidated. A new four-storey mosque is later built to accommodate the namazis.

attractions.name: Spanish Mosque
attractions.description: A landmark mosque built in the Moorish Revival architectural style.

attractions.name: Indira Park
attractions.description: A sprawling 76-acre park near Tank Bund with a nice, but polluted, little pond and boating.

attractions.name: Sanjeevaiah Park
attractions.description: An open space north of the Husaain Sagar. It houses the second-tallest flag of India. About 100 species of resident and non-resident birds and more than 50 species of insects and butterflies are present in the park. The park hosts several events for the public occasionally. Events ranging from roller-skating races to social awareness campaigns, the park has encouraged public initiatives.

attractions.name: Snow World
attractions.description: One of India's largest snow-themed parks.

attractions.name: Gymkhana Ground
attractions.description: The sole cricket ground in Secunderabad.

restaurants.name: Alpha
restaurants.description: Popular for beja fry, available only in the morning and served for breakfast.

restaurants.name: Paradise Restaurant
restaurants.description: This restaurant is one of the oldest places serving Biryani and of late has lost some of its sheen owing to explosion of business Also serves the best falooda in Hyderabad. It has both a sit-down restaurant and takeaway. They have various branches, but confusingly there imitators with similar names. There is another branch at Kothapet which is roughly 3 km from Dilsuknagar
restaurants.address: Paradise Circle, M G Rd, Secunderabad

restaurants.name: Aangan
restaurants.description: Mughlai, Chinese and Hyderabadi dishes.
restaurants.address: 1-8-1/0/B, Yatri Nivas, Sardar Patel Rd, Secunderabad

restaurants.name: Nanking
restaurants.description: Hyderabad's oldest Chinese restaurant.

restaurants.name: Utsav
restaurants.description: Indian vegetarian cuisine, has received good reviews.

restaurants.name: Malgudi
restaurants.description: The name is inspired by the fictional South Indian town created by R K Narayan. It has an ambience that suits the name, with waiters clad in dhotis. Serves food from the four southern states that are rare in other restaurants, like gutti vankai or kodi pulusu. Service is extremely fast. In Hyderabad, it has 3 branches.

restaurants.name: Tulips - The Coffee Shop
restaurants.description: Famous for its midnight biryani and buffet.
restaurants.address: 1-26, Hotel Green Park, Greenlands Rd, Begumpet

attractions.name: Baidyanath Temple
attractions.description: According to Hindu mythology, Ravana went to Mount Kailash and prayed to Lord Shiva, who gave him a Jyotirlinga to take to his land, with the promise not to place the lingam anywhere else. In case that happened, the lingam would remain fixed on that spot forever. The gods, who were unhappy at the prospect of the divine lingam being established in the enemy kingdom, which would render them powerless against their adversary, worked a trick on Ravana. He mistakenly handed over the lingam to a Brahmin, who grounded it at Deoghar. Ravana did his best to uproot it but beyond breaking the tip he was unsuccessful. In deep remorse, he used to come to this place everyday and worship the lingam by offering water from the Ganges. Historically the temple is dated to 1596. The temple has almost all god & goddesses and whole temple is built on a single rock. During the month of Sawan (June–July) people from across the country come to offer Ganga jal to the divine shivalinga. For centuries, devotees,

attractions.name: Ramkrishna Mission Vidyapith
attractions.description: The Universal Temple of Sri Ramakrishna held in the bosom of the Vidyapith campus is a place of attraction to the religious minded. There, morning prayer and evening services (Aratrikam) are conducted by the resident boys as part of their daily routine. Religious festivals, observances and worships are carried out in it.

attractions.name: Trikut Hill
attractions.description: Source of the Mayurakshi River. Vehicles come to the base but one has to walk up. A ropeway has been built to ferry people to the top. Other than the ropeway, tourists can also use the stairs to reach the top. The hill is covered with clouds in rainy seasons and waterfalls and small streams are visible from July–September. There are views from the top of the mountain.

attractions.name: Rikhia Ashram
attractions.description: Rikhia peeth is the tapobhumi (place of spiritual sadhana or practice) of Swami Satyananda Saraswati, founder of the Bihar School of Yoga, Munger. Swami Satyananda came to Rikhia with the sankalpa to live in seclusion, on 23 September 1989.

attractions.name: Fun and Adventure Water Park
attractions.description: A water-based amusement park.

attractions.name: Khammam Fort
attractions.description: This fort was built by Kakatiya rulers and was managed and extended by Nizam. It offers a nice view of Khammam town. There are steps constructed to facilitate climbing.

attractions.name: Narasimha Swamy Temple
attractions.description: This temple of the "Narasimha Swami" deity is quite famous and also the reason for the name of "Khammam". On a hill top, it offers nice views especially in the evenings. The hill top is accessible by car.

attractions.name: Danavaigudem Park
attractions.description: Danavaigudem Park is a picnic spot on the banks of Munneru river. You can check out the drinking water supply plant here, and you could also have a nice walk crossing the river on the dam, depending on the flow conditions.

attractions.name: Tank Bund
attractions.description: An evening at Tankbund near sequel resorts is a good pastime.This place is also used as walkers park in the morning.

attractions.name: Bhiwani Zoo
attractions.description: A small zoo with around 10 types of animals, including hippos, gharials, and peafowl. Takes 30 minutes to one hour to see them all.

attractions.name: Star Monument
attractions.description: The architectural showpiece of the town, shaped as a hexagonal pyramid with large white stars adorning the sides.

attractions.name: Atal Setu
attractions.description: India's longest sea bridge, also known as Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link (MTHL). Named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, the bridge connects Sewri in Mumbai to Nhava Sheva in Navi Mumbai, across the Mumbai Harbour.

attractions.name: Mango Garden
attractions.description: Mango Garden, a must-visit place for couples and children. It is a small garden for almost all age group people.

attractions.name: Mini seashore, Juhu Chowpatty
attractions.description: Boating, toy train and lot of fun, bhel puri, pani puri, gola etc.

attractions.name: Parsik Hill
attractions.description: A very cool place on hilltop. People prefer to come here for morning and evening walk. Youngsters come here to have fun and just chill out. It is closed most of the times in the rainy season because of the landslide. A must to visit this place in evening hours if you are around. It is best to visit this place when the monsoon just starts. During this time there is an enchanting dew and also a slow waterfall often called the Pandavakhada waterfall.

attractions.name: Rajiv Gandhi Maidan
attractions.description: Lots of temples for doing Pooja and meditiation, and a good trek.

attractions.name: Rain Tree Marg
attractions.description: Has beautiful views of Navi Mumbai

attractions.name: Sarovar Vihar Garden
attractions.description: Like a second marine drive, provides a beautiful view of the sea, a drive from Vashi via the Palm Beach Road ends at Belapur

attractions.name: Seven Wonders
attractions.description: Park for all ages, it has the Seven Wonder statues. It is a huge park with joy rides. Water pool and fountains to view. Fruit shape huts to seat and take photos. Cool hang out with kids.

attractions.name: Pandavkada Falls
attractions.description: Monsoon tourist attraction for people from far and wide. Authorities are strict in not allowing people to visit this place in monsoon on account of accidental deaths in the waterfall.

attractions.name: Utsav Chowk
attractions.description: One of the most famous landmarks in the area and it stands out for its eye catching architecture which is a humble reflection of the Roman and Greek architecture.

attractions.name: Belapur Fort ruins
attractions.description: The fort was built by the Siddis of Janjira. It was later conquered by the Portuguese, and then Marathas. In the early 19th century, the fort was captured by the British. The deliberate damage wrought led to a decline in the strategic importance of the fort.

attractions.name: Dronagiri Fort
attractions.description: The ruins of the fortification are seen on the fort. There is a church Nossa Senhora da Penha in good condition, but without any idol or inscription. The church is in the inner fortification. The main gate to the fort is situated on the south of the church 50 m away. The arch of the gate is broken, yet the guards rooms are in good condition. The Ganapati carved on the key stone is placed in one of the guard room. From the main gate a path way leads south to the Village Karanja. In between a Vetal mandir in ruined state is located. The pathway starting from the back of the Vetal mandie leads to large water tank in good condition situated among the forest. The fort is accessible in all seasons. The trek to the fort is simple and safe. Being close to Uran and Karanja, the fort was strategic importance since old times. The entire hill is densely covered with forest.

attractions.name: Central Park
attractions.description: The project of Central Park is to make a public park with Navi Mumbai's ethos reflected into the future. It is under construction but is open to public. The large amphitheatre has hosted many public shows. An ISKCON temple is attached to this park. To the west of this park is Pandav Kada waterfall and CIDCO developed golf course.

attractions.name: DY Patil Stadium
attractions.description: The cricket stadium in the Navi Mumbai area hosts several international cricket matches and domestic championships such as the Mumbai T20 league and Times Cricket Shield. Wankhede matches in the Indian Premier League as well as Womens Premier League have been played at the stadium. The stadium also hosts international cricket tournaments and concerts.

attractions.name: Rajiv Gandhi Joggers Park
attractions.description: A hot-spot for joggers of all ages

attractions.name: Sagar Vihar
attractions.description: A cool place to chill out with friends; a must to visit during evening hours.

restaurants.name: Bhagat Tarachand
restaurants.description: Pure veg restaurant.

restaurants.name: Flavours
restaurants.description: Intercontinental cuisine. You can sit at the counter and enjoy your drinks (including the Bartender's Special).

restaurants.name: Hot Cross Cafe
restaurants.description: A very relaxing coffee shop where they serve a variety of hukka (sheesha) at a very minimal rate. One of the best places in Navi Mumbai for hukka and mouth watering and fresh pastries.

restaurants.name: Hotel Ruchi
restaurants.description: Possibly the best Keralite food you can find in the city. The restaurant itself is pretty small and unnoticeable but if you notice it, don't miss it. Try the Kerala Parotha with Chicken Masala and the idiyaappam and appams for breakfast

restaurants.name: Jaslok
restaurants.description: All sorts of snacks and sweets. Pani Puri, Vada Pav and Rasmalai, Jamun are the delicious items.

restaurants.name: Nanumal Bhojraj
restaurants.description: Damn good restaurant for Sindhi and Punjabi food.

restaurants.name: Navaratna
restaurants.description: One of the oldest restaurants in Vashi. It serves great food in the traditional Udipi style.

restaurants.name: Sri Krishna
restaurants.description: Good vegetarian food. Great watermelon juice! Home delivery available. Try the gadbad ice cream.

restaurants.name: Tunga
restaurants.description: Good place to eat. Excellent ghee chapaties.

restaurants.name: Vasundhara
restaurants.description: Pure veg restaurant.

restaurants.name: Viscious circle
restaurants.description: Mouth watering kebabs and non veg dishes, good ambience, drinks and a large projector screen.

restaurants.name: Gupta's
restaurants.description: Great range of toast sandwiches And pizzas.

attractions.name: Ambala Air Force Base
attractions.description: One of the oldest airbases in the world, the home base of Jaguar Squadron.

attractions.name: St. Paul church
attractions.description: Christian cemetery on same road.

attractions.name: Huda Town Park
attractions.description: A popular place for running, yoga and other forms of exercise.

restaurants.name: Halwai Bazar
restaurants.description: "Golgaps and Chat: Unforgettable experience with original with 7 flavours", Kishori Lal at Halwai Bazar, Ki Kachori, Pahalwan Ki Khasta Kachori, Omi Ke Chole Bhature at Vijay Ratan Chowk.

restaurants.name: Puran Singh Ka Dhabha
restaurants.description: Standard Punjabi eatery with vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes on the menu. The original Puran Singh Ka Dhabha is next to the bus stand, the ones facing the highway are copies. Puran Singh's son and widow now run the restaurant.
restaurants.address: Shop No:10, Grand Trunk Rd, Shastri Market, Dhandari Kalan

attractions.name: Koil Sagar
attractions.description: One of the famous tourist attractions of West Telangana with a Veerabadhra temple called Koil Konda. Every year, there is a celebration (Jathara) held by nearby villagers.

attractions.name: Manyamkonda
attractions.description: A hilltop shrine of Lord Venkateshwara. There is also a temple of Lord Shiva. The ideal time to visit this temple is at the time of Jaathara, celebrated every year during January or February. The road to the hilltop is very curvy and exciting. Before entering the road that leads to this temple, there is another temple at the bottom of the hill of Devi Padmavati.

attractions.name: French Cemetery
attractions.description: The French Cemetery contains 150 tombs and is located on the Grand Trunk Road opposite Lal Dighi (a large lake). The eminent persons buried in the French Cemetery in Chandannagar includes Duplessis, the founding father of French Chandannagar and pioneering meteorologist Henry “Storm” Piddington, who also finds mentioned in Amitav Ghosh’s novel The Hungry Tide.

attractions.name: Nritya Gopal Smriti Mandir
attractions.description: Built by Sri Harihar Seth, and donated to the people of Chandannagar. This building still serves as a theatre hall and a library. It was first of its kind in the entire locality.

attractions.name: Liberty Gate
attractions.description: One of the original two gates that were constructed on 14 July 1937 as the gateways to the French colony of Chandernagore. One was on the north side on the way to Chinsurah, and the other was on the south side on the way to Bhadreswar. Only the southern gate survives out of the two. The gate bears an inscription with the coat of arms and the French motto liberté, egalité, fraternité, meaning "liberty, equality, fratermity".

attractions.name: Vivekananda Mandir
attractions.description: A meditation centre.

attractions.name: Dourgachorone Roquitte Memorial
attractions.description: Locally known as Joṛā Ghāṭ (জোড়া ঘাট, literally "twin ghats"), this memorial is dedicated to Dourgachorone Roquitte (দুর্গাচরণ রক্ষিত Durgācaraṇ Rakṣit), the first Indian to receive the Legion of Honour (French: Legion d'honneur), the highest French order of merit. Despite struggling in childhood, he gained a lot of wealth by his trade to the French, as well as Malaysia, Rangoon (present-day Yangon), Trinidad, Hong Kong, Jamaica, Egypt and Mauritius. As a philanthropist, he opened free schools and pharmacies, supplied free food grains and also sponsored pilgrimage. He also served as the mayor of Chandannagar as well as a judge in the local court. The memorial was built in 1921, on the donation of his son Shamachorone Roquitte.

attractions.name: Dupleix Palace
attractions.description: One of the oldest and finest museums in the entire region. It boasts a beautiful collection of French antiques which are difficult to find anywhere else in the world, including the cannons used in the Anglo-French war, wooden furniture of the 18th century etc. The institution still teaches French through regular classes.

attractions.name: Underground House
attractions.description: Another beautiful example of the advancement in the knowledge of architecture and the aesthetic sense of the people of those earlier days. Its lowest floor is submerged in the River Hooghly. Rabindranath Tagore had frequently visited this edifice and appreciated a lot about it. He felt that the place influenced him to a large extent and broadened his intellectual capabilities. He has mentioned this house in many of his famous novels. Social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar also stayed in this building before Tagore.

attractions.name: Roquitte House
attractions.description: The 19th-century residence of Dourgachorone Roquitte and his family. The Roquittes were textile magnates in Chandannagar before diversifying into other businesses. The building was built in phases.

attractions.name: Nandadulal Jiu Temple
attractions.description: Considered to be the finest specimen of Bengal-style docālā (দোচালা, "double-sloped") roof temples. It was built in 1739-40 by Indranarayan Roychoudhury.

attractions.name: The Sacred Heart Church
attractions.description: The beautiful church stands for over two centuries to mark the beauty of the architecture during the French period - a good place to visit for historians and tourists alike. The remains of the Church of St. Louis are also an attractive tourist spot.

attractions.name: Chuti Park
attractions.description: Operated by the municipal corporation.

attractions.name: Wonderland Park
attractions.description: Operated by the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA).

attractions.name: New Digha Park
attractions.description: A popular picnic spot among locals, with a name ostensibly similar to Bengal's most popular beach destination. So, don't get confused while driving to your destination!

restaurants.name: Abhinandan
restaurants.description: Decent food.

restaurants.name: Bhooter Raja Dilo Bor
restaurants.description: Chandannagar outlet of the Kolkata-based Feluda-themed restaurant chain, literally meaning "the king of ghosts has given a boon". It is famous for its hilsa (iliś) dishes.

restaurants.name: Restaurant Sundari
restaurants.description: One of the oldest restaurants. Though food is not so good.

restaurants.name: Royal Biriyani
restaurants.description: Serves good biryani, though the standard is deteriorating.

restaurants.name: Satyam Garden Restaurant
restaurants.description: Set amidst a small garden, and a huge historical building called Nrityagopal Smriti Mandir.

restaurants.name: Shalimar Restaurant & Bar
restaurants.description: A restaurant in a French colonial building. The food tastes good as well.

attractions.name: Cossimbazar Palace of the Roys
attractions.description: The former royal palace of the Cossimbazar royal family, turned into a heritage property.

attractions.name: Old Cossimbazar Palace
attractions.description: ThisThe place is known as Boro Rajbari and belongs to the Nandi family. It is totally in ruins, and the interiors are not accessible.

attractions.name: Old English Cemetery
attractions.description: The Old English Cemetery contains several tombs and graves, including the tomb of Mary Hastings, wife of Warren Hastings and that of her infant daughter. There are several other graves in the cemetery, but most of them are unmarked.

attractions.name: Dutch Cemetery
attractions.description: The Dutch Cemetery of Cossimbazar dates back to the early 18th century. The oldest grave is of Daniel Van der Muyl, who died in 1721. The cemetery has 47 tombs, most of them obelisks. The cemetery houses a white temple-like tomb housing the mortal remains of a Dutch East India Company official, Tammerus Canter Visscher. Incidentally, there is a similar grave in Chinsurah.

attractions.name: Residency Cemetery
attractions.description: A heritage Christian cemetery protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Many important British residents and military personnel lived in Berhampore were buried in this cemetery.

attractions.name: St. Mary Armenian Church
attractions.description: It was constructed in 1758 by Khoja Petros Arathoon. The church closed down after its last sermon in 1860, but was reopened in 2005. Although not a functioning church, it is well maintained and is housed in a large compound complete with a landscaped garden. It is a small church and there are several graves inside the church.

attractions.name: Byaspur Shiva Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple with terracotta works. It was built in 1811 by Pandit Ramkeshava Devasharman, and is said to have been inspired by the temple in Baranagar (near Azimganj) built by Rani Bhabani.

attractions.name: Murshidabad Maharaja Krishnanath University
attractions.description: A public state university in Berhampore with Oxford-inspired architecture. It was established in 1853 as a liberal arts college by Maharani Swarnamoyee Devi. She named it after the demise of her her husband Krishnath Roy, who dreamt of establishing an academic institution. Author Brajendranath Seal developed the college infrastructure further.

attractions.name: Saidabad Rajbari
attractions.description: Built by Maharaja Nandakumar Roy's son-in-law, the palace was later converted into a museum and district library.

attractions.name: Laldighi Park
attractions.description: A great place to (re)discover love.

attractions.name: Rabindra Sadan
attractions.description: Watch theatre.

attractions.name: Ritwik Sadan
attractions.description: Watch documentary films.

attractions.name: Barrack Square
attractions.description: The central ground of Berhampore, as part of the fortified British cantonment. It is surrounded by various bungalows and barracks, all of which are now used as government offices.

attractions.name: Madhav National Park
attractions.description: Madhav National Park lies between Agra-Bombay road and Jhansi-Shivpuri Road. It is spread over an area of 157.58 km2. A drive through the park watching animals is very exhilarating experience. The Park is haven for wildlife and wildlife – buffs. The park remains open throughout the year and boasts of large numbers of chinkara, Indian gazelle and chital.The nilgai, sambar, chausingha, blackbuck, sloth bear, leopard and the common langur are the other inhabitants of the sprawling park. The national park is equally rich in bird life; Chandpata, the artificial lake, is the winter abode of migratory geese, pochard, pintail, teal, mallard and gadwall. Other residents include the cormorant, laggar falcon, paradise flycatcher and golden oriole. Loud cracking notes of white-breasted kingfisher flying past, harsh crocking of grey heron or quacking of spotbill duck and numerous lesser whistling teals resting at the bank of lack with a leg tucked away and head folded back in to the body; and cheet

attractions.name: Son Chiraiya Bird Century
attractions.description: Famous for Golden Bird.

attractions.name: Scindhia Chhatris
attractions.description: Shivpuri is famous for graceful,intricately embellished marble chhatries (cenotaphs) erected by Scindia Princes. Set in an elaborate Mughal Garden, are the cenotaphs, the royal Chhatries dedicated to Scindias.Facing each other across a water tank are the Chhatries of Madhav Rao Scindia and dowager queen Maharani Sakhya Raje Scindia, in a delightful fusion of Hindu and Islamic architectural styles, with their shikhara – type spires and Rajput and Mughal pavilions. Ceremonially attired retainers, with flowers and incense tend to both cenotaph house life-size images of the Scindias, and these religiously, daily.

attractions.name: Bhura Kho
attractions.description: Natural spring which is a picnic spot.

attractions.name: Bhadaiya kund
attractions.description: Man-made spring and a picnic spot.

attractions.name: Narwar Fort
attractions.description: 9th century fort famous for the love story of king Nal and queen Damyanti.

attractions.name: Khaspur
attractions.description: The Capital of Old Cachari Kingdom. Beautiful place with the ruins of the fort used by the Cachari Kings.

restaurants.name: The Godfather
restaurants.description: Delicious food. Reasonable prices. Vegetarian options.

restaurants.name: Hasty Tasty
restaurants.description: Serves good vegetarian food.

restaurants.name: Nahaz
restaurants.description: Specializes in Thai and Chinese fast Food, The most happening place in Silchar

attractions.name: Dhenupureeswarar Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple built between 956 and 973 CE during the reign of Parantaka Chola II. A number of religious festivals are celebrated at the temple, including Pradosha, Panguni Uttiram and during Navaratri, devotees visit to offer special pujas.

attractions.name: Kumaran Kundram
attractions.description: The Deity of Lord Murugan in Kumaran Kundram is considered to be equivalent to the one in Swamimalai. small hillock at Kumaran Kundram

attractions.name: Ranganatha Temple
attractions.description: This temple is one of the 108 places considered sacred by Vaishnatives. Legend has it that sage Valmiki, after composing the Ramayana, prayed in the temple and saw the divine darshan of Lord Vishnu in three forms.

attractions.name: Nanmangalam Reserve Forest
attractions.description: Popular among bird watchers and is home to about 85 species of birds.

attractions.name: Arignar Anna Zoological Park
attractions.description: Chennai has the distinction of having the first zoo in India, which was started in 1855. This park is said to be one of the biggest in South Asia. The wildlife population is exhibited in a large open-moated island enclosure with a simulated natural environment. More than 170 species of mammals, birds and reptiles are housed in this park. Lion safari vehicles, elephant rides, battery operated vehicles are some of the facilities available. The peak time is during Pongal and weekend holidays.

attractions.name: Pallavaram Hill
attractions.description: A hilly park with walking trails, and views of the Chennai skyline.

attractions.name: Nurpur Fort
attractions.description: Fortress built by the Pathania Rajputs, more than 900 years ago. It was damaged due to the great earthquake which struck this region early in 1905 AD. It is quite famous in North India, and the temple inside attracts tourists from all across India.

attractions.name: Shahpurkandi fort
attractions.description: The fort is one of the main attractions of Pathankot city. It was built in 1505 AD by a Rajput chief, by the name of Jaspal Singh Pathania. It was strategically located to have control over the Kangra and Nurpur region. The fort is in ruins, and is famous for its temples and the view it commands over the Ravi river.

attractions.name: Kathgarh Mandir
attractions.description: An important ancient Shiva temple 30 km from Pathankot towards Indora/Chanour (HP). During "Naag panchami", the gap between two shiva parvati holy stones reduces and during "shivrathri" the gap increases. There is no clue as to how that happens. But truly it' has a magic of its own. This temple is very historical temple. It is said that this temple was constructed at the time of Alexander The Great.

restaurants.name: Makhan da dhaba
restaurants.description: If you really love to eat spicy Punjabi food, then visit "Makhan da dhaba" near the railway line. It is very famous for its cheap and tasty food. It serves Dal Tarka, Channa Masala, Muttar Paneer and many more spicy dishes and any two people can eat good food for only ₹50. This may be among the cheapest and tastiest food in the area.

restaurants.name: Moti Mahal Grand
restaurants.description: Moti Mahal is the best restaurant in Pathankot with its lounge bar, terrace Moroccan open bar & restaurant & a party hall to cater parties up to 200 people, which is a branch of well known moti mahal restaurant of Delhi. Moti Mahal’s Tandoori Trail showcases great recipes, some inherited and some a result of experimentation by the author, which are as delicious today as they were 57 years ago. This is a collection of secret recipes offered to the lovers of good food and as a token of their loyalty towards Moti Mahal’s cuisine worldwide. Enjoy and savour each of them. Besides this treasure house of recipes, a picture gallery of unique photographs of Kundan Lal Gujral at several award ceremonies, as well as with various dignitaries including former president Zakir Hussain, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi and Kennedy.

restaurants.name: Healthy Bites
restaurants.description: A good fast food restaurant.

restaurants.name: Honey Bun
restaurants.description: It is a fast food restaurant and a bakery shop near Hotel Woodland. Its amazing ambience will surprise you. The prices are very reasonable. It is the best place in the town where you will get best value for money along with great eating experience.

restaurants.name: Hotel Woodland
restaurants.description: Dhangu Rd., in the heart of the city. With the finest restaurant, spacious and well equipped rooms it is the most obvious choice for most of the travellers. It is a two-star hotel, certified by the Hotel and Restaurant Association of Northern India.

restaurants.name: Spice n Ice
restaurants.description: Cuisine: Tandoori, Mughali, Indian, Chinese, continental.

attractions.name: Gajanan Maharaj Temple
attractions.description: Kanhor is among the well-known religious places located in a serene & scenic place. The temple is situated just outside of Badlapur village on a small hillock surrounded by fields and greenery all around. The enchanting natural beauty around the temple is another attraction for the devotees who visit the temple.

attractions.name: Khandoba Temple
attractions.description: The temple of Lord Khandoba is located in Moolgaon, a small village, around 4 Miles (6 km) from Badlapur Railway station. From the temple, you can see the panoramic view of Badlapur, Kulgaon and Vangani. The best time to visit this place is around September to November.

attractions.name: Kondeshwar
attractions.description: Kondeshwar has a beautiful waterfall along with a pond. There is a temple of Lord Shiva and hence the name Kondeshwar. Kondeshwar is remotely located away from the noise and urban pollution, with the nearest village located about 20/25 minutes by walk. Though Kondeshwar is a very beautiful place to be during a monsoon period, there have been many accidents and fatalities due to unsafe swimming practices by people who have very less knowledge of the crevices under the water. Many people have died due to the turbulence of the waterfall and they were taken inside the crevices from where it is very difficult to come out due to the heavy force of water.

attractions.name: Kondeshwar Shiv Temple
attractions.description: This is a very old temple.

attractions.name: Kondeshwar Shiv Mandir
attractions.description: Very old temple in a beautiful place.

attractions.name: Bhoj Resort
attractions.description: Facilities include Sauna, Steam bath, Rain Dance, Swimming Pool and camping environment tent facility

restaurants.name: Farmer's Den
restaurants.description: A riverside resort for the day and overnight picnics, multi-cuisine, ample space and greenery, cable TV, and Barbecue nights.

attractions.name: Cuddalore Government Museum
attractions.description: The collection represents the history, culture, flora and fauna of the district. Natural History specimens include South Indian timbers, fibres, swans, bears, lizards and snakes. Wood fossils and ammonite fossils are also on display. A sculpture garden in the museum welcomes visitors. In this sculpture garden Sivalinga, Nandhi, Vishnu, monkey sculptures, Narashima, Surya and Chandikeswara are displayed. The development of Tamil script, a dinosaur model and a model of Kali sculpture made of Fibreglass are kept at the entrance of the building.

attractions.name: Fort St. David
attractions.description: A ruined British fort.

attractions.name: Pataleeswarar Temple
attractions.description: A Shiva temple of Pallava and Chola periods.

attractions.name: Silver Beach
attractions.description: 2nd largest beach in Asia.

restaurants.name: Anandha Bhavan
restaurants.description: Post Office Stop, Manjakuppam.
restaurants.address: Krishnalaya Complex, Krishnalaya Theatre, 06, Imperial Rd

attractions.name: Trikuteshwara Temple
attractions.description: An 11th–12th century Chalukya-era temple complex, among the largest and most ornate in Gadag. The main sanctum enshrines three Shiva lingas, traditionally interpreted as representing the trinity of Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshwara. The complex includes a stepped temple tank and a separate shrine that once honoured Saraswati alongside Gayatri and Sharada — one of relatively few temples in India dedicated to the goddess of learning, though regular worship there lapsed after the shrine was damaged during a historical invasion. Look closely at the pillars and ceiling brackets for the fine figural carving typical of the "Gadag style."

attractions.name: Veeranarayana Temple
attractions.description: Built in the 11th century under the Kalyani Chalukyas and substantially renovated in the 14th century under the Vijayanagara Empire, this Vishnu temple unusually combines three architectural idioms in one structure: a Vijayanagara-style entrance gateway (mahadwara) and tower (gopura), a Hoysala-style pillared hall (ranga mantapa) with an ornate garuda-stambha, and a Chalukya-style inner hall next to the sanctum. It is protected as a monument of national importance by the Archaeological Survey of India. The temple's central claim to fame is literary: the Kannada poet Kumara Vyasa is traditionally said to have composed his Mahabharata here around 1425–1450, and a particular pillar inside is pointed out as the place where he wrote. An inscription dated 1539 records a grant to the temple from the Vijayanagara king Achyuta Deva Raya.

attractions.name: Binkadakatti Zoo (Gadag Zoo)
attractions.description: A small municipal zoo established in 1972, a straightforward outing if you're travelling with children or have an afternoon to spare.

attractions.name: Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
attractions.description: It is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. Three aartis (ritual) performed daily; at 7AM, at noon and at 7PM.

attractions.name: Haldia Dock Complex
attractions.description: Commissioned in 1977, the Haldia Dock Complex acts as an alternative to the Port of Kolkata. The port is used mainly for cargo ships.

restaurants.name: The Golden Harvest
restaurants.description: Northwest frontier cuisine
restaurants.address: City Centre, Debhog, The Golden Retreat

restaurants.name: Hotel Dreamland
restaurants.description: Bar with music. Good place with soothing ambience.

restaurants.name: Royal Harbour
restaurants.description: Good crowd in the bar with high class officers and businessmen frequenting the place. There is a protocol and dress code for this place so no non-sense is allowed here.

attractions.name: Raiganj Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: Several types of migratory birds arrive here each year from South Asia and coastal regions. They start arriving in June. The migratory species includes open-bill storks, egrets, night herons and cormorants. The resident birds are kites, flycatchers, owls, kingfishers, woodpeckers, drongoes, etc. Ornithologically, Raiganj Wildlife Sanctuary is a very important heronry.

attractions.name: Bahin Rajbari
attractions.description: One of the significant historical buildings of Uttar Dinajpur, on the banks of the Nagar River and near the border of Bihar. Zamindar Ishwar Chandra Chowdhury built the palace out of bricks. It has large rooms and a veranda.

attractions.name: Mohanta Masjid
attractions.description: A Mughal-style mosque built in 1425 and owned by the Mohanta family.

attractions.name: Pirpukurer Dargah
attractions.description: A dargah of Syed Burhan, built around 1758. Syed Burhan was a leader of the Fakir-Sannyasin rebellion of the late 18th century. The dargah is named after the pond in front of it, where a fair is held on the occasion of Poylā Boishākh (14-15 April).

attractions.name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
attractions.description: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Raiganj and one of the few churches in sub-Himalayan North Bengal. The cathedral features glass and ceiling paintings, prominent pillars on both sides modelled on Greek columns, carved doors and a high altar with a hexagonal dome on top.

attractions.name: Uttar Dinajpur District Museum
attractions.description: The museum has a collection of pottery works, terracotta sculptures and Surjapuri (a Bengali/Maithili dialect) manuscripts.

restaurants.name: Mangalam
restaurants.description: Pure vegetarian AC restaurant

attractions.name: Malda District Museum
attractions.description: The Museum dates back to 1937 and is under the West Bengal Directorate of Archaeology. The museum was started as a place of exhibits of artifacts found in the Malda district. The museum houses beautiful stone and bronze specimens dating back around 750 AD to 1200 AD. The exhibits include ancient coins, stone inscriptions, copper plate inscriptions, manuscripts, arms and weaponry of the medieval period. There are also ancient statues of Hindu gods and goddesses dating back to the 4th and 5th centuries.

attractions.name: Nimasarai Minar
attractions.description: Nimasarai Minar is a collapsed tower with projected spikes. Namasarai literally means halfway inn. It lies halfway between Gour and Pandua in Malda. The probably the place housed an inn in ancient town but no trace of it can be seen today. Only the collapsed portion of the tower stands. Although nothing much is known about the purpose of the tower but historians believe it was constructed as an indication tower for travellers. It was believed that lanterns were put up on top of the tower to guide travellers to the sarai. The projected spikes were probably used for hanging the served heads of executed criminals. The 500-year-old tower is said to be a replica of the Hiran Minar in Fatehpur Sikri. The tower stands on an octagonal base. The upper part of the slightly tapering tower has collapsed long ago. The structure is about 18 feet high and consists of two stories. The stories are marked with projected cornice.

attractions.name: Subhankar Sishu Udyan
attractions.description: There is a restaurant inside. You can also take a boat riding.

attractions.name: Manaskamana Mandir
attractions.description: Visit this pious Hindu Kali temple.

attractions.name: Ramkrishna Mission Ashram
attractions.description: You can visit the place during the evening, experience the chanting and the prayer.

attractions.name: District Library
attractions.description: Read newspapers and local classifieds for free. The library is open from noon-7PM.

attractions.name: Jaunpur Fort
attractions.description: The name Sahi Quila literally translates into royal fort. The fort dates back to the 14th century and was constructed by Ibrahim Naib Barbak, a chieftain of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Over the years the fort has gone through various modifications and extensions. The fort stands on an artificial mound on the north bank of Gomti. It is irregular quadrangular in shape. The fort is surrounded by two sets of walls topped with battlements and reinforced with bastions, The entrance is through the east and the interiors are reached after passing through two gateways. Nothing much is left in the interiors apart from a mosque and a hammam.

attractions.name: Mosque
attractions.description: The mosque dates back to 1376 and was built by Feroz Shah Tughlaq's brother Barbaq Shah. The mosque has three arches on the eastern side and is topped with three domes. There are pillared extensions on the north and south sides. Slender minaretes add to the elegance of the small mosque. The mosque also has a slender minaret in front of it.

attractions.name: Hammam
attractions.description: The Turkish Hammam is located next to the mosque. The hammam is located next to the mosque and is built in Turkish style. The hammam consists of a series of domes complete with turrets allowing light to pass in. The interiors are accessible and consist of a series of rooms connected with a maze of passageways. The rooms consist of water tubs connected with a series of water channels supplying hot and cold water.

attractions.name: Shahi Bridge
attractions.description: A picturesque 16th century bridge across the Gombti which was constructed during Mughal times. One of the finest example of the engineering in the medieval period of India.The old bridge over the Gomti River in Jaunpur dates from 1564, the era of the Mughal emperor Akbar.

attractions.name: Atala mosque
attractions.description: The mosque was constructed in 1408 by Ibrahim Shah Sharki. The foundation stone of the mosque was laid by Feorze Shah Tughlaque in 1393. It towers to a height of 100 ft and have three towering gateways. The mosque has intricate stone works.

attractions.name: Jaunpur Jami Masjid
attractions.description: Built by Hussain Shah Sharqi, the 15th century is one of the largest in India. Situated inside a walled complex it has domed gates on the eastern, northern and southern sides. The mosque lies on the western side and consists of a dome flanked on both sides by vaulted roofs.

attractions.name: Char Angul Mosque
attractions.description: This small mosque is a hidden gem. It is located deep inside the Mufti Mohalla locality of Jaunpur and is difficult to find. Unlike the other Jaunpur mosques it doesn't have a towering gateway but still has its share of elegance.

attractions.name: Lal Darwaza Masjid
attractions.description: This Mosque was built in 1447 (as per inscription of this mosque), during the reign of Sultan Mahmud Sharqi, by Queen Bibi Rajyi, dedicated to Maulana Sayyid Ali Dawood Kutubbudin, a celebrated saint (Maulana) of Jaunpu. This mosque is also located inside a large walled complex with the mosque at the western end. There are gates on the other three sides.

attractions.name: Jhinjhari Masjid
attractions.description: A small and elegant mosque with a towering arched gateway complete with intricate calligraphy from the Koran along with floral and geometric design. It was constructed by Ibrahim Shah Sharki.

attractions.name: Tomb of Shah Feroz
attractions.description: Feroz Shah (not to be confused with Feroz Shah Tughlaq) was a commander of Babur. The tomb consists of a single domed structure.

attractions.name: Tomb of Sher Zaman Khan
attractions.description: The tomb houses the mortal remains of Sher Zaman Khan, a Farukabadi Nawab. It is a spectacular structure crowned with a massive dome. Sadiy, it lies in neglect.

attractions.name: Tomb of Qaliach Khan
attractions.description: Qaliach Khan was the governor of Jaunpur during Akbar's reign. His tomb consists of a single dome flanked with chhatris on both sides.

attractions.name: Sheetla Chukia
attractions.description: Temple of Sheetla Devi

attractions.name: Archaeological Museum
attractions.description: The museum's main attractions are a collections of sculptures during the medieval kingdom period as well as fossils and stone tools from a much earlier era in the ancient site of Dhol Baha, northwest of Hoshiarpur.

attractions.name: Takhni-Rehmapur Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: You will come across nilgai, wild boars, peacocks, deer and leopards at this sanctuary.

attractions.name: Swaran Theatre
attractions.description: One of the oldest cinema complexes in town. Classier but pricier than the cinemas in the malls.

attractions.name: Miraj Cinemas
attractions.description: A large cinema with good acoustics. The popcorn and snacks are quite costly.
attractions.address: J's Eminent Mall, The Mall Rd, Manavta Nagar

attractions.name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple
attractions.description: A temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, where he is worshipped as Adi Kumbeswarar.

attractions.name: Airavatesvara Temple
attractions.description: A temple dedicated to Lord Shiva and a . Built during the Chola era, the temple is named after Lord Indra's elephant Airavata.

attractions.name: Kasi Viswanathar Temple
