attractions.description: Named after the famous temple in Varanasi, this temple worships Lord Shiva as Vishvanatha and his consort Parvati as Vishalakshi.

restaurants.name: Gowrishankar Hotels
restaurants.description: A Vegetarian Restaurant in the premises of Kumbakonam New Bus Stand

restaurants.name: Murali
restaurants.description: Kavitha Hotel - Thirumanjana Veethi Near Kumbeswarar temple

restaurants.name: Meenatchi Restaurant
restaurants.description: Good veggie food.

restaurants.name: Paradise Resort
restaurants.description: Try it for over the top stuff.

attractions.name: Fateh Burj
attractions.description: Fateh Burj is the tallest victory tower (minaret) in India, at 328 feet tall.

attractions.name: Gurudwara Amb Sahib
attractions.description: A historical shrine commemorating the visit of 7th Guru of Sikhs.

attractions.name: Lalan Wala Peer
attractions.description: An Old Dargah

attractions.name: Musical Fountain Floral Garden
attractions.description: Located in the Floral Sculpture Garden

attractions.name: Inderjit Singh Bindra Stadium
attractions.description: Built in 1993, for the time being this hosts Punjab Kings in the Indian Premier League, but they are expected to move to Maharaja Yadavindra Singh Stadium in Mullanpur, Chandigarh. The ground (capacity 45,000) has unusually low-set floodlights to avoid dazzling aircraft at nearby Chandigarh airport, but its main problem in that it's hemmed in by housing.

attractions.name: Arabic & Persian Research Inst
attractions.description: This institute houses a superb collection of Arabic and Persian manuscripts, some of them lavishly ornamented with gold, rubies, emeralds and pearls.

attractions.name: Sunheri Kothi
attractions.description: The golden mansion is the focal point of Tonk. A fairly ordinary monument from the outside, the interior is richly ornamented with stained glass, mirrors, stucco, and gilt. Other interesting buildings are those built to accommodate the British officers.

attractions.name: Banasthali Vidyapith University
attractions.description: Women's university, inaugurated by former Chief Minister Hiralal Shastri.

attractions.name: Temple Dev Dham Jodhpuriya
attractions.description: Dedicated to Lord Devnarayan. The temple houses the shrines of Sri Sawai Bhoj Gurjar, Taradey Panwar, Bhuna Ji and Mehandu Ji.

attractions.name: Hathi Bhata
attractions.description: Built by Ram Nath Salat in 1200 AD, it's a major attraction. It is said that the Pandavas had food here during their exile.

attractions.name: Bisalpur Dam and Bisaldeo Temple
attractions.description: This dam is built on the Banas river, which is the biggest source of irrigation. Bisaldeo temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva and a source of tourism, is also built here.

attractions.name: Shri Diggi Kalyan Ji Tample
attractions.description: The temple of Shri Kalyan Ji Bhagwan, considered to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. The temple was built by King Digwa.

attractions.name: Baram Baba
attractions.description: A popular temple. Durga Pooja (10 days) is celebrated here.

attractions.name: Puri Temple
attractions.description: huge temple of Lord Shiva

attractions.name: Shiv Ji
attractions.description: a famous temple

attractions.name: BRP
attractions.description: A dam located south of the city.

attractions.name: Kodachadri
attractions.description: A very refreshing and spiritual place where Adi guru Shankara Charya enlightened.

attractions.name: Koodli
attractions.description: Place where the rivers Bhadra and Thunga join.

attractions.name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple
attractions.description: This temple was built by the Veera Narasimha, the grandson of Vishnuvardhana belonging to Hoysala Dynasty in the 13th century A.D. The temple has idols of Lord Srikrishna, Lord Purushottama, Lord Ganesha, Goddess Sharadamba and lord Narasimha. The temple is built on a star shaped platform.

attractions.name: Daman Ganga Dam
attractions.description: A dam on the Daman Ganga River, the lifeline of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

attractions.name: Shahidi Park
attractions.description: Literally meaning the "park of the martyrs", on 25 June 1989 26 RSS volunteers were gunned down by terrorists. A memorial was built and committee was set up at the park and on the first Sunday after 25 June each year, the committee pays tribute to the victims of the attack.

attractions.name: Gokul Baba Mandir
attractions.description: This Mandir is Lord Shiva Mandir. Here are also Ram Janki Mandir and Durga Mandir. Many devotees come here. After Diwali a very big Mela is held here.

attractions.name: Kalyani Devi
attractions.description: A very spiritual temple.

attractions.name: Van Devi Mandir
attractions.description: Van Devi Mandir is a famous temple. It holds a fair, which is conducted every year by the villagers, is very famous and enjoyed by a lot of children.

restaurants.name: Awasthi
restaurants.description: Local Indian food.

restaurants.name: Manoranjan
restaurants.description: Local Indian food.

restaurants.name: New Hotel Green Palace And Green Restaurant
restaurants.description: Special cuisine.

restaurants.name: Suruchi
restaurants.description: Fast food place specialising in egg rolls.

attractions.name: Bishnu Temple
attractions.description: This stone temple is built over a platform with a Bengal hut-shaped roof and arched entrance. The temple dates to about the 14th century CE. A stone, called "Narayan shila", is worshipped here as the deity of the temple. Earlier, a 12 armed Lokeswar Vishnu idol was being worshipped as deity, which has been stolen long before. The temple is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

attractions.name: Ghaghar Burhi Temple
attractions.description: A small shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali, it is the oldest temple of Asansol.

attractions.name: IISCO Steel Plant
attractions.description: Operated by Steel Authority of India (SAIL), the IISCO Steel Plant is one of the major steel plants in West Bengal.

attractions.name: Manoj Talkies
attractions.description: You can watch all newly released movies here. Good cinema hall; one of the biggest with a seating capacity of almost 1800.

attractions.name: Nehru Park
attractions.description: A beautiful park on the banks of the Damodar River. A cast iron statue of Nehru, casted by IISCO, is in the park. There is an eatery in the park. There's a big pond inside the park with boating facilities. You can get great views of the Biharinath Hill from the park.

attractions.name: Panifala
attractions.description: A picnic spot with a lake for boating and beautiful garden of flowers.

attractions.name: Satabdi Park
attractions.description: There are facilities for paddle boating and a few rides for children. Nice place to spend the evening.

restaurants.name: Gangar Hotel
restaurants.description: Dhaba type. No pretensions of luxury. Delicious Bengali food - dal-aloobhaja must try; fish range from rui and chital maachh to ilish and varieties of chhoto maachh; those who like can also order mangsho or dimer dalna.

restaurants.name: Garam Masala
restaurants.description: Bombay Hotel presents a complete vegetarian AC restaurant in the market place.

attractions.name: Bhutan Gate
attractions.description: A traditional-style Bhutanese gate, used as a gateway between India and Bhutan.

attractions.name: Chaurasi Gumbad
attractions.description: A square-shaped landmark comprising of nine domes and 84 arches. Built in an Indo-Islamic architectural style, it is believed to house a tomb of one of the Sultans of the Lodi dynasty, who ruled parts of Northern India from the 15th to 16th centuries.

attractions.name: Ocean World Water Park
attractions.description: A water park full of swimming pools and slides.

attractions.name: Matsyagandha Lake
attractions.description: The U-shaped lake next to Matsyagandha Temple sometimes has boating services available.

attractions.name: Crocodile Breeding Centre
attractions.description: The centre has around 10 male and 10 female mugger crocodiles which you can see up close. The guides are very knowledgeable.

attractions.name: Brahm-sarovar
attractions.description: The memoirs of Al Beruni, called 'Kitab-ul-Hind' mentions this sacred water tank. The water tank is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is said in the scriptures that the holiness of performing 'Ashvamedh Yajna' can be achieved by a dip in this sacred water tank. This place is believed to be the land where civilization was born. Lord Brahma is said to have created the universe from this land. Just in the vicinity of this sacred place are the Birla Gita Mandir and Baba Nath's haveli. The sight of Kurukshetra is exquisite especially in winters when birds migrate from ever different landmasses to take a dip in the waters. Best seen during the 'Deep Daan' and Aarti during Gita Jayanti in the later November and early December.

attractions.name: Chatti Patshahi Gurudwara
attractions.description: The Sikh Gurus visited Kurukshetra from time to time. Pilgrims go to the Pundits of their area and sign in their register after taking a bath.

attractions.name: Jyotisar
attractions.description: A pilgrimage site, where the Bhagavad Gita was spoken.

attractions.name: Sanhit-Sarovar
attractions.description: Situated at a distance of 3 km from Kurukshetra Railway Station on Pehowa Road, Sannihit Sarovar is believed to be the permanent abode of Lord Vishnu. It is believed that entire range of Tirthas assemble here on the Amavas day and if a man performs Shradhs at the time of solar eclipse and takes bath in this tank, he acquires the fruit of 1000 Ashwamedh sacrifices. The tank is 500 yards in length and 150 yards in breath. Pilgrims are led first to this holy spot at the time of solar eclipse. The idols of Lord Vishnu, Druv Bhagat, Lord Hanuman and Goddess Durga are placed here. Pilgrims also visit to Pandas and Tirath. Purohits who have their offices on the banks of Sannhit Sarovar, keeping the records hundreds of years old of the pilgrims coming from various parts of the country. People come here for Shradhs of their ancestors.

attractions.name: Snow Yard
attractions.description: This former waste disposal site for marble processing byproducts is now a snow-themed park by the Kishangarh Marble Association (KMA). It is a popular attraction among photographers as the calcium-carbonate-rich slurry has built up into white "mountains", which evoke the glacial fields of Switzerland more than the Thar Desert Rajasthan is known for. Several Bollywood movies are shot here for a snowy backdrop without the exorbitant costs for exotic places.

attractions.name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
attractions.description: A good place to hang out. This holds the record of largest rock built dam in the world. Nagarjuna konda, a "must see" island inside the reservoir, museum of Buddhist and ancient historical articles. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is one of the largest dams built in Asia. It is in Nalgonda district. It is built on the Krishna River between Guntur and Nalgonda districts. It is one of the earliest hydro-electric projects of India. Nagarjunasagar dam, which was completed in 1966, is 124 metres high and 1 km long, and has 26 crest gates. Located at a distance of 150 km from Hyderabad, Nagarjunasagar is an important irrigation dam on river Krishna. This is the tallest and biggest masonry dam in the world. It creates the third largest man-made lake in the world.

attractions.name: Canary Hills
attractions.description: Close to the town lies the Canary Hill which has a well laid out park and is studded with three small lakes and an observation tower. From the top of the hill, in the north-east, one can admire the beauty of the forest whereas the south direction gives the full landscape of the town.

attractions.name: Chandwa Dam
attractions.description: An area for picnics and other fun activities.

attractions.name: Hazaribagh Lake
attractions.description: The Hazaribagh lake in the town also attracts tourists and visitors. It is a popular picnic spot and place for water sports.

attractions.name: Narsingh Sthan Temple
attractions.description: Temple dedicated to incarnation of Lord Vishnu.

attractions.name: Anicut Dam
attractions.description: Not to be confused with the one near Tiruchirappalli.

attractions.name: Gopegarh Heritage and Nature Eco-Tourism Centre
attractions.description: A good picnic spot

attractions.name: Jagannath Temple
attractions.description: The temple was built in 1851, possibly at the request of a descendant of the Ganga dynasty of Odisha.

attractions.name: Jora Masjid
attractions.description: Notable for Annual Urs festival.

attractions.name: St. John's Church
attractions.description: One of the rare churches in Southwest Bengal.

attractions.name: Balurghat College Museum
attractions.description: Many antique collections including coins, inscriptions, sculptures, terracotta, ornamental stones, etc. of ancient ages are preserved here.

attractions.name: Bangarh
attractions.description: An archaeological site with structures from the Maurya Empire to the Pala Empire.

attractions.name: Bolla Kali Temple
attractions.description: Kali Puja is being observed here every Friday following the Rash Purnima. A fair is organised for three days.

attractions.name: Dargah of Shah Ata
attractions.description: A brick-built structure built as early as the 14th century. It is a square, roofless mausoleum enclosing the grave of Molla Ataruddin, also known as Shah Ata. Its lower portion is made of stone.

attractions.name: Kaldighi Park
attractions.description: A large number of migratory birds flock to this place during winter.

attractions.name: Sarengbari
attractions.description: A small forest with an exquisite picnic spot. There's a small hut with drinking water facilities. Permission is required from Hili Block Development Officer (BDO) to visit the area.

attractions.name: Martand Sun Temple
attractions.description: This Kashmiri Hindu temple is an important and protected archeological site. The ruins remain impressive with its decorations and construction.

attractions.name: The Mughal Gardens
attractions.description: With terraced lawns, cascading fountains, and paint-box-bright flowerbeds, they are most charming for tourists. Some of the Gardens of this District and City are: Achabal, Kokernag, Verinag, Sherbag, Daksum, Pahalgam and more.

attractions.name: Kotla Vijayabhaskara Reddy Botanical Garden
attractions.description: Tents are available for longer visits. The paved walkways take you through the 19 sections (Vanaja) in the Patil. The bamboo and palm sectors are major attractions, with varieties of bamboo trees separated by a 3-metre (10 ft) distance. Special signboards are erected at each bamboo variety indicating its generic and scientific names. The palm sector has diverse species. Here you can find a variety of flowers in abundance, such as yellow and purple cosmos, blue salvia, red raselia, etc.

attractions.name: Shilparamam
attractions.description: Designed as a contrast to the futuristic Cyber Tower that lies across the road, the crafts village of Shilparamam ("sculpture village") guards the entrance road to HITEC City. The intent is to showcase and preserve the old. There is a bazaar where you can buy assorted handicraft and art work. There is also an entire village where you can find realistic-looking sculptures of villagers carrying out their traditional crafts. You can also find a rock museum which contains natural rock formations that allegedly look life-like. Pay by UPI or cash as credit cards are not accepted by most shops. Also next to Shilparamam is Shilpa Sandhya Vedika, a location for eating and shopping.

attractions.name: Aalankritha Art Gallery
attractions.address: 41 A, Kakateeya Hills Ext. of Jubilee Hills Road No. 36

attractions.name: Hussain Shah Wali Dargah
attractions.description: The mausoleum of Hussain Shah Wali, a Sufi saint of Golconda during the Qutb Shahi dynasty. He is best known for the Hussain Sagar in Hyderabad. The dargah was built by Abdullah Qutb Shah in his honour.

attractions.name: Ameenpur Lake
attractions.description: A major sport for birdwatchers, with various resident and migratory birds like flamingos, egrets, herons, cormorants, kingfishers and river terns.

attractions.name: Durgam Cheruvu
attractions.description: A popular lake, often called "Secret Lake" since it's hidden between the Jubilee Hills and Madhapur. Under the rule of the Qutb Shahi dynasty (ca. 1518–1687), this lake served as the drinking water source for the residents of Golconda. Nowadays, it is popular among tech workers to relax after their daily grinds. There is an amphitheatre, and the On the Rocks cafeteria. Boating is also available. A cable bridge with dancing fountain also adorns the lake.

attractions.name: Khajaguda Talab
attractions.description: A small lake brimming with species of birds, snakes, snails, and lizards. Khajaguda Talab has been beautified with shoreside sculptures and floaters in the lake.

attractions.name: Osman Sagar
attractions.description: A large reservoir and a popular tourist destination, especially in the monsoon season when the reservoir is full. The Gandipet Eco Park at Osman Sagar has a 2.5-km long boardwalk, an aquarium, a butterfly garden, an open-air theatre and a sensory park.

attractions.name: Mrugavani National Park
attractions.description: This park has a large variety of plants; animals such as the Indian hare, civet cat, mongoose, cobra, Russel Viper and bird species.

attractions.name: Ocean Park
attractions.description: A water-theme park.

attractions.name: Treasure Island
attractions.description: Theme park with go-karts.

attractions.name: Emaar MGF Boulder Hills Golf and Country Club
G. M. C. Balayogi Stadium
attractions.description: A multipurpose stadium with both indoor and outdoor activities. The outdoor (athletic) stadium is used mostly for football matches and it is the host stadium of Hyderabad FC. The indoor stadium is one of the home arenas for the India's prime basketball league, the UBA Pro Basketball League.

restaurants.name: Ginger Court
restaurants.description: Mughlai and Indian Chinese food.
restaurants.address: H No 1-74/1, Guttala, Hitech City, Madhapur

restaurants.name: Olive Garden
restaurants.description: Do not be misled by the name and expect Italian. It serves passable Mughlai and Punjabi fare.

restaurants.name: Collage
restaurants.description: A good choice for a lunch or dinner buffet in HITEC City. The service is courteous and the spread is tasteful though not extensive. The biryani is flavourful and the rest of the Indian fare is also quite decent.

attractions.name: Ramoji Film City
attractions.description: Spread over 2,000 acres, it is a film-themed park combined with a studio, unabashedly modelled after Universal City in California, United States. Opened in 1996, it is the world's largest film studio. It was conceived and developed by Ramoji Rao, a media and film baron, whose film production house Usha Kiron Movies is a major producer of Indian films. The city encompasses massive buildings, gardens and other sets suitable for filming movies. Fans of Indian movies will find many locations where scenes from their favourite films were shot. Inside the city are complete facilities for the film's pre-production, production and post-production work. In addition, there are theme parks, rides and other attractions, and opportunities for shopping and dining. There are three hotels inside the city catering to various budgets. Visitors can easily spend a weekend or more with their families and not tire of the place.

attractions.name: Shilparamam, Uppal
attractions.description: It is an arts and crafts village located in Uppal. The village was conceived with an idea to create an environment for the preservation of traditional crafts.

attractions.name: Telangana State Archives and Research Institute
attractions.address: Rajya Abhilekha Nlym, Upl Road, Tarnaka

attractions.name: Victoria Memorial Home
attractions.description: A historic school and orphanage located in Saroornagar. It is housed in Saroornagar Palace, a palace of the Nizam of Hyderabad.

attractions.name: Ashtalakshmi Temple
attractions.description: A popular Hindu temple of the Goddess Ashtalakshmi.

attractions.name: Hayat Bakshi Mosque
attractions.description: It was constructed in 1672 during the reign of Abdullah Qutb Shah the fifth Sultan of Golconda, and named after Hayat Bakshi Begum.

attractions.name: Moula Ali Dargah
attractions.description: The 400 stairs bring you to a place of worship built by the Asif Jahis. The Moula Ali Dargah was built in the memory of Hazrat Ali, the son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad. Legend has it that Yakoob, a eunuch in the court of Ibrahim Quli, went to the hill after he saw Hazrat Ali seated on it. To his surprise, he saw the impression Ali's palm on a stone, which he had dreamt. He had the impression cut out and installed in a shrine. Ibrahim Shah later built a mosque beside the dargah. A Ashurkhana , a Baradari (pavilion) and a Naqqar khana (place for beating drums) were built during the Qutb Shahi period

attractions.name: Sanghi Temple
attractions.description: A replica of Tirumala Temple.

attractions.name: Kapra Lake
attractions.description: Located close to A.S. Rao Nagar is famous for its idol immersion events during the Ganesh Puja festival.

attractions.name: Saroornagar Lake
attractions.description: This lake is a pleasant space for young couples to spend their evening. It has large pedestrian spaces, and abundant lighting at night. One side of the lake is lined with a solid wall, with a two-lane undivided road on the wall which is neat and exciting to drive. A problem is 'eutrophication' which is caused due to water hyacinth. The lake smells sometimes, but that is the nature of any urban waterbody. An important event that takes place here is Vinayaka Chaturthi (a Hindu festival in which Lord Vinayaka's statues are immersed in water). All roads lead here on the day of the Lord Ganesh's nimajjanam.

attractions.name: Shamirpet Lake
attractions.description: A Nizam-era lake, populated among birdwatchers. The lake is highly patrolled by police due to several cases of drowning.

attractions.name: Mahavir Harina Vanasthali National Park
attractions.description: The largest green space in Hyderabad. This dense forest area was established by the last ruler of Hyderabad, Mir Osman Ali Khan, for hunting. It was declared a national forest in 1975 on the 2500th anniversary of the nirvana of the Jain sage Mahavira. It is home to black buck, cheetal deer, peacocks, wild boars, rabbits, various types of snakes, and many species of birds. Furthermore, it has a special park for parrots. It also has many medicinal plants. The special trees in it resemble dense thickets. There are hostels for tourists' entertainment as well as accommodation.

attractions.name: Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium
attractions.description: The home ground of Hyderabad cricket team, Hyderabad women's cricket team and Sunrisers Hyderabad.

attractions.name: Saroornagar Indoor Arena
attractions.description: Indoor sporting arena with a capacity of 2,000 people. A wide number of sports and many national and international players can be seen here.

attractions.name: Golghar
attractions.description: Captain John Garstin built a Golghar for the storage of food for the British army with storing capacity of 140,000 tons in 1786.

attractions.name: Mahatma Gandhi Setu
attractions.description: The bridge over the river Ganges connecting Patna and Hajipur.

attractions.name: Kumhrar
attractions.description: Explore the ancient ruins of Pataliputra. Of the 80 pillars (Fa Hien, in 5th century CE, found the pillars shining as bright as glass) excavated at the site; only one remains.

attractions.name: Bihar Museum
attractions.description: Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar. It has several galleries, including the regional gallery, the contemporary gallery, the historical art galleries and the gallery on Bihari diaspora. The museum is open from 10:00 to 19:00 except Monday. However, the history part is closed after 17:00 hours and only the Children's Gallery is open from 17:00 to 19:00. Ticket costs for Indians are as follows: Adults - ₹100, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹50, Students - ₹50, while for foreigners is: Adults - ₹500, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹250, Camera - ₹100

attractions.name: Deep Narayan Singh Museum
attractions.description: Small local history museum, named after independence hero and first minister of Bihar, Deep Narayan Singh, who was born in Hajipur.

attractions.name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya
attractions.description: A public museum showcasing the life and principles of Mahatma Gandhi. It contains an exhibition containing photos, paintings, sculptures, manuscripts and quotations; all the major events in his life are told here. There is also a section containing photographs of his childhood through the various phases of Gandhi's life, including being taken to the crematorium. The building also houses a library which has a rich collection of books, magazine, literature and audio-video material related to Gandhi's life.

attractions.name: Indira Gandhi Planetarium
attractions.description: Among the largest and best planetariums in Asia, it attracts a large number of both domestic and foreign tourists. The planetarium has regular film shows on subjects related to astronomy and also holds exhibitions.

attractions.name: Patna Museum
attractions.description: It has more than 50,000 rare art objects, with many related to India in the ancient, middle ages and the British colonial era. Don't forget to see the Holy Relic Casket with the sacred ashes of Lord Buddha, and the beautiful statue Yakshani.

attractions.name: Shrikrishna Science Centre
attractions.description: The main science museum in the city with over 50 exhibits on physics and mathematics, with an emphasis towards optical illusions. Targeted towards kid aged 10 and over but adults will also have an enjoyable time the first time around.
attractions.address: West Gandhi Maidan, Raja Ji Salai, Dujra Diara

attractions.name: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Science City
Rajendra Smriti Sangrahalaya
attractions.description: A museum dedicated to Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India.

attractions.name: Bharatiya Nritya Kala Mandir
attractions.description: A crafts museum and a multi-purpose cultural centre. The building contains dance and drama studios, a gallery space, and an art museum.

attractions.name: Kali Temple-Darbhanga House
attractions.description: One of the oldest temple of Goddess Kali.

attractions.name: Pathar ki Masjid
attractions.description: Built by Pervez, the elder brother of Shah Jahan and the first Mughal prince who made Bihar his residence.

attractions.name: Padri Ki Haveli
attractions.description: Oldest church in Bihar. When Roman Catholics first arrived in Bihar, they built a small church in 1713.

attractions.name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
attractions.description: The birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

attractions.name: Maner-Sufi Saint Shrine
attractions.description: You can buy famous Maner Ka Ladoo(Sweets). Maner Sweets is one of the popular shops that specializes in these. However, avoid going there in the late evening or night.

attractions.name: Sonepur Cattle Fair
attractions.description: Largest cattle and animal fair in Asia. It is held in November in Sonepur which across the Ganges from Patna.

attractions.name: Buddha Smriti Park
attractions.description: A large park constructed in former jail ground is an oasis from noise and bustle of the city. Quiet meditative place and air conditioned libraries are the real relief even for a waiting time for the train. The large stupa is where ashes of Buddha originally from Vaishali are kept. There is a laser show in the evenings, which is related to the history of Bihar from the Ramayana to present.

attractions.name: Funtasia Water Park
attractions.description: Contains attractions like waterslides, wave pool, swimming pools, multi-cuisine restaurant, coffee shops, souvenir shops and a banquet hall.

attractions.name: Gandhi Maidan
attractions.description: Gandhi Maidan is the heart of this city today.

attractions.name: Sanjay Gandhi Jaivik Udyan
attractions.description: One of the most popular picnic spots in Patna. It consists of a zoo and a botanical garden.

attractions.name: Shaheed Veer Kunwar Singh Azadi Park
Patna Golf Club
attractions.description: With some very tough holes, this well-maintained course situated downtown will prove interesting to amateur and pros alike. The Patna Golf Club is set in beautiful surroundings.

attractions.name: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri
attractions.description: The Tomb of Sher Shah Suri follows the Indo - Islamic form of architecture. It was constructed by Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan and was constructed between 1540 - 45. The octagonal tomb stands on an artificial island located at the center of a square man made lake, hence the name Pani Roza. Each side of the square lake measuring 427 meters. The entire complex is fenced and the entry is through a dome pavilion styled gateway on the north side. The Tomb is a protected monument under Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). The island, housing the tomb, is connected to the main land by a causeway from the north side. The causeway was broken and was reconstructed by ASI in 1914 - 15. The causeway has two arched openings connecting the both sides of the lake. The island is surrounded by battlement with four octagonal chatris at the four corners. Each of the three sides (excepting the one on the west) have two projected square chhatris. The main tomb is octagonal and has two levels. There are chatri

attractions.name: Tomb of Hasan Shah Suri
attractions.description: Hasan Shah Suri was Sher Shah's father and his tomb lies just east of his son's tomb. This also is designed by Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan and is a protected monument under Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). The architecture pattern is same as Sher Shah's Tomb but it is smaller in size and is located on ground, hence the name Sukha Roza. Hasan Shah’s Tomb is surrounded by a high wall with gateways on three sides. The western wall houses a mosque and has no gate way. The boundary wall houses four chatris in the four corners. Unlike the Sher Shah's Tomb the lower level has no chatris at the corner, instead the space between the first and second level is filled up with 24 small domes, 3 each on the eight sides. the interior contains the grave of Hasan Shah along with several other graves, sadly the interior is kept under lock and key and access is denied. Sadly the Tomb of Hasan Shah is not well maintained and local boys play cricket in the tomb complex.

attractions.name: Tomb of Islam Shah Suri
attractions.description: Islam Shah, also known as Salim Shah, is the son of Sher Shah. He is the second ruler of the Sur Dynasty, and ruled from 1545 - 54. The tomb follows the plan of Sher Shah's Tomb, but it was supposed to be bigger and the pond larger, Sadly it was never complete. Today the unprotected monument lies in utter neglect and a few pillars and arches are all that remains of the incomplete tomb. The pond also has lost its former glory and so have the causeway. Interior contains several graves, which are exposed to the open sky. Some of the graves are new and it seems the interior of the tomb still functions as an active graveyard.

attractions.name: Tomb of Alawal Khan
attractions.description: Mir Muhammad Alawal Khan (Alawal Khan) was the architect of the tombs of both Hasan Shah and Sher Shah. Sher Shah commissioned a third tomb in Sasaram, which was meant for the architect himself. It was Sher Shah's unique way of paying tribute to his favourite architect, something unparalleled in the history of the world. Today the tomb lies in the southern end of Sasaram. Sadly it lies inside the compound of an active Muslim Graveyard and is not easily accessible. The tomb actually is a walled complex with an entry gate on the east, The gate was crowned with two chatris one of which have collapsed. The interior contains a mosque and the grave of the master architect.

attractions.name: Kandahar Quila
attractions.description: This small fort like structure is located in the vegetable market area of Sasaram. Locals refer to it as the Kandahar Quila and nothing much is known about the history of the structure but it is in a very sad condition. The area in front of the structure is used as a garbage dump and also doubles up as an open public urinal. The interiors of the structure are used by locals for playing card and drinking alcohol.

attractions.name: Maa Tara Chandi Temple
attractions.description: Maa Tara Chandi Temple is one of the "52 Shakti Peetha". The right eye (Netra) is said to have fallen here. It is dedicated to Maa Durga or Maa Shakti.

attractions.name: Kankaleshwar Temple
attractions.description: Yadava meets Bauhaus – a somewhat daring synthesis of old temple building fabric (probably from the Yadava dynasty from the 13th century) and a functional factory style. The temple has a large inner dome. Muslim zealots cut off the heads of all the outer figurines. Inside, the portals to the three sanctuaries are interesting. In order to get to the temple, Kneipp wading is required when the water level in the temple pond is higher, not an easy exercise given the moss-covered stones. But you can hold on to the railing.

attractions.name: Khandoba Temple
attractions.description: 1.5 km from Mansur Shah Dargah is the unusual original Khandoba Temple. It has two towers decorated with stucco and it is somewhat reminiscent of the palaces in Rajasthan.

attractions.name: Khazana Fountain
attractions.description: This site is not well known. The fountain dates from 1583. However, the visit is only worthwhile for hardcore archeology fans, because nothing spectacular opens up for the inexperienced visitor.

attractions.name: Shahinshah Wali Dargah
attractions.description: A tomb of an important Muslim personality. She is always visited by believers. The Daragh is not particularly interesting architecturally, but exudes a nice atmosphere. It can be reached by walking 750 m east of Kankaleshwar Temple or by taking a car.

attractions.name: Mansur Shah Dargah
attractions.description: Here are some covered tombs in a beautiful garden, one of which is made of intricately worked marble. This degree is that of the 18th century Sufi Mansur Shah. The tombs stand on the east side of the river about 1.5 km north of Kankaleshwar Temple.

attractions.name: Kalinka Devi Mandir
attractions.description: Kalinka Devi Mandir is known for its great history. During the Kalinka Devi pilgrimage, people come from far and wide to seek the blessings of the Goddess kalinka devi and his four sister deities. Many devotees visit the temple of Goddess Kalinka every year, especially from the Kasar community, as Goddess Kalinka is the deity of the Kasar community. Digras is 47 km from Parli Vaijnat railway station. Bus services are provided by State Road Transport Corporation.

attractions.name: Parli Vaijnath
attractions.description: Parli Vaijnath has one of 12 jyotirlingas all over the world, one of which is at Vaidyanath Jyotirlinga.

attractions.name: Ghurni
attractions.description: The Bangalore-based Deccan Herald has written, "“We have clay dolls, toys and even clay sculptures in different parts of India. But there has been nothing to match the clay doll artisans of Krishnanagar in the Nadia district of West Bengal. The creations of these artists are displayed in most of the handicraft museums of the world. In India, we have a large display of these dolls in the Shankar's Dolls Museum in New Delhi. One look at the clay dolls and we are amazed at the reality with which the artist has displayed the character of the model." Exhibitions of Krishnagar dolls have been held in London, Paris and Boston. Doll makers market their products personally to the local people as well as to the outside visitors. Sales are also made through Krishnanagar Mritsilpa Co-operative Society, Nadia District Service cum Marketing Co-operative Industrial Union Ltd., and West Bengal Handicraft Development Corporation Ltd.

attractions.name: Krishnanagar Roman Catholic Church
attractions.description: It stands out for its distinctive architecture. There are 27 oil paintings describing the life of Jesus Christ. There also is a Protestant church in the same compound.

attractions.name: Rajbari
attractions.description: The Rajbari has a beautiful Durga temple in the courtyard. Jhulan Mela is celebrated in July-August, Baro Dol is held 12 days after Dol Purnima in March-April.

restaurants.name: Adhar Chandra Das & Sons
restaurants.description: Claims to be inventor of Swarbhaja and Swarpuriya. Shop founded in 1902. This shop was famous for the shooting of the movie Sabar Upore, starring Uttamkumar and Suchitra Sen. Many other sweetmeat novelties available.

attractions.name: Vani Vilasa Sagara Dam
attractions.description: While driving from Bangalore to Chitradurga, it is kind of on the way. This is a very old dam, built in 1907. The view is incredible from here. You are allowed to walk on the dam. There is also a temple close by.

restaurants.name: Krishna Bhavan Cafe
restaurants.description: Vegetarian restaurant.

restaurants.name: Venketeshwara Cafe
restaurants.description: The best non-vegetarian restaurant in Majestic Circle area.

attractions.name: Arunachaleswara Temple
attractions.description: The major tourist and religious destination of the town. The temple has several tall towers in a symmetric arrangement. The temple has several ponds and a thousand-pillared hall. It is full of artistic and legendary sculptures. The "Rajagopuram", principal tower of the temple, is one of the tallest in the state. Like all other Shiva temples, it has a large "Nandi". The temple hosts several cultural, religious and literary events.

attractions.name: Kandha Ashram
attractions.description: Situated just outside the town.

attractions.name: Ramanar Ashram
attractions.description: Situated just outside the town. This is basically a cave where the saint meditated in his early days of enlightenment.

attractions.name: Shivalayams
attractions.description: In addition to the Arunachaleswara temple, there are nine small "Shivalayams" (Lord Shiva temples) along the Girivalam path, each representing the "navagrahas". About 7 km from the Arunachaleswara temple is "Adi Annamalai" (அடி அண்ணாமலை), a large temple. This temple was built before the Arunachaleswara temple. "Ner Annamalai" (நேர் அண்ணாமலை), which is located exactly halfway along the Girivalam path is also a site of interest. From one of the sites along the Girivalam path, a part of the mountain looks like "Nandi" (head of a cow). There are display signs for this: Nandi Darisanam(நந்தி தரிசனம்).

attractions.name: Auspicious Days
attractions.description: Pournami (Full Moon) Day and Karthigai Deepam Festival

attractions.name: Girivalam
attractions.description: The most popular activity in Tiruvannamalai is "Girivalam", which is walking barefoot around the Tiruvannamalai hill. Legend has it that the mountain itself is an incarnation of Lord Shiva, and walking around brings good fortunes. There are 8 lingams one in each direction 360 holy tanks, mandapas and ashrams around the Arunachala hill. Every month on full moon day, scores of people travel to the town for "girivalam". Girivalam is also common on the first day of every Tamil month. Usually, Girivalam starts and ends in front of the Arunachaleswara temple. The Girivalam path is about 13 km (~8 miles) long and has well-maintained concrete/tar roads with pedestrian platforms. One can also do it by cycle, two-wheeler/three wheeler. By foot it takes about 3-5 hours, by bicycle it takes 60-90 minutes. Bicycles are available for renting at nominal rate of ₹10 per trip, auto rickshaws (three wheeler) charge up to ₹150 for a trip. The path is well lit at night and is equipped with sanitation faci

attractions.name: Karthigai Deepam festival
attractions.description: The most important festival for the town, is celebrated during the months of Nov/Dec (full moon day of the Tamil month, Karthigai). The most important event of the festival is lighting a "Deepam" (a large lamp made with several litres of ghee and a several-meter-long cotton wick) at 6PM on the full moon day of Karthigai month. The light can be seen from several towns/villages within a 30 km diameter. Millions visit the town on the day to do "girivalam" and "climb" the mountain. The town literally lights up with fireworks all over. The festival begins 10 days before and concludes 3 days after the full moon day. The "deepam" burns for at least a week. Television and radio channels in Tamil Nadu broadcast the event live. Buses operate to the town from every corner of the state and from major towns in neighboring states.

attractions.name: Kaithal Fort
attractions.description: Restored in 2016.

attractions.name: Tomb of Razia Sultan
attractions.description: Purported to be the place where the only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was originally buried.

attractions.name: Balu
attractions.description: An Indus Valley Civilisation site which has yielded many plant remains.

attractions.name: Tomb of Sheikh Tayyab
attractions.description: The resting place of the 16th century Islamic saint.

attractions.name: Kalayat Ancient Bricks Temple Complex
attractions.description: A temple complex built in the 8th century and now partially in ruins. It has the oldest surviving temples made from brick north of Delhi. Based on the Gurjara-Pratijara architectural style, they creatively make use of floral motifs.

attractions.name: Chacha Nehru Children Park
attractions.description: Named after India's first prime minister, the lush green park has a dinosaur-themed playground, keeping kids entertained for hours. There is also a 1 km walking and jogging path for fitness lovers.

restaurants.name: Vegetarian Village Restaurant
restaurants.description: Modern Indian family dining.
restaurants.address: 2nd Floor, Padma City Mall, Karnal Rd

attractions.name: Rewari Railway Heritage Museum
attractions.description: This museum holds the oldest surviving steam locomotives, including the Fairy Queen. There are exhibits of toy and model trains, railway equipment used in the 19th century, a 3D virtual reality coach simulator and short documentary films showing the railway history of India.

attractions.name: Mithi Vav
attractions.description: 18th-century stepwell which is four-storey deep. Now neglected but still an attraction, it was probably built from material from previous monuments. It has fine carvings of Ganesha, Bhairava, Apsaras etc.

attractions.name: Pataleshwar Mahadev Temple
attractions.description: According to local legend, the Chaulukya king Siddhraj Jaisimha was born in Palanpur so his mother Mayanalla Devi had ordered to build a stepwell. During the construction a Shivalinga was found so a temple was built instead of the stepwell. It is believed that it was a habitat of the serpents.

attractions.name: Joravar Palace
attractions.description: Old palace of Nawab. There are beautiful paintings in the courtroom and the stair has fine sandalwood decoration. Photography with permission.

attractions.name: George V Club
attractions.description: A private sports club now. Nawab Sher Mohammed Khan built it to commemorate coronation of British King George V in 1913.

attractions.name: Pallavia Parshwanath Jain Temple
attractions.description: Beautifully carved marble Jain temple.

attractions.name: Jahanara Baug
attractions.description: Beautiful large garden built by Nawab Taley Muhammed Khan dedicated to his Australian wife Begum Jahanara aka Joan Falkiner.

attractions.name: Old City
attractions.description: Explore the traditional haveli mansions with carved wooden facades and brackets in gated communities called pols in Moti Bazar, Nani Bazar, Jhaveriwad, Teen Batti, Paththar Sadak and Khoda Limda areas.

attractions.name: Diamond Market
attractions.description: There are around 50 diamond wholesalers along this road. Any shop will show you how they cut and polish diamonds in their workshop. Palanpuri Jains are well known for their hold on diamond business around the world. You may find them in Belgium too!

attractions.name: Palanpur Museum
attractions.description: Explore the artifacts and history of Palanpur. 2 hr.

attractions.name: Shahi Roza
attractions.description: Several stone-carved royal cenotaphs. Poorly maintained.

attractions.name: Kirtistambh
attractions.description: The four-storied memorial pillar was built in 1936 for Nawab Sher Muhammed Khan by Nawab Taley Mohammed Khan. The marble plaques on the surface are inscribed with the history of Nawabs and information about Palanpur. It is located on the traffic island.

attractions.name: Mira Gate
attractions.description: In 1750, Nawab Bahadur Khan built a brick and mortar city-walls of Palanpur. It was 3 miles round, 17 to 20 feet high and 6 feet broad with seven bastioned gateways, and, at the corners, round towers armed with guns. The gateways of the city-walls were Delhi Darwaja, Gathaman Darwaja, Malan Darwaja, Mira Darwaja, Virbai Darwaja, Salempura Darwaja, Sadarpur Darwaja or Shimla Darwaja. Only Mira Darwaja survives today.

attractions.name: Gayatri Mandir
attractions.description: A large new Hindu temple.

attractions.name: Mansarovar Lake
attractions.description: Early Jhalori ruler Malik Mujahid Khan built this lake dedicated to his queen Manbai Jadeja in 1628.

attractions.name: Check Photo collection of A. L. Syed (1904-1991)
attractions.description: He was an official photographer of Nawabs of Palanpur. Contact his son Azmat Syed.

attractions.name: Sur Mandir Carnival Cinemas
attractions.description: Watch Gujarati or Bollywood films. Snacks and beverages are available too.

restaurants.name: Street Food at Guru Nanak Chowk
restaurants.description: The street food vendors serve variety of food in the evening to late night here.

restaurants.name: Janta Kachori House
restaurants.description: Oldest and best known shop for eating Kachori.

restaurants.name: Jayanti Fafda House
restaurants.description: For lip-smacking fafda-jalebi.

restaurants.name: Hotel Guptaji
restaurants.description: Affordable and tasty Punjabi meals.

attractions.name: Parnera Hill
attractions.description: It is a hill with a small old fort and a temple. Mainly considered as northern most hill of western ghat.

restaurants.name: Raja Rani Wada Pav
restaurants.description: Very famous for the Wada Pav.

attractions.name: Gaula Barrage & Riverfront
attractions.description: A quiet reservoir and wide pebbly riverbed, favoured for birdwatching, sunrise walks and quiet reflection. The forested foothills form a dramatic backdrop. Locals come here to picnic and bathe; there are no shops, so bring water. The stretch downstream is ideal for light trekking and riverside yoga.

attractions.name: Damuadhunga Forest & Gaula River Trail
attractions.description: An easy, unpaved walking route that follows the river into sal and pine forest. Rich in birds (kingfishers, barbets, forktails) and occasional sightings of barking deer. The trail passes small shrines and ends at a forest rest house. Mornings are most rewarding; go with a local guide or in a group.

attractions.name: Gaula River Suspension Bridge
attractions.description: A pedestrian hanging bridge across the Gaula River, offering fine views of the valley and the forested hills. A peaceful spot to watch the river rush beneath, and a popular photo point.

attractions.name: Bhabar Forest Checkpost & Nature Walk
attractions.description: Entry point to the Gaula forest range, with marked nature trails and bird-watching hides. The checkpost staff can advise on current trail conditions and recent wildlife sightings. A small entry fee may be charged.

attractions.name: Haidakhan Ashram
attractions.description: An international spiritual community founded by the mystic Haidakhan Baba, set in a wooded valley beside a stream. The main temple and meditation hall are open to day visitors. Silence is expected; modest dress and removal of shoes required.

attractions.name: Kali Chaur Temple
attractions.description: A small, ancient hilltop shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali. The 20-minute climb through a scrubby forest rewards with sweeping views over Haldwani, the Gaula valley and the Shivalik ridges.

attractions.name: Sheetla Devi Temple
attractions.description: A revered Shakti temple in the railway colony, especially vibrant during Navratri. The compound exudes a calm, deeply local spirituality.

attractions.name: Maa Nanda Devi Temple
attractions.description: The focal point of Haldwani’s largest fair, Nanda Devi Mela (September), when streets fill with processions, folk music and local sweets. Outside festival time it is a peaceful small temple.

attractions.name: Golu Devta Temple, Kathgodam
attractions.description: A small temple dedicated to the much‑loved Kumaoni deity Golu Devta, the god of justice. Travellers often stop here to offer a bell before starting a journey into the hills.

attractions.name: ISKCON Haldwani Temple
attractions.description: A vibrant temple with continuous kirtans and a small vegetarian restaurant.

attractions.name: Shiv Mandir, Kathgodam
attractions.description: A small, ancient Shiva temple with a stone lingam and peaceful courtyard.

attractions.name: Gurudwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha
attractions.description: A welcoming Sikh gurdwara; the langar (community meal) is open to all.

attractions.name: St. Joseph’s Church
attractions.description: Early 20th-century Roman Catholic church with stained‑glass windows and a quiet garden.

attractions.name: Moti Ram Babu Ram Government Post Graduate College
attractions.description: Founded in 1960, a prominent institution with a graceful older building reflecting the era’s institutional architecture.

attractions.name: Government Medical College
attractions.description: Major healthcare and research campus serving the entire Kumaon division.

attractions.name: Old Kathgodam Railway Station Building
attractions.description: The original 1884 station building, a charming piece of colonial railway architecture.

attractions.name: Gaulapar Fruit & Vegetable Market
attractions.description: Kumaon’s largest wholesale produce market. Arrive before dawn (4-8AM).

attractions.name: Sanjay Van (Chetna Park)
attractions.description: Well-maintained park with a man‑made lake, paddle boats, shady paths and a cafeteria. Entry ₹10.

attractions.name: Mini Forest Park (Nagwan Area)
attractions.description: A tree-covered park ideal for a quiet stroll or jog, managed by the forest department.

attractions.name: Rajiv Gandhi Park
attractions.description: A small riverside park with lawns, children’s play equipment and benches overlooking the Gaula.

attractions.name: Earthinators – SOS: Revive India
attractions.description: A youth‑led environmental organisation based in Haldwani. Their flagship project organises tree-plantation drives, riverside clean‑ups and nature education walks along the Gaula. Visitors can join a weekend activity by reaching out through their social media; it’s a meaningful way to connect with the local community and give back to the fragile Himalayan ecosystem.

attractions.name: Arasavalli Sun Temple
attractions.description: One of the few sun temples in India.

attractions.name: Kurmanathaswamy Temple
attractions.description: Sri Kurmam is a small village just outside the city, which has a famous temple dedicated to Sri Kurmanatha, second avatar of Lord Vishnu. There are regular bus services from the bus stand which takes around 1 hour to drive the 13 kilometers Alternatively, you can hire an auto rickshaw and it generally costs ₹150. On the way to Sri Kurmam, you can visit Surya Narayana Temple at Arasavilli (approximately 2 km from Srikakulam bus stand), dedicated to Sun god.

attractions.name: Danthavarapukota
attractions.description: A Buddhist site with stupas, said to be associated with the Battle of Kalinga by Ashoka, as Danthavarapukota was the capital of Kalinga.

attractions.name: Janardhana Swamy temple
attractions.description: Beautiful gopura.

attractions.name: Kunthi Betta
attractions.description: Good place for trekking.

attractions.name: Varadaraja Temple
attractions.description: 12 feet high deity.

attractions.name: Malavalli temple
attractions.description: Magnificent temple with an ornate gate near a lake

attractions.name: Srirangapatna
attractions.description: Remains of Tippu's Fort, Tippu's Summer Palace, Sangam, Tippu's shrine (Gumbaz), the famous Ranganatha Temple and other places of historical importance

attractions.name: Bluff waterfall
attractions.description: Trolley ride to reach the small hill with a power station

attractions.name: Sangama
attractions.description: Three rivers meet here and there are many riverside cottages

attractions.name: Karigatta hillock
attractions.description: Beautiful temple. The area is ideal for trekking.

attractions.name: Mandya Town
attractions.description: This little town is an ideal place to spend two days eating very good food and walking in the gardens around. Being an affluent locality, restaurants and hotels of good quality are easily available.

restaurants.name: Maddur Vadas
restaurants.description: This snack is available in many roadside stalls in and around maddur and mandya. It is made up of floor mixed with sliced onions. There is a famous small shop for this in maddur.

attractions.name: Kanchrapara Airfield
attractions.description: A historic airfield, used during World War II by British and American fighter jets. This area is used by Indian Air Force for special purposes.

attractions.name: Kanchrapara Railway Workshop
attractions.description: One of the major workshops of Indian Railways. The workshop is open for public in the occasion of Vishwakarma Puja every year.

attractions.name: Dimapur Ao Baptist Church
attractions.description: The largest church in Asia.

attractions.name: Ekteswar Shiva Temple
attractions.description: The temple is dedicated to Shiva, also called Ekteswar. It was built by the Rajas of Bishnupur. The temple was built of laterite but had subsequent additions of sandstone and brick. It is a solid structure, not generally seen in Bengal. The temple was not built in the Bengal style. The top has probably faced damage and so it seems incomplete. Charak Puja is celebrated in the Bengali month of Choitro with great enthusiasm.

attractions.name: Sonatapal Sun Temple
attractions.description: A large temple ascribed to the Rajas of Bishnupur. It is a remarkably solid and tall temple made of brick. Close to the temple, and on the low ground, which is under water during floods, are several mounds. The mounds, as well as the temple, are ascribed to Salibahan. The mounds near the river are said to be part of his garh (fort).

attractions.name: Nagzira Wildlife Sanctuary
attractions.description: Considered to be a "green oasis" in the easternmost portions of Maharashtra, Nagzira hosts a number of migratory birds species, including 13 that are endangered. Notable mammals present at the sanctuary include the tiger and sloth bear.

attractions.name: Navegaon National Park
attractions.description: Another hotspot of diverse flora and fauna. It is a popular picnic place among the locals. The best time to visit is during the winter when a large number of birds flock to the lake in the national park.

attractions.name: Bhitiharwa Ashram
attractions.description: The torch of freedom movement started here by Mahatma Gandhi in 1924. The Satyagrah Andolan started from here as well.

attractions.name: Valmiki National Park
attractions.description: A dense forest and a holiday spot in the periphery. According to mythology it was the residence of Sita, wife of lord Rama, with Luv and Kush, her sons, for years in the Valmiki ashram. Now it is a sanctuary with wide range of animals and goons with pistols.

attractions.name: Searsole Rath
attractions.description: The brass chariot used in the Ratha Yatra celebration of Raniganj.

attractions.name: Pilibhit Tiger Reserve
attractions.description: The protected forest holds an amazing ecosystem of over 400 square miles and provides a good prey base for the elegant cats. Other National Parks like Corbett and Dudhwa in India and Royal Shukla Phatan in Nepal are close by..

attractions.name: Nehru Nagar Garden
attractions.description: A pleasant park and garden.

attractions.name: Prerna Stal Park
attractions.description: The park includes a popular memorial for the late Indian freedom fighter Jawaharlal Darda.

attractions.name: Craig Park
attractions.description: Scenic views of the Hooghly at sunset.

attractions.name: Nandakishore Temple
attractions.description: An at-chala temple with terracotta reliefs.

attractions.name: Ramprasad Vita
attractions.description: Birthplace of Ramprasad Sen, known for composing various hymns and poems. The Ramprasadi tune used to sing his song has influenced various composers, including Rabindranath Tagore. There's a Kali temple next to his house.

attractions.name: Ananda Ashramam
attractions.description: Daily lecture sessions from 3:30PM to 4:30PM. Free food and accommodation to all visitors. Gardens, Bhajan Hall, Goshalas and Library. The Panchavati Garden is an elevated seating place ideal for meditations and daydreams under the canopy of five sprawling trees. There is a special field for growing grass for the cattle and the small gazebo in the middle of the green field is an ideal location for writing poems as birds and butterflies surround you all the time.

attractions.name: Guruvanam
attractions.description: An ashram in a forestlike silent place.

attractions.name: Kareem Forest
attractions.description: 32 acres filled with medicinal plants, birds, insects, reptiles, amphibians, small animals and microorganisms. Popular with students of Botany and Zoology.

attractions.name: Madiyan Koolam Temple
attractions.description: This temple is dedicated to Bhadrakali.

attractions.name: Nithyananda Ashram
attractions.description: Underground caves, Meditation lessons.

attractions.name: Theyyam Temple
attractions.description: Dedicated to Bhadrakali. During the temple festival in May/June and December/January, the ceremonious theyyam is performed here.
attractions.address: Madiyan Koolam, near Kanhangad at Manikoth

attractions.name: Yellow Hills
attractions.description: There is a Hanuman temple and Chirutheyi Cave here. Some other smaller caves are used for generating drinking water.

restaurants.name: Cita Pani Restaurant
restaurants.description: for chicken specialities

restaurants.name: Malabar Delicacies
restaurants.description: There are many restaurants offering authentic Malabar meat and fish preparations.

attractions.name: Chitradhara Waterfalls
attractions.description: Shaped like a horseshoe, it is a popular picnic spot.

attractions.name: Chitrakoot Falls
attractions.description: The third largest waterfall in India, justly known as the "Indian Niagara Falls", will not disappoint you. This spectacular horseshoe-shaped fall is formed where the river Indravati abruptly collapses into a 100 feet deep cavern. The mouth of the fall, when in full profusion, is over 1,000 feet wide. Chitrakot is best seen during and after the monsoon, between July and October. If you want to take photographs, the light is best in the afternoons. Accommodation available, a couple of hundred metres away from the falls. Chhattisgarh Tourism Board (CTB) offers Log Huts (on stilts) with a tariff of ₹1000/- + Luxury Tax of ₹50/- (As on July 2007 - check up with Chhattisgarh Tourism Board for the latest tariff).

attractions.name: Mandwa Waterfalls
attractions.description: javascript:

attractions.name: Teerathgarh Waterfall
attractions.description: This 300 ft high waterfall is actually situated in the Kanger Valley National Park (about 15 minutes from the park entrance), about 37 km south of Jagdalpur (You need to take a detour from NH 212 - the road to Bhadrachalam). The fall here splits into multiple falls, creating a stunning vista. While the Teerathgarh falls are not as wide as Chitrakot, you may stand almost under them, or walk across the top to sit on a rock rising up out of the middle. Well maintained steps lead down to the bottom. There is a small temple on a large rock opposite the falls. All around are the ruins of a 1,000 year old, advanced, Hindu civilisation. Teerathgarh makes a lovely picnic spot. Get down to the base of the falls, and spend time observing the falls in their full glory. Directions - Boards to the falls are virtually non-existent, so be prepared to ask around a bit - locals are co-operative though! The best time to visit is from October to February.

attractions.name: Chaneti Buddhist Stupa
attractions.description: This ancient monument was built during the reign of King Ashoka of the Maurya Empire. It is round in shape, made of bricks, 8 meters in height, in the area of about 100 sq meters, is an old Buddhist Stupa. According to Hieun Tsang, this was built by the King Ashoka.

attractions.name: Kalesar National Park
attractions.description: Kalesar National Park and adjacent Kalesar Wildlife Sanctuary are protected areas in Kalesar of Yamunanagar district. Jeep safaris are available on 3 motorable tracks during the designated park opening months.

restaurants.name: Dalroz Baker's Cafe
restaurants.description: Famous for its baked foods and cakes though they also serve other Western fare, including pizzas, burgers and nachos.
restaurants.address: 2nd Floor, SCO 91, Yamunanagar Rd, Sector 17, Huda

attractions.name: Chharra Airfield
attractions.description: An abandoned airfield used by the United States Army Air Forces during the Burma Campaign (1944-1945) of World War II.

attractions.name: Saheb Bandh
attractions.description: A calm lake with ambient sound of water and birds during dawn and dusk. Great for relaxation and walking.

attractions.name: Haripada Sahitya Mandir
attractions.description: A research centre and library. It was inaugurated in 1960 by central minister Humayun Kabir in 1960. It displays exhibits collected from different areas of Purulia District.

attractions.name: Maha Mrityunjay Temple
attractions.description: Mahamrityunjay Mandir, 18 km from Nagaon town, is famous for being world's tallest Shivlinga (phallus sculpture dedicated to the Hindu god, Shiva), at 126 feet tall. It is situated in Narkasur path, Puranigodan, Nagaon district.

attractions.name: Trinetra Ganesh Temple
attractions.description: Ancient temple, dating back to 1299.
attractions.address: Opposite Hotel hill View Ranthambore Road

attractions.name: Chamatkar Temple
attractions.description: A Jain temple.

restaurants.name: Manisha Restaurant
restaurants.description: Vegetarian café popular with the locals.

restaurants.name: Ranthambhore Chokhi Dhani
restaurants.description: Popular for daal baht.

attractions.name: Raghunath Palace
attractions.description: It is a white, two-storey palace. This palace is open for public only on the day of Dussehra every year. It's an old tradition that the heir of royal family of Surguja meets and greets the visitors on Dussehra and the festival is celebrated in a pompous manner.

attractions.name: Kuntala Waterfalls
attractions.description: These waterfalls, highest in Telangana, are some 30 km out of town. They are a popular day trip, not only from Adilabad but even from Hyderabad. Legend has it that the waterfalls derived they name after Shakuntala, beloved wife of King Dushyanth. They are said to have fallen in love with each other in these beautiful surroundings. The story also tells that Shakuntala used to bathe near the waterfall. To get here, take a bus to Neredikonda and a taxi or rickshaw from there.

attractions.name: Jainath Temple
attractions.description: 21 km out of town, this temple complex has all the architectural treats of the Jain temple style. In it, you'll find stone inscriptions in prakrit, including 10 ślokas, or verses.

attractions.name: Paris By Scooter
attractions.description: All Vespa scooter rentals and Paris guided City tours include the collect and picked up from, your hotel in Paris.

attractions.name: Eiffel Tower
attractions.description: No other monument better symbolizes Paris.

attractions.name: Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile
attractions.description: The Arc de Triomphe exudes grandeur and offers a central view of the city.

attractions.name: Champs-Élysées
attractions.description: Widely regarded to be one of the most recognizable avenues in the world

attractions.name: Notre Dame Cathedral
attractions.description: Impressive Gothic cathedral that was the inspiration for Victor Hugo's novel The Hunchback of Notre Dame.

attractions.name: Sacré Coeur
attractions.description: A church perched on top of the highest point in Paris. Behind the church is the artists' area, in front are spectacular views of the whole city.

attractions.name: Opera Garnier
attractions.description: Masterpiece of theatre architecture of the 19th century built by Charles Garnier and inaugurated in 1875 housing the Paris Opera since it was founded by Louis XIV.

attractions.name: Catacombes de Paris
attractions.description: Used to store the exhumed bones from the overflowing Paris cemetery. The bones of more than 6 million bodies lie here.

attractions.name: Grande Arche de la Défense
attractions.description: A modern office-building variant of the Arc de Triomphe.

attractions.name: Panthéon
attractions.description: Underneath, the final resting place for the great heroes of the French Republic including Voltaire, Victor Hugo, and Marie Skłodowska-Curie; above, a marvellous view of the city.

attractions.name: Père-Lachaise Cemetery
attractions.description: Unlike any cemetery in the world. Ornate grave stones, monuments set among tree lined lanes. See the graves of Jim Morrison, Oscar Wilde, and Frédéric Chopin, among many others.

attractions.name: Sainte-Chapelle
attractions.description: Exquisite stained glass chapel. More beautiful interior than the gloomy Notre Dame Cathedral.

attractions.name: The Louvre
attractions.description: One of the finest museums in the world of art and culture. Home of the Mona Lisa and innumerable others. Enormous building and collection, plan at least two visits..

attractions.name: Musée d'Orsay
attractions.description: Incredible collection housed in a former railway station. Works by the great artists of the 19th century (1848-1914) including Monet's "Blue Water Lilies, Renoir's "Bal du moulin de la Galette", van Gogh's "Bedroom in Arles", Whistler's "The Artists Mother", etc.

attractions.name: Rodin Museum
attractions.description: Collection and archives dedicated to the sculptor Auguste Rodin, in a charming home with garden.

attractions.name: Picasso Museum
attractions.description: Contains the master's own collection.

attractions.name: Musée Marmottan-Monet
attractions.description: Over 300 paintings of Claude Monet. Also, the works of Berthe Morisot, Edgar Degas, Édouard Manet and Pierre-Auguste Renoir. "Impression Soleil Levant" by Monet is on display.

attractions.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
attractions.description: [Jardin des Tuileries] Houses "The Water Lilies" (or "Nymphéas") - a 360 degree depiction of Monet's flower garden at Giverny. Also, impressionist and post-Impressionist paintings by Cézanne, Matisse, Modigliani, Picasso, Renoir, Rousseau, Soutine, Sisley and others.

attractions.name: Musée Delacroix
attractions.description: Housed in the home of painter Eugène Delacroix.

attractions.name: Centre Georges Pompidou
attractions.description: The museum of modern art. The building and adjoining Stravinsky Fountain are attractions in themselves. Closed for renovation until 2030.

attractions.name: Les Invalides
attractions.description: Very impressive museum of arms and armor from the Middle Ages to today. Also contains the tomb of Napoleon Bonaparte.

attractions.name: Musée national du Moyen Âge
attractions.description: A medieval museum exhibiting the five "The Lady and the Unicorn" tapestries, housed in a part Roman, part medieval building.

attractions.name: Musée des Arts Décoratifs
attractions.description: Showcasing eight centuries of French savoir-faire.

attractions.name: Carnavalet
attractions.description: Museum of Paris history; exhibitions are permanent and free. Renovated 2017–2021.

attractions.name: Cité des sciences et de l’industrie - La Villette
attractions.description: Science museum primarily for children.

attractions.name: Mémorial de la Shoah
attractions.description: Paris's Holocaust Memorial Museum, in the heart of the Marais on rue Geoffroy l'Asnier. Free Entry, weekly guided tours. Second Sunday of the month there is a free tour in English.

attractions.name: Jacquemart-Andre Museum
attractions.description: Private collection of French, Italian, and Dutch masterpieces in a typical 19th-century mansion.

attractions.name: Guimet Museum
attractions.description: One of the largest collections outside Asia of Southeast Asian, Indian, Afghan, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean art.

attractions.name: French Open
attractions.description: One of the four tennis Grand Slam tournaments. It is scheduled for two weeks from the last Sunday in May. The event, on clay courts, features the world’s top-ranked tennis players.

attractions.name: Stade de France
attractions.description: France's national stadium has a capacity of 81,338, and hosts concerts and various events. Soccer clubs sometimes play here when their home stadium is unavailable.

attractions.name: Maison Européene de la Photographie
attractions.description: Important center for contemporary photography with a large exposition area having three or four major expositions per year dedicated to contemporary photography. Housed in an updated hôtel particulier built in 1706. There is a large library, auditorium and café. Their archive houses over twenty thousand works of art. Admission is free every Wednesday from 17:00 to 20:00.

attractions.name: Better Paris Photos
attractions.description: Better Paris Photos offers instructional tours and workshops that combine hands-on learning of essential photographic techniques with guiding to, and commentary about, the most photogenic spots of Paris. Led by English-speaking photographers and instructors, these tours are open to all skill levels and interest.

attractions.name: Le Foodist
attractions.description: In the Latin Quarter, Le Foodist is an cooking school that offers French Cooking, Pastry and Baking Classes, Wine Tastings initiations, Food Tours and Hosted Gastronomic Dinners. Led by French Chefs, courses are made in English, small classes, with the ambition of teaching both the technique and the history of traditional French recipes.

attractions.name: Le Cordon Bleu Paris
attractions.description: Offering both long-term professional programs as well as short term hourly sessions, Le Cordon Bleu is one of the most famous culinary schools located in the heart of Paris. Le Cordon Bleu is considered to be the guardian of French culinary technique through its culinary programs that continue to preserve and pass on the mastery and appreciation of the culinary arts that have been the cornerstone of French gastronomy for over 500 years.

attractions.name: La Cuisine Paris
attractions.description: La Cuisine Paris is an English-friendly culinary school located in the heart of Paris, right on the Seine that offers expert teaching of the essential techniques of cuisine française. Led by an international group of English-speaking chefs all trained in classic French cooking, these classes are open to all skill levels and tastes.
attractions.address: 80 Quai de L'Hôtel de Ville, Paris 75004

attractions.name: Funaoka Onsen
attractions.description: Funaoka Onsen is one of the oldest public bath houses in Kyoto still in operation. Its classic building is an excellent example of bath house architecture of the beginning of the 20th century. Funaoka Onsen is popular with both locals and visitors and is a must if you have an hour to spare.

attractions.name: Toei Kyoto Studio Park
attractions.description: Toei Kyoto Studio Park is an active film studio which continues to be used for the filming of period dramas. Visitors may visit the outdoor sets used in many samurai movies, and if they are lucky, could potentially observe the filming of a period drama.

attractions.name: Goa Gajah
attractions.description: The centerpiece here is a cave dating back to the 9th century, the entrance to which is an ornately carved demon's mouth. Inside are some fragmentary lingam and yoni statues, as well as a statue of Ganesha. Large, carved guards stand around pools near the entrance, and a little path leads to a waterfall, rice fields, and some Buddhist stupa fragments. Some parts of the Goa Gajah complex were not excavated until the 1950s. Nominated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. 30-60 min visit without guide. Unclear if dirt path to rice fields and elephant river is usable/maintained.

attractions.name: Gunung Kawi
attractions.description: Dating from the eleventh century, this is presumed to be the burial complex of King Anak Wungsu and his many wives. Reached by climbing down 371 steps, the location at the bottom of a steep valley lined with paddy fields, is quite stunning. The smaller complex on the south side of the river is presumed to have been built for the King's wives, while the larger complex is thought to have been the residence of the King himself, and perhaps his concubines. The structures are carved into the sides of a steep river valley, and the river crossed by twisting trees and vines. You must take off your shoes before entering into the central pura complex. About 1 km downstream there are further tomb cloisters. On the way back up, take a break at Cafe Kawi which has cold drinks for Rp10,000 and up. If you haggle for a taxi from Ubud, it should cost no more than Rp150,000 to get there and back, with the driver waiting for you while you make the visit. Sarong is included in the entry and free, so you c

attractions.name: Pura Kehen
attractions.description: One of the most attractive temples in the whole of Bali, and as it is slightly off the beaten path, one which receives relatively few visitors. The temple was founded in 1206, and has an especially impressive 11-tiered meru in the inner courtyard. When you visit here take a little extra time to look around Bangli. It is a quiet and attractive market town.

attractions.name: Puri Saren Agung
attractions.description: This was the palace of the kings of Ubud until the 1940s, and some royal descendants live there to this day. Parts of the complex are off limits to the public, but entry to the rest is free, and this is Ubud's best setting for dance performances (see Do). 10-15 min visit without a guide.

attractions.name: Tirta Empul
attractions.description: One of the holiest temples in Bali built around hot springs that still bubble in the central courtyard. The Balinese come here to bathe and purify themselves physically and spiritually, and during Galungan, the sacred barong masks are bathed here. The complex dates to 960, but the present buildings are largely modern reconstructions. Visitors may participate in the traditional purification ritual (melukat) by wearing a sarong and entering the bathing pools. Observe local customs and avoid entering if not appropriately dressed or during certain religious restrictions.

attractions.name: Yeh Pulu
attractions.description: This complex of rock carvings is close to Goa Gajah but far less well known. The carvings date from the fourteenth or fifteenth century, and are set in a very attractive rice field. You can reach Yeh Pulu on foot through the rice fields from Goa Gajah, but you will definitely need a guide for the 45-minute walk as there is no path to speak of. In addition to the carvings, there is a holy well here, and the attendant priest will be happy to bless you with the well water. Temple dress code applies (you can rent a sarong at the ticket counter without extra charge). This is a much underrated and under-visited site, and is highly recommended.

attractions.name: Chapel of Mother Goddess, Rajarajeshwari Tripurasundari
attractions.description: A modern chapel dedicated to the feminine aspect of the divine, such as Kuan Shih Yin, Mary Magdalene, Mother Mary, Lakshmi, Durga, Kali, Saraswati, Gayatri and others.

attractions.name: Saraswati Temple
attractions.description: Taman Saraswati Temple, also known as Pura Taman Kemuda Saraswati, is a graceful water temple located in the heart of Ubud, Bali. Dedicated to Saraswati, the Hindu goddess of wisdom, learning, and the arts, this temple is renowned not only for its spiritual significance but also for its striking beauty—especially the elegant lotus pond and water garden that stretch out in front of its ornately carved gates.^Built in the late 20th century by famed Balinese architect I Gusti Nyoman Lempad under commission from the Ubud royal family, the temple blends traditional Balinese architecture with classical Hindu iconography. Intricate stone reliefs adorn the walls and gateways, many of which depict figures from Hindu mythology, including Saraswati herself holding a manuscript and a veena, symbolizing knowledge and the arts.A wide path flanked by blooming pink lotuses leads visitors from the street to the temple entrance, though the inner sanctum is reserved for worshippers, the outer courtyard a

attractions.name: Pura Gunung Lebah
attractions.description: Pura Gunung Lebah sits at the confluence of the Campuhan and Wos rivers beside Campuhan Bridge. Dating from the 8th century, it is one of Ubud's oldest and most sacred temples. Dedicated to the spirit of the surrounding valleys, the temple is known for its peaceful atmosphere, traditional stone carvings and lush jungle setting. It also marks the southern entrance to the popular Campuhan Ridge Walk.

attractions.name: Agung Rai Museum of Art
attractions.description: Showcases works by well known Balinese artists, as well as international artists who made Bali their home such as Walter Spies, Adrian Jean Le Mayeur, Rudolph Bonnet and Arie Smit. The only painting in Bali by renowned Javanese artist Radan Saleh is exhibited here. They also run workshops for thirteen different aspects of Balinese art and culture. Price includes tea or coffee (hot or cold) at their cafe.

attractions.name: Blanco Renaissance Museum
attractions.description: Before he passed away in 1999, Spanish artist Antonio Blanco was an absolute fixture on the Ubud art scene. His former home is now a museum showcasing his sometimes bizarre but always interesting work. Think Salvador Dali transplanted to Asia. In the garden you can take pictures of the exotic birds flying around. A gallery and a studio is connected to the museum. Also, there is a family temple and a vegan restaurant here.

attractions.name: Museum Puri Lukisan
attractions.description: When it opened in 1954, this was the first private museum in Bali. Three buildings showcase traditional and modern Balinese art. The displays are a little musty and English labeling is spotty, but some of the works, particularly the carvings, are quite amazing. Exhibits by noted artists I Gusti Nyoman Lempad and Rudolph Bonnet, among others.

attractions.name: Museum Rudana
